Like many others on here, I have been a devoted fan  since the first The Sims game came out.  With Sims 1 & 2, I typically bought each expansion/stuff pack as it came out.  However, I waited quite a while before I got into Sims 3.
It is true that buying everything at once can be expensive, but I think I got base game through Showtime here on Steam during Christmas 2012, which meant everything was greatly reduced in price.  If you can do that, then I think you'll find it's a bit easier to swallow the pricetag.  You can also prioritize which ones you get - Katy Perry's Sweet Treats and Movie Stuff are two of the ones that I feel you can reasonably wait to get until they're on sale, as they don't add a whole lot to the game in my opinion.
For those that have complained about stability or other issues with the game, I  recommend NRAAS' mods, particularly Overwatch. ErrorTrap, and Saver.  They vastly improve the game.  There are also a ton of other mods out there that fix or add in various things, although I primarily use NRAAS and then a few from
.
Overall I highly recommend this game if you like sandbox and simulation games.  I have yet to play the Sims 4, but I'm waiting until those have been out for a while in the hopes that any bugs will be repaired by either EA or modders.

awesome, action packed, hack and slash game. The amount of gameplay content is very high, the best in the series, especially considering the tones of gameplay hours that u can spend on 5 different characters, some old and some new. This is the DMC 4 Special Edition, the HD remaster of the 2008 DMC 4 game that featured a new character nero alongside the franchise champion Dante. This time in special edition, Capcom has added 3 new playable character to the game, 2 of which (Lady and Trish) were already part of the DMC 4 storyline but weren't playable, and the other is non other than fan favourite vergil. Vergil features newer move set than that featured in DMC 3 Special edition, not to mention all 3 characters have their own openings and endings (with trish and lady sharing the cutscene :D ).
Now about the gameplay :
Those who know the DMC series will find this to be really satisfying to play and master. Each new characters feature tonnes of new gameplay mechanic and combos that makes the returning DMC 4 players something to keep engaged. Vergil especially has been reimagined properly in terms of his gameplay. He is far more satisfying than the DMC 3 vergil although this version shares the same art style (with HD textures/model) of the DMC 3 vergil.
Lady brings a whole new style to the DMC franchise, ranged gameplay. Her ranged offensive power play is really fun to play as, especially when she's the only character who doesnt have a DT, so health regen is really a problem for her unlike other characters. Trish is also fun and features massive area of effect damage play style than others.  Very good for the "Legendary dark knight" mode's hordes of enemies that fills the screen.
Performance
I run a old system that can run most games in average graphics and DMC 4 SE didnt trouble me at all in terms of performance . Considering it to be a remastered 2008 game i didnt expect to cause problems other than few game crashes here and there as i alt+tab or pop-up the steam interface (its weird) .
TL/DR
really great game coming from DMC series, tonnes of gameplay hours for those hard core gamers. Pretty much same content, enemies and bosses. Except for the new playable characters (Vergil/Lady/Trish) there is no other change. The game saves Automatically which saves lot of button presses and precious time :D. 2-3 additional skins for all playable characters (including the pre-order bonus skin).
Would recommend this for any hack and slash fan, especially to a DMC fan :D

Devil May Cry 4 Special Edition is another successful notch on Capcom’s remastering bedpost, as it comes in with enough content and vast difference between the characters to make it worthwhile playing through all over again. A solid game from 2008 just got better and although not up to par in looks compared to more modern games, the gameplay is rock solid and shows that graphics aren’t always indicative of all round fun. For its cheap price Devil May Cry 4 Special Edition comes highly recommended, although be warned of the puzzles which might need some external help to pass.

I played this game for way longer than I should have because it's such fun. Primarily a strategic rather than tactical game (due to the chaos of actual battle). The only issue I had was the fact that the AI lords cheat when conscripting. You can beat an AI Lord, wipe out his army, take all his villages and disgrace him to high heaven. However, he will still end up being able to field an army that is larger and more experienced than one that you could field with the same resources / conditions. I got around this by enabling in game cheats, which may not be the way everyone wants to play.
No hour on this game is wasted. Period.

is a supernatural themed visual novel made by Spanish developers Eternal Night Studios.

Trick and Treat is a visual novel from Eternal Night Studios, now the first thing to take notice of before starting down the proverbial rabbit hole that is this VN is its name;  Trick and Treat, you can see that instead of the usual "or" they have chose to use "and", so the name carries a rather intriguing and different meaning, but what?.....Well......I dont like spoilers so that's for you to find out for yourself.
The events of Trick and Treat occur on all hallows eve. Our main characters are three 17-year-old friends from a small town. I wont go to deep into the the character bios as finding out about them is all part of the experience, however Ill give a few details about the main character. You play as Axel, you wakes up at the very beginning of the VN in a strange and foreboding forest, alone and without friends. Ahead of you is a great adventure if a somewhat short one but there are eight different endings which  increases its replayability greatly.
This is a VN that just has to be experienced saying pretty much anything would spoil the story for you, Trick and Treat is a very well written and thought out piece of work; Visually its alright, music its good however its the endings that really sold it for me. Length wise it is not the longest I have come across, however it will no doubt keep you interested throughout its duration and as I said it has a great deal of replayability.
Overall Trick and Treat is beautifully written piece of work it has an Interesting Storyline; It is visually appealing, the characters are interesting, though simplistic its fluid style makes it very enjoyable.
(Like all my reviews I do not put a score as it is my belief that games like all forms of art are subjective and therefore it is impossible to afix a number to them)

The game itself worked very well and the gameplay was, for the most part, fun. Graphics are good and the larger maps, with aricraft and tanks are quite enjoyable. Armour in the game is also quite fun, and there is ample oppertunity for you to get the weapons necessary to defeat armour. The maps are very good and well designed, with them having varying sizes and different features to make them unique.
However, with even a slight dip in internet speed, the game becomes difficult to play, with enemies not loading or your gunfire not causing enemy damage. Some of the guns in game are unbalanced, I`ve come across people using weapons that are nearly one hit kills and while realistic (which a good thing) in gameplay terms it can be very annoying. I feel there may also be balancing issues, not huge ones but more experienced players are put in games with less experienced ones.
On another note, where is the UK and Japan? These two nations, both key players in the Second World War, are completely rejected from the game. Being British myself, I would love to play as a Red Devil Paratrooper or drive a Churchill Heavy Tank. Japan would be really interesting to play, with their army being styled and operating differently to the other nations already in the game. The French would also be a great addition, with their tanks being some of the best on the planet at the time. With the addition of the UK, other Commonwealth nations could be added as well such as Canada and Australia, each with different skins and weapons.
To conclude, the game can be enjoyable if  your internet connection is good. The maps are great as is the gameplay, most of the time. The problems with the game would be easy to fix, given time. Adding Britain, the Commonwealth, Japan and France would make the game better, opening it up to more people.

Mortal Kombat X is a fighting game that I recommend everyone who enjoys fighting games to try out. If you are a longtime MK fan, then owning the game is a must. I had read review after review about MKX. I was on the fence about whether I should buy it or not. The complaints about lack of PC support and the lack of additional DLC were at the top of my mind. However, my strong appeal for the MK universe won out and I decided to purchase it. I purchased it for full price too, and several of the DLC that looked good to me. I was not disappointed at all.
The gameplay is fairly fast and brutal. If you make just a couple of mistakes, you do not survive the match. The combos are well done, with enough flow to keep the game moving, but not so much that they take up the entire focus of the game. Say, like in KIller Instinct. Great game, completely unrelated to this review, except that in KI, long strung out combos are the focus of the gameplay. In MKX, combos add to what you can do to the opponent, not your only method for winning.
You are free to experiment and implement your own combos with a mix of basic, half combos and special moves. The controls are well done and respond when you press them in the order you tell them to. I did not notice any lag or having to input my combos over and over again to get them to work.
Each character has a different feel and then within that, each character has 3 variations to choose from. Some variations work better for other people. Character choice feels like it is more of a matter of personal preference than anyone being too powerful. A couple of minor exceptions being Jason Vorhees and the Predator, two optional DLC characters. They feel a little over powered for my tastes, but they are still fun to play every now and then.
Graphics of course, are excellent. My only problem with anything graphical or gameplay wise is that my laptop must be plugged in to not have any slowdown. Killer Instinct is the same way, so I believe that my graphics card doesn't run at maximum settings until it is plugged in.
The pricing of the DLC is something that I'm not overly fond of. However, as I enjoy the game, I am more than happy to support the developers for their work and purchase any DLC that I find that adds to my game. The game was a full and complete game when I bought it. The roster was solid, in my opinion. I had no issues with it. When I found out that I could buy a few more characters to add to my game, I was more than happy to shell out a few more dollars to add them. I view the DlC as more like an expansion to the game. Not necessary, required or needed, but definitely appreciated and it adds to the game's lifespan.
Okay, I'll admit that I do not play online, so I cannot rate that  aspect of the game. I found out a few years ago that I play like a mix between the CPU being put on hard/medium. I play decent, but am not great. Some players I found that I could crush beneath the weight of my boot. Others I wondered how what they were doing was even possible. I felt like they could read my mind. Throw me when I go to block, hit me high or low, opposite of what I was doing, and juggling me like a professional circus act. So, I don't feel the need to play complete strangers. The local multiplayer, though, is great. Grab an in-law or friend and sit down and beat the other person senseless. Maybe even perform a fatality just to rub it in that you won. So if you have anyone that you can play locally, this game is a great way to pass some time.
For being a fighting game, there seems to be a lot of content with it. The Faction Wars, which I haven't dealt with much yet, so I cannot say how much I like or dislike them. The krypt for unlocking in game costumes, fatalitiies and so on. The traditional arcade style tower mode to find out a specific characters ending that has no bearing on the actual story, but still fun. Living towers that change over time and have different tasks to complete and ways to fight. It all just adds to the game, making a standard 2D fighter a lot more interesting. The story mode is fun, fairly short unfortunately, but continues straight on from MK9. I actually like their reworked stories and how it is progressing. Bringing in children of longtime characters was interesting, but it worked well for me.
Overall, my experience with MKX has been a solid positive experience. The rosters are well rounded, gameplay is clean and tight, graphics are excellent. Fatalities just add to the fun as does local coop. Fans of fighting games should definitely pick this title up.

Addressing a response, "I assume you think the same of Super Mario?", it gets a pass because of it's age, but I don't think the original is a particularly good platformer compared to some newer platformers.
With slippery controls, less than eye-popping graphics, and repetitive enemies and boss battles, the original Super Mario Bros. had much room for improvement.The Mario series itself acknowledged as much by adding and innovating over the years, accepting that the original wasn't the peak of the genre.
Similarly, if Super Blue Boy Planet turns out to lead to more interesting, longer, and more fun sequels, I'll think of those games as being better. However, while the average value of the series as a whole might increase, I maintain that the original game doesn't become better for it.

With the release of DmC: Devil May Cry, its easy to think that Capcom had forsaken its beloved action franchise. However the release of Devil May Cry 4: Special Edition definitely sees a revitalization with the series we've all come to know and love.
This title is loaded with bonus content that ranges from additional replayability in the form of new characters all the way to artwork. By far the most anticipated feature in the game is the ability to play as Dantes twin brother, Vergil. Speaking from personal experience as a seasoned DMC veteran, I can confidently say that Vergil is an absurdly powerful character, but simple game mechanics hide the true depth of his gameplay.
In addition to Vergil, Trish reappears as a playable character and Lady makes her debut here. Trish is a much more control oriented character, using the Sparda to keep enemies at bay or pull them in, and her lightning attacks stagger enemies in place allowing her to land some heavy shots. Lady on the other hand, being a human, relies on her gunplay to get the job done. Wielding dual model 1911 pistols, a shotgun and her trademark rocket launcher Kalina Ann, Lady can keep enemies at bay with relative ease before blowing them to kingdom come with a barrage of missiles. You would think that a character with little to no melee attacks has no place in the DMC family, but rest assured, Lady is just as Stylish as the rest of them.
While the new characters are a nice breath of fresh air, the overall game itself leaves a little to be desired. Even with the updated graphics, there are no new levels to the campaign, and some (including myself) might feel a little shafted that Vergil, Lady and Trish do not have separate campaigns all their own, complete with all new levels and possibly enemies.
In the end, what we have is a true Devil May Cry game with loads of bonus stuff to do and play around with. Just like DMC3SE before it, the game adds very little when it comes to new game modes and a lack of new levels, but the sheer amount of content that is laden within this game far outweighs the sins that it can possibly commit.
I highly reccomend this title to any and all gamers.

Well, this review is not for those who like this kind of RPGs. Rather, I would pen it down for those few like me who usually hate top down. Well, I love action RPGs - fallout 3, Fallout New Vegas and Skyrim are the among the best single player experiences I can remember. But when it comes to top down, I just used to have a scorn for the genre.
I tried diablo 3, torchlight and torchlight 2 (a torchlight fan) at a friend's house long back. I hated it and never looked towards it for months to come. It is accidentally that I had some $4.00 in my wallet and TL2 was on sale that I purchased it. I wanted to try it again, even though I was 99% sure it won't appeal me.
I was wrong. The game is GREAT. But to realize its greatness, there are three things you must keep in mind:
- Don't think that you are playing an action game. There is very little skill of swiftness on mouse and keyboard required in this game. So, definitely not an action game.
- Play it for at least 15 hours, level up to level 25 and then judge.... things keep on adding, new skills start appearing, interesting scrolls begin dropping out of chests and skilled monsters... it is then that you understand how amazing this game is.
- If you are dying more, it is not that you are not able to deliver enough clicks-per-second, it just means that each of the clicks has an ignorantly cascaded set of skills behind it. So, activate the right skills and wear the right armor. I started learning new things about the mechanics when I was 3 hours into the game and am learning totally new things till now (e.g. For torchlight 2 players - sets of armor... the purple thing written in some armor's description... something I learnt at mty 29th hour).
I played the game for 15 hours on normal, realized that I was very ignorant about the game's mechanics, deleted my character, started a veteran character and adorned it with better perks this time... continuing with it.... glad that I started the game again..

Mankind Divided is the long-anticipated sequel to Deus Ex: Human Revolution, it’s received a lot of flak for its performance issues, inclusion of microtransactions, and ending, but is it really that bad?
I’ll be placing the summary first and then expanding a bit on specifics, mostly the controversial areas of the game. Unless you want to hear more specifically on one of those topics, the summary is probably good enough.
The gameplay is Human Revolution on steroids. More of the same only better, with a few very cool new augmentations (and a few not that cool), and amazing level design that gives a huge variety of ways to accomplish an objective. The visuals are absolutely gorgeous, and the sound design and music are of the same gold standard that we’re used to from Human Revolution. The game is very demanding performance wise, though personally I feel the hardware premium is well worth it considering the immaculate visual quality and incredibly dense environments of the game. The sidequests are also of the highest quality, the main story is cool enough (not as good as DX1 or HR) but not very fleshed out, and the ending, while I disagree that it's all that abrupt, it is disappointing all the same. If the game had another fully sized hub such as london, and dealt more fully with some of the questions raised, it could have been an all-time great. Instead, it could be the first part of a great trilogy, but plot-wise it's just not quite all the way there on its own.
Just ignore the Pre-Order DLC and Microtransactions, they don't impact the main game in any way, and should be skipped - Just like breach mode, where the microtransactions work like any f2p game. It's nothing to skip the rest of the game over though, which is solid Deus Ex. Make sure you do enough research on whether or not you can run the game well enough to satisfy your needs. If having a fully fleshed out, satsifying story arc is the deciding factor on whether or not you buy, wait and see if the two upcoming story DLC resolve everything more fully. If you're like me and just clamoring for any more Deus Ex you can get, buy this game now.
First off, here’s how the Microtransactions and pre-order bonuses/DLC effect the main game:
They don’t. This isn’t Payday 2. This isn’t Evolve.  The *only way they impact the experience is if you’re philosophically opposed to their existence at all. Even then, I don’t believe this should be the microtransactional hill to die on.
Desperate measures is the Pre-Order bonus mission and until the two story DLC from the season pass are out, the only DLC portion worth paying attention to. It was enjoyable, and much longer than the 15 minutes I'd previously heard described (more like 45+ minutes if you have any sense of exploration at all). It should have just been included in the main game, so that's my DLC Gripe.
Specs: GPU: MSI GTX 970, RAM: 8 GB, CPU: i5 4690k, Storage: 240 GB SSD
The game has received a lot of criticism over its performance, with many comments saying it doesn’t look nice enough to justify its demands. That’s not exactly true. It is true, however, that the minimum and recommended specs weren’t lying. With one tab of chrome open I found my memory usage peaking at around 7 GB, and my CPU usage at 85-90% I was able to run the whole game on a mixture of medium-high settings with dips down to 45 FPS at the most intense areas and 60 fps the rest of the time. You will want to run the game on an SSD, and even then the load-times will take 1-2 minutes (meaning it’d probably take 8 minutes or so on a conventional hard drive). I didn’t have any of the reported crashing issues or stutters, so I can’t speak to those, but almost everything big has been fixed in the 3 patches since release.
I believe that the reason the game is so demanding, and the load screens are so long is because for the main hub areas, it tightly packs an awful lot of detailed interiors into small physical locations. There’s just a ton of stuff going on and no loading time or pop-in when you pop into those shops with little knick-knacks and easter eggs all over the place, or those apartments with an endless amount of cereal boxes and magazines (not to mention all the NPC’s buzzing about).
The game is undoubtedly the most demanding I’ve ever tried to run on my machine, and I feel like that’s been rewarded with just about the nicest eye candy and level design I’ve ever played with.
The game is absolutely gorgeous, especially the lighting, which is on par with if not ahead of the likes of Bioshock Infinite and Alien: Isolation. The screenshots don’t do it full justice.  The audio is also fantastic, particularly the soundtrack which is pretty much more content of the same quality and style that we got in Human Revolution. I do miss the art style of Human Revolution, and while daytime Prague was interesting, I was pretty worried for a while that the game would never truly feel like Deus Ex, because you need the perpetual night time for that. (Don’t worry, it gets there)
This is the complaint that holds the most merit for me. I can get past the other issues well enough, but the main plot and particularly the ending is a little tougher to pin down. Many have called Mankind Divided “half a game”, or compared it to the first act of Human Revolution, and while I think that’s a bit harsh, it’s certainly a lot closer to the mark than the rage over the microtransactions or the complaint that “the graphics that aren’t good enough to warrant such
poor performance”.
Where Deus Ex 1 and Human Revolution each have a wonderful variety of locations, and are self-contained and satisfying, Mankind Divided spends 90% of its time in one hub. That’s not to say that the only hub is bad. In fact, it’s probably the best single hub the series has to offer – It’s certainly the most detailed and lively.
While I wasn’t shocked by the credits rolling when they did like some reviewers, after reflecting on it for a few days it is ultimately disappointing. It’s so packed with sidequests and exploration that it doesn’t seem fair to called it half a game. Maybe 75% of a game. It’s not even the sheer number of main quests, it’s that it’s all too much build-up and not enough just getting down to it. The best example I can come up with is if Fellowship of the Ring ended right after the Mines of Moria.
This is another area the game really shines, and really adds a lot of value to the game, offering a nice number of sidequests, each being of the highest quality. Where other RPG’s might have one or two really good sidequests (with the rest being fetch missions to pad play time), each and every sidequest in the game is its own story.
I haven’t spent much time in Breach Mode yet, and I’ve already been shown how to pay to win via microtransactions and all that. So far the missions I’ve done have all been extremely short, but whether it’s good or bad, it really has almost nothing to do with Deus Ex and shouldn’t be counted on to be anything special at all.
I can speak only for my own experience with the game’s performance. I realize that many of you had more specific issues such as crashes or freezing, most of which I believe are fixed now. I’m not referring to these completely understandable criticisms, but to the sort of complaints that argue things like FPS the game dishes out at ultra just isn’t good enough.

The game itself worked very well and the gameplay was, for the most part, fun. Graphics are good and the larger maps, with aricraft and tanks are quite enjoyable. Armour in the game is also quite fun, and there is ample oppertunity for you to get the weapons necessary to defeat armour. However, with even a slight dip in internet speed, the game becomes difficult to play, with enemies not loading or your gunfire not causing enemy damage. Some of the guns in game are unbalanced, I`ve come across people using weapons that are nearly one hit kills and while realistic (which a good thing) in gameplay terms it can be very annoying. I feel there may also be balancing issues, not huge ones but more experienced players are put in games with less experienced ones.
On another note, where is the UK and Japan? These two nations, both key players in the Second World War, are completely rejected from the game. Being British myself, I would love to play as a Red Devil Paratrooper or drive a Churchill Heavy Tank. Japan would be really interesting to play, with their army being styled and operating differently to the other nations already in the game. The French would also be a great addition, with their tanks being some of the best on the planet at the time. With the addition of the UK, other Commonwealth nations could be added as well such as Canada and Australia, each with different skins and weapons.
To conclude, the game can be enjoyable if  your internet connection is good. The maps are great as is the gameplay, most of the time. The problems with the game would be easy to fix, given time. Adding Britain, the Commonwealth, Japan and France would make the game better, opening it up to more people.

Solid core concept, and with the recently launched DLC, it's more of the same thing, but in a very good way! The basic premise of Infested Planet is that you have just a small group of elite soldiers to battle through an endless swarm of aliens to destroy their hives and gain victory.
The DLC (Trickster's Arsenal) gives you additional battlefield maneuverability (teleport your troops anywhere, call down temporary solider backups, etc) which gives a greater number of tactical options to utilise your ammo resource. At the same time, the aliens also get some new toys such as the hive runner which attempts to re-establish the hive elsewhere after you've destroyed a hive.
The gameplay can feel slow if you are playing in the easier levels. To truly enjoy the intensity and the game's value, you need to bring on the pain and go Ironman Mode and play at the highest difficulties.
The weekly skirmishes offer randomised maps and a scoreboard to see how well you are doing against other players, which provides great replayability value.
I purchased Infested Planet a while back, but immediately purchased the DLC when it came out. I sincerely recommend this to anyone who enjoys tactical decision-making at your own pace.
My only (minor) grimace is the lack of map objectives apart from destroying the hives. In the campaign, one map that stood out for me was the one where you had to bring back canisters to your base while trying to fend of the infested assassins. Adding randomised additional map objectives such as these would significantly amp up the intensity, replayability and thoughtfulness required on the player's part, which I'm sure hardcore Infested Planet players such as myself would immensely enjoy.
9/10 - a solid piece of work!

Woodle Tree 2 is a charming game with open-world aspirations following lead from games such as Mario 64. It's quite accomplished in it's world and character design but does fall a little short on game mechanics, having a basic charged attack that's very tricky to aim and a jump that sometimes struggles to avoid the overly critical hit detection of the side of ledges and walls. Despite it's niggles though, Woodle Tree 2 has allot of character and is often fun beyond it's promise. The price point allows you to try without buyers remorse and it appeals to all ages, so get it for the kids and try it yourself. Also, the world is quite large and has some variations in biomes allowing a slightly different play feel each time. Just don't expect allot of polish in the movement and combat mechanics at this stage of the game.
Pros:
* Cute Characters and world design
* Big world to explore
* Fun level design and puzzle elements
* Price
Cons:

Infested Planet is essentially a tactical RTS, but without the messy resources and busy manufacturing queues. As commander of space marines, you are tasked to wipe out whatever baddies you come across, and these guys adapt to your tactics, and will throw you quite a few surprises. Think of it more as a puzzle, than a straight combat game, and you should have fun.
The graphics are fairly minimal overhead view without fancy-shmancy 3D options. No rotation, just scrolling. The idea is simple: start with one "base" area, and you need to beat back the alien horde with your marines and maybe some sentry turrets, but you need RPs (resource points) to build them, and you can also use RPs to buy enhancements for your teams, such as medical pods (healing), grenades, shotgun upgrades, minefields, officers, and so on. Some are semi-permanent, others are single-use buffs only.  RPs can only be earned by killing alien hives.
So basically the trick is build the right stuff at the right time. if your marines got killed, replacements are sent down to the nearest conquered "point". Your marines also have some heavy weapons (think RPGs) that can be used to kill individual units. If you find some "metal" you can have it dragged back to the control points where it is added to your RPs. You can also find ammo crate which gives you back your "ammo" (for heavy weapons) immediately rather than wait for it to SLOWLY regenerate.
As you beat up aliens, you unlock more toys to play with, such as extra med pods, shotgun, minigun,  extra marines, officers, etc. But obviously, the alien horde gets better too. First it's just swarm, then alien hives gets "gunners", then they can generate their own "marines", mines, mini-spawn nodes, hive artillery, speed rush... and more. You can play either story missions or "raid" missions. Story missions advances the plot, while raid missions just earns you money that lets you unlock even more toys.
So the key is build just enough to help you take out one hive at a time and build defenses to hold the points, but there's a lot of different ways to do it... Do you blitz the hive and accept casualties, or do the turret leapfrog, i.e. build turrets to cover each other and advance slowly but surely?
I've went through a dozen missions by now and there's two dozen more to go, and there are weekly challenges, and there's some updates coming soon. You can repeat the "raid" missions to earn more money for the goodies.
All in all the game is a lot of alien blasting fun as you groan at loss of each marine and cheer when you take out each hive. The game may not be flashy, but it is a lot of fun. Highly recommended.

Deus Ex Mankind Divided could easily be a 10, but apparently the game was rushed in some aspects, the story in particular. When reviewers criticized the story, I was very sceptical already, but when I played the game I was pleasantly surprised. The story keeps you motivated and carries you through the game, but the problem is that it looses all its momentum towards the end, with an extremely abrupt and unsatisfying ending. I bet all my money that they couldn't do the ending they wanted to do because of time or money constraints.
This problem with the story takes away a lot actually from the experience, especially for hardcore Deus Ex fans like me. The game teases you with connections to the very first Deus Ex, just like Human Revolution did, but it doesn't do anything with those. It's just a friendly reminder that they haven't forgotten the first game. But after Human Revolution I really was hoping for them to connect the story of Adam Jensen to the first Deus Ex with J.C. Denton, but apparently we have to wait for another game for that to happen, and after this ending I am very sure that that will happen :)
Also great were the side missions. They offered a lot of variety, all of them were different to each other, and in true Deus Ex fashion you have tons of options for solving each mission. For this Deus Ex they wanted to balance the different playstyles better. In Human Revolution playing non-lethal stealth was the playstyle which got rewarded the most. That isn't the case anymore. The problem I have though is that combat feels very bad. If you go for a lethal or combat heavy approach you might be dissapointed. It's not bad if you go for a "hit & run" like strategy, where you pop out of cover, headshot 1 or 2 enemies, then change our location and attack from a different angle.
But when you play this game like a first person shooter, it won't be satisfying to play at all, at least it didn't for me and I quickly changed to a stealthy playstyle (which I wanted to do anyway, just tried combat). The main problem for me are the weapons, they look amazing, but they have terrible sound design and feel awful. They have no kick to them, no weight, no recoil. Weapon customization also isn't as deep as it could be at all. There are three ammo types for almost every weapon, normal for normal enemies, armor piercing for armoed enemies, and emp to take down electronics for a few seconds, and all of these ammo types make sense.
Then you have a few attachments, like laser sights and red dot sights, but that's it. There is nothing more. You can upgrade the stats of some weapons, but that is also not very rewarding, headshots are enough most of the time anyway (which is a good thing). Thankfully tho they took out some of the unneccessary stuff. Especially regarding the augmentation system, which was heavily improved, but still isn't perfect. All of the new augmentations are really fun to use and USEFUL, but the problem still is that some augmentations are more or less useless, some are clearly better than others, some (like cloak) are overpowered. They wanted to counter this problem by having a new "overload" system. When you choose a powerful augmentation, you have to sacrifices another one to use it, and that is a great system actually, but there is a side mission which allows you to use everything without penalty and that breaks it again, for no reason actually.
But I haven't talked about the awesome things yet, the reason this game has such a high score anyway: The level design, the AI, the HUB world of Prague, the side missions. Unlike in Human Revolution the levels feel much more realistic, even though they offer so many options to the player. That is great level design. Oh I also haven't talked at all about the amazing art style, but that was a given anyway since Human Revolution was also fantastic in that regard. I am a little dissapointed by the soundtrack though, it's not bad, but by far not as good as Human Revolution or the amazing soundtrack of the first game.
Actually if you aren't a hardcore Deus Ex fan, you might like this game even more than me, or you might dislike it because you are not prepared for some of the "weirdness" of these games with illuminati etc., but the game very cleverly portraits the current situation of the real world actually, and I'm suprised no one mentioned it before, but maybe that's because it's so obvious to everyone? Woodle Tree is back in Woodle Tree 2: Worlds. This time, Woodle Tree's home has been invaded by an evil force and you have to fight them and beat them into submission in any brutal fashion (using your handy leaf) and send them back where they came from!
This game is a cute 3D platformer/adventure game, with a number of collectible items and berries. I enjoy the open world, though the long loading times annoy me a bit. Thankfully, they don't come up very often. I'm running a very high-end PC, so I'm a little surprised at the load times, but it's not a big deal.
I am very thankful for the tutorial path ahead of your home, not too far from your starting point. It gives visual depictions showing you what certain things do and how to perform actions and special moves. Unfortunately, since they are images, if you reassign your keys or mouse buttons, the ones in the image will not be the one triggering the action. This can't be avoided.
It's a lot of fun to run around, whack bad guys (or even guys just chillin' minding their own business), and collect berries to get weapon upgrades, defense upgrades, and other perks. Woodle Tree 2 has a pretty decent drawing distance, but I wish it could draw as much as your computer can handle. I'd be able to render and see the entire Woodle universe. :)
There are a couple of bugs. A minor one is that occasionally certain NPCs can walk through solid surfaces (like walking into the side of a raised patch of dirt) and occasionally you can walk through what looks like a wall. This could be intentional, but I'm not sure. The other bug (and this one is more serious) is that if you respawn after dying, and you attack an enemy that you already killed and respawned when you did, your attacks go right through it and don't harm it. I'm sure this is easily fixed and will be fixed before long.
Good things to look forward to are unlimited lives (you respawn at the last checkpoint you triggered, clearly marked as a stump on the ground with a swirl inside it), unlimited ammo, more than a dozen upgrades and unlocks, a number of different enemies, a HUGE open world to explore, and collectibles that unlock furnishings and decorations for your house. I have no idea if the decorations are purely cosmetic or if they serve a purpose/function, but they don't seem to do anything. It's neat seeing them in your house, though.
PROS:
-------
+ Unlimited lives (uses a checkpoint system)
+ Massive amount of places and space to explore
+ Several upgrades and unlockable perks
+ Many collectibles
+ Interesting and helpful tutorial area near your starting point
+ Cute and very nice graphics without requiring a workhorse PC
+ The areas I've explored so far are distinct from one another and easy to distinguish
+ Excellent price for the amount of fun you can have with it
CONS:
-------
- Still a couple of bugs to work out, but no big deal considering it's Early Access
- Hitboxes seem slightly off (but mostly in your favor)
- Can be a bit tricky to control your Woodle Tree and the camera until you get used to it
Overall:
If you like cute platformers like Super Mario 64 but want a lighter, simpler version, this can be the ticket. What are you going to do with $4 instead of buying this game? You can buy half of a beer at a sporting event, one combo meal at McDonald's (or not even a full one), or a small coffee at Starbuck's. This game will give you hours and hours of fun and it's about the price of 2 gallons of gasoline in the USA.
This game will take you farther than 2 gallons of gasoline.

This game is very reminiscent of the old sidescroller shooter flash games like the Raze series, the likes of which i still remember dearly spending almost a hundred hours on, and i wouldn't be surprised if the developers took those games as heavy inspiration. Holodrive takes the same basic concept from those games and introduces new mechanics, especially new options for fluid movement which i really appreciate for gameplay's sake beacuse i can't help but think about the new aspects it brings to games like Team Fortress 2 and the likes.
The game also has customization which is always a plus for me specially when it doesn't impair gameplay and implemented correctly. The art direction is simplistic and makes room for a lot of customization options for each body part so every player can look unique if they so chooses and still keep the art syle consistent.
Weapons are varied (although the starting gun and the plasma gun feels too similar) and feel good to use and the ones that seem OP at first can be easily countered by other weapons. The roster consists of classic flavors, from the Rocket Launcher to the Rail-gun-esque sniper rifle. Everyone has a stock of 7 weapon slots to choose from mid game and additional alternatives to each slot can be unlocked through unboxing loot boxes you get every level-up. Additionally, an alternative weapon for a single slot will be available for free for a period of time, kinda like the weekly roster in LoL, so you'll never have a lack of toys to play with.
However, the issues with a game as new as this is the lack of players, and consequentially, the lack of servers in regions other than Europe and the Americas. Hopefully with enough marketing and exposure, this game can come into the mainstream and attract new players.
All in all, this game is one of the best fun i've had from a free game in a long time, i can't recommend it enough that you give it a try, especially with a friend or two, and have some straightforward pvp fun. It is free after all!

- Pretty easy to set up and play with friends.
- Unlike many games, you don't need to worry when you mess up a character's skill points. You can respec them in between games, which refunds ALL skill points for no cost. Put the points wherever you want, and think about it later! XD
- Pretty good graphics. Nothing revolutionary, but still pretty good.
Cons:
- Animation glitches sometimes.
- Controls seem a little jumpy at times, although they are usually fine.
- Aiming your ranged attack has no crosshairs or anything. Some home in though, so not a huge issue.
- VERY COMPUTATIONALLY INTENSIVE. The lowest setting, "Potato" only barely works on my computer despite it being a 3.5 GHZ 10 core processor. While the graphics are good, they are not nearly good enough to warrant that kind of power draw. I can't imagine why on earth it would be so bad. Fallout 4 runs better on my computer.
Lastly, the reason for many of the bad reviews is because if you do singleplayer, many of the enemies can stun lock you in corners making it so you cannot do anything until you die. This, however, is because the game is meant to be multiplayer. Usually, there would be other people who would be helping beat up said enemies, so they would not be able to do that. You can safely ignore any review that says such, as it means they probably don't understand how the game was meant to be played.

I'd give this game a 7/10.
Pros:
Responsive Action combat - The combat feels fluid with some nice basic combos, you can get out of tough situations with a well timed dodge and it rewards teamplay well with team attacks.
Decent character models - The character models are exactly the same as the ones in the show so they have hours of design poured into them, the animations for the game fit with the animation style of the show and are pleasant to look at.
Good voice acting - Similarly to the character models the voice acting is the same as the show and this bring little bits of life to the game.
Variable skills trees - the skills trees although basic provide a variation of ways to play each character.
Horde mode - Horde mode is great. It's a weird mash up of action combat, turret defence and zombies that is significantly better than the campaign. It provides a refreshing style of gameplay I don't think I've experienced anywhere else, however it could certainly be expanded upon.
The rank system - This is both a pro and a con it, it adds a long term goal the game sorely needed, it resets your characters allowing you to progress again after reaching various requirements that get increasingly more challenging, like killing x amount of x or gettings x amount of revives.

Good music and sound effects - The game sound is satisfying with each hit, and the background music is pretty decent.
Cons
The campaign - The campaign is okay to play through once or twice, some levels are good for farming exp, but for the most part the pacing feels slow and the objectives fairly repetitive and boring. This could change in future updates if they decide to release harder campaigns with more bosses as more grimm are revealed in the show.
The rank system - This is both a pro and a con, unfortunately: ranking up resets everything, this includes the campaign (meaning you have to start over from the first mission if you want to play solo) as well as all your progress towards any of you challenges which discourages you from going for any of the challenges because you'll loose them again pretty soon, counter mastery for example requires 300 counters which aren't used too often and the game will punish you later for going for it. Finally there's no significant reward for ranking up at all at the moment other than a different badge next to your name.
Revives - One of the upgrades you can get increases the speed at which you revive people, after ranking up you'll loose the challenge requirement (of 5 revives) in order to get this quite significant speed increase. It is fairly difficult to revive people without it and if someone revives someone with the quick revive whilst you do the slow revive, they'll beat you and you wont get credit, this can make obtaining the challenge requirement quite difficult, especially seeing as it's an almost mandatory skill for multiplayer. They could fix this by rewarding players doing the slow revive if someone beats them too it anyway or just changing everyone to the fast speed and not having a skill for it, though I don't mind their being a skill to speed it up as it gives players who play risky an extra skill point.
Skill trees - Although being well thought out for the skills they do have they feel small and unfilled out. I personally would like a second skill tree full of weaker passive effects that uses rank as a method of obtaining skill points, this would encourage more people to go further as well.
Max number of players is 4 per game - This game could really benefit, especially in horde mode, of having 12 player options, this would create a team of players at each security node and would create a lot more options in how they could build each encounter and it would feel much more like a multiplayer game rather than one person split at each node, occasionally running to someone else and building a turret at their node to help out.
Grimm - There's not really a lot of Grimm/monster models, not many have been released in the show so it's not really surprising but it leaves things fairly limitted.
In my honest opinion this is a very satisfying action game to play, horde mode is great and has made this game recommendable, the story has been expanded and the introduction of new characters makes me feel like this game is now what I would consider a full game although admittedly you have to buy the new characters. The content is certainly still lacking in places, but what it does right it does right, it has the basics down and leaves me looking forward to where they could go in the future should they continue to update the game.
For fans of the series it's in my opinion worth a try as it's one of the better games adapted from animation that I've come across.

This is a game that heavily wears it's Smash Bros inspiration on it's shoulder. Make no mistake though; it's a solid enough game to stand out from being just another Smash rip-off.
While the game is in early access at the time of writing this, the gameplay already feels quite tight. Controls are tight, the 2D graphic style is crisp, and the fighting animations are oftentimes gorgeous.
The developers seem to have chosen a very elegant means of character development. Here's how it works:
- There's a handful of weapon types (currently eight) which each have their own unique moveset.
- Every character in the game is assigned two of these weapons they can swap between in battle, with no two characters sharing the same exact weapon combination.
- One character with a spear will use the same basic spear moveset as every other character who uses it.
- Signature attacks (special/smash attacks) are character-unique moves which give each fighter their own utility and feel.
Is a moveset too strong? Nerf the weapon associated with it. Is a character too weak? Buff their signature moves. Blue Mammoth Games did a great job laying the foundation for a much larger, but still manageable, roster in the future.
Reiterating the fact that Brawlhalla is in early access, it does have odd areas that feel incomplete. Occasional menu bugs, rare display issues, that sort of thing. Thankfully I've not hit anything that effects gameplay itself.
There's nothing negative I can think to say about this game which can't be fixed with a bit of polish and time. If you like Smash Bro games, my advice is to try to cast aside whatever thoughts you may have about this being a SSB clone and give it a fair chance. You may find yourself surprisingly impressed!

It's basically Smash delivered on PC with a slight hint of MOBA(in the way it deals with with characters and free character rotation, in-game currencies and cosmetics). There is no pay-to-win in this game as every gameplay-affecting aspect(that is to say, new characters) are unlocked with a currency that is earned by playing, and not paying. You can spend money on pure cosmetics, and already there is a lot of customization in this area of the game.
It controls well, plays well altogether and feels like a proper Smash game to the extent one might imagine a 2-D, PC-Indie-Cartoony sort of style would work as a Smash clone. The netcoding is a bit iffy, however, with an ugly tendence to lag you all the way to the bottom of the map and into certain death on a rare occasion, though I'd say 95% of the time it runs smooth as silk, with hits connecting and detecting to a satisfying degree, and perhaps even on the same level of quality and feel as an actual Smash game.
The character designs are interesting, and the customization both with and without purchaseble content is worth a mention. The way weapons work make it easier for new players to figure out what characters suit them best, and the subtle differences in seemingly similar movesets make for interesting battles.
If you want Smash on PC, in the form of an original IP, with reliable online and local multiplayer and some original ideas to the formula, this game is worth a shot.

It's basically Smash delivered on PC with a slight hint of MOBA(in the way it deals with with characters and free character rotation, in-game currencies and cosmetics). There is no pay-to-win in this game as every gameplay-affecting aspect(that is to say, new characters) are unlocked with a currency that is earned by playing, and not paying. You can spend money on pure cosmetics, and already there is a lot of customization in this area of the game.
It controls well, plays well altogether and feels like a proper Smash game to the extent one might imagine a 2-D, PC-Indie-Cartoony sort of style would work as a Smash clone. The netcoding is a bit iffy, however, with an ugly tendence to lag you all the way to the bottom of the map and into certain death on a rare occasion, though I'd say 95% of the time it runs smooth as silk, with hits connecting and detecting to a satisfying degree, and perhaps even on the same level of quality and feel as an actual Smash game.
The character designs are interesting, and the customization both with and without purchaseble content is worth a mention. The way weapons work make it easier for new players to figure out what characters suit them best, and the subtle differences in seemingly similar movesets make for interesting battles.
If you want Smash on PC, in the form of an original IP, with reliable online and local multiplayer and some original ideas to the formula, this game is worth a shot.

Transmission is a free to play "expansion" set in the Half-Life universe. Based on the Half-Life 2 Source engine, this expansion is An FPS same as HL2 made of a bunch of levels built with really good details and mostly characterized by a very dark atmosphere. Levels are mostly structured to avoid fights and solving puzzles or riddles by properly exploiting darkness, ambience, physics and props you might find in place. Only the last chapter is more action oriented but still there are some clever alternatives that might spare you some energies.
There are some nice Music tracks which are mostly heard during some action or fights to give more mood to the situaton.
Despite the well built levels and the puzzles this mod has some issues, mostly achievement related, and few minor bugs. I didn't notice anything serious anyways and the only issues I've noticed are achievement-related. On a bad note there's the lenght of this mod. It's pretty short, and besides that it lacks some story, some living character. There are notes that give some background, ok, but it doesn't compare to Portal Stories: Mel, just to make an even example, as it lasts twice and there are some dialogues.
This doesn't mean this expansion is bad, it means it's just a simple but well planned expansion. I appreciate the fact that this mod has been structured with riddles and clever solutions alternative to direct fights without exaggerating... Because this isn't portal. Well done.

is a shining testament to the fact that old-school, singleplayer linear fps gameplay is far from outdated or boring.
is awash in a tense and brooding atmosphere that keep the player on edge. Will the game jump at you in typical horror fashion? Will it throw enemies at you in a shooting gallery? Suspense keeps the player travelling around every bend of the sewer and through each abandoned warehouse. Long-time Half Life 2 fans will feel right at home as most weapons and enemies are of the familiar Half-Life 2 fare, besides a new physics manipulation device that replaces Gordon Freeman's iconic Gravity Gun.
you occasionally hear chatter from above you while crawling through tunnels, or gunfire from faraway blocks. The game surrounds the player with a sonic backdrop that is highly convincing, truly immersing you in the game's environments. At a few pivotal encounters in the game, music seamlessly blends in to set the pace without breaking the game's flow, and it is nothing short of stellar.
the only signs of life you encounter are the carcasses of Resistance fighters, hidden caches and cryptic graffiti that take the form of QR codes. This slow drip of exposition through atmospheric story-telling, letting the player piece together a story from clues in the environment instead of being blasted instructions by obnoxious NPCs or quest journals makes every tentative step you take into the unkown in the game very meaningful. The environments are desolate, with shades of pale metallic blue that pervading the relentless loneliness of the levels you traverse.
If compared with Valve's own Half-Life levels, this mod would feel at home standing shoulder-to-shoulder alongside the best levels that Valve has ever made.

text: Woodle Tree 2: Worlds is a definite improvement from the first game, while keeping aspects of the first to still resemble the original. This game has a fantastic art style, gameplay mechanics, and soundtrack. It's early access title does mean the game is not complete, and could cause issues, however, thus far I have yet to encounter anything that has made it unpleasant to play. This game has a beautiful art style, and its fun and cute for everyone. Definite improvement from Woodle Tree Adventures. ( Not that the first game was bad, believe me it was great! )

"Woodle Tree Adventure" got a high fame as a decent violentless and cute Mario64 clone. Also it  gained a wide reach due to many rounds of free giveaways of 10k copies. Now comes out the highly anticipated sequel "Woodle Tree 2: Worlds" whose map is quite huge in comparsion to the predecessor. It just has to be reasonable as a concept of a new open world game. You decide the order the levels you play. The game got even an epic story: like a dark evil force is threatening the world. 7 giant locked trees (levels to find the 3 drops) have to be released + the famous big tree from the first part is also there.
Atm the game is in EA. That means the devs want to listen to community giving them some inspirations to add more content lateron. A first change to part1 is that you equip the special accessories (leaves / hats / masks / shields) in shops spreaded all over in your valley when you reach a certain number of collected berries (you don't loose berries) instead of earning them at your own house.
In general the game engine is quite stable but sometimes the graphics lags even on lower settings. Because of the huge worldmap it needs in certain level sections area buffer loads. Then the screen blurs & freezes and a woodleface appears upto 1 min. A great feature (which I haven't tested yet) is the 4 player local coop. You can select from 4 different characters and play them over controllers. Ofc new meachnics like double jumps or leaf parachuting are amazing for the gameplay.
There's so much to discover. This game is filled up with tons of easter eggs, a hidden QR code, many collectibles, new enemies and friends, speed boosters, elevators, checkpoints and hidden entrances. Just explore! Enjoy in each world a different lovely soundtrack.
Basically you search the map to enter berry colllecting levels. In order you have to find & open the gates with the spiral sign. But you can also restart the game and all berries will respawn at their original locations again. Berry collecting seems to be atm a big aim: the last achievement 4/4 is to collect 10k berries ...

Woodle Tree 2 actually shows a lot of promise and greatly improves off of the first one. Its bright and colourful visuals are the main selling point. Its platforming has greatly improved and the camera works a lot better. The game encourages exploration by rewarding players with additional berries and random collectables such as statues.

The combat however, is not so fun. Its clunky, slow and awkward. There is a pretty simple moveset with only button assigned to combat. Tapping B does a basic swipe attack that you need to be Insanely close to an enemy to do any damage, which usually results in your character getting hurt in the process. Holding B sends out a water droplet projectile that moves way too slow to be of any use.
You are giving very little direction on where to go at times which often results in getting lost and having to back track.
However, despite these issues, I still think It is a good game but could still use a tiny bit of work.

While often seen as a wannabe Smash clone, Brawlhalla seeks to standout and be it's own, competitive-level game.
Pros:
- Simple to play (low input-execution requirement).
- Despite the simple mechanics, Competetive Mastery is still very apparent.
- Thus, the game is open both Casual and Competitive audiences.
- Balanced Characters.
- Accessible development team.
- All frame data is easily accessible to everyone via Training Mode.
- Charming, cartoony characters with good scenery and music to go along with the mood.
- Very low system requirements.
- Lag only affects the lagger, not everyone else.
- All fights are saved as small-sized (1~3 KB) replays
- Spectator Mode.
- You may choose/switch servers (US, EU etc) at any time.
- Solid match making system in both 1v1 and 2v2 Ranked Modes.
- Free to play with a cosmetic Cash Shop (i.e. spending money on the game does not give you an advantage - this game is not PayToWin)
Cons:
- The game is still in Early Access Beta, so you might run into a few bugs.
- The game is still in Early Access Beta, so there isn't much use for your Gold (in-game money) as of yet.
- Spamming heavy/signiture attacks is a valid playstyle at mid to low levels of play. (Spammers are destroyed in higher level play)
- The game is painful to play if your connection isn't perfect.
- There is a small bug you will have to get used to, even on perfect connections: attacks may seem to make contact within a 1 frame window, but actually don't in reality. This happens when you land an attack that BARELY hits the target but the target moved out of the way or dodged within that 1 frame instant. It gives you cues that the attack landed when it actually didn't and might throw your game off if you aren't prepared. Its the tiny imperfection of playing online that just can't seem to be gotten rid of.
Description:
Brawlhalla is a simple to play, online battle arena game with it's foundational gameplay being that of Super Smash Brothers: damage the opponent to send them futher and knock them out of the stage. With it's input-execution skill requirement being so low (simple to play) it focuses mainly on fundamentals, reaction speed and timing to express a individual player's level of skill, as opposed to difficult input combinations and advanced techniques (comparatively to Marvel vs Capcom, Street Fighter and Super Smash Brothers).
Characters are not 100% unique (which can be seen as a pro and a con). Each character, known as Legends, have access to two weapons which they can find spawning on the stage. Each weapon has roughly 8 shared attacks between every Legend that uses that weapon, and 3 Signiture attacks unique to that specific character, which highlights their playstyle. The weapon combination, unique signiture attacks and unique stats (Attack, Defense, Mobility and Attack Speed) are what separate one legend from all the rest. It also allows for easy character switching due to the shared weapon attacks. Every character has the same attacks while unarmed.
Characters are meticulously balanced for competitive play every patch and the developers are open to feedback. All frame, damage, hitbox and hurtbox data is easily accessible to all players within the game's training mode - no information is hidden.
It is a fun game, available to both Casual and Competitive audiences alike, able to support chaotic 8 player battles, intense 1v1 duels, cooperative 2v2 skirmishes, along with a few for-fun modes outside of Timed and Stock.
I highly reccommend Brawlhalla. It has great potential to see the competitive spotlight of the gaming community.

Everyone and their grandmother would compare this game to Super Smash Bros, (which I will refer to as "Smash") and I will not reject that statement. It is similar in that you basically hit your enemies until they fall off the stage. If you have played Smash then you know how this game works for the most part. If you haven't played Smash, then go play it.
There are actually 3 reviews in this review. If you HAVE NOT played Smash then read the review below. If you HAVE played Smash but only CASUALLY then read the review below the second dotted line. If you have played Smash COMPETITIVELY then read below the third dotted line at the bottom.
--------------------------------------------------------
Have not played Smash:
In this fighting game, your objective is to knock you opponents off the stage as apposed to a traditional health bar. To do this, you must weaken your enemies with weaker attacks which, if done right, flow together as combos pretty well. Weakening enemies makes them recieve more knockback from your attacks. When they are weak enough, hit them with a strong attack and launch them off the stage. To aid you along the way, there are weapon pickups and a few items. Each character has a different combination of two weapons that they can use. Holding a weapon drastically changes your character's moves. There are also a few other items. There is a bomb which simply explodes in the face of anyone you hit after throwing it, a mine which does the same but sticks to a surface instead of bouncing, and a... horn thing... which summons a... fire thing... that charges across the stage, hitting enemies. It's pretty fast-paced and is a good change from your traditional button-mash fighting game.
tl;dr
This is a fast paced game where you have to rack up damage on your enemies and launch them off the stage. If you like fast-paced fighting games then you will probably like this, though the style is different than most traditional fighting games.
--------------------------------------------------------
Have played Smash casually:
There are a few things that set this apart from Smash.
This game has significantly less items than Smash does. There are only 3 items in the game and weapon pickups. The biggest difference between this and Smash is that each character has a different combination of two weapons that they can use. Holding a weapon drastically changes your character's moves and is essential to winning any game unless you just want to Bruce Lee your way to victory which is a tad difficult. There is less "stuff" happening on the stages compared to Smash, which many would consider a good thing (Basically, you won't die because the stage shot a laser through the middle). The controls (not the specific buttons/keys used) are similar to Smash so it should be easy to pick up if you've played Smash before. It is also worth noting that you can throw your weapon which will free your hands for another pickup (and might also hit an enemy if you aim it right).
tl;dr
This is a very good alternative to Smash; if you like Smash, you will probably like this,
--------------------------------------------------------
Have played Smash competitively:
This game is similar to smash however, even if you want extra items off, there are essential pickups in this game which are weapon pickups. Each character has a different combination of two weapons that they can use. Holding a weapon drastically changes your character's moves. These are essential to winning, but will not just win you the game like some Smash items will. They simply give you your kit, so to speak. To be fair though, the items in this game are not that obnoxious and are actually fun to use. Two of them are throwable explosives which can easily be avoided and one is a horn that summons a... fire thing to run in a straight line across the screen, again easily dodged. Anything you pick up is throwable which can hit and enemy and will also free up your hands for a different pickup. There is one "Final Destination/Omega" stage in this game as of this review. You can also set it to stock as apposed to timed matches. This game does have spot dodging and rolling as well as air dodging, but it does lack the shield that Smash has. Each character has 3 jumps instead of two and all of them can wall jump which will reset your jumps, as will getting hit by anything. Something worth noting in this game, is that each character has a set of weak moves (jabs, tilts) as well as a set of special moves which are essentially your smash attacks. When in the air, your move set changes to having aerial moves and two directional specials (up and down) with the up-air special being your recovery move.
tl;dr
You can actually pick up this game very well if you play Smash competitively and I'd recommend it too.

This game is fun with friends and if you only play local with friends then it's a 10/10 for quick fun. However if you're seeking any real competitive element akin to Nintendo's Smash series then you will be sorely disappointed. I'm speaking from the perspective of a Platinum ranked 1v1 Ember player. This game's high end gameplay is filled with button mashing spam, if you are not throwing out a hitbox or a dodge at any given time then you are not playing correctly. Why? This is due to the fact that moves in this game have little to no startup frames or end-of-move lag. Someone spamming sword neutrals in the air and on the ground for example leaves about 5 frames of vulnerability that require you to breach the range of there swords and also touch them with the hitbox of your move lest they just spam out their neutral again and catch you.
The skill element just isn't there, good competitive fighting games are built on the premise of reading your opponents moves and then punishing them. I can call out reads on my opponent all day but this is the only fighting game where reading your opponent doesn't allow you to punish them. A heavy attack of hattori for instance will cover a huge radius with it's hitbox, leave her in the air behind said hitbox and then have nearly no end frame lag. The only way to punish this is move is to literally pre-emptively dodge through the attack, pre-emptive because their is no start-up lag on this huge heavy attack. In this scenario you are forced to dodge frame towards the opponent and simply get hit if he just stands still and does any other move instead.
There must be a counter to this obvious inbalance? Yes there is, it comes in the form of throwing your weapon. Throwing your weapon will hitstun the opponent and allow you to re-equip and attack the opponent within the same frame. Due to the fact that there is no priority, deflection or parry systems in this game it ends up devolving into who can throw their weapon the most. An excellent read followed up by a perfectively timed smash is all made pointless when the enemy throws their weapon at you at the last second with no punishment available for such an audacious and should-be-punishable move. I could go on forever about the games combat flaws but honestly for a free to play game it is good fun but very shallow. I don't recommend taking this game seriously as a competitive fighter as you will disappointed with the shallow button mashing, weapon throwing facade it turns into at high levels of play.

This game is how you do dungeon crawlers right. The story itself is decent with nothing to brag about, Save the world from the Dark Alcehmist and so on, and bits of lore here and there. What makes the game great is the amount of variety in the game.
There are 4 classes, Ember mage, Beserker,Engineer and Outlander in the game, Each with 3 distinct skill trees that offer interesing ways to deal with enemies. Use the Engineers skill tree " Constuct " to build Machines that willl cut down foes with machine gun fire, or Golems to smash any oppostion. Play as an ember mage and use Fire, Ice and Lighting for destrucitve effects that you can chain and combo together. Each role has a distinct combat style with each skill tree giving that class a certain role, or multiple. You also get a pet of your choice. Pets act as companions. They will fight for you, carry items and you can even send them to the town to buy and sell items
The level design seems simple, basic and bare-bone at first. how ever looking around you can find hidden quest for secert levels, with of course hidden and rare loot. Locate fishing holes to fish and find certain types of food to feed yout pet and give them buffs. Find shrines for powerfull buffs and and chance to fight bosses for loot. Use portals to compelete challenges for gear and fame. With so much hidden content in the middle and late stages of the game, youll find out it takes much longer to beat a level if you explore enough.
Multiplayer is a great add-on. The loot system ensure no one nabs your bling-bling after a tough dungeon run and all classes support each other in some way. Let the beserker and engineer take the blunt of the attack while the ember mage nukes from a distance and the outlander focuses on the tougher enemies.
Mods have to get attention. You can play two ways. Play default and play with mods. These two act like accounts so dont worry if you think mods will intferre with you default characters. Mods give a huge amount of content. My favorites are the classes you can choose from. You can get mods that add new classes or pets, give 2X the xp or 2x the skill points, unoffical expanison packs, Diablo hud or better lighting, better loot or just a different font. With hundreds of mods you can make the game feel like how it should to you. But you can only have 10 mods active at a time.
All of this for a bargin of $20. The content of this game easily makes it a $60 game but runic games  quote" Some people just dont have $60 lying around". THIS IS HOW YOU MAKE A GAME AND SELL IT. Most triple AAA games falsey advirtise or over exaggerate and end up with a lack luster amount of content and people paying for a decent enough game but not what was promised to them. Coming from a die-hard Devil May Cry fan, I can say I was pretty stoked for this game. Playing as Vergil was one of my favorite things in DMC3. And to play him again in DMC4? Well my excitment was through the roofs. I pre-ordered the game and played it on the day of its launched.
However, the game didn't live up to my expectations, why? Well first I'll start with Vergils campaign - there is none. Granted I'm still at Mission 07, and this could be subject to change. But when you start the game, you recieve a cutscene stating that the game takes place decades before the original DMC4 would. The cutscene then goes on to Vergil being badass by slaying demons. After he kills them all a crowd comes out and passes him, with one random female looking his way after he walks by. What happens next? Absolutely nothing. There are no cutscenes, there is no plot. Hell, even the map doesn't change despite the game taking place decades before the original game.
Which proceeds to my next complaint. All the levels are customized as if they were still for Nero. There are some objects that you're meant to use Devil Bringer to obtain. Yet you can not, as Vergil is unable to reach them. For example in Mission 06. When you first enter the underground level. You'll see a Vital Star on the other end of the pathway. Which you can not reach due to an invisible wall. And while I'm on the topic of Mission 06. The first Agnus boss fight where you need to break the glass that seperates you from him. Normally you'd use Devil Bringer to chuck Gladius demons at the glass. With Vergil? You just wail on the glass until it breaks. If there's another way, please inform me.
Now I know Capcom never promised Vergil to have his own story line nor have they commented on it, but the opening cutscene is a bit of a tease. But all-in-all, would I recommend this game? Yes, that is if you love Vergil. Right now I'm enjoying stringing his combos together and feeling awesome while doing it. And after this I can't wait to go through with Lady and Trish, then finally Dante and my all around favorite character - Nero. All I can say, is don't come into the game expecting more than just new characters.

Some people say it is a bit short for them to enjoy.  I disagree because even though it only has four chapters, it is an interesting story of a person who has been seperated from a resistance group against the combine forces.  In fact, right as you get the crowbar, a scanner appears and you can destroy it if you want to.  Later on you get an interesting weapon that acts similar to a rocket launcher in the fact that it shoots a powerful projectile that explodes on contact with anything, and allows you to blast jump (kinda), but the main upside of it is: it does not hurt you at all (excluding fall damage), and technically has infinite ammo.  Downside is: it takes auxilary power, which is what you need to sprint to escape from any dangers you cannot handle, and the amount used per shot is about 20-25%, meaning you only have about 5 shots before you cannot use it.  Thankfully auxilary power regenerates somewhat quickly.  At the end of the whole thing, you have a decently large battle against some combine troops, including some of the more powerful ones which can only be killed with rocket launchers.  To aid in this battle, the rooftops and the shed have rocket ammo on(in) them, which can be picked up at any time.  I hope this review was helpful to those who are doubtful of this small but interesting game.  If you are still skeptic, or want to try it for yourself, go ahead.

The game follows a simple story: Japan nearly gets destroyed by a war, and those who fled or managed to escape are brought together by a geisha and a samurai to rebuild what was destroyed and preserve the traditions of old Japan. You must do this by earning money, of course, and you earn money by playing a Match 3 game with three different ways to play them: Swap Mode, Chain Mode, and Pop Mode. After each Mach 3 game is completed, you're rated based on how many moves you took to complete the Match 3 game, type of mode used (Relaxed or Challenger. Relaxed means you have infinite amount of moves and Challenger means you have specific amount of moves to use to complete the Match 3 games), and final score. You're then given an amount of money based on how well you did. You do this to rebuild buildings and eventually restore what was lost.
For what this game is, it is very simple. It's addicting and will keep you busy for a few hours at a time. Though they have a small selection/library of music they cycle through, it's still very calming to listen to, and feels very culturally true to Japan. The gameplay is simple but not at all complicated. Despite how many current hours I have logged in at the time of this review (which is 14 hours), I haven't completed the story yet. Though I'm sure later on I'll finish it and I might come back to give my final thoughts on just the story.
For now, here are my final results in a general stance:
- 8.5/10
- 7/10
- 7/10
- Reasonable. Would recommend purchasing at current price.

Beautiful and sometimes darkly mature echo of the fairytales that taught us about the world as children. Throughout the journey of two siblings trying to save their dying father, I experienced themes of death and acceptance that hit me on an extremely personal level, visited fascinating dreamlike locations, and interacted with the world in completely unique ways. And though Brothers’ unconventional twin-stick adventure controls often tripped me up along the way, this short storybook walkabout is as attractive as it is affecting.
Though your adventure begins in a Nordic-inspired village filled with pleasant townsfolk and simple stories, you’ll eventually make your way to ancient battlefields where the rivers flow with blood, frozen lakes that contain unknown horrors beneath the ice, and prisons perched high atop lonely castles.
