Let's start with a quick Pros and Cons list and then I'll add some depth to the review.
Pros
+ Engaging Story
+ Emergent Story
+ Unexpected Variant Endings
+ Quality ambient music throughout
+ Best ending saved 'til last (MUST complete other endings to unlock)
+ No Nudity, No Sex scenes (except passionate kissing), No language, No Dating
+ None of the other immature 'mature' content that some authors resort to in order to increase interest in their story.
Cons
- Translation to English is not always strong
- Fairly basic images
- Images don't always show the story as written
- First few endings seem arbitrary
- Long periods of reading with very few choices
- Dialogue lacks depth at times
More Detail
Starting off I was quite disappointed in this game. It calls itself a visual novel, but very little variety in the very basic visuals left me feeling that I'd wasted my money on this game (and the game is FREE).
The early story feels very contrived and very predictable, in pretty much the same way as the back story of almost any cheap RPG does. I mean, seriously, three teenage boys going to spend their Halloween night in the woods where others have disappeared on past Halloweens. You have to admit that sounds as contrived as you would ever find in any game.
After my first very abritrary seeming death, the only thing that kept me hanging in there was pure stubborn-ness. The game had good reviews, so surely the other choice had to be better.
Each alternate path adds to the storyline, while cleverly introducing questions about the real story that kept me unsure until the very end of the final (unlocked) ending.
What appeared to be a B-grade Halloween horror story turned into a well-constructed A-grade 'not horror' story (no spoilers here).
It took me three hours to read through all the possible endings. So, this game is quite playable in one evening.
If you have read this far in my review, let me suggest something to you. I think the story unfolds quite well if you experience the endings in an order. Without micro-analysing the endings to come up with a specific order that you would have to write down or come back and read, here's an easy way to do it that will still work well for the story:
When you a given a choice to make in the game, hit ESC and save your game on the decision screen. Always take the first option whenever given a choice. After you've seen the ending, LOAD the last choice made and take the other path (all choices are binary). This will get some of the poorer endings out of the way early, and the story will unfold interestingly later (remembering that you will need to see all the endings and if you don't read your way to each ending you will miss important plot points, even on the 'bad' endings).
Graphics: 3/10
Music: 7/10
Story: 9/10
Replayability: 2/10
Overall: 8/10

Provided that you avoid playing the games if/when you get odd lag spikes, Brawlhalla is a fresh take on the Smash Bros. sort of fighting game which offers technical, movement-based gameplay that's really fun, with a high skill ceiling. The choice between weapons, and the more balanced items compared to the Smash Bros. games adds a new layer of adaptability to gameplay, and, even if free-for-all may be imbalanced by the items, 1v1 gameplay is a very technical, skill-based and well-balanced affair, which is very enjoyable to delve into and master.
Of course, if there's one gripe I have, it's that mysteriously, I find myself the victim of crippling lag which doesn't occur in other games, for some reason, at seemingly arbitrary times.
Regardless, many people won't experience this lag, and Brawlhalla has a lot of competitive, technical, and most importantly FUN gameplay to offer to those who are willing to just try.
I'm a little bit sad that I lost my ranked streak to lag, but the game is fun, and it's in early access, and I'm glad to support it.

I was pretty shocked that a game I picked up for 79p and had last played about 12 years ago turned out to be one of my most enjoyable gaming experiences in recent memory.
Don't be fooled by the game's age - if you've never played Red Faction before, or, like me, had simply forgotten about it over time, it's immediately obvious that it's a surprisingly solid shooter, and a fantastic PC port to boot, given it's age. The controls are smooth and responsive, and whilst the default mapping is not entirely intuitive this can obviously be corrected quite easily. This smooth control scheme lays a solid base over which the rest of the game is very competently assembled.
Visually, Red Faction is head and shoulders above many shooters of the time, offering varied locals (from claustrophobic mines, to sterile office environments, to sprawling underwater caverns), a good dose of atmosphere, and of particular note - fantastic lighting. The lighting in this game holds up so well that I often found myself just walking around the environment observing how the lighting effects the various surfaces around me. The levels are often non-linear, which can be confusing at times, but more often than not simply makes the environment feel like a more realistic, lived-in place. You can play multiple times and find new things every time, which for a game that is essentially a corridor shooter, is pretty cool, I think.
Gameplay is quite varied with well-designed gunplay supplimented with stealth, driving, flying, and submarine sections. The stealth is passable, and if you follow the rules everything works. The flying and diving vehicles control beautifully and blowing up an enemy sub underwater results in some great underwater explosion effects which are imaginative and impressive even in hindsight. There's a raft of fun weapons to use as well, most of which have their own alternate fire, including the most fantastically OP flamethrower in video game history.
The soundtrack is a standout, with wonderfully moody electronic tracks perfectly supplimenting the action, and giving the game an irreplacable personality.
And of course I have to mention the environmental destruction. Whilst it isn't exactly a gameplay staple as much as it is a useful gimmick, it absolutely improves the experience when your battles dynamically scar the environment around you. Walking away from a gunfight with holes in the walls and scorch marks on all surfaces is a great feeling, and it's the moments when you forget about the mechanic, and then an enemy blows a hole in the wall you're hiding behind that you truly appreciate just how much this little touch does to improve the immersion. It's worth noting as well that this mechanic completely changes your multiplayer experience for the better, as you can strategically shatter your opponent's cover around them - I've never played more local VS. in my life than I did this game when I owned it on PS2.
Now it's not perfect, of course - the voice acting for the NPCs is repetitive, and the quality of some of the character is often poor, but in saying that, it's not uniformly bad, so I can personally let it go. It's also a game that occasionally leaves you wondering where to go as there is no mission objective screen as far as I can tell. However, there's a number of problems that I solved by simply blowing giant holes in the wall until I made a path around the obstacle, and I'm still not sure if I did the right thing or not. I, for one, call that the mark of a pretty cool game. Other than that though, I'd have to nit-pick to name issues that really bugged me.
Red Faction has single-handedly restored my faith in the quality of games released around the early 2000s - a time in which I feel a large number of developers' reach exceeded their grasp. Sure, it's not the most ground-breaking shooter, and it has its issues, most of which were somewhat characteristic of games at the time. But when it plays so well, and is so much fun, who cares? Given that I'd played it so much when I was younger, I expected nostalgia to be playing a large part in my judgements, but it's been so long that it was like playing it anew, and I just found myself genuinely excited by what the game offers.
I'd highly recommend this to anyone looking for a fun, well-designed shooter, with a decent amount of variety and some neat gameplay mechanics.

This is the first game that I bought and played on steam.
Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is a marvel of storytelling and clever gameplay and a must buy for players who enjoy such.
The first thing that I should say is that unlike what the notice says on the store page, this game does not require a controller to play.
Gameplay and story:
During the game you control these two characters with the arrow and wasd keys as the camera adjusts itself to the area that you are playing. The game itself is relatively simple and linear, requiring the player to overcome easy obstacles in the way of the protagonists' journey to save their ill uncle. In the course of their quest, they assist others in need and grow closer as brothers. It is slightly challenging to get ahold of controlling the brothers simultaneously at the start of the game but becomes much more fluid and easy as you progress through the levels even with a keyboard. Complement to the controls, the challenges along the way begin to require more ingenuity as you learn to control the brothers.
Graphics:
The areas themselves are beautifully designed and the game pauses every once in a while to allow you to enjoy it. From climbing crumbling ruins to scaling massive caves the game uses every area to show you just how beautiful and well crafted it is.
Sound:
There is no major dialogue so to speak but everything in the game is clear without it using too many words. What the lack of dialogue gives way to is a wonderful soundtrack that captures the emotional range of the story in ways that dialogue would never have. As the game becomes darker the longer you play, the sounds and music mature likewise.
Overall:
On the front, Brothers may look like a simple, light hearted puzzle adventure for a casual player. Playing it, I've come to appreciate the subtle and fine ways that this game was made elevating it in quality above many of the other games that I play. The story and gameplay are simple, the music complements the graphics excellently, and the entire experience is an emotional journey as two brothers enter dark and dangerous worlds to save their family.
I cannot recommend this game enough and constantly badger anyone who would listen. It is a quick (approx 6 hr) playthrough and the ending left me sobbing. I have to say, this is a different caliber of gaming. I've never experienced anything like it

The graphics are beautiful, and this is the kind of world I would spend hours exploring. So many details that only left me wanting to know everything about this world. I highly recommend this game. I think it's worth the full price, but I picked it up on sale.

This was definitely my top pick from the 2014 steam summer sale. A demonstrative example of “easy to pick up, hard to master”. I found this game particularly enthralling as an RTS fan. It manages to be innovative and approachable despite fundamentally understanding the cornerstones of a fantastic real-time strategy experience. It has both static and dynamically created maps adding to it’s replayability as well as periodic events. The developer also seems like a genuinely passionate fellow from what i have seen of his interaction with the community.

I was very impressed with this game's overall polish and design! It is aesthetically pleasing, though symplistic, but takes a slightly different approach to the normal RTS style game. While it is fairly light on story it has a solid single player campaign and a good multiplayer which is very challenging. The campaign isn't a push-over either as the later levels and even some of the challenges  within the campaign (side missions) make it difficult to proceed/profit. Even after you acquire enough money to purchase your upgrades, which they make easy enough so that you can progress without banging your head against a wall, you can play previous missions again but even with your fancy upgrades they scale with you maintaining a challenging design.
What I was probably most impressed with was how they managed to change what I was used to seeing as an RTS into a completely different kind of play style but still make it really challenging and satisfying to accomplish when you finally push through! My longest game took me nearly 40 minutes from having to sit there and hold back the alien hordes while attempting up to seven different strategies all with limited resources as you have to keep pushing forward to get more resources and thusly allowing you to keep pushing forward.  Instead of building up a base and collecting resources to create your military units this one gives you some units and your buildings are only created to aid in their mission. Beautifully designed.
I purchased the game on sale but this game is really worth the full $14.99, in my opinion. If you like strategy games I'd recommend this one!

Rating 6.5/10
Overview: First Person Shooter
The Good
+ Graphics look great especially outdoor environments.
+ I love the western frontier setting.
+ The story and characters are really well done. The story is told over the course of 15 levels switching between two characters and retelling certain events from different perspectives.
+ Good soundtrack
The Average:
Controls and animation feel stiff and cumbersome. There are times when you can jump and grab a ledge easily and other times you are not allowed to jump over a knee high barricade because the game designers don't want you going a certain way.
The game features stealth sections every once in a while to break up the gameplay. Although its nice to have a change of pace, these stealth sections are average at best. Enemies will sometimes spot you a mile away while other times you can crouch right in front of them. Worse, if you do get spotted you have to replay the entire section over again, granted they are not very long but still frustrating none the less.
Shooting mechanics are average. Guns have no weight or feel to them, have poor accuracy and often times gets pretty frustrating to get through certain sections.
The bad
- While the graphics are good, especially the outdoor environments, textures and character models are bad.
- The last main mission has respawning enemies making for a very frustrating experiences causing you to abuse quick save/load to get by certain sections
- game crashed a few times

This pack contains Narcissu 1 and 2 which are available separately on Steam (for free, if I'm not mistaken) and which I've reviewed separately. The series deals with emotional themes, such as the lives of terminally ill young people and can definitely be a powerful read. This includes an additional Epilogue for Narcissu 2 which was not available previously and is quite good.
The DLC in this collection also includes A Little Iris, which is a story set in medieval Europe and differs the most from all the other titles. This one was very interesting and I read through it in just a couple of sessions. Next up is Narcissu Zero which takes place before all the other entries and explains how everything got started with the hospice. Very moving with some twists I didn't expect. Finally, Narcissu: Sumire which I had a bit more trouble getting into. It just didn't have the same feeling as the others and I found myself a bit bored at times. There are also some author's notes and tiny side stories as well as other extras.
I would say the collection is defintely worthwhile but you may want to experience the original stories first before trying all of the DLC. Make sure you're in an OK place emotionally as some may find the constant talk of death and illness to be hard to handle.
On a final note, I found this release to be a bit unstable with the launcher often crashing when I would exit and some DLC not being compatible with the screenshot feature on Steam.

Story: You probably already know. The plot is like reading chapter 1 of a novel. I guess the 2 story DLC's will shed more light on the lingering questions.
Gameplay: This is where mankind divided truly shines. You have so many ways to achieve your objectives and so, the game offers a lot of replay value. But as far as this game is concerned, the shop is entirely optional. You earn a lot of credits and praxis points so there is no need to purchase anything. The single use consumables hardly make any difference in the long run. The best thing about the pre order offer is the bonus mission that comes with it. It offers an additional 30 mins of game play time although its not a must to enjoy the main game.

Overall: 8/10

I normally don't write reviews, I leave that to other, more literate people. However, my experience with this game is so bad I feel the need to warn people away from it.
First off, my setup includes an ultrawide (21:9) monitor, and this game has horrible optimization problems with that. To their credit, they have released a patch that fixed *some* of the problems, but not everything has been fixed. Furthermore, it would either stretch the game, or not run at all when I tried to change the resolution to 1080p (16:9). I had to resort to changing my system resolution to play it properly. Is it really that hard to release a game that doesn't have game breaking issues?
Onto the gameplay. To be fair, the gameplay is quite well done, which is what got me through the issues. Levels are intricately made, and exploration is rewarded with secret passageways and a lot of loot. Gun play, on the other hand, can still be improved. Shooting feels sluggish and changing weapons are a hassle (I played with a controller so the shortcut bar was unavailable). I found myself sneaking through the entire game to avoid that.
But my main problem, along with game breaking bugs, is the fact that the story is so poorly written and so short, I can't help but wonder why it took 5 years for this game to be released. I finished the game with 15 hours logged, and that includes all but 1 side mission, along with around 2 hours of trying to fix aforementioned bugs. 13 hours for a $60USD game!? Even DX:HR was longer than that! Characters are underdeveloped, and some were shown in the beginning, but never again until the endscene AFTER the credits rolled. The villain wasn't given a proper backstory, and I still don't know why he did what he did. Choices didn't matter, whether you sided with the police or the Augs.
The ending itself felt like it was cut short, I had more questions then I had answers after the credits rolled.
All in all, the game felt like a cash grab, which is disappointing because I loved the last game. A lot could have been done better, but they decided to release an unpolished crap to make some money. I guess that's the trend these days.

while using its assets.  It's a nice experience that does create a sense of paranoia, but is still on the relatively easy side.  Once you get the Energy Pulse Cannon, then you'll see that there's really no reason to have any of the other guns (save for the RPG launcher), which are littered all over the place. This game has 4 acts and you should finish in a little over 1 hour. The only hard parts to expect are the swarms.  If you're bad at swarms, then you might find the swarms overwhelming, yet manageable.

Brilliant. Didn't know what game I wanted to play today, so I played this. Start to finish, as soon as I had gotten past the intro part the world had me hooked, tons of wonder and a desire to learn about this crazy world. The minimalism in actually explaining what you experience through the story is in no way a detriment, if anything questioning what you see makes this hook you even deeper.
If you've ever had those moments where you find yourself wondering what the actual world in a story is about and how it works, this game has that in buckets. If you like stories that span the emotional spectrum, this is for you.
Normally I'd check the store page and make recommendations based on the price tag of a game, but this experience is worth 20$ easily to me. That's coming fresh from playing it, being aware of the negatives, like the simple control scheme and linear pathing, the easy puzzles and casual-esque game play, the overused "Eeeee-eee-Eeee-eee-eee" in the soundtrack, etc. There are negatives, plenty. None of them detract enough from the experience this game offers. It's a phenomal example of good storytelling and not a word is spoken. It's basically just an interactive movie but an extremely compelling example of video games as art.
Bottom line, if you play this for 4-5 hours and beat it, I sincerely doubt you'll want the time or your money back for what this offers.

Wasn't expecting much from this due to it being a port, but was pleasantly surprised.
- found the graphics and sound surprisingly good - the models, sound effects and environments are nicely done and definitely immerse you in the WH40K atmosphere.
- Interface is intuitive, smooth and uncluttered (though I would expect this from Rodeo given their experience with this type of game)
- Plays quite fast for a turn-based strategy game, and not as punishing or demanding as something like Mordheim, for example, so quite easy to get into. However, though simplified, I wouldn't say it's too 'dumbed-down' as core aspects such as overwatch, LOS, skills etc are all there.
- Variety of different types of marines (tacs, assaults, devastors) with different skillsets to level up.
- The different marine chapters add character to your team; as well as Ultramarines, Space Wolves and Blood Angels, the Enhanced Edition adds Black Templars, Dark Angels, Imperial Fists and Silver Skulls). Not only do these have distinct models and unique wargear, but you also get occasional banter between members of different chapters during missions.
- Lots of weapons and wargear to collect (with no microtransactions in this version thank goodness)
On the negative side, given the random loot aspect of this game I'm surprised that there isn't some sort of mission generator - yes you can replay campaign missions to farm loot and experience but inevitably this is going to feel a lot more repetive than if you could generate random missions. Also the rng aspect of the loot can be frustrating when you get a high tier weapon that cab only be used by marines of a particular chapter and class that you don't have.

Red Faction is a renowned FPS that conceived the Geomod engine, software with the ability to alter level geomotry with explosives to access secret locations. Red Faction is the organized movement of a dissident rebel faction of miners under the Ultor Corporation, whos actual intentions are to experiment on the miners and the alien inhabitants of mars known as the plague. Parker, a miner caught up in the debackle, assists the Red Faction as Ultors influence grows awry. Red Faction is a unique title that spawned a franchise from basis of shapable geography, various ways of traversing the environments by taking advantage of Geomod, and even cave pockets, while pointless, gives an even deeper layer of depth to the levels. The drawbacks of the game? Dialogue can be quirky, Parker himself has less depth than a blank sheet of paper, the enemy AI is spastic and CANNOT stop themselves from moving around, you can get yourself stuck in places, and even withold progress of the game by using Geomod in certain places, such as stairwells. To the games excellent graces, it is brilliantly paced, has an amazing soundtrack, satisfying world altering with the Geomod, and immersive environments. This is my favorite of the Red Faction series, and I'd definetly recommend this game for anyone who likes destructable environments and a challenge.

Red Faction Review (Spoiler Free)
"A year in the Ultor mines seemed like a great way to straighten myself out. Man, was I a fool".
(Story)
The year is 2075.  Earth's resources are dwindling forcing the colonization and resource mining of other planets.  The Ultor Mining Corporation has set up shop on Mars and regularly brings work and security personnel to the planet via shuttles from Earth.  Aimless protagonist Parker decides to spend a year working in the mines in an attempt to figure out what he wants to do with his life.  Upon arriving on Mars however, he sees a very different picture than the one Ultor's recruitment campaign painted on Earth.  Forced to work in terrible conditions, miners live under the authority of Ultor's private military.  Making matters worse is the mysterious "plague" spreading among the miners and Ultor's restriction of flight's back to Earth.  The flash point is reached on a seemingly routine day and Parker soon finds himself in the midst of a revolution.
(Gameplay)
Played in first person, gameplay is mostly shooting and exploration, with a few stealth levels thrown in for variety.  Red Faction is very akin to Half Life, requiring you to solve puzzles and defeat bosses/enemies in special ways without too much hand-holding.  Levels load as you play and string together much as they did in Half Life.  What made Red Faction unique was the Geo-Mod technology.  Using explosives or drills, Parker can blast his way through rock, concrete, and other materials, giving Red Faction a degree of player freedom.  Enemies driving over a rock chasm?  Destroy the bridge they are on and watch them fall.  Can't find a way to open that door?  Use C4 to make a tunnel next to it.
There are several vehicle segments in the game, where Parker may pilot drilling equipment, submarines, tanks, or fighter craft.  On foot, Parker has a vast arsenal of weapons from shotguns and assualt rifles to rocket launchers and even a flamethrower (hilarious to use).  The stealth levels require Parker to use a disguise, silenced weapons and to hide bodies.  These segments are my least favorite and can be aggravating at times.  Boss fights are occasional, though some are more memorable/innovative than others.  Ammunition can get scarce at times, even requiring you to go into a fight with a few rounds in each weapon.  Make no mistake, this can be a difficult game if you do not play it a certain way.
(Design)
Ultor's underground facilities and mines feel vast thanks to good environment design.  Mine tunnels, vast caverns, underwater bases, executive offices, military installations, and the Martian surface are all different in sight and sound.  Guns have a nice sharpness to them and exlosions create debris and balst marks.  Voice acting is good though at times the characters sound a little mono-tone.
(Final Comments)
Half Life with vehicles and destructible environments is a good metaphor for Red Faction.  Parker's story is different than Freeman's but if you enjoyed the journey through Black Mesa, you will likely enjoy traversing the mines of Mars.  Challenging yet oddly satisfying, Red Faction will slick your thirst for destructible landscapes and a decent stroy in retro fashion.

Back in 2006 Techland were still relatively unknown. Having released Chrome before hand, a shooter that got a rather mixed reaction.
They followed up with Call of Juarez. Going even further into their own direction they decided to focus on a wild west themed shooter built on their own in house engine.
What we got was a gorgeous looking shooter that palyed like a spagetti western with bits of Robert Rodriguez attitude here and there.
I bought the original retail release back in 2006 and after finishing it, I hadn't ever really returned to it. But, recently I bought the game again on STEAM and decided to give the entire series (yes even The Cartel) a proper rerun.
With the first Call of Juarez I'm still in love with the verys imple and direct style of the game. While at times still wonderfully beautiful in it's visuals, it still comes up short on character animations, which were a bit stiff even back in 2006.
And at times, the character models even look a bit rough, as if they are not up to the same level of quality as the levels themselves. The levels... vast, wide open areas. They don't offer much (or any) in the way of exploration. But, they are large enough to give you the feeling of how large the wild west was.
The story, is good. Nothing great, but nothing bad. It's solid writing, decent voice acting... but nothing I want to spoil or get into. But, the game is worth playing simply for Reverand Ray alone. His character is and will always be the best part of the first two CoJ titles.
The other main character Billy, is... okay. But, at times he's more annoying then engaging and a lot of the time I simply wanted to return to Ray.
Gameplay is were the game falters. Switching back and forth between Ray and Billy, offering up variety in gameplay and level design. Something most shooters struggle with.
With Ray, it's a more straight forward shooter experience. He's a brawler, strong and a very talented gunfighter. Billy, is weak, but fast and sneaky. And very skilled with a bow and arrow.
While the variety is nice, it's also here that problems arise. Ray's levels are wonderful. WIth his armor chestplate able to deflect shots, and his concentration mode being able to down multiple enemies quickly. Issues arise during the "dualing", never a great setup... a mouse cursor bug on mordern OS causes the game to be incredibly frustrating during these parts.
As for Billy, while the platforming works very well and the stealth is actually done very well also. Billy is very weak, and more often then not they throw you into combat situations as him. Often expecting you to try and just run from them instead of fighting.
But, as weak as he is even one lucky shot as you're trying to run (or ride away on a horse) can kill you.

From the moment you start playing the game you can tell the studio was very ambitious and put a lot of heart into this western fps title, however, either due to their inexperience, budget constraints or some drunk binges between level and gameplay designers, they also created mechanics and levels that led to a lot of frustration.
Throughout the campaign you play as either Billy or the Priest. They both play quite differently based on the mechanics and weapons they get in the levels. The Priest is where the meat of the game is. Fun, fast, frantic shoot em up action with slo mo, dual pistols, shotguns and rifles and the occasional stand off western style(which is pretty meh because its timed and thus you know exactly when the opponent is about to shoot).
As a counterpoint to that, to let the player take a breather, Billy gets the levels where he has to stealth and platform. This would be fine, except both elements are pretty flawed. Stealth is mostly fine and will provide little to no challenge as you can sneak by anyone as long as they're not looking directly at you, however platforming is really really bad. First of all, you get a whip which you can use to attach to trees. The hit detection is very poor and you'll often only be able to use it only specific branches or trunk of a tree, which sometimes turns it into a tedious guessing game. The whip is also a missed opportunity as you could have used it in clever ways in combat to reposition enemies and grab items, but ultimately its for swinging from trees. Then the very worst part of platforming is that an animation plays out every time you reach for a ledge and Billy makes a noise. Now, in the early levels thats fine, if a bit annoying. BUT. Some level designer decides to a create a whole mission around you climbing a mountain. Now imagine that you have to wait for an animation and sound to play out as you're climbing 30-40 ledges, sometimes up to 6 in a row.
The only redeemable quality about Billy is that he gets to use the bow, which is one of the best and most fun to use weapons in the game as you slow down time when you aim with it and its fun to take out enemies from a long range. Now, i mentioned that you had to a climb a mountain. That mission is part of series of bizzare quests involving a shaman thats easily the worst part of the game. You have to hunt 3 rabbits, which would be fine if they weren't REALLY REALLY SMALL, and some of the areas you're supposed to find them have grass twice as big as the rabbit. Even after the string of horrible shaman related quests, most of Billys quests after that resolve around platforming and solving puzzles all of a sudden, it takes a bizzare turn, as if the developers didn't know what to do with the character and the approach they were taking.
Besides the mentioned shaman quests which have pretty poor level design, you will also be revisiting the same levels with both characters for the majority of the game(due to budget constraints im guessing), which also makes me think that the shaman quests were implemented just to extend the playing time.
Talking more on the side the pros than cons, as I mentioned, it's really fun to play as the Priest Ray and the horse riding and horse combat in this fps is surprisingly really really good, which makes for exciting chase scenes. The game also creates an immersive atmoshphere and has a passable story. Billy isn't really likeable as a character, but Ray is definitely the highlight in the story, a flawed man on his own path to redemption, his voice acting really stands out as one of the best I've heard in a game ever, and stands tall above the passable voice acting of the other characters. It's grizzly and haunting.
Overall, it's hard to recommend the game to everyone. I can see that playing as Billy could really turn some people off this game and the levels in which you play as him become more flawed as you go along, but the Ray segments are all fun shoot em up segments, and evne Billys levels have some exciting moments. It's definitely flawed, but if you can get past that it's a short, fun campaign.

I normally don't write reviews, I leave that to other, more literate people. However, my experience with this game is so bad I feel the need to warn people away from it.
First off, my setup includes an ultrawide (21:9) monitor, and this game has horrible optimization problems with that. To their credit, they have released a patch that fixed *some* of the problems, but not everything has been fixed. Furthermore, it would either stretch the game, or not run at all when I tried to change the resolution to 1080p (16:9). I had to resort to changing my system resolution to play it properly. Is it really that hard to release a game that doesn't have game breaking issues?
Onto the gameplay. To be fair, the gameplay is quite well done, which is what got me through the issues. Levels are intricately made, and exploration is rewarded with secret passageways and a lot of loot. Gun play, on the other hand, can still be improved. Shooting feels sluggish and changing weapons are a hassle (I played with a controller so the shortcut bar was unavailable). I found myself sneaking through the entire game to avoid that.
But my main problem, along with game breaking bugs, is the fact that the story is so poorly written and so short, I can't help but wonder why it took 5 years for this game to be released. I finished the game with 15 hours logged, and that includes all but 1 side mission, along with around 2 hours of trying to fix aforementioned bugs. 13 hours for a $60USD game!? Even DX:HR was longer than that! Characters are underdeveloped, and some were shown in the beginning, but never again until the endscene AFTER the credits rolled. The villain wasn't given a proper backstory, and I still don't know why he did what he did. Choices didn't matter, whether you sided with the police or the Augs.
The ending itself felt like it was cut short, I had more questions then I had answers after the credits rolled.
All in all, the game felt like a cash grab, which is disappointing because I loved the last game. A lot could have been done better, but they decided to release an unpolished crap to make some money. I guess that's the trend these days.

I am really surprised with this game. I bought it because of the visuals + the low price (during sales) so I wasn't expecting much, but I actually had a lot of fun with it.
Visually it's an impressive game. No, not in a technical way, but in an artistic one. The enviroment/colors/lightning are really great and well blended. Sometimes I stopped playing just to take a closer look to the background, really cool. If you're someone who likes to watch the work of artists this game will certainly be a good purchase.
Audiowise it's great also. The ost blends well with the visuals and the voice acting is really well done. Most of the story is told throught narrative ("book scenes" while loading the level) so there's almost no lip syncing, but it's not really necessary.
Gameplaywise it's a solid game. No, it's not groundbreaking, but it's really good at what it advertises as. Movement is fluid, the progression system makes you curious to see more and the level design overall is well done. The only major downside is the difficulty: it's easy on single player and even easier co-op. For me that's not really a problem because I played it to relax, but people who likes "meat boy" arcade style won't like it for sure. It's way slower and more forgiving.
Lorewise it's ok. It's not deep ( by any stretch of the imagination) but it also doesn't try to be. It tries to be like "a childish fairy tale" and it manages to. Really light hearted and predictable.
So, overall, considering the ~10 hours to beat it, at least solid 8 for me (arguebly 8 - 9). Since I bought it for like 1,50 dollars it's probably the best purchase I've ever made on steam. Tottaly recommend it.

I like things simple. So here's a simple review:
Have you never played a DMC game? Watch some online reviews first. It's not the strongest in the series, but still a great deal of fun.
Have you played through it once or twice and had enough? Don't buy it. If you're not already enamoured with the game, the extra features won't cut it for you.
Are you a huge DMC fan? You don't need my opinion. You probably already bought it.
Bottom line: New players and veterans will likely be the only ones to enjoy it.
Waifus, Swordfus, and Gunfus. What's more to want? Vergil.

So of now I have played every character and beat their campaings (Do not be confused, everyone goes through the same campaing)
And I must say, I never had this plenty of fun in a game in a while. I alreadly reviewed DMC4 vanilla, so you should read that, as here we will look at how Special Edition expands upon DMC4.
No matter how we look at it DMC4 lacked in content greatly and Special Edition easily makes up for it with 3 new characters with their play styles, new costumes for each character, new cut-scenes for the new characters  (They don't add anything to the story but it's nice to see these characters again) and tweaks to the gameplay and few graphical changes.
The main selling point of this edition is the Dante's twin brother Vergil who first appeared in DMC3 and was first playable in the DMC3's Special Edition, he now returns with far greater move list than ever before, he borrows some mechanics from DMC3 and DmC and also has new moves and concentration mechanic, this makes him the defenitive version of Vergil.
He is equiped with three weapons, that being Yamato, Beowulf and Force Edge. He also can summond swords which he can use in many ways to damage the enemy or to combo them. Best way to describe Vergil's play style would probably be "risk/reward" as you have concentration mechanic, a bar which fills up when you slowly walk around in a fight and dodge attacks and sucesfully hit the enemy, it depletes when you run or get hit (when you get hit it goes down to zero) the more of this bar you have, the stronger Vergil's attack become, he is still very strong even without, but with it he is a beast. Vergil is a perfect character for everyone, for beginners and experts, even though experts who are used to his DMC3 gameplay will have to get used to few changes, such as trick down being only usable only in devil trigger amongs of other features which are only avaible in his devil trigger form. Vergil is an incredibly fast character with his main way of getting to enemies being teleporting, his teleporting is really quick and can be pretty much spammed for all enternity.
I am a big fan of Vergil's gameplay, as time goes on I may actually start maining him instead of Dante.
Lady and Trish share their campaing, with Lady going through Nero's mission and Trish's Dante's. Lady is a gun focused character she is basically an upradged gunslinger from DMC3, but with far greater strenght than ever before, she packs two pistols which can be charged to 3 levels, when charged shots are fired in the air it gives her a knockback, which can be proven most useful, she then also has a shotgun which also can be charged to 3 levels, when fully charged it is an incredibly OP weapon which pretty much blasts away anything, and then there is Kallina An, as you've expect it can be charged to 3 levels.
Lady was a surprising character who somehow works, she is really a lot of fun to play and changes the way you play the game entirely. I honestly didn't expect her to work as well as she did. Because Lady isn't a demon her "devil triger" is her throwing grenades all around herself destroying everything around her, just like Nero's DT it has a lot of invicible frames, which suits Lady perfectly as she is a character who isn't meant to get too close to enemies
Then there is Trish who has a Sparda's sword and her fists of fury and Pandora's Box. Trish's gimmick is that she doesn't weapon switch yet she can use these weapons on the fly. She is a very flashy and fun character mostly meant for crowd control, after she throws her Sparda's sword she can do different moves with her fists, she is very quick and can disable enemies from attacking very quickly, yet she deals  lower damage, even with that she is very effective and fun to play.
Special Edition also comes with new costumes, with Nero receiving his prototype costume which he was meant to have in the vanilla, it looks wonderful, he also has a costume where he cosplays as his daddy Vergil, it's cute I guess.
Dante has of course Sparda's costume...and Donte (DmC) costume, which funnily enough he looks better in it than Donte.
Vergil has corrupted Vergil costume and Vante costume.
Lady and Trish have their costume as DLCs, even though their costumes which you buy are easily the most "meh" Trish's Gloria costume is nothing to behold, I never liked Gloria's design, and Lady's DMC3's look doesn't look right to me for some reason
You still have free costumes as these characters though, Lady has a costume where she cosplays as Trish and Trish has the costume where she cosplays as Lady.
As fot the tweaks, and things I noticed, everything seems positive and an improvement, let me list:
Gyroblades activate much much faster, they're pretty much fixed now and are no boring chore anymore
Dice Game has been slowed down and is much easier to do and manipulate to get to where you want it to go, it's actually kind of nice now, believe it or not.
All character's "spring" abillity activates right away, making the exploration throughout levels much faster.
All characters can now throw the swords which Nero only could throw around with his buster, they do it by simply hitting it.
Dante's round trip seem to activate faster.
Proud souls drop rate is doubled
AUTO-SAVES!
That is all I could find, I am happy with all  these changes though, as for graphics, it is more questionable, the game adds some nice lighging effects into the game which makes the game look prettier than before, but then there is the motion blur which some will despise and it doesn't help it cannot be turned off, I like it though, I think it's nice and makes it seem like the game is even faster, still, there should be an option to turn this damn thing off.
Any other parts where the edition dropped the ball? I guess it bothers me that new characters have no new battle themes, you'll just be "bringing the fables from thy tomb as kinghts loam" again and again. Which is unfortunate, I love DMC's soundtrack, I always did and I was looking forward of hearing new tracks, oh well.
So why should you buy Special Edition? Wel, it's not a hard buy in my opinionl;
If you really liked DMC4, it has a lot of content so it's easy to justify it being bought again
If you never played or bought DMC4, just buy this, don't bother with vanilla DMC4, there is no reason to buy that over this.
Definetelly recommended
Disclaimer: Please do not get into microtransactions which are here, only the costumes (Gloria, Lady) are hidden behind a pay wall, rest of the game's content can be unlocked without you having to throw money into your screen, please do not support this travesty. Do not encourage Capcom to put this into their next titles.

Anyway, this game is the cat's meow. I haven't felt this satisfied after playing a single player game in a while. Even all of the boring dialog and crap is pretty tolerable! There's just the right amount of boring dialog crap mixed in with the real point of any game, the gameplay.
The setting is actually pretty interesting too because of the parallels it draws with some modern socio-political issues involving prejudices or whatever. I always thought "Aug lives matter" was really insensitive to current events and the people deeply affected by them, but I now realize after playing the game that it's not insensitive at all and the game really put me in a position to consider different perspectives from a mostly netural perspective. That stuff was interesting and made the game feel alive while still exploring the effects of wide-spread prejudice issues through fiction.
The gameplay its self is the cat's pajamas. I'm talking really swell, here. Though I think it's pretty easy, I'm looking forward to playing the game on the difficulty setting you have to unlock. But boo!
There's a negative! Why do I have to play the game once to unlock the hardest difficulty? Boo, I say, boo!
Other than that, now that the mouse problem is patched and I got the right FOV, the game plays like butter. I have a pretty decent system though, a bit outdated, but I didn't seem to have any technical problems.

I've only played this game about 4 hours as of the time of this review.  I purchased the game for $1.50 on a 90% off sale and at that price, its a steal.  No, its not SUPER deep, there is overwatch mode and each character has 4 action points to split between moving and shooting.  That said, there are varied Space Marine legions to recruit from.  Unique and mastercrafted weapons, and some great banter between your characters, I don't know that I could say full price is worth it, but definitely worth it next time it goes on sale if you want a casual little fun tactical strategy game with progression.

First of, let's get the low hanging fruit out of the way. By low hanging fruit I mean the ridiculous microtransactions and save file exclusive DLC. Obviously, this is a cancerous way of implementing DLC into a game. In fact, this is probably the worst example of blatant developer greed I've ever seen.
Now that that's out of the way, let's move on. Next of, the story- it's total garbage. It all pretty much just serves as setup for the next game. Also, there's only one boss fight and it's pretty underwhelming.

That all being said, the gameplay is very much on point. It's probably some of the smoothest most satisfying gameplay I've played in a while. The level design is pretty great as well. There's a lot of verticality to areas now and it allows for a lot of new ways to approach each situation. The atmosphere is also really interesting and immersive just like Human Revolution's. All of the new augments are really cool too. I fell in love with the nanoblades.
All and all, if you go into Mankind Divided looking for a good story, you'll be sorely disappointed. If you go in looking for some slick gameplay and a cool cyberpunk atmosphere, you'll probably be pretty satisfied.
Story is a bit on the weak side but still relatively decent nonetheless. Gameplay is great and the side missions really contribute to the immersion. No regrets with this purchase.

I got the game massively discounted at 90% off retail. It's a good turn-based strategy game akin to Invisible Inc or XCOM series. I'd say this is a go on sale but otherwise the 14.99 is too steep, perhaps even for staunch Warhammer fans. I got it at a steal of 1.49, and am very pleased with what's present.
Unlike XCOM, there isn't too much cover provided in the game thus far as of the prologue. You're either in line of sight or not of the enemy it seems (no reduced damage or option to duck behind cover, at least during the prologue..) you do get a variety of weapons and unit types to use, however, and can (if you keep them alive long enough...) upgrade their abilities to have passive traits and other abilities such as a Cleave that hits 2 enemies instead of one. Certain character classes are better close range, while others can be upgraded to be more accurate when doing an Overwatch type ability waiting for enemies to walk by. There is a thick "fog of war" type effect which adds to the tension of not knowing what's ahead or how far to spread your characters out, but this also causes a weird-looking texture popping in effect during enemies turns that can be a little jarring.
For what the game is (a turn-based strategy game) it provides everything you'd expect from that genre including the aforementioned abilities and character upgrades and an unforgiving difficulty. I am a fan of the Warhammer universe, so admittedly biased to like the character and enemy designs. There could be more enemy and attack animation variety, but the bullets flying through the air as you cut aliens down look pretty nice, as do the lighting effects. I wish you could control the camera more as you're relegated to a mostly overhead or 75 degree ish angle looking down at the action. Sometimes the camera wigs out and sends you flying into a corner but it's easy enough to recover, and the general playing area is never too huge to get lost from the immediate action.
The game is sorely lacking music of pretty much any kind, particularly during more tense battle moments it would be nice to hear SOME kind of music. It's beginning to be really noticable as I hear the same sound effects from the same attacks over and over... As I upgrade my characters and the levels and enemies become more varied ( I am just completing the Prologue... so the variety of enemies may change and the sparse -nonexistent?- music may still be yet to make an appearance) those complaints aside I really like the game, but I am a fan of the universe already, and could see people not that into the overarcing setting not being too into this game.

Infested Planet is a relatively simplistic Real Time Strategy. The basic premise is that the enemy has infinitely spawning alien bugs, and you have infinitely spawning Marines. Your job is to slowly advance your territory, conquering enemy hives and turning them into bases. More bases gives you more resources to summon more marines, or to equip them with bigger weapons, or build enhancements on your bases.
Of course there's a catch: Every time you conquer a hive, the enemy gains a new bonus, such as more armor for its insects, the ability to spawn new types of insects, longer ranged attacks, or whatever. This essentially means that as you're gaining more resources, you also need to spread your forces thinner to protect all of your bases, and the enemy is also getting stronger, so the match gets more difficult as it goes on.
It's not a very difficult game. I found it to be a fun challenge for me and I beat the story campaign in about 7-8 hours, but I'm really bad at RTS games. A seasoned veteran of Starcraft and similar games should probably steer clear, because it will just be too easy for you.

This game is nearly ten years old, I'm not going to lie to you, it's aged. Not in a good way like a wine either.
The Good:
The first person shooter mechanics work well, though they do feel like an older style. This game tends to be "run and gun", think Quake, but perhaps a little more tactical. The enemy AI don't exactly outwit you, although, do they ever in a first person shooter? The combat is surprisingly fun, and the bullets feel surprisingly real. You get shot in the head with a rifle in real life, chances are you're ♥♥♥♥ed. You get shot in the head with a rifle in Call of Juarez? Chances are... you're ♥♥♥♥ed. Don't get me wrong though, this is no Dark Souls. The combat can be challenging (at least I found it so on normal difficulty), but you're not going to be repeating fights over and over again.

The Bad:

At the time Im writing this review, I've only played the main game, which means I DID NOT play the DLC story, yet. The DLC story (which aperantly now comes automaticaly with the game), is now downloading, but lets et to the vanilla Trine 2.
I played this game about a year ago, even more, and I loved it. The artstyle and asthetics are beautiful, and the overall graphic capability of this game is high, and it manages to create a wonderful, magic world. If you didnt play the original Trine, the main mechanic of the game is built around 3 characters that you can switch between at any time - a mage, a knight and a thief, each has their own specialities. The mechanics for each character are good and solid, and the game is fair to you at any time. The controlls work absolutly fine, and perhaps even better, with keyboard and mouse, so theres nothing to worry about.
But lets talk about actuall gameplay. Trine 2 is a 2.5D action puzzle platformer, where you fight a large veriety of enemies at a large veriety of different locations, and solve different puzzles. The story is set in a magical well realized fairy world, and the excellent voice acting really brings the characters and the story to life. The world is graphicly and astheticaly gorgeos, and imersses you in the second you load the game. The story is told as if it was a bedtime story, and the overall fealling is fantastic. The pltforming is solid, but not as sharp and resposive as a game like Super Meat Boy. If youre in for a hardcore platformer (like Super Meat Boy), go find it somewhere else. Trine 2 focuses a lot on puzzle solving and combat, both of which it does very well. The combat feels greate, and the puzzle solving is hard enough without being frasturating. Even tho the game doesnt give a true puzzle chalange in multiplayer, it has an incredible co-op multiplayer mode, where you have to get all the characters across the level, instead of only controlling one at the time and switching. You see, Trine 2 isnt a normal character switching game, it transforms all of the characters into one character, so if one character made it through the level, all the others did. But the multiplayer really does set up a challange for every puzzle fan like myself.
At the bottom line, Trine is an incredible experiance, and one I think has to be experianced by everyone. So if you didnt, now is the perfect time to pick the game, and probably also the fantastic soundtrack.

Review for the English version:
Needs a proper editor. I made it ten minutes in before I quit the game. The translation is pretty bad, full of run-on sentences, misused words, and constantly jumping between past and present tenses. I understand that English is probably not a native language for the development team (judging by the writing in their developer updates), and that's perfectly fine; but if you release a visual novel (i.e. a written work) that's badly written, you're going to get a bad review.
Objectively speaking (i.e. not judging by the plot or characters or any of the creative aspects, but purely from a factual stance on the writing and grammar), this game is bad.
DISCLAIMER: WHAT I'M GOING TO SAY NEXT IS PURELY MY OWN OPINION. I HAVE NO EVIDENCE FOR ANY OF IT.
I find it highly suspicious that the first game from an unknown development team (at least, unknown in the English VN circle) has almost 1500 reviews, and 3 curator reviews, after one month. What's more, 100% of the helpful/recommended reviews are positive, and almost all of them have been voted on 20+ times. The play times of these reviewers vary from 2-3 hours to as much as 13+ hours (which contradicts with the play times of the most recent reviews, some of which are less than 1 hour). Two of the helpful/recommended reviews are almost identical; to paraphrase, they both praise the true ending, and are both one sentence long in total. These are all my unbiased observations, and I have done no further research into these observations to turn them into anything more. Take them for what you will.
END DISCLAIMER.

The Sims is the best life-simulation game around, hands down. I personally enjoy the Sims 3, due to the open world nature(opposed to the Sims 2, just in your house, or Sims 4, with locations, but not just one big world), and the enormous amount of add-ons that can go in to customize your game. Want retro 70s clothes? They have it. Seasons? Check on that. Pets? Hell yeah. Vampires, witches, and things that go 'bump'? You bet! With dozens of worlds, thousands of outfits(and what can only be billions of combination outfits), and hundreds of building materials/household items you can buy, this game is already incredible. But the best part is in life simulation. Every sim, no matter how much you try, will look different, act different, and have different wishes. Even minor things like having a hotdog will propel your sims into a whole new world of wishes and hopes, from cooking, to a new job, to opportunities that accompany this. Every single playthrough is different, and that allows you to experiment as many times as you wish. Even with a single game is varies greatly day-by-day. One day, you could have an aspiring author, the next, they want to join Sunset Valley's Finest, or their worst. How they react, is up to you.

First of all: I played the first GunZ with friends a lot. I played GunZ1 over 200+ hours and it was really a great game.
Well. If you never played GunZ before, try that game. It have some interesting stuff and rewards you for getting online. You can play with your friends under the banner of your own clan and fight some dudes online. Crawl up the ladder and get some EXP, to get new skills. Also, choose one of five/six base-characters and be some unique figure InGame my costumize your character. There are some ways to play the game as you like, GunZ offers you may option here. It have also a Tutorial-Level, so the games explains you the main-gameplay mechanics. This is a great thing, too.
So, my contra.
I played GunZ2 for barely 2,5 Hours. I tried it with some friends, and my gameplay experience was really rough.
I mean, sure. It is a sequel. What do you expect, there have to be new stuff in it. Well, yes. But GunZ2 does feel really strange in many points.
a)
The menu-design is quite complicated. You dont get any hits whatssoever, what the numbers at the Tesla-Shop means, what Refinery is, why it is important to collect those crystals and all that. Sure. A awesome friend of mine told me about it, but seriosly: The developers must explain those important mechanics. When you just play the game along, GunZ2 won´t explain you how all this stuff works. I mean, right. Use Google. But don´t forget, this is a game. A game should be explaining stuff like this. Good games do that.
b)
The feeling, when you encounter other player, is just frustating. There are several games out there which support an own server for newbies or player, which play on low level. So GunZ2 is acctually throwing you in Servers, which are filled with high-level players, so skill does not help at all, when you realize that they have all those skills and weapons, they earn after they had played this game for hours. It would be cool, when GunZ2 had an newbie-server. But they don´t. In fact, it feels like they don´t even have some system, which tries to create a fair lobby, where players have the same level (+/- X).
c)
One of my biggest downers are the way the host-servers works. During online-play, it was an extrem sad experience. If an player was host and his internet-connection was not so good as it should be, the match was a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ So, sometimes the game recordnice it that the host should be switched, sometimes not. I dont know what the IF-Causes are, but Hell - It was super frustating. Some people may think at this point, that they gameplay-experience is just fine. As I checked intels about those host-connection, some Users have more or less problems depends where you actually play. Me, as a European, had really troubles playing GunZ2. And my ISP is alright. Never had problems playing games over the Internet.
At this point: Playing campain was simply good. When you play in a privat lobby and you know that someone in your lobby have a good and stable connection to be the host, everything works fine. But like I sad before, if you play with People online - Nope.
d)
And my last point: The game is free and use the good old Play&Win. You can get premium stuff, which allows you to get powerful items or increases the chances to get great stuff. Also the typical things like EXP-Boost etc. If you okay with this stuff, go ahead. Just a simply warning at this point.
Well. Those are my main points.
Like I sad, GunZ is a good game. It can be fun. But those problems destroys the possibility to have really good fun. You cannot fix this as a player, so this game is not playable for a guy like me. Try it out, find out if you like this game and when you do and don´t have those problems I had, Awesome. Im glad for you.
Have fun and don´t forget - This is just my opinion.

Call of Juarez is the first of a rather unremarkable series of western shooters. The series is about half and half in my opinion. Bound in Blood and Gunslinger are both great entries in the series. This one is the original and all I have to say is that it's outdated and unremarkable. It runs like crap on high end PCs in DirectX 10 mode and it feels janky at 60 FPS. The bullet time is awkward (you have to holster your guns first and then whip them right back out while trying to shoot with two auto piloted crosshairs) and the stealth is just god awful. The premise is cool, where you play two characters playing a game of Cat and Mouse with each other but that's all I have to say that's positive. Many might say this harkens back to the older, more open first person shooters. While this may be true, it still doesn't change the fact the game gives you very broad objectives with very little hints as to what you actually need to do to complete these objectives and not die four times doing a simple task such as "Jump out the window of a house". *NEW* -Review -
It seems some viewers would like to more know about 'Himeko's Epilogue' and DLC which this 'Anthology' purchase gives you. So instead of just a tip on how to best enjoy Narcissu, I added a review to be more helpful. Here's a short version summery of my feelings on it and the other DLC, with as little story spoilage as possible.
-Himeko's Epilogue
Months after playing, I recall 'Himeko's Epilogue' as a charming yet bittersweet experience. The story wasn't the gut-wrenching tragedy that was Part 1, as the author didn't get me as intimately attached to the protagonist character. I suppose 'Himeko's Epilogue' is a different flavor of story from Part 1; sad, yet relaxed, following Himeko's narrative faithfully, while adding snipets of history to beloved Setsumi's past. With Setsumi now far less involved, the supporting characters who were not prominent figures in Part 2, (and didn't seem like they would be very interesting), are back. I am pleased to say that they helped this final piece earn a recommend at $3.
-A Little Iris
I had the false impression, since all the stories are lumped together as DLC, that it would be similar in plot to Setsumi or Himeko's story. But to me it shares nothing in common with those stories. In this one there is much death, of the murderous kind.  The author constantly left me uncertain of the outcome, as the plot twists in 'A Little Iris' were very well designed.
One downside to 'A Little Iris' is that it shares the same music as 'Ame No Marginal'. I couldn't accept that, so I just found some decent 'depressing/sad' piano music on youtube to repeat.
Hellraiser's OST also fit parts of the story nicely.

It's OK.
I recommend it, but it's only OK.
In Deathwatch (a PC port of an IOS game) you control 5 space marines in a mission to...kill some stuff. Just about every mission can be broken down to either "defend for X number of turns" or "Go to location Y." The gameplay is simplistic, but gratifying. Identify enemy, shoot enemy, take cover, end turn. Level ups, traits, and perks keep things fresh; but there's a massive overarching issue.
As an IOS game, Deathwatch originally came with microtransactions. These have since been removed, but the collectible card system still remains. A new card pack is unlocked every 4th level and contains a new marine and 2 pieces of rare loot. Additional card packs can be unlocked by donating 5 items every 4 levels. The problem is that this sets the game at a deliberate slow pace where upgrades and new weapons are rare. This problem compounds with new characters.
Higher tier characters come with more unlockable traits. Many of these traits require between 4,500-12,000 XP. A standard campaign mission will net you about 1,200-1,800 XP. Again, this brings the pace to a grinding halt and encourages players to get rid of their starting marines as soon as possible. It also encourages players to buy more cards to get high tier marines, but this is impossible because microtransactions have been removed.
Three side notes about game design:
1. Devastators don't work as they should: Devastators, as in normal 40k, can weild heavy bolters. In most 40k games, the heavy bolter is used for anti-infantry. In Deathwatch, the heavy bolter is just a low-damage, long-range multi-melta. Heavy bolters can fire a maximum of 2 shots per turn. Loading screen tips even explain that Devastators can easily be surrounded. The problem then is that larger heavy weapons use 3/4 of your AP, leaving you only 1 AP to move. Since most missions involve traveling long distances, Devastators become useless as AP is shared between travel and weapon usage.
The heavy bolter can either fire twice or go into overwatch and fire once.
The lascannon can fire once or go into overwatch.
Loading screen tips insist assault marines are the risk/reward, but the real risk/reward is if your Devastators will get a shot off.
2. Death + XP loss: With a few exceptions, you usually won't know what you're getting into with a mission. If your character dies, they lose all their XP, not just for the quest, but the XP you've been saving for that new trait. If you go back to the main menu, the entire squad loses all of their XP. This is needlessly frustrating and doesn't achieve anything in a single player game.
3. Overwatch is poorly implemented: I alluded to this earlier, but when overwatch here is compared to overwatch in Space Hulk, it's just horrific. In Space Hulk, so long as you set your unit to overwatch units would fire indefinitely. This made it difficult for genestealers to win, but they had both numbers and the possibility of a weapon jam. In Deathwatch, most units only have 4 AP. It costs 1 AP just to set overwatch, each attack uses an AP (though some units can purchase a 1/3 chance for a free shot), and if a unit is damaged, they exit overwatch. All of this is compounded by overlapping overwatch. Units have an enormous field of view, which can often overlap. If you put 1 unit in overwatch, you get a maximum of 3 attacks. But because of overlapping and a lack of advanced tactical input, if you put 2 adjacent units in overwatch, you STILL get a max. of 3 attacks.
Pacing, leveling, and class design are a complete disaster, but the game is still pretty fun.

At the time Im writing this review, I've only played the main game, which means I DID NOT play the DLC story, yet. The DLC story (which aperantly now comes automaticaly with the game), is now downloading, but lets et to the vanilla Trine 2.
I played this game about a year ago, even more, and I loved it. The artstyle and asthetics are beautiful, and the overall graphic capability of this game is high, and it manages to create a wonderful, magic world. If you didnt play the original Trine, the main mechanic of the game is built around 3 characters that you can switch between at any time - a mage, a knight and a thief, each has their own specialities. The mechanics for each character are good and solid, and the game is fair to you at any time. The controlls work absolutly fine, and perhaps even better, with keyboard and mouse, so theres nothing to worry about.
But lets talk about actuall gameplay. Trine 2 is a 2.5D action puzzle platformer, where you fight a large veriety of enemies at a large veriety of different locations, and solve different puzzles. The story is set in a magical well realized fairy world, and the excellent voice acting really brings the characters and the story to life. The world is graphicly and astheticaly gorgeos, and imersses you in the second you load the game. The story is told as if it was a bedtime story, and the overall fealling is fantastic. The pltforming is solid, but not as sharp and resposive as a game like Super Meat Boy. If youre in for a hardcore platformer (like Super Meat Boy), go find it somewhere else. Trine 2 focuses a lot on puzzle solving and combat, both of which it does very well. The combat feels greate, and the puzzle solving is hard enough without being frasturating. Even tho the game doesnt give a true puzzle chalange in multiplayer, it has an incredible co-op multiplayer mode, where you have to get all the characters across the level, instead of only controlling one at the time and switching. You see, Trine 2 isnt a normal character switching game, it transforms all of the characters into one character, so if one character made it through the level, all the others did. But the multiplayer really does set up a challange for every puzzle fan like myself.
At the bottom line, Trine is an incredible experiance, and one I think has to be experianced by everyone. So if you didnt, now is the perfect time to pick the game, and probably also the fantastic soundtrack.

Alright, first thing's first: I don't care if there are microtransactions. They do not affect the quality of the game or its content. I played this game through on the first playthrough on the highest difficulty and found no need to purchase them. With that out of the way, I'll try keep this brief:
Pros:
-The game's greatest strength is its environmental design. The level design is tight and filled with possibilities, and every area is dressed up to feel like a real place. I've only played this game in stealth, but from what I delved into with the combat, you have more lethal abilities than ever before and they seem extremely fun to use.
-Not only is the level design great, but the city of Prague is so bustling and lively, and filled to the brim with character and content. Deus Ex is one of the few remaining franchises that trades quantity for quality, in terms of how densely packed the game world is, and I really wish there were more games that followed in its footsteps. This series is truly one of a kind.
-The side content is the best part of the package this time around. The sheer variety of activities you can do is wonderful. I really don't want to give anything away about the side content, but I will say that if you don't do everything, you're sorely missing out.
-Finally, the sound design is fantastic. The music is all wonderfully composed; the ambient noise really helps ground the world; the voice acting is all up to par. This is also one of the few games I can feel comfortable amping up to max volume without getting my ears blown out.
Cons:
-The loading times are atrocious. On the most recent patch (v1.2 build 524.15) I noticed loading times were approximately halved but they're still extremely long. Can't help but get taken out of the experience when a cutscene ends and then slaps me straight into a loading screen.
-The story is bad. It's baaaaaaaad. While the character interactions and dialogue is all there and works, the "theme" that's incorporated into everything barely hits home, if ever. I would very much prefer if the next entry in the series just drops the pretense of being philosophical and just makes the plot an emotionally driven character study like the narrative of this game and Human Revolution have been. It's much easier to swallow the rambunctious adventures of Adam Jensen and his quest to spite the illuminati if it's not trying to say something profound about racism.
That about covers it. This is a fantastic game and I think it's well worth your time and money, but if you're in it for the story, just, set your expectations low. Extremely low.

Short version: Mankind Divided is good. Square Enix sucks. I requested a refund for the Season Pass because SE sucks. Still, this review is ultimately positive because the game is good. Have I said that SE sucks yet? Because they do. :o
DX:MD is a sequel to 2011's HR, which means it's a sequel to a prequel... but still a prequel... gaaaaah. Anyway, yer Adam Jensen again as he tries to unravel conspiracy things ongoing from HR, but made more ugly this time around thanks to how the last game ended. Essentially... "normal" humans don't trust the augmented anymore, and that distrust and hate is on full display throughout the entire game. The main plot revolves around it. The side-quests frequently have it come up. Even your wandering around the open city areas of Prague will put it in your face.
The parallels between both history and recent events are blatantly obvious. The intense hatred for augmented people and herding them into seriously unpleasant ghettos is very much reminiscent of Nazi Germany's treatment of Jews, though they are not outright murdering augmented people here. But the behaviors of the authorities and police forces in this mess not only channel the Gestapo, but the recent tensions in the US about the excessive militarization and aggressiveness of the police. There's even a callback to Jim Crow segregation as there are "natural" and "aug" sections of the city trams that you regularly have to use. And since you are playing as an augmented character, even one with special clearance and as a member of an anti-terror organization, that pretty much means that you will be subjected to ALOT of offensive comments and behaviors directed your way, simply for having robot parts on you.
It should probably come as no surprise that despite the fact that there is nothing to gain from doing it, my tendency to knock out or even outright shoot cops who♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off was common. In fact I probably killed more police in this game than any other enemy type since I tended to go non-lethal alot. I also often chose to ride in the "naturals" section of the trams because segregation can eat♥♥♥♥♥♥and so can the cops who bother me about it the instant I exit those trams. In fact at one point in the game where I went through a story mission filled with cops that I ended up gunning down, it was actually reported as a terrorist attack by the in-game news. An anti-terrorist agent committing acts of terrorism. Consider me amused. XD
Since it's a "Do Sex" game, it's rather obvious that the story is well-done, and that the gameplay is essentially HR's gameplay, but with some new toys and improvements here and there. I particularly liked the number of references made to the original Deus Ex, with quite a few notable characters/organizations from that game (Bob Page, Joseph Manderly, Morgan Everett, the NSF, Sillouette, etc.) directly appearing or being referenced. Considering how good HR is... it's not a huge leap to say that MD is also a winner. And since my reviews are mainly based upon how good the actual story and game are, this game gets a solid recommendation from me...
...
...However. This will be the last time I buy a Square-Enix game at full price unless they fix their behavior. Obviously i'm talking about the one-time use DLC and... ♥♥♥♥ing microtransactions... in a singleplayer game. What. The. ♥♥♥♥. I'd add performance issues to that list too, but I actually had few problems with this game. I did have one crash and the loading times were rather long, but that was it. The game ran fine, and even the obnoxious "business practices" were easy to ignore. I didn't even know there were in-game microtransactions until a friend told me. And I was disgusted.
It's not enough to make me rage on forums and give this a negative review. For one, the game itself, as I already said, is pretty good and that's what truly matters. And second I am just not the type to get ragey, stir♥♥♥♥♥♥up on forums, and go around downvoting every positive review a game has despite the fact that those people (probably) have nothing to do with the source of their anger.
No... I vote with my wallet. I requested a refund for the Season Pass, if only to tell SE to go to hell in a small way. Square-Enix, thanks to what they have pulled with this game, is now on my game developer♥♥♥♥♥♥list alongside EA (whom I haven't bought a single game from in 5 years) and Ubisoft (who seems to hate PC gamers). Sure... one person doing this might not add up to much, but I'd rather do this than get mad on a forum. There are plenty of people doing that for me.
So, for those of who you have yet to get Deus Ex: Mankind Divided, I ask you to wait. It's a good game, which makes the shenanigans SE pulled all the more annoying because good games don't need shady tricks to make more monies: they are supposed to speak for themselves with their own quality. But since Square-Enix sucks, I ask that you refrain from buying this game until it is deeply discounted in a Steam sale or simply by the passage of time. And when that time finally comes and you can actually play this game... enjoy. :D
TL:DR Mankind Divided is good, but Square-Enix can go ♥♥♥♥ itself.
