Volition, Inc. provides an amazing action experience that brings you back through the ages. Red Faction is the start of an amazing series which provides a possibly reality to early space colonization.
You play Parker a man who travelled to Mars in order to work for Ultor Corporation and create himself a future. Ultor Corporation lures miners with the promise of a future. Little do they know the corporation is manipulating the media to show people a completely different light of what is really going on. Breaking basic Human Rights Ultor is essentially torturing miners forcing them to work in terrible conditions. But all is about to change as the Red Faction rises up from the dust and who is going to be unwittingly a part of the rebellion, but Parker. As you progress through the campaign you learn more about the horrible tortures that Ultor is actually conducting.
The campaign is broken up into 12 levels: Mines, Registration, Abandoned Mines, Gryphon, Canyon, Comm Center, Barracks, Docking Bay, Geothermal Plant, Capek, Subway, and Shuttle. The game takes you through the underground of mars, through canyons, and to space itself. Throughout the campaign you will be put against bosses, environmental hazards, and hordes of enemies.
The game has an array of difficulty levels that allow you to enjoy a casual simple first person shooter to a hard-core gaming experience. Red faction has a variety of weapons: FCA-26 Rail Driver, UAR-42 Assault Rifle, F-1TL Fusion Rocket Launcher, URL-6T Rocket Launcher, UBS-4 Riot Shield, UFT-1 Flame Thrower, UCB-24 Control Baton, USP-16 Pistol, UAP-32/20 Sub Machine Gun, UAS-18 Shotgun, UHG-90 Offensive Hand Grenade, URC-15 Remote Charge, JF60 Heavy Suppression Machine Gun, MK/SG-1 Defender Pricision Rifle, and USG-50 Sniper Rifle. The massive combination of weapons provides a very deep gameplay experience allowing you to go for a close and personal combat all the way to a long-distant assassin. The scenery is highly destructible allowing you to blow holes into walls, destroy furniture, and even destroy parts of scenery making it fall onto enemies below.
Red Faction is an amazing first person shooter that offers amazing combat and a fantastic story. Red Faction may be an older title, but it offers features still not fully offered in games today. The campaign has pretty decent length and you will not be regretting the purchase. This game is a fantastic experience, and I would recommend getting it as part of the Red Faction Collection when it goes on sales. As the other titles of the series are definitely a great group of games.

Wow. What can i say about this? It's the kind of game that should have been made with the Aliens liscense. You've got space marines. You've got enemies where one doesn't pose a threat, the threat comes from the huge numbers of them. It's a game that makes you feel badass. You've got troops in the single digits, and you're taking down tens of thousands of aliens. It makes you feel awesome. Powerful.
It's a practically perfect strategy game.

Not perfect, but enjoyable.
The story is simple but effective, with memorable battles and diverse (narratively, not mechanically) objectives.
Gameplay is easy to understand with enough variety provided by the weapons and talents that it isn't simplistic. You move and shoot like any tactical turn based game. The missions are all fairly straightforward ether go to a certain point, survive some amount of time, or kill everything. It might get a little more complex, like kill a certain target THEN go to a point. Or go to a point to plant a bomb, then go to another point. Overall it's good, not ambitious or well polished, but serviceable and without any major mistakes.
The lore is fairly light, but organically integrated. The marines will occasionally just banter with eachother and talk about their experiences and preferences, for example once while carrying samples through a kill zone one of them asked another how he felt that the mundane humans regard the emperor as a god, there were a few back and forth between the team members before the space wolf said that the truth would come out in the wolf time.
The game crashes/freezes/bugs out occasionally. Which is annoying, but if you close the game and restart it, it auto saves in the mission so you don't lose any progress. So not the worst bugs I've seen.
You get better gear and marines through a collectable card system which is random and makes the game pretty grindy if you are wanting something in particular, but it also adds a bit of excitement to every round conclusion because you might draw a legendary weapon or hero... or another bolter. Seriously, every tactical marine comes with a bolter equipped by default, there is literally no situation in which you will find yourself wanting another basic bolter because if the marine could equip it, he already has one. But overall the card aspect is fun.
The weapons feel good to use (well, except the plasma guns. Personal preference) and they all have different playstyles. For example a bolter shoots volleys of rounds, so while it may do 34-50 damage, that's assuming they all hit, which they probably wont, but because it's a volley that means that they won't all miss ether, and each hit is another chance to do crit damage. While a melta gun is a single shot that ether hits or doesnt. It has a shorter range but higher damage. The plasma gun shoots volleys like the bolter, but can be overcharged and might overheat... things like that.
The special weapons sometimes have a few special rules to add to the weapon, or adjust the stats to make the weapon radically different in some way, or some of them just have higher damage. But the higher tier weapons also have lower accuracy. Strange, but it works because it makes an interesting choice between weapons that will hit more often or do more damage... for lower level marines it's often not worth it, they need to level up before they can really take advantage of the best weapons.
The enemy is a little light on variety, but some of the larger tyranids are terrifying to behold. Harder difficulties make the enemies more threatening obviously.
Sound is good, the ambient sounds and the tyranid calls are very atmospheric... but it cannot be turned down, in case you were planning to listen to a podcast while grinding for XP and loot.

My first Deus Ex game was Human Revolution and I gotta say I was pleasantly surprised when I played it-It was very good and I enjoyed it a lot. I loved the story, the gameplay and the characters, I didn't like some of the mechanics and a few minor things but overall was a great game.
Mankind Divided addresses some of the issues of HR and from what I have played so far(about 25-26hrs) I gotta say that is a big improvement over it. Visually of course, as well as gameplay-wise this one is superior. The style, the music, the voice acting...it is all great. If you liked HR you would love this one as well.
Now onto the performance and graphics-the game looks very good-the models are excellent, the environments have great deal of details also. I love the lighting and the effects in the game. That said the stiff animations during dialog and the lip sync is pretty bad and I am surprised that it doesn't even feel any better than HR. Performance-wise the game needs a bit of optimization but it's nothing to cry about. I am running the game fine maxed out (no MSAA) at 1440P and it's perfectly playable. Could it be better-yes! Is the worst-far from it. People also are complaining about crashes-never had one for aver 26 hrs...so I don't know what the deal is there either.
Overall this is a great game and it deserves positive reviews, most of the negative reviews out there are about micro transactions and performance...micro transactions are optional and you can't expect towards the end of 2016 to max out every game at 1440P with a gtx 970...it is just not going to happen.

What can I say, well for one I highly recommend this game. Having played Human Revolutions many years ago on the xbox 360 I was incredibly excited to play this upon release. Gameplay wise its excatly what you would expect from a Deus Ex game, the Aug options allow you to tailer Adam Jenson's abilites to suite your'e own playstyle. Prague is very well modeled with multiples ways in and out of situations making it highly replayable, you can opt to be stealthy and systamtically take down the enemy without alerting them, or you can attempt a more "guns blazing" approach.
The story and theme go hand in hand, i've seen some reviews stating it felt rushed and poorly explained but if you take the time to immerse yourself in the game world, listen to the conversations of NPC's and complete the numerous side missions it all comes together.
Visually the game is beautiful with day/night cycle adding a sense of depth to the overall atmosphere, immersing you in a believable dystopian future.
Now for the cons:
I have to admit I am not a fan of day one DLC or microtransactions, especially in a singleplayer game (the ability to only use paid for items in one save only is frankly insulting aswell) However, these dont really impact on the game in anyway, the DlC of course would be nice, but I shall wait till larger expansions are released. The microtransactions you can avoid entirely as the game world is filled with all the loot you'll ever need.
Their have also been some problems with crashing, specifically in the Shooting range that I have noticed. But you must remember it is only a few days after release and that the technical issues will be dealt with in time.
Altogether I'd give this a solid 9/10 and would highly recommend as the game can be played out numerous times, with each playthrough being different and eachtime you'll possibly find new rooms or hidden routes to explore.

If you're a fan of Spaghetti Westerns or say Stephen King's Gunslinger series, you'll probably like this game. This game is basically a Spaghetti western, from the story line to the bullet-time-like concentration mode. The story is linear and central to this game. For those who insist on an open world, this game is not for you. I noticed quite a few reviewers gave a thumbs down to the game simply because it was a linear game.
That said, there are some really annoying things about this game. The physics don't work right at times. For example, you can get stuck trying to simply jump a broken fence or onto a crate. Not being able to pick something up that's inside a drawer you just opened is also annoying. You'll have to try to figure out how to crouch in just the right position in order to target the item.  It's just unnecessary frustration. I also really hate that they made jumping a mandatory skill in the game. You'll find yourself falling because you timed your jump between platforms wrong. This isn't a Mario Bros. game, so why am I doing that anyway?
All in all, I really do like this game. The developers captured the essence of the Spaghetti western like no other game.

Full Disclosure: I'm a Dynasty Warriors ♥♥♥♥♥. I've been playing the series since I was in high school when Dynasty Warriors 3 released. I'm pretty much guaranteed to buy and play every new DW game that comes out. It's only much later in hindsight that I can say which ones were lacking. DW6, for example, was pretty subpar, and I remember feeling disappointment while playing it.
DW8:E is a fun game. It melds the DW repetitive hack-and-slash with the rudimentary concepts behind the Romance of the Three Kingdoms game, but in an incredibly simplified form. Nonetheless, I enjoyed this game a lot, as I've always been a huge fan of Risk-style gameplay (conquer territories, make diplomacy, etc). Hell, Romance of the Three Kingdoms X is still one of my favorite games to this day.
I think the only thing I don't like about this game is its lack of english VAs. I played the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of DW3 and DW4, and horrible dialogue and mispronounced Chinese names were part of the goodness that was this series. Starting with DW5, they began pronouncing the names right, and now, with DW8:E, they dropped the english VAs altogether. It's not a game killer for me, but it is something I miss.
Bottom line: if you love DW games, you'll love this one. If you hate the mindless button pressing of DW with a passion, then you should probably look elsewhere. Regardless, from a fan's perspective, highly recommended.

I have been meaning to write a review for this game and I am only now really getting around to it.
Before beginning let me state that this review does come from the bias of someone who does heavily enjoy the Dynasty Warriors franchise. That in mind, I hope others who might be a fan of the series as well might be able to take what I say about this particular game more to heart.
On to it: The Empire series is one of my favourite in the DW’s line, I probably play them more than the main game series to be quite frank. That being said, Dynasty Warriors 8 Empires was a bit of a let down compared to past installments. I believe anyone who might have never played an Empires game or even a Dynasty Warriors game who would still be able to pick this game up and thoroughly enjoy it.
I initially played the game on my PS4, where I had to stop because it kept crashing my system, so instead reluctantly rebought the PC port. Which is really all it is, a port to the PC from the PS4. The controls can be really off-putting at times, and I would highly suggest never playing this game without a controller. Going into a full list of cons, again, I want to state that these will be coming from the perspective of someone who plays the actual series and not just this singular game alone.
Cons:
-The game is a step back from previous versions. Dynasty Warriors 7 Empires had MUCH more content in it. More dialogue, better cut-scenes, an overall better system. It was just a better game. So to see DW8E get worse was really… discouraging to someone who pretty much dropped $100 just to be able to keep playing the game.
-Character customization options have literally not changed at all. Facial adjustments have maybe slightly improved? Otherwise it’s mostly just all brought over from DW7E.
-To any long time fans of the series, it’s really not worth $50. I mean, that’s a really hefty price-tag, and while I do feel perhaps some buyer's remorse from having paid double to keep playing, I also enjoy Empires enough that I really would have preferred to be able to play it on my PC. Even if the PC port is kinda okay.
-This is redundant, and I know it is, but it really bothered me how bad interactions and dialogue were. There is no visiting cities anymore? No walking about and actually seeing how your rule affects people. It’s just an occasional cutscene, and it really takes away from the immersion of the game.
-Children system is still trash, and you can only have one. And from what gameplay I have done, your spouses no longer heal you if you’re on the battlefield with them and injured.
-DW8 in general was a step back from DW7 as it was, so truthfully, I can’t be too surprised that the Empires series suffered some as well.
Pros:
These judgements are steered more towards new players of the series, as the game still does have redeemable qualities.
- From just a game standpoint alone, it’s fun. There are lots of campaigns to do, and hours worth of difficult battles to participate in.
-You can have your own character who can marry off any random officer or notorious officer and have a kid who you can also play with. As stated in the cons, the system isn’t amazing, but it’s still a fun little thing that’s there.
-Tons of variety in characters and fighting styles. Really, there is SO much to choose from, it’s great.
-It’s a hack and slash, so you get to run around killing thousands of people and it’s pretty rewarding for just that alone.
-The added strategy of the Empire series allows you to try different techniques in how you would like to take over all of China. You can rule with an iron fist, be really benevolent, or be downright tyrannical. Depending on which route you choose, your gameplay might prove to be more difficult, which is part of the enjoyment of the game.
-You don’t have to be a ruler. You can assist in helping bring someone else to power. Tear someone else down. Overthrow rulers, etc. The possibilities are really quite high.
In the end, while it might be easy for me to say “this game is bad compared to DW7” objectively it is not a terrible game by any standards. If I had to drop a flat rating on it, I’d give it a 6/10 and I do recommend it to people who might like to try an Empires game on the PC. I think anyone who might want a fun game to play would like it for what it is, but anyone who has ever touched a DW game beforehand would be able to clearly see its glaring flaws.

Let’s give an actual review:
Cat Goes Fishing is literally a game where you are a cat and you cast your line into the water and grab a fish. The water is full of types of fish, all with different attributes. Generally, you start by getting a small fish, then you use that as bait to get a bigger fish and so on. Then you sell the fish and buy upgrades, like a big rod and a boat. To increase variety and give goals, the game has an optional quest system that ranges from easy to difficult.

It’s addictive and simple, but has everything you would want for this type of thing. The constant upgrades and range of fish types give the game more variety.
I suppose my only criticism is that being a cat has almost zero effect on the game. The protagonist could have been a person and that wouldn't have changed anything.

Main plot is glorious and consists of different little stories you can discover (or miss) on your way. It also has a lot of symbolism which is often a part of gameplay. Some people say that it's too short (around 5 hours), but in my opinion the length of the game is ideal for the story being told. It brings new elements of gameplay in every chapter, so you simply have no time to get bored with them. It keeps the game interesting until the very end even if you don't like the plot (what is unlikely). The game also provides picturesque landscapes like every 5 minutes.
Technically it's a platformer with some little puzzles. Unique feature of the game is controlling two characters at the same time. It can seem difficult at first and it definitely needs more coordination, but controls are simple and very well done. In overall the game isn't hard to beat. Game runs well on old systems (see system requirements). Also it's fully compatible and comfortable to play with keyboard.
I highly recommend to play and complete this peace of art.

Tight, focused, exciting gameplay.
Graphics are crisp and bright and tell you exactly what's going on, while being full of style.  Menus, character portraits, and icons are all expertly made.
Perfect UI.  You can zoom as far as you want.  Everything has a shortcut, they're visible in-game, and they're on the left of the keyboard.  You receive appropriate alerts, and the range and orders of every unit can be seen.  Everything about the UI says "oh, they thought of that too".
Mutations and upgrades keep things fresh.  Try random missions or continue with the story.  There's a "daily challenge" I haven't tried yet.  There doesn't appear to be an "easy" or optimal strategy.  Use what works in different situations.  Use the generous money you get from missions to buy new technology.  This game is excited to get the goodies in your hands.
The gameplay is fluid.  You might be losing, badly; that doesn't mean you can't regroup and win.  Everything can be redone in the middle of a mission and early mistakes can be recovered from.  It's hard as hell and it can be frustrating.  But persevere and you'll break through.
Very impressed with this game.  Paid $15 and have been absolutely delighted.

You play a mercenary commander aiding the army colonisation of a new planet. Unfortuantely, it has a bug problem.
Infested Planet adds what most tower defences lack; actual strategy. Surprisingly well balanced, this game isn't going to punish you, but it's not going sit down and take it either.
The 10 to 15 min missions and forgiving nature make this a very agreeable "I only have a little while" title.  You can even surrender a mission at any point and still walk away with a little of your merc pay. Some of the missions don't even need you to progress to make cash. It's a case of not dying.
So what do you spend your merc pay on? Well, for a start, upgrades. The odd thing about them is that while many games do the same, the offerings here really give flexibility. It doesn't truely matter WHAT you unlock, but rather what you build on map. Even if you buy an upgrade you didn't want, no worries. You can't undo it, but you're not cockblocked.
You can also purchase one-shot additional mercenaries. You'll never run out of things to spend cash on, nor missions :)
My best tip : minefields are often a better choice than a turret if you can use it in a chokepoint.

Torchlight 2 takes everything that has come to define the action-RPG genre and delivers it all in an incredibly well polished package. From fast paced brutal hack n’ slash combat to immersive diverse level design to an abundance of loot, Torchlight 2 has it all. Developed by Runic Games; a small Dev team of around 30 members in Seattle WA, they prove that they have what it takes to create a quality product that can compete and even outshine the likes of juggernaut developer Blizzard and their own ARPG Diablo III.
The game starts the way you would expect an Action-RPG to start, by choosing your characters class. The game offers four different classes to choose from; Outlander: the gun wielding bad♥♥♥♥♥class, Engineer: the steampunk style, tinkering, gadget using class, Embermage: the typical wizardry spell casting class, and the Berzerker: the warrior heavy hitting class.  Each class feels different enough from one another where your play throughs still feel fresh and entertaining if you decide to give the game another play through as a different character. The combat is fast paced and hectic, the best way to describe the way it feels would be to call it a “controlled chaos”, meaning that while at times things do get crazy as you’re being ambushed by a massive horde of enemies, but you never resort to just spamming mouse clicks to succeed, you have to understand how your characters class works and use that knowledge to stay alive. For example; if you are an Embermage, you aren’t going to be able to rush head on into hordes of enemies and make it out alive like you would as a bulkier Berzerker.
Next to the combat, the games second greatest strength is the level design, with each map being randomly generated you will never experience the same thing twice. This allows the game to continue to feel fresh if you decide to do multiple play throughs. While randomly generated maps aren’t anything new to games, Torchlight 2’s random generation feels like they are gorgeously hand crafted levels, if you weren’t already aware of the R&G then you wouldn’t ever be able to tell by the games gorgeously laid out levels and dungeons.
The developers also paid a strong attention to detail in the weapons, armor, and items in the game. With such a large diverse number of weapons and various armors to equip you won’t become bored from having to use any one weapon or set of armor for any long period of time as there are loot drops and chests galore located all throughout the expansive dungeons you’ll be crawling your way through. But what good would such a large trove of weapons and armor be without an expansive onslaught of enemies to vanquish? Have no worries, the game has a large array of varying enemies to slaughter, from hulking snow beasts to dark lord necromancers the game does not burn you out on any one style of enemy.
Torchlight 2 is best played with friends, but even if you don’t have anyone to play with Torchlight 2 provides you with a trusty animal companion who will fight alongside you. Not only does your pet companion work like a beefy tank to distract enemies when you have to run off and heal, but they are also your errand running slave, they double as a 2nd backpack that can be packed full of all the valuable loot that you’ve managed to acquire. You can then send your pet off to the market with a shopping list of various health and mana potions and he will sell your loot and return with the potions, this eliminates the need to travel all the way back to town yourself and interrupt your questing. Not necessarily a revolutionary gameplay mechanic but it is incredibly convenient and keeps the game pace going full speed ahead.
Torchlight 2 doesn’t do anything that hasn’t really been done before, it’s not new or innovative, but it does take everything good that has been done before and bundles them all together and manages to deliver them all perfectly. The combat is seamless and the expansive diverse levels and dungeons leave much to explore. The game has so much to offer and I would highly recommend Torchlight 2 to anyone looking for a fun fast paced gameplay experience.

I really enjoyed playing this game. I truly did. I played the hell out of the campaign, and had a lot of fun doing heists and racing with randoms online. It's just a damn shame that Take 2 and Rockstar decide to become greedier than ever before and ban any and all modding of the game. I feel that modding is an essential part of PC gaming in general; it lets the more passionate fans of video games take what they love and craft it into something that makes their game more unique, more optimized, and more improved. Mods let the users make the game theirs. It lets users play the game they want to play.
Ultra HD Graphics and Optimization? Sure, let's make the game look better and run nicer.
Custom maps and campaigns? Yeah, I'll try something new.
Turn my character into Sonic the Hedgehog? ♥♥♥♥ it, why not.
Mods make the game yours, and more importantly, they add to the game's longevity. Thanks to the modding community, games like the original DooM and DooM II, released
, are still relatively active today thanks to players who dedicate their time to create custom map packs, weapon mods, multiplayer game modes, and full-fledged total conversions. Giving players the creative power to take your game and make something that you would have never thought to make is fundamental in keeping the game fresh and fun to play. It's a goddamn shame that Rockstar and Take Two are destroying the reputation of arguably their best-selling game ever by preventing their most passionate customers and fans from changing the game into something new, possibly better. I feel that Rockstar and Take Two are shooting themselves in the foot with a nuke, and it's already starting to show, at least in the overall feedback. At the time of writing, Recent Reviews are Overwhemingly Negative and the Overall Reviews are Mixed. In time, I hope they realize that stripping one of the most appealing aspects of PC gaming isn't the way to go. Unfortunately, I'm not holding my breath. Unless the stars align and they reverse their decision, I will make an effort to stop supporting any and all games from either of these companies.

Now before I go into detail this was a very hard choice for me, chosing between reccomending and not. Given all of the issues, bugs, even the microtransactions I still chose to give this game a recommendation. (Feel free to scroll down for the actual review of Mankind Divided, several paragraphs are for history/background and my general feeling/facts throughout the games series).
I have been a fan of the Deus Ex series since I was a wee lad; 15 years I have been a fan of this game since it's initial release of the first Deus Ex back in 2000. The first Deus Ex was one of the first FPS games I had actually played and I grew up playing it, so much that I memorized most of the game from start to finish and tried various and uncountable amounts of playthroughs (sadly this was before I had steam, otherwise I would likely have over 5k or 10k hours in the game).
But that is besides the point; it was rich in story/lore, the freedom of choice and the way you wished to handle it was what made the game an absolute beauty. It was definitely worth playing and I would still reccommend people to play that one first before any other game of this series.
We all know that Eidos made some mistakes with Invisible War and it didn't live up to it's predecessor, however the story behind that one was also thick and unique (not to mention the experimentation of a new engine, if I'm not mistaken). Either way, the game was good in my book despite how much people disliked it for whatever reason that may be.
Deus Ex Human Revolution came around, to someone who is a fan of the series I was shocked with joy. The wait was well worth it, the 8 years waiting for a new game was well worth it. It was mocked no doubt with the "Saving Tong" DLC, though this was a bit minor and wasn't really a huge issue except filling in a small blank spot in the story.
((Review)) Finally Mankind Divided came along, when the game first came out I was extremely hyped as I had been wanting to play this game for the longest period of time since it's initial debut. When I found out that it was extremely graphically intensive and that it was poorly optimized my hype started to wither a bit. I was afraid that I would not be able to play this game at all, let alone at at any quality.
Funny enough even at low the game still maintains a good basic quality (if you can even believe me). I'm aware that people have to turn off MSAA and all that junk to get some frames, and yes people have ranted about it too, even I would if I wasn't smart enough
What really kicked the bucket was the fact that the content that you got, the "Storage" that people will notice when they open the inventory is that you cannot use those items once you start a whole new game or playthrough. Once you pull it out of your inventory, it's gone, POOF! What they are doing is implementing a similar thing that Diablo did (if I can legally bring that up), with the non-stop constantly online single player. That is exactly what's going on in this game. You cannot access items if any of them while you are offline, this would be infuriating to anyone in the fanbase let alone only able to use the item once via pulling it from the storage (and never being able to put anything -in-).
People forgot that, or did not write as much about it since from reading other reviews others were focused on the little microtransaction market in the main menu. I can understand from a perspective that people would be upset with this; it ruins the hard grind that people worked for to progress in the game. From a marketing perspective it probably did seem smart on paper or may have worked in the past, however it's a smack across the face to the community as a whole.
The storyline for Mankind Divided is extremely thick and vast and I love every moment of it. Al-though the game is extremely negative in mostly any other way, with not only non-augmented people but even aug's as well hate your guts. From being called a hanzer, to a clank to even a wrench this game shows a great hatred towards a very specific type of people and all you can do and wonder as a player is "how can I fix this or make it better?". I would be worried about people with emotional instabilities when it comes to playing this game and would recommend breaks and to play other things in-between sessions.
Besides that the storyline is vastly thick and your choices do have a huge impact early on and mid-way through the game. I feel like the consequences of killing is far greater than knocking someone out, sadly some portions of the game you cannot get such a good "outcome" by doing either or (not really spoilers).
I absolutely love the customization aspect and the various types of ammunition, it's a bit of a shame that I cannot equip a silencer on something like the battle rifle or the revolver. The upgrading and messing with weapons could be worked on more, but I find it interestingt and acceptable to play around with.
Through it all I am openly willing to give this game some time to work on it's bugs, fixes, glitches and see if they implement or work on more stuff to overall improve the game. I would definitely recommend getting this game, if not at-least give the game a month's time to work out the kinks and bugs and further optimization graphically.

As with many other reviews I recommend playing Human Revolution first before you play this game so you can get more of the back story. It does have a video at the beginning of the game that will catch you up on the story if you have not played the other game yet.
Let me start by addressing some of the issues I had playing this game so far, the first thing I noticed when I started playing was the out of sync lip movements to audio. It can get a bit annoying when you see someone talking and have to wait for the audio to catch up with the movements. another issue I had was at one point in the game I was spotted and everyone went into alert status. This is usually not a problem, just hide and eventually that status will go away and you can continue sneaking around. After 10 minutes of hiding in a hidden room away from everyone the status never went back to normal. Eventually I just gave up and let the massacre begin. The last issue I had was related to performance, this may not necessarily be a game problem but as of yet, AMD has yet to release a game driver that may or may not address the sudden frame rate drops. I am running a i7-3930k, 32gb ram, and a FURY X and am able to run on very high with msaa turned off and most of the time I’m at 60fps+ with a few drops down to the low 50’s upper 40’s. I am sure this will improve with time and am looking forward to the DX12 update.
Now for the positive, this game is loaded with places to explore and plenty of content with more to come if you buy the DLC. I have 29 hours into this game so far and I believe I’m about ¾ of the way finished. This is doing most of the side missions and jumping between being a pacifist and going terminator on certain groups of people. The amount of choices is quite refreshing compared to most games where they just force you down a single path. Your actions and the way you handle conversations can completely change a situation. The story is great so far and complements Human Revolution really well. This is truly a great sequel to the other games and I really hope they do more of these.
I’m not a professional reviewer but I would give this game an 8 out of 10. With a bit more polish that could easily go up.

Very fun, addicting game. I've played for more than 200 hours and still keep getting back into it.
This game has more RPG elements than my second favorite Empires game, Samurai Warriors Empires 2.
GAMEPLAY 8/10
You play as an officer instead of a force.
As a free officer, you can take on quests, raise relationships with other officers or form a vagabond unit and join battles.
If you join a force, you have to work your way up from Lieutenant -> Officer -> Prefect -> Marshal / Strategist and maybe Ruler.
You do that by raising your Merits (exp) either through battles or completing objectives.
In battle, you can choose up to 4 objectives to get more Merits (like defeating a number of officers or taking a specific base).
Outside of battle, you can choose from a list of objectives like Forming a alliance or Raiding an area.
As a Marshal / Strategist, your Ruler may offer to step down and leave you in charge, or you have the option to rebel and take the country for yourself.
Battles are typical DW 1-against-1000 hack n slash, you take over bases to create a supply line from your bases to the enemy's main base and then take over their main base or defeat their commander. If you're the commander you can give orders like Attack, Defend... or give individual orders to each officer which is nice.
There's a Way Of Life system that changes your title according to the way you play. So for example if you donate money to the people then you may get Benevolent Ruler, if you use tactics like Rumors, Alienate then you may get Wiley Tactician.
But it seems to me that this affects other officers more than your own so I don't really care about it.
This game is best played with a controller but it still shows the keyboard keys on the game interface, so it's annoying to figure out which key corresponds to which button.
SOUND 5/10
Decent, typical DW rock guitar music in battle. Japanese voices.
GRAPHICS 6/10
Decent. Unique officers have good models but models for Created / Generic officers are low res. Battlefields are bland.
STORY 6/10
Each scenario has a unique battle from the book but that's it.
Familial relationships are not recognized so you may get a request to swear a brotherhood oath from your dad :)
You can get married and have a kid. Your kid's appearance is generated using the parents' appearances and he/she will grow up and join your force.
REPLAYABILITY 9/10
There're 5 scenarios and so many officers (unique and generic) to choose from.
You can choose to play as a mere Lieutenant / Officer and follow orders, or as a Prefect to be in charge of a city, or a Marshal / Strategist / Ruler if you're ambitious.
You can also create characters and scenarios or download them from other players. You can replace a generic officer with a created one, so if you feel like Hua Xiong needs a unique model and a different moveset, you can do that.
The biggest disappointment to me is the endings (or ending, since they're all the same). No matter how you played, the ending will be you walking with your officers, say 1-2 lines about uniting and then some flashbacks of the scenes that you saw during the game, that's it.
SW2E's endings were much better.
If there were more endings, the replayability would be 10/10.
OVERALL 9/10
If you like DW with light RPG elements, and like playing as an officer instead of a force, you'll like this game.

if you have played any of the games on console you will recognise the game. that said, it is different to previous empires games i have played - there is more depth, things you need to do other than recruit/defend/invade/threaten/ally. i like the added depth. setting up the screen mode was trial and error plus google and steam guide - i dont know why they put 2 separate screen size settings but i kept selecting 1920x1080/1920x1200 by mistake resulting in the game launching in my laptop at 640x480 or something - i had to select the setting above (1920x1080/1920x1080).
lack of english voice acting makes it sound odd, but the subtitles and menus are mainly fairly clear. i had to google for things like how exactly to set up the controller buttons with xbox one controller like i am used to and it still reverses the western use of X/A and O/B on ps/xbox controllers for menus - apparently using O for ok is a ps japan thing, with x being cancel. once i got used to that, and found a ps4 online manual for the game i could set up the controller buttons properly. i guessed which i should use on xbox one controller for the touch pad on the ps4 controller. otherwise the buttons are pretty easy if you have dw8 xl complete - once i remembered the buttons for the xbox 360 game dw 6 empires it is logical. if you remember guard being L1/LB then the next setting is going to be L2/LT and so on. there are some guides also on how to. this game handles an already assigned button better than DW8XL did - didnt have to unassign all buttons first.
one word of warning - stop whatever you are doing if you own the games and win 10 and go right now to settings, type control panel in the search box and in control panel go into ease of access and find the keyboard sticky keys setting, SETUP STICK KEYS, go into that and uncheck the bit that enables them if you press shift 5 times or hold it down for 8 seconds. i just lost 4 hours play because the stupid win 10 popup grabbed focus and took me out of the game. alt tab seemed to be fine, but that popup caused some fixed graphic as if i was starting a new game and chosing a kingdom to come up and freeze the game so i had to quit it by closing from task bar.
the added features and depth make it very different in many ways from previous empires games like SW2 empires or DW6 empires. thats unusual - normally they dont change much except the maps and adding more playable officers (taking generic ones like Xu Shu was in DW5 for example and making them a unique weapon and outfit and a story mode). i am enjoying it besides the problems. im glad i bought them while on sale. if you liked the series previous games i think you will like this one despite the strange japanese voices (the men as usual sound like they are 20 pretending to be 40 years old putting on a deep gruff voice).

I don't think this is a great game or the worst game ever. I think more work could be put into it for sure, but here goes. If you're looking for a quick and easy clicker/idler then it's worth a play. I don't agree with the prices for the entire DLC which is $78 USD total with a 15% discount on each of them. You can play this game for a bit, but don't expect a lot to come from it.
Pros:
+ Decent sound effects and music although repetitive.
+ For a clicker/idle game it's not too bad.
+ Easy to understand.
+ The game is fairly playable without paying money, but not if you want it to continue while your game is closed.
+ You get heroes and Gods to help you out quickly.
+ You can get weapons to increase your heroes damage.
+ You don't have to restart the game to use the Wood Souls, you can use them immediately (not sure what the point of restarting is).
+ Souls are used to evolve heroes and boost skills.
+ There's an online leaderboard you can see where others have went up to on stages.
Cons:
+ I think the heroes and Gods come too quickly and you don't see any more for a while (if ever?)
+ DLC is quite costly and getting all DLC is 1 achievement.
+ The only way to idle and  get currency without the game open is to pay for one of the DLC's.
+ Each hero has a stamina bar for attacking which you can get rid of by paying real money.
+ Aside from at least 4 of the heroes looking like a copyright in their own, they all look like a p3n1s. I think some more time could have went towards their appearance.
+ 1920 x 1080 resolution for window mode isn't properly adjusted completely. It's just slightly off. Enough to play, but bugs me just a bit.
+ Needs more content, reduced DLC prices, some DLC shouldn't have to pay for and should be part of the game and other adjustments and additions.

So first off I absolutley reccomened this game to any fan of RWBY. Even if you know nothing about the show but just want a fun third person action game then give this a shot. Now on to why I enjoy it.
Aside from the awesome experience of fighting Grimm as some of my favorite characters the action is solid. Its smooth, responsive, and the combos are fairlly easy to pull off. My only gripe is that the double light then heavy attack combo is obviously the best. There isnt really a point of using any other. The Ultimates on the other hand are all effective and the branching upgrades add satisfying variations to combat and teams. Speaking of upgrades, each character has an upgrade tree to use points accquired from leveling up. There is only room for slight variations but they differ enough that I don't consider the limited amount an issue. I do however hope that they bring some kind of reward for prestiging your characters, as of now all you get is an emblem next to your name.
There are a total of eight characters in the game, four in the base and four included in a DLC pack. While it may not look it, there is some stratigic typing amongst them. If you want a more supportive role then Weiss and Jaune are they way to go. Want to pack a punch? Then run with Yang. Speed and AOE, choose Ruby. Now as for some characters being included in DLC, I believe this is a fine use of DLC. The pack comes with a whole team, four characters, and they each bring their own unique spin to the game. For only five dollars it's a fair trade.
Story is a little on the lacking side but i enjoyed it all the same. It brought some interesting new elements to the world of RWBY that I wouldn't mind seeing in the show. The levels themselves are fun although very repetative with four or so open areas filled with enemys to kill, segmented by small corridors to traverse and collect hidden xp items. The recent edition of a horde mode was a nice touch and lets you show off your fully leveled charaters strenghts.
The game revieves fairly frequent updates ranging from bug fixes to enitre UI, and gameplay changes. Over my time owning and playing the game, which I bought back in it's early access days, I have noticed that the devs truely do seem to listen to their base and act quickly to effect any negative major changes or bugs.
Overall I highly recommend this game to RWBY and action fans alike. Its a great play and I look forward to whats added later on.

I really enjoyed playing this game. I truly did. I played the hell out of the campaign, and had a lot of fun doing heists and racing with randoms online. It's just a damn shame that Take 2 and Rockstar decide to become greedier than ever before and ban any and all modding of the game. I feel that modding is an essential part of PC gaming in general; it lets the more passionate fans of video games take what they love and craft it into something that makes their game more unique, more optimized, and more improved. Mods let the users make the game theirs. It lets users play the game they want to play.
Ultra HD Graphics and Optimization? Sure, let's make the game look better and run nicer.
Custom maps and campaigns? Yeah, I'll try something new.
Turn my character into Sonic the Hedgehog? ♥♥♥♥ it, why not.
Mods make the game yours, and more importantly, they add to the game's longevity. Thanks to the modding community, games like the original DooM and DooM II, released
, are still relatively active today thanks to players who dedicate their time to create custom map packs, weapon mods, multiplayer game modes, and full-fledged total conversions. Giving players the creative power to take your game and make something that you would have never thought to make is fundamental in keeping the game fresh and fun to play. It's a goddamn shame that Rockstar and Take Two are destroying the reputation of arguably their best-selling game ever by preventing their most passionate customers and fans from changing the game into something new, possibly better. I feel that Rockstar and Take Two are shooting themselves in the foot with a nuke, and it's already starting to show, at least in the overall feedback. At the time of writing, Recent Reviews are Overwhemingly Negative and the Overall Reviews are Mixed. In time, I hope they realize that stripping one of the most appealing aspects of PC gaming isn't the way to go. Unfortunately, I'm not holding my breath. Unless the stars align and they reverse their decision, I will make an effort to stop supporting any and all games from either of these companies.

I had been enjoying my experience, making my way through the campaign. I had thought the lack of music a bit odd, but apperently it is "atmospheric." I was on the first mission of chapter two, when one of my marines deployed on the far side of the map and I had to keep him alive. The rest of the squad met up with him, as I crushed wave after wave of tyranid bolt catchers. I moved one of my marines onto a bridge, next to another marine, to grant more covering fire. The marine seemingly teleported to the spot that I had moved him, and showed he still had an action despite taking all four moves.
After this, the game would not respond. The other marines had taken their actions already, so no way to command them. Just a marine who claimed to have one action left, who was also not responding to any commands. The end turn button would not pop up, escape would not work, enter, and space would not work. I did not want to lose the progress made on the mission, but I was left with no choice but to leave and restart.
That is when the game hit me with an over costly fine. I had 1k to 2k experience on each marine because I needed around 3k to get the next skill point. Leaving the game wiped out all of their experience that had been saved up, which was one to two missions worth. I went to the steam forums, to see why there would be such a heavy fine. What I found was post after post of people compaining about the bug I had encountered and how the developers had effectively abandoned the game after launch. This game has been out for months and still has game stalling bugs. Development decisions make those bugs game breaking. I do not recommend this game to anyone, even during a steam sale.

A damn good strategy game. Very much like starship troopers kind of setting.
A mix of RTS and Tower defense games.
Basically you have lots of alien bugs coming to you from all sides and you have to defend your bases against them. At the same time you get some Marines to go clear out the nests and capture bases to get more resource points which you can spend on builds/upgrades (weapons, support items, etc), and defenses/buildings.
The difficulty increases as you capture more bases through the mechanics of the enemy obtaining abilities ("mutations").
There are variations in missions available in the campaign. While ideally you want to capture all the bases in a mission, there are various objectives that are cruicial to the difficulty of the game. One example would be protecting a convoy so that you can get resources to build, instead of the usual means of capturing bases.
The difficulty increases as you advance in the campaign.
Also:
1) Random missions (maps are also randomized), which are available to earn money, which you can use to unlock weapons and other upgrades to be made available in missions.
2) Skirmish mode against the aliens.
I'm in love, this game is a ton of fun.

A very interesting take on the real time strategy genre, Infested Planet eschews the building of extensive bases and farming of resources to speed up the maps into small, 5 - 10 minute frantic bursts of action. You have six marines to control and they are all the units you get. As you progress you unlock air strikes, new weapons and buffs, and defensive turrets to build. In the first couple of maps, it's very simple: Find the enemy and shoot it. Once you have some missions under your belt and the game starts to alter the rules on you, battles become chaotic, and desperate, contests of survival.
There is surprising depth here, and the game has random maps to keep things interesting. There is no multiplayer option, but for a something that doesn't require a large time (or money) investment, Infested Planet serves well as a quick fix for fans of rapidly played real time strategy games.

Very inventive controls and really great worldbuilding. The environments were all really beautiful and interesting and the way you move through them was surprising throughout.
I wasn't as emotionally invested as some people seem to have been, but the story works nonetheless and the controls and environments were enough to leave me with a very positive impression of the game. The game becomes increasingly surreal as you progress through it, and it made the world this takes place in really interesting. I would absolutely love to get more background information about some of the things I saw in the game.
The great thing is that the game doesn't tell you anything through text or dialogue. The dialogue that's there is all in a made-up language, and there's nothing to read. Instead, the game SHOWS everything and it does a very good job at that. Everything is clear enough to get from A to B and solve the puzzles without many problems, but vague enough to remain mysterious.
The controls are also a pretty good point about the game. A controller is basically a must. Each brother is controlled by one of the analogue sticks, and each has an interact-button. You control both brothers at the same time, and... it just works really well. All the puzzles are easy enough to grasp within a few seconds but still require some finesse to get right. Even so, the game isn't really about the puzzles so much as about the story and the two brothers from the title.
The game takes about 3 hours to complete, perhaps a bit longer if you try to get all the achievements, which are basically just tiny extra bits of story that can be really good in their own right.
I would definitely recommend this. It's not a game you can sink countless hours in, but it's definitely worth the trouble of picking up and playing through at least once.

I think at this point, my time invested speaks enough about my opinion of the game itself.  It's closely monitored, patched frequently, upholds good free-to-play practices, and the developers are all-around great people.  The combat is finely tuned, the netcode is wonderful, the matchmaking is fast (if a little silly in terms of skill sometimes), it's built from the ground up to support keyboard + mouse and game controllers, and there's no pay-2-win at all.  If you're even slightly considering giving this a try, you should download it immediately and hopefully get hooked.
The only real issues are that after a couple hundred hours, it's getting a little stale.  Lately the focus has been on the e-sports environment when I really feel that more content, and more fleshed out content would make it much better for everyone involved.  The characters are pretty much vehicles for different weapon combinations with a few unique attacks in there (their "sigs", or signature attacks).  They don't have any voice lines, all the light attacks are the exact same, and their animations are all identical aside from their sigs.  The maps are pretty boring, again focusing on flat fairness instead of creativity aside from like one map that is asymmetrical, and they don't release maps very quickly at all.  The graphics themselves work fine, but there's also much to be desired in terms of creativity and flair on the stages and backgrounds
I suppose instead of rambling on about little things, it's easier to sum it up by saying this: in about a year and a half, there has been much progress, but a lot of it has been very "safe" progress.  Little tweaks to combat week by week, but nothing really exciting aside from 2 new weapons.  Mostly skins, color swaps, and non-stop frame tweaks.
But trust me.  The first 500 hours?  Positively awesome and exciting.  It still is, but there's still so much room for improvement.

Still, I never would have thought that a sequel was going to animate my screen and I couldn’t have been more wrong about it.  Trine 2 is here, I’ve played it and, since I’m a hard-working guy, here’s a very meticulous review.
Same as the first game, the three heroes, The Wiseman, The Knight and The Thief…pardon me, I meant The “Inventive woman” are united by a magical artifact called The Trine, whose goal is to protect the land from a new threat. Therefore, the inevitable goblin infestation. So, the three characters are up for a new adventure which, unlike the first game, takes a little longer time to play.
In a very bizarre way, Trine 2 makes me think of Terry Pratcher’s novels, maybe because of its strange atmosphere that I picked up by reading this author’s books. The Universe presented in this title is so subtle that you can only be overwhelmed with its complexity. Even if it is an Indie game that we are talking about, the narrative value can not be ignored since this time, the characters are better shaped by their developers, humanized I might say, from the voiceover’s point of view as well as from the action’s point of view. I will even go further and say that Trine 2 offers a very pleasant story for all ages, even if it’s a 12+ game, precisely because the narration has something to offer to everyone. Nostalgic to say at least! Still, there are some missing bricks to this wall. The key of this story is nice indeed, but the main problem is the poor narrative construction. I think everybody would have been happier if someone would have added some solid touches to this aspect. The motivations are clear, meaning that the land is full of goblins, but the story as a whole concept could have been more complex. Who knows, maybe Trine 3 will surprise me when the time comes.
The three key-elements that a player must take into consideration when starting this game are : cooperation, cleverness and physics. These elements are as important as the three main characters. Even if, on a regular basis, Trine 2 is a platformer, these elements are very necessary while dealing with a certain level. At the beginning of the game, there is a tutorial to teach you what every character can do. The Wiseman, because he is your starting point, is not the every-day Gandalf that everyone got used to. He is more of a clumsy magician for he has no idea what a fire ball really is. Still, he has his own tips and tricks, he can make objects appear from nowhere, such as boxes, or even make them levitate to get to certain locations.
The Knight, on the other hand, is the muscled genius among the three characters. Even if he’s not very bright, he’s compensating by his strength, also being the best choice when it comes to a one on one fight with your enemies. Equipped with a shield, a hammer and a sword, he’s the defensive one of the trio. Last but not least, The Thief. And no, you’re not going to break chains or sneak behind your enemies, because her abilities are more rogue-like.
She has a hook to reach to certain points otherwise inaccessible and an elastic loop to fight at the distance. What’s truly interesting and new is the way you switch between these characters to complete a level. The puzzles are sometimes so twisted that they really work your cleverness off! But that doesn’t mean there’s only one way to deal with a puzzle. Frozenbyte finally made it with this platformer: the experience is multidimensional, despite of its puzzle-platformer prejudices. To solve a certain puzzle, the player has at least three ways, which is pretty unexpected among the game mechanics that other developers use.
The characters’ control is absolutely beautiful. After pressing a key or a button if you’re playing on a controller, the task is immediately registered by your game. This is one of the most satisfying platformers I’ve played since Sonic Generations. No platformer fanatic could ever find a misstep concerning this aspect. The game control is perfect, I would say.
Trine 2 is not only made of twisted puzzles, but also of battle sequences and a handful of bosses every now and then. These fights are meant to break the monotony of a certain level, full of enigmas. Still, the gameplay is so rewarding that the player can use his characters’ abilities to knock down the enemies. And because something had to be done when it came to options, each hero has a set of five abilities that can be improved using the experience points you get. What I find extremely stressful is that some of the abilities you get using this tree are only necessary for a specific level. The player has to reassign some of his points in order to finish a portion of the puzzle. I must say that this procedure is free, so you don’t have to repeat anything to get more experience afterwards.
One of the major gains of this game is the cooperative multi-player, online and local, a huge step from the previous game and probably one of the reasons for which we strongly recommend a bundle. Two more players can be added to one session, each one of them being able to control in an active way one of the three characters, which makes the puzzles a lot easier, as far as I’m concerned. That being said, I must admit that I found myself playing this game even for the third time, just because it’s fun to find new ways to complete a level: a very nice move coming from Frozenbyte, although Zon@ thinks they should have done this from the beginning.
We are finally getting to graphics. Did I mention this is an Indie game that comes from a small studio where are working about 20 people? Well, Trine 2 is a masterpiece of beauty. Want to hear something more spectacular that this? The game engine has been totally reconstructed. The game not only that looks divine, but its physics is very accurate. From the well animated background to the small details , nothing has been left out. And everything is the work of a very small, but talented, team. I know it sounds like I’m trying to get under their skin, but I’m telling the truth. The animations, the flow, the light and all the other elements gave me the impression that I was watching a moving painting. The colours also made a huge impression on me, one I will not easily forget.
The sound itself is quite an experience. Not only that the narrative part is well represented on script, but the voices and the entire performance of the characters are as authentic as they could be. It sounds just like a very posh movie. The soundtrack is exactly what the game needed to complete the atmosphere: the way it highlights the key points of the game makes your blood rush and your adrenaline keep pumping which turns the whole experience into a sound feast.
Is Trine 2 a good game? I’ve been praising it a lot so yes, it is! It’s one of those games you have to play in order to find out what a creative genius really means. If the first game managed to get my attention, Trine 2 has upgraded to a very high standard among platformers.

I should also note that playing via a PS4 controller works just fine without any additional setup. Just make sure you plug it in before starting up the game; it doesn't seem able to detect adding a controller after that.

Back in the day Steam was what every gamer dreamed about: a centralized place to allow for non-mainstream games to exist and where patches/updates and valuable troubleshooting tips could easily be found.  So where do these negative ♥♥♥♥♥y gamers come from?  I have no idea.  I looked up some of my most favorite games and the first 10 reviews or so are all negative thumbs down from gamers who like the game and have 100 hours + in.  What the heck is that?
So now onto Warhammer Deathwatch.  The first set of negative reviews are from gamers who liked the game so much they bought both the tablet/mobile versions and the PC versions.  I have never heard of anyone buying 2 versions of the same game.  You're upset that the newer version didn't have the content you expected?  Really?  Any smart buyer would tell you to wait to see the content it had. Is it the be all and end all of all WH40K squad turn based games?  Maybe not but is it awesome and enjoyable?  Absolutely.  At first it seems like a very simple format with not much too it, but as the levels increase, your quest for cards becomes an addiction, and detailing your squad out with champions, heroes and new gear makes it a lovable format.   And what other squad turn based game set in WH40K are you going to play?  Get off it!
Some gripe its a cash grab?  Are you kidding me?  WH40K squad turn-based????  That is a niche of all gamers.  There's not many of us to cash grab from.  Not to mention the detail that went into this game is a labor of love.
Simply put its a good game that is very enjoyable.  What I like about it?  Very easy to learn and go through the missions.  So much so that when you beat the campaign it ups the difficulty, and I played through both upped difficulties.  Let's you play with many cool chapters and heroes.  Many customization options with a huge variety of weapons and leveling up options.  At the end of the day its addictive and fun.  Its not perfect but it is great value.
Worthy thoughts for improvement are:
-AI is dull, comes straight at you after spawning which is ultimately fine but sometimes it moves melee guys infront of shooters who then cant shoot.
-The card system is random meaning you could put a 100hrs in and never get the card (marine/gun/misc option) that you're looking for... totally agree with another reviewer requisition points should be used to unlock cards or a tech tree to work towards what card you want.  Though at the same point it does make it addictive to play through the campaign again at higher difficulties...
-the campaign is quite easy and short, maybe a 3 - 4 missions are tough.  On the next level of difficulty it gets a bit more challenging and on the last difficulty setting every mission becomes incredibly tactical where any miss step could mean the entire loss of your squad.  The quickness makes replay value very enjoyable as you give it a go with different squads
-if you're guy dies you only lose XP not a permanent death
-there should be different movement between regular squad members to assault marines to the devastator marines, they all have the same movement points and cover the same amount of squares.  Assault marines should have jump capabilities or cover more ground with their movement points.
-Devastator marines are weirdly balanced.  They have the heaviest guns which are great against big targets but require 2ap to fire when confronted with more targets they can easily get overwhelmed.  Does it make sense my devastator with his heavy bolter facing 4 small targets can only take out 2 if he hits?  Shouldn't he be able to take out all if they're in the line of fire?
-no real mission preview; would be nice to able to customize your team for the type of mission (you're only given a vague idea of the mission) and you cannot restart as quitting the mission ends in a defeat whereby you lose all XP for all characters
-you cannot reset the game to start again
All in all this is a fine turn based game for the price, nothing special but Iove it.  It has a lot of potential and if they start generating alot of DLCs then this can be one heck of a game.  We will have to see what comes of it.  Highly recommended if you're looking for a squad turn based game.

Empire Mode and the editors form the backbone of this game, but split screen co-op and Free Mode is also available. The Officer Editor has the most options, naturally inflated by the DLC. The other editors let you create troop uniforms, custom mounts, factions and flags, and even custom scenarios. The game also randomly pollonates each new game you play with "guest characters" gathered willy-nilly from all over Steam, or whatever system you play. You can also set the Officer Editor to randomly generate a character you can then polish into one you wanna play - initial results alternate between AMAZING, hilarious, and just plain wierd.
Empire Mode serves up different premade scenarios, including DLC; you'll find yourself playing the Gathering Of Heroes scenario most of the time, because it randomizes ALL the involved factions depending upon how you choose to start off. Play as a Ruler and swing a pretty big stick right off the bat; start off as a Free Officer, form a vagabond unit and raise your own flag, or bend your knee to somebody, and claw your way up the ranks.
It's one of the best birthday presents I got, but don't take my word for it alone. It's better to wait for a sale, or play Xtreme Legends - Complete Edition first.

Pretty straight-forward, and the fish do not relatively move a large distance, so you can expect the same cluster of fish to be hanging out in the same areas. Once you memorize their approximate locations, it becomes less of a random experience like how real-life fishing is, but becomes repetitive execution.
Can probably be improved. I had fun, I don't deny that, but at the price, I think other titles within the same genre offer a better experience than this one, albeit being unique.
Do yourself a favor and spend a few hours with this game and make sure to find all of the endings.

My first exeperience with this game was on the PS2. I bought it for a buck and heard it was really good. However on the PS2 the only thing I could seem to concentrate on were the really inaccurate controls that were so bad that the auto aim system simply made the game playable. Without the auto aim the game was impossible to play. So when I got into PC gaming I decided to pick this version up for 2 bucks because of mouse and keyboard controls. Well, mouse and keyboard didn't help me out as much as I thought they would which brings me to my first issue with this game. The enemies move abnormally fast which would be ok if they didn't take an absolute ton of bullets. They will take less if you shoot them in the head all the time but if you hit them anywhere else they are like sponges and alot of times your ammo supply does not allow for tons of sloppy shooting or body shots. Then there is this amazing story and unparalleled humor that everyone raves about in this game. It might have been something back in it's day, but it dramatically pales in comparison to a game like Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon. I played through the entire game and never had any laugh out loud moments.
Fortunately the game was not a complete waste. Halfway through the game you do get some much better and very well deserved weaponry that makes the already difficult game much more enjoyable as you are not horribly underpowered anymore. The game is still very challenging and you will die, but it will actually be fun instead of feeling so one sided. The end boss fight made you feel helpless and bored at the same time as you would get your♥♥♥♥♥handed to you until you discovered where to run and hide. Then it was so easy it was almost insulting. Overall if the first half of the game had been as balanced as the second half it may have been worth while. Just when I started having fun with the game it ended.

Red Faction is worth a buy if you're a fan of the later games in the series, and maybe haven't played the earlier ones.
This is the first installment in the RF series, and having played the later games I am glad to have played this and seen the origins of "Parker" and "Eos". The story is pretty good, although the game can make it a little hard to follow at times.
I have found that it can be easy to miss certain buttons that you need to properly complete the game, but overall the layout of levels and such is very good. The AI for enemies is pretty terrible, and increaing/decreasing the difficulty will basically speed up the strafe rate of enemies. You've probably experienced this before if you've ever played an old game.
Played using keyboard & mouse. No issues with controlling throughout the game.
Graphics are ok for the age of the game. Everything is ok until you start blowing the environment up, then things start to get a bit wierd.
Some of the parts of the OST are a bit too overly dramatic and loud, but most of it is pretty good. Very dramatic when needed and the base ambiance music is very nice. The sound quality is ok considering how old the game is.
Surprisingly, there are still some multiplayer servers out there running.
This game is a ngihtmare to get running initially (If you don't have DX8), but once you have everything set up it will work fine. The URL
will come in handy, and check out the forums & guides for more detail on how to get everything set up if you have issues.
To reiterate, definitely worth it if you are a fan of the series, but otherwise I wouldn't recommend getting it.

Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is one of the best games that has creative mechanics and uses the two-player co-op best.
A controller is NOT required to play, you can play with a friend using your keyboard. All the segments of the game make use of the two players and this is a huge achievement in the game design perspective. You should be playing the game because of that­, no questions asked.
As for the ending. (I'll keep it spoiler-free) a rule of thumb is to make the player feel like they made the situation better and give the player a feeling that they've done something rewarding. The ending of this game is the complete opposite. Not only you feel like you end up in the same situation as the beginning, I also almost felt like the final situation was worst.
I don't feel like I won something, I don't have any feeling of rewards. I just feel like I ran a marathon for 3 hours and then you get nothing from it at the finish line.
A touching story, intricate puzzles and a beautiful leveldesign lead to a game that is well worth it's money.

Played a lot, love KOEI, but frankly, this game is almost a scam.
- The gameplay is exactly the same as all dynasty warriors ever. They create a new character, a new weapon, some small and useless change on the mechanics, but those are clearly things that were added only for it to show something was added. Nothing relevant, you can pretty much play for weeks without using or noticing those "new mechanics"
- The "empires" part of the title, along with the advertising, are there to trick you into thinking there is some strategy or tactical aspect on this game. There is none, there is only a fake strategy aspect. You can pretty much play this game disregarding strategy at all and win just by mashing buttons.
- in the entirety of the game there is a clear feeling that KOEI picked up things they already had available and rushed to release in a way as to call a "new" game, without any considerations as to whether this game will be good or bad. All they wanted was to come with a finished product that would earn then some money while costing the less possible amount. In that regard, they must have been very successful.
Keep in mind: This very heavy review you are reading comes from a KOEI fan. That is how bad this game is.

DEATHWATCH - "A bunch of random marines with random guns and gear".
Bottomline is if you buy this its flaws will sooner rather than later kill the experience.
Do not buy this game unless it is under $5.00 at full price it is a money grab for a lazy port onto PC.
I have had some fun with this game, but its cost and design issues killed it for me.
It feels like a missed opportunity to make it into a good PC game. It is missing alot of normal options you would expect on a PC game. One thing that just bugs the hell out of me is not being able to start a new game. Sure you can replay the same levels again and again grinding gear and exp  or play the game on harder settings but start again from fresh nope. Sometimes people like the option just to start again.
The next major flaw in my opinion is the randomized rewards. It is so time consuming the amount of grinding you need to do plus the amount of luck you need to get the team of marines you want. Let alone getting them equiped with the weapons and gear you want. The system carries the hallmarks of its origin having been set up to encourage people to spend real money to get more random rewards cards than normal. The option to make purchases with real money has thankfully been removed but the random rewards remains. After 50 hours i still do not have a team or weapons close to what i want. I have replayed the same levels many times to get points for unlock cards only to get the same marine, weapon or piece of gear you dont want over and over. You end up hating the game instead of enjoying it.
These are just two things that majorly took away from the experience for me. There are more design issues you will come across if you buy this game that just bug you and your computer.

As an avid fan of Diablo 1 and Diablo 2, I was sorely disappointed by the gameplay and support put forth by Blizzard into Diablo 3. My search for a new hack 'n' slash RPG that I could sink my teeth into began. After sinking countless hours into games like Titan Quest (which was never fully completed and released with many bugs. Still recommended though!) a couple of former Diablo developers went and made Torchlight. The first game was great: well balanced, fun, hours of replayability...but it lacked multiplayer.
Torchlight 2 brings together all of the same great elements from the first release, and adds multiplayer and even more replayability with Steam Workshop's player created content! With four classes to choose from, multiple playthroughs, the ability to switch difficulty settings at any time, and high character leveling capabilities, you can literally spend weeks playing this game by yourself or with friends. My only complaint about this game is that the Embermage appears to be a bit overpowered (OP). However, if you're new to the Diablo-esque genre of hack 'n' slash, loot-♥♥♥♥♥ gaming then you may like the prospect of making things a bit easier on yourself in the early-game.
Ratings out of 8 bits: 1 bit = low, 8 bits = high.
Graphics:
. Although a bit dated by 2015 standards, the game's lush and colorful landscapes are almost as enticing as the myriad of color effects for spells and attacks. On many occassions I found myself snapping screenshots of exotic locales as if I were on vacation.
Sound:
. Coupled with the beautiful graphics of Torchlight 2 is an amazing soundtrack of intrigue with intermittent cries of enemies as they shatter and explode.
Story:
. Even though effort was put into this RPG to give it a compelling storyline, it felt forced and overused at times. The cutscenes were lower-budget than the gameplay, and, although using a different art style than Diablo, the story smacked of the Diablo storyline. Seeing the evil mage fleeing into the desert reminded me too much of the wanderer from Diablo 2 always moving East. I would have liked to have seen more of a unique storyline than just unique artwork for the cutscenes.
Gameplay:

. Although this title brings together everythings Diablo and Torchlight fans have come to love, I can't help but feel that not enough was done to separate this title as different than Diablo 2. I'm happy to say that this is totally playable on a MacBook Pro with the integrated Intel HD 5100 graphics or higher (running macOS Sierra). The minimum recommended hardware made me think it wouldn't even run, given that it only listed discrete graphics cards. (Sometimes games require features that integrated graphics cards don't have). But on lower settings, I can get around 30 frames per second at 1280x800, with occasional frame drops. It actually does run on high settings, but the frame rate is abysmal and only useful for gathering pretty screenshots. I haven't played enough of the game yet to really review it by content, but I figured folks might want to know what I was wondering—does it work on a MacBook with integrated graphics? While I can't speak for lower-grade graphics cards than what I have, I can say that at least for mine and probably higher, the answer is "yes." I should also note that playing via a PS4 controller works just fine without any additional setup. Just make sure you plug it in before starting up the game; it doesn't seem able to detect adding a controller after that.
