Being a huge fan of RWBY, this is one of the best Hack-and-Slash games I've ever played. There are 10 chapters in the campaign mode, that takes somewhere between 2-3 hours to beat without dying. It also has multiplayer, up to 4 people, for campaign mode. There is also horde mode, where you must survive 10 waves of Grimm and protect certain points of the map.
CONS:
-Few attack moves (although you can upgrade them).
-Very laggy if you don't have a good graphics card (laggy on Windows 7, but fine on my Windows 10).
-Fighting can get repititive (but I don't care, this game is so fun!)
-Only play as team RWBY unless you buy the JNPR addition pack.
PROS:
-The story is like a whole nother volume of RWBY that you control.
-Voice acting is great.
-Story is intriguing.
-You get to kick Grimm butt.
-Multiplayer makes the campaign more fun.
-Chat on multiplayer.
-Horde mode is a great fast way to pass the time.
This is all just my opinion. If you really enjoy RWBY, I suggest this. If you enjoy hack-and-slash games, I suggest this. Other than that, this game may not be for you.

This is my very first interactive e-book. I'm a bit suspect to say anything regarding this e-book (since I'm a crazy lover of the Portal series - and of Valve, their brilliant creators), but I loved this SO MUCH! I was honestly expecting more of a screenshots/pictures showcase and a few gadgets here and there with a little bit of text, but reading about each team and each developer of this game and the problems they've faced in this journey was an amazing experience. I always admired Valve products, even before falling in deep love with Portal, and I knew making games as part of such a huge (and world-class famous) company was a tough task, but I REALLY underestimated how complex the process of game creation could be.
I, as a starting game developer, always thought "I want to make my own company, recruit my own team, develop my own games and become a successful game developer". I always knew it would be hard, success isn't something you achieve in every dream. Then, after a couple years of small games and mods, a (now friend of mine) small developer invited me to participate in a small game development crew. It was so fun, and it still is (we're more active than ever!). I then thought "Maybe not only MY gaming company, but something shared between me and this small new team". Then I stopped focusing only on the games from Valve and started looking closer into it's developers and employees. I always heard a lot about Valve, about how their employees had a lot of freedom over their projects and such, and, although the idea was amusing at the time, I didn't "grow it". Working at Valve seemed not only like a far dream for a small gamer like me, but also not so much inviting, since, although Valve was a great company (it still is, but I had different opinions about it at the time), I never gave too much importance to any "future" involving directly me and Valve.
Then this book came up. I saw a bit of it, then wanted to buy it. It stood on my Steam wishlist for quite a long time, until another friend of mine (who was gifting me a lot of Steam games - dunno why) asked me if I wanted him to buy me "The Final Hours of Portal 2". I immedatelly said "No.", but not because I didn't want this e-book, but mostly because I didn't want to give him more reasons to spend money on me and because I wanted to buy it myself to have the "accomplishment" feeling. The same feeling I had when I had the chance of buying Portal 2 and playing it for the first time. It was amazing, the excitement and joy of trying something new. Then I bought it, just a couple days ago (pretty late compared to Portal 2's release, right?). I started reading it, it was amusing and fun. Then it started getting more interesting, pretty interesting, way more interesting, amazingly interesting. I finished reading today, but I also made sure of not doing ANYTHING ELSE in this computer. Today, all I did was read this e-book. And I don't regret even a bit. If I had known it was going to be this good, I'd have definitely spent more money on it. Totally worth every cent. I'd even say it was a bit unfairly cheap!
Now you might be asking: what does it have to do with what I said about starting my own company? Well, at the time, I dreamed of being the leader, the big boss behind great games, and I used to think that being an employee wouldn't cast too much light on myself. I know it sounds egotistical, but I just didn't want to be unnoticed. Today I am proud to say that I don't need that anymore. I may not be a great game developer today, Gabe Newell may not see this text I'm writing right now, I may not even get close to Valve's HQ anytime in my life time, but you can be sure of two things: first today Valve is my dream-company, and the only place I feel like I'd be 100% happy working on; second, if I ever have the wonderful chance of working there, I'll never let go of Gabe's legs. They'll have to prepare me a room, cause I wouldn't be leaving that building anytime soon!

Short review...
OVERALL SCORE: If there was a neutral recommendation I'd give it but as it stands... call it a 4.5 of 10. More if they fix the alarmingly common conflict with firewall and start up issues (if you are going to buy, read the full review) .
WHEN SHOULD YOU BUY? (even if you like it still): Maybe if it's on sale for 35% off or more, and if you're ready to address the issues getting it to play, and if you can't get the app store version (or just must have the Dark Angels or Black Templars)
In more detail...
I wanted to give this game a positive rating so deeply, I did. On the original portable version I absolutely would, however the PC version... it does more harm then good. What it adds, and yeah it is some neat stuff, doesn't replace the functional and game play issues created.
First off, and for many the most important note in this review, to get it playing many people (many, I keep using that word for a reason, check the forums here) have to flag it passed their firewall during install or after... and THEN still tell Steam to make sure to open it only in windowed mode. A game less than 4 years old that takes forum searching for TWO notable problems to get working, and then a few people still say they have issue, I like this companies games (they're fun at their core, that's a big plus!) but, that's tough to overlook. Yes I got it working but that sucks not everyone can.
Second, and this is more opinion, this game really benefitted from microtransactions. A small amount of them (<10$) were kind of core to convenient game play. They took those away in PC version, and while they added some stuff which true was kinda cool and bonus points for that, now the problem is it's ALREADY a 'grindy' game and having to wait longer for things you want (and occasionally need) made it grindier.
Particularly when you add in that you have to level your team it becomes problematic, grind on grind on grind problematic. When enough tier 3-4 marine cards don't drop you end up playing with guys you'll level only to have to remove and relevel later when better teammates drop. 3x grind is not a good transition.
On the portable version you could spend say 8$, and if you can't spend 8$ more on something you enjoy go back to the kiddie table because that's less than 1 drink at a decent bar with friends, and you'd be almost guaranteed that, along with the cards you earn through playing, by Act 2-4 you'd have a team that could really be your 'final' team if you so desired and the problem is solved... you could just PLAY.
In the current PC version? Bad luck can leave you at Act 7 (or more) knowing you're going to have to go back and level new guys still.
That's grind multiplied by grind multiplied by grind if the Golden Throne doesn't shine on your luck.
In short, without microtransactions, this game really needed a way to just spend points, even a lot of points, to directly buy higher level (at least Tier 3) cards. It did NOT have this and, by all accounts, will not be patched to have it.
To be clear, the PC enhanced edition isn't a crap product from a crap company... it's a slightly subpar adaptation of a good product from a good developer. The portable version is a 7.5-8 (or more) of 10, credit where that's due, and the PC version with a few fixes might one day be that. Let's hope.
I do also recommend checking out their Warhammer Quest game here on Steam. On the PC version it's actually IMPROVED over the portable version.
(Edited: Put the abbreviated scores first, split a block of text that was hard on the eyes, also called more attention to the firewall and windows mode issues which people who buy will probably need to know to play, and noted when it might be worth buying.)

The gameplay is actually pretty fun, and while pretty grindy, missions are decently quick and the upgrades to your units through skills/weapons do make them feel more powerful, like an upgrade should! The final nail in the coffin of WH40K: Deathwatch? The Devs have publicly abandoned this game. Thats right folks, these bugs are never getting fixed. Tablet gamer presents, another playable game on a tablet!
One of the classic hack and slash games in history that myself have personally grew up with.
The goods:
- Playable on a Surface Pro 4 (Musou/skills graphics and effects are blurred to compensate the resources demand)
- Customisation mode with not only character customisations, but also banners, animal mount/companions, your pawns etc with a wide range of selection to choose from.
- Marriage and kids :D (Though the kids grow up to adult age in just a few game months O.o)
- Be a Cao Cao the dictator, Liu Bei the benevolent, Sima Yi the traitor or Sun Qian the I-never-really-paid-attention-to as a ruler of your lands using any characters of your choice, alternatively play as a massive suck up and get promoted from being a pawn (Lieutenant they say) with the title system. (Let everyone remember who you were for generations to come with the God of War title!)
The meh:
- Replayability... that comes with a catch! (Things get really repetitive over time)
- Chaos mode is quite fun, though not very chaotic for a DW Veteran, otherwise hard and below are simply too easy for me. Though ultimate mode is a challenge, loved it.
- Cutscenes have different lines depending on your character/their voice tones, though cutscenes remain the same
- Local Co-Op (A function since forever ago on consoles, though keyboard controls are awkward)
The bad:
- Where's the death they promised me :( Why do generals flee or receive heavy injuries but can't kill them off unless I capture them, I wouldn't mind slaying Lu Bu a couple of times
- Stages are pretty similar to one another (Maps)
- Limited amount of strategies in the field
- 1 action per turn (I doubt your government only pass 1 act per month, let alone an absolute monarchy system)
- The gameplay mechanic hasn't changed by much since when it first came out
- Thus doesn't seem to worth the price tag unless it's on 50% off, and defs not worth selling separately from the Xtreme Legends edition
Overall the bad seems to outweight the good. I have been loyal to this game since playing DW2 when I was a kid. However it's starting to get to the point that it's no longer worth the bucks for the bang, would definitely hope DW9 is as good as TK advertised on Dec 2016.

Techland starts the series with the epic western mystery action adventure. Call of Jaurez draws you in to a world of hardship and torment that plagues the old west. In particularly how racism and corruption of the older days impacted the life of Billy Candle, a young man.
Call of Juarez is a Western style action game. The story is incredibly interesting, but honestly takes a while to get into. Call of Juarez is a western mystery surrounding the story of the gold of Juarez. The story surrounds the protagonist Billy Candle, a boy without a father, from the little town of Hope (an ironic name). Billy ends up being caught up in a mystery of whether he may or may not have murdered his parents. The death of Billy’s parents and the prejudice of the Hope forces Billy to go on the lamb. Reverend Ray, brother to Billy’s mother’s lover, hunts Billy for this crime. In order to start a new life Billy is set for Juarez, but will Reverend Ray catch him?
In the campaign you play both Billy and Ray throughout. Billy as he is on the lamb and the Reverend as he hunts him down. There are fifteen chapters to the game, and they only become longer as you progress further. Each chapter begins with a dialogue read either by Billy or Ray. The story is rather gripping, but I didn't start really caring much about the characters until about Chapter VII. The game has some levels that are incredibly long, while others than are very short. I would recommend saving a lot during the game as for me the Auto-Save feature did not work. What is most interesting is how the levels are designed; some of them are essentially open world while others are pathways. For an older game, 2006, the levels can be quite expansive and rather innovative. Some of these levels will require you to solve puzzles, other will require you to complete tasks, but most the time you will just be running and gunning like a madman.
Once you’ve mastered the basic mechanics of the game there is not much more too it. Billy Candle should always use the Bow and Arrow as it causes time to slow for him. While Reverend Ray should always quick draw as it causes time to slow for him. There are many different types of weapons, but you will notice that as the game progresses they are all essentially the same and pistols with quick reload are always the best bet. Rifles win over shotguns, because you will never be close to enemies that need a big dose of Lead (Pb). And on the incredibly rare occasion you find one, a scoped rifle is the best gun. The weapons break over time, so you will be constantly throwing away your guns and essentially selecting the same ones.  The movement is rather clunky, but for a 2006 title it does a good job. If you are interested in getting into Call of Juarez series (although I have not played Bound in Blood) Gunslinger is a completely different game with no references to the original. So you could start wherever you want and just work your way back to this one.
I beat this game on Medium Difficulty, but I would say I was really upset I couldn't play it on Hard Difficulty. I wanted to, but the first episode where you had to run away from the rain of bullets was essentially impossible, so because of that one annoying part I had to play the whole game on medium.
If you like Westerns, you can get past the mechanics/graphics of older generation games, and are interested in an epic adventure then this is the game for you. The game presents a lot of challenges, mystery, character development, open world environments, and combat. The game was incredibly easy and I never was really posed with a single challenge, although a lack of challenge just makes the game seem like a 80s action movie. Call of Jaurez is a fun game coupled with a fantastic campaign. I recommend Call of Jaurez, especially if you can get it for a good sale.

The hilarious thing here is that an energy system like that can work out if it's reset when you die or when the round ends because that way it is just a way to prevent fights from going on and on with runners trying to pick up heals.  However in the current system you take your energy with you to the next round so quite often you have people 1 hit killing the enemy team right at the start of a new round which is honestly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
Unfortunately this is not where it ends, to make matters even worse people that do good in a match get punished because if you kill people a few times they get a revenge buff which vastly increases their damage against you.

So yeah, no wonder the game is near dead this soon after release.  It's hilarious to see that random Gunz 1 private servers have more players on them than Gunz 2...maiet seriously dropped the ball.
Now does this mean I completely hate the game?  No not at all,  I like the fast gameplay and if I overlook the imbalance then I am even enjoying the classes. So just for the funny nostalgia concerning that bug I will raise the score of this game to a 3/10.

Graphics - 6/10 - Average - Nothing super special, special effects on lotto items and purchases are.. Alright. There's a mediocre customization set as well, but better than none.
Gameplay - 7.5/10* - A blaze~! Note*: The game is extremely fun, however the characters seem to be a little imbalanced. Too fun to pass up, even dying is kinda fun at times as you struggle. Campaign is null after a while, but exciting at first to get you up on your feet (To pvp).
Community - 8.25/10 - Spectacular~! The community is pretty cool actually, other games in it's category cannot even compare; However the community is quite small, queues can take long during non-peak hours, up to 8 minutes at one point of my hour half of gaming.
Customization - 4.5/10 - To me this is the biggest drawback to the game, there's no "RPG-Elements" to customize your character different than others(To suit you). There's not a large variety of accessories or additionals to give you a "Unique look". There's only 4-5 outfits per a character, and only 2 uniques in the lotto. That's about it - Even weapons seem a bit lacking.
Replayability 7.5/10 - The game's different characters/classes vary so much that everytime it's something different, each person brings a different build to the table, forever changing, and forever being different. However, it's a action hack and slash, or gun's blazing... However you have to gain skill to practice each character, and there's a steady of characters that take a while to level to max (To gain access to all skills).
Overall - Slightly Above Average (6.75).
However, if you play the game specifically just for the action, pick-it-up, skill based Rumble, this is it. Nothing get's better than this at it's rumble play if you disregard the customization and graphics, the game easily snags a easy a memorable 'Great Game' (7.75)

What a surprising little gem.
The mechanics are simple: just click to cast and hold to reel in!
The artwork, while almost elementary, is cute, clean, and consistent. It serves the purpose well; simple and cute artwork for a simple and cute game.
Despite the simplicity of the controls, there is actually a perfect amount of difficulty instituted here. You've got to craftily avoid smaller fish to get to the bigger ones, or combo the smaller ones as bait for larger and larger fish. The better the fish, the more money you get for them. Money is spent on an assortment of fishing rods, powerups for each rod, boats, and even extras like one-use bombs and larger hooks. The balance in the game seems perfect; even hours later, I'm still catching new fish and have only unlocked half the rods and boats and powerups, and I'm still getting new quests for bonus money.
Oh, and you can catch adorable hats for your cat to wear which give different bonuses!
The only thing I can't seem to find is an options menu, but the sounds and music are so unobtrusive that for most people it might not matter much.

As you might have guessed, this game is about fishing !
You are a cat, and your goal is to catch as many fish as possible. This is how you do : firstly, catch a small fish, then use it as a bait to catch a medium one, and finally use the new bait to catch a large fish. The challenge is there : getting the big fish (shark, maw, ...) is not a piece of cake !
You will be rewarded with money by selling fish and completing quests. With money, you can buy new rods (+ upgrades, 8 different kinds, choose wisely), some useful devices/items (rockets, bombs, ...) and boats that allow you to catch more kind of fish by navigating on the sea.
You will also find hats while fishing : you can only wear one, so choose wisely in order to get the bonus you want ! You cannot stock them, you can only keep the one that you are wearing. Tip : I think the best one to wear is the baseball cap, because being able to have two quests at the same time is great, especially if you are stuck with one, since you cannot drop it.
In the end, this game is simple but pretty fun, even though it is a little bit grindy if you want to unlock everything and get all of the achievements.

This game is truly awesome.
You start as a peasant (though having a male character with noble blood makes progression a bit easier) and work your way up to being king of your own faction, and eventually emperor of the whole land.
The thing I really like about this game is the flexibility of what role you want to play. Once you get a feel for the different kings and factions, it's usually pertinent to select a king for whom you will be a vassal. Want to help a faction become strong, building relationships with the troops, and help them crush a different faction or two, only to start siphoning off those troops for your own faction and rebel? Would you prefer taking the banner of a claimant to one of the factions and putting them on the throne of said faction? Perhaps you'd like to just be a successful mercenary until the political intrigue develops further? Much of the game's progression is a bit cerebral and imagined, so to speak (like a tabletop game). I don't think that is necessarily a bad thing.
The combat is interesting and quite fun to master. Protip: try to stay on your horse and kite them.
The different factions bring different troop trees to the table, each specialising in different things (archery, crossbows, large-shielded infantry, horse archery, heavily armored horses with polearms, etc) and you can build your army with combinations of these, and tell them what to do on the battlefield. For example, archers hold here on this hilltop, infantry charge.
The game is showing its age a bit, however that doesn't mean you should not play it.
My biggest criticism is it's grindy, but this can be mitigated by using mods, such as Diplovexed, which is my favorite vanilla mod (which gives you the added depth of the Diplomacy mod and Vexed's reduced grinding).
I -highly- recommend trying the Prophecy of Pendor mod, which is content-rich and still being updated (this is probably the best mod). If it had the diplomacy mod too it would truly be perfect, but I digress.
Also check out the battle size mod, letting you adjust how many units can be in the battle at once (units beyond that number come in reinforcement waves). I usually use about 1000 troops at once.
If you're not sure about this game but are somewhat interested I say definitely pick it up on a sale. It usually goes for something like six dollars. That's totally worth it.

There's an equation in the gaming industry that every developer seems to believe: popular genre A + popular genre b = awesome!  In practice, sometimes this is true (first person tower defense games are ok), but in the case of Call of Juarez, it simply leads to jumbled, subpar gameplay.
It's not even fair to say that Call of Juarez is a hybrid, it's basically two different games in the same shell tied together with a crappy story.  You could get much the same experience by playing a level of Thief, and then playing a level of Call of Duty.  Well, sort of, both of those games are much better designed than their respective segments in Call of Juarez.
Starting with the sneaky bits, in Call of Juarez there doesn't appear to be all that much actual sneaking.  Apparently to the developers, jumping out of windows is the same as sneaking, because you do that an awful lot.  Even if you do manage to sneak past your enemies, the game will just have them find you anyway at the next set piece.  Also, a hallmark of sneaking games is the relatively open level design and expectation that you'll find your own way around.  Call of Juarez thinks you're too stupid to handle open levels, so the everything is just linear with a couple of crate puzzles thrown in.
The shooting bits are hardly any better.  Every shooter has to have its AWESOME SHOOTER MECHANIC THAT NO ONE HAS EVER DONE BEFORE to differentiate itself, and in the case of Call of Juarez, it's a quickdraw mechanic.  In practice, this is sort of the wild west version of bullet time from Max Payne except for the fact that your character can't hit the broad side of a barn.  In most fpses I can crack off head shot after head shot, but the controls are so soft in this game that I'm lucky if I manage to shoot in the general direction of my foes.
There's not to say there aren't some cool things about this game.  For one, you play as a preacher for the shooty bits, and there's nothing cooler than a preacher with guns.

The gameplay is ok for the game (not great but not bad) but the coding is messy and even potentially dangerous to some GPU's. The game near always runs at 100 percent gpu load or at least close to it, pushing your temperature to ridiculous levels. I used to have an R9 280x and it almost melted it, reaching the 90c levels, which apparantly that card can handle but that can't be good for it.
I now have a GTX 1060, a more powerful yet much cooler and energy efficient card. My model is one of the coolest on the market, it runs other GPU intensive games at 60c. But this game with it's below average graphics has reached the highest temperature i've yet recorded on that otherwise cool running card. 69celcius at 100 percent load! I've tried to use third party softwares including nvidia control panel to force v-sync but to no avail. No program seems able to detect it.
Bottom line the game is badly coded, and potentially bad for your hardware. It's badly in need of a technical update which sadly is unlikely to ever happen. Give it a shot if you must but tread carefully, especially if your card has a big power draw and doesn't have the best in ventilation or fans.

since the early access the game has changed some things, however not its core mechanics.
and ever since i first played this game i've changed some of my thoughts about the game, how well does it fair right now as a smash alternative? lets find out.
imagine smash bros, but with less options (limited edge guarding,no special moves,grabs,shields,short hops)
now immagine that most of those options go into the recovery of the character.
with that, you get brawlhalla.
originally i thought the idea was pretty lame, the action would be set at a snail's pace, with everyone having unnecesarily high peaks,incredibly laggy moves and few options when it comes to fighting.
however the game tries to work around this giving each character 2 weapons, specifically for creating balance and diversity in the cast, some weapons have safer recoveries, others have more knockback on aerials, others have spikes and so on, lastly and as i mentioned before.
characters tend to have attacks that for the trained eye might look very suceptible, slow and in general just aweful, its because of 2 reasons.
1: because its designed to be a "simplified smash" with more managable frame data instead of moves that come out on frame 1,have an invincibility frame and can be canceled...for whomever gets that joke then i'll asure you, its to avoid moves like that being in the game. (the most op moves you'll find are pressure/kill moves which are countered fairly easily)
2: these moves, not only are your kill moves, they can be used in the air.
now this may look dumb but you need to be under these circumstances to use a kill move in the air, first off you need to save your spot dodge in the air before using one, next, you can't use more than 1 every time you go into the air, lastly you can only input the kill move during a spotdodge, and it cannot be charged.
what this means for you is that you can use your kill moves for edgeguarding, it can kill very early but its far more risky than just using your aerials.
my veredict for this is that its pretty fun, it feels distinct, responsive and can get pretty tense at times.
since this is a multiplayer game, the biggest focus is its gameplay, and thus a dedicated section for this one, however its not going to determine the quality of the entire product, so i present to you a list of pros and cons.
+the character designs are nice looking, although the theme is valhalla there are many character themes in this game, its a nice mix of ci-fi and medieval roots...atleast to mention a few.
+although the chibi artstyle is kinda hard for the eye, both the backgrounds and animations make justice to the game's presentation.
+matchmaking is overwhelmingly fast, the max time i had to wait untill i found a match was of 30 seconds. wow, aside from that, 9 times out of 10 i found someone around my skill level so the system will surely queue you against players of your skill level.
+the developers are very nice people, when i first wrote my review, i got a very civil and chill response from them. (<3)
+the soundtrack is nice, although not extremely memorable, it sets the tone fairly well.
+the game balance is pretty good, since all the characters have 2 weapons, they always have similar matchups, its similar to the rock papers sissor formula, meaning every weapon is good at beating something, and another weapon is good at beating the first one and so on.
+its a fighting game that's properly optimised for keyboard, nice job.
+atleast 50% of the playerbase isn't an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
-atleast 50% of the playerbase is an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, its even, but you are going to find some salt.
-although the balance is good its at the cost of every weapon having similar tilts, you might feel weird switching to a new character, only to find out this one also uses an axe, the difference being the kill moves it has, but not the frame data on the normal moves.
-you may find problems mapping 3rd party controlers, although it supports plug and play it isn't perfect, personally i've gotten used to it, which was fairly easy but its still a bad thing to have such issues, the main problem seems to be that not every button gets recognised by the controler, again, the game is optimised for keyboard play but still.
in the end you might enjoy brawlhalla if you like smash, fighting games or are just have never played smash before and are looking for an alternative.

Goddamned I wish I could give this game a positive review but Square Enix ruined it.
The atmopshere is great, DE:HR did a good job on portraying Detroit and Hengsha and DE:MD did an even better job at creating a believeable city of Prague. The difference between AUGS and normal human's is also quite believable. If you like the big corporation/Illuminati theme of Deus Ex you surely won't be dissapointed.
Ways of playing, there are several ways to play this game. My first approach was complete stealth and pacifist. I completed the game without to much trouble on the hardest difficulty (I didn't ask for this was not unlocked yet). I have also heard of people playing this game guns blazing and they had a great time as well.
Level design, level design has always been absolutely great in the Deus Ex franchise but Mankind Divided nailed it. There are a lot of ways you can complete levels (hacking, vents, disabling security, secret area's, elevators, other ways of reaching your objective by the use of augments; think breakable walls, jumping high, hacking lvl 5 etc). I think that level design is the best ive seen in years so that is admirable.
Diversity of missions, there is a wide array of different missions which are all different. Some missions are better than others but I liked the missions as a whole.
Lets start of with the obvious, the pre-order fiesta. There is just no excuse for the slap in the face you got for pre-ordering this game. Items you can use once, a in game shop, a half hour "extra" mission?
Performance, I run a pretty good setup but some area's in the game had stutters and didnt run all that smoothly. Secondly the loading times are so long you can get a cup of coffee at your nearest coffeeshop and be back before it has loaded (train station travel primarily).
Lip-sync, the lip syncing is just plain bad it is so bad that it kills the atmosphere. In one part of the game Miller seemed like some sort of ragdoll which really reminded me it is a videogame I was playing.
The ending is so bad. I was taken by surprise by the sudden end and non-DeusEx ending we got with this game. I felt like I was approaching the second half of the game when suddenly "You have unlocked NewGame+" popped up in my screen. Square Enix really screwed us over with this abrubt ending of this game.
This game could have been a 9.5/10 experience if the ending wasn't such a major failure. It felt like I bought 50% of a game. The atmosphere was great and it was truly a Deus Ex game but the several negative aspects of this game leave me with a 7/10 for the game and a 0/10 for Square Enix.

(March 24, 2016) OK, so literally 2 days after I complain about the serious lag, the devs release a new update with servers localized to your geographical area (I'm US West, for example). And that severely reduced lag. I'm happy to once again say I can fully recommend this game!
TL;DR: Game is SUPER laggy in its current state (March 22, 2016), to the point of being nearly unplayable sometimes. And no, it's not my computer; this game is not graphically intensive and I always get 60 FPS even when it's lag-hopping my character off of cliffs for me.
Below this is my old review. Honestly, this is an awesome game. It's one of my favorite. It has casual brawler fighting, and competitive fighting, which is awesome for the reasons I outlined below in my original review. However, recently the lag has become unbearable. Like, I lose matches most of the time because the game changes where I am due to lag. One second I'll be on a platform, and then the next second I'm falling off the stage to my death... and losing the match. It's not such a big deal in casual; stuff like that happens. But in competitive, it's KIND OF A BIG DEAL to lose more than 50% of my matches because of lag! This game is highly popular; I've recommended it to all my friends in the past, and most of them play it, some more regularly than me. I know it's free to play, and I know it's beta, and I love the game, but... it's unplayable in its current, ultra-laggy state. The devs need to invest in more servers or software updates that will fix this problem. If they do (and I'll be checking every week or so), then I'll gladly change my review to recommend the game, but... de-ranking in competitive because of lag-related complications? It's unacceptable.
I'm still relatively new to this game, but I love it already. I used to play Super Smash Bros Brawl with my brother on our Wii, and this very much reminds me of that.
Since I know my own writing style, here's a TL;DR version: It's a good game. Get it, get your friends to get it, tell them to get their friends to get it, etc. After all, it's free. There are some problems; spammers, lag, and not much of an intro to the game, but all in all, it's a REALLY strong game. And it's still in Beta! Support it and it'll no doubt become even better!
But here, let's start off with an in-depth analysis of the game that I've experienced so far. I say it like that because I've only played casual so far; I have no experience with how comp works.
The cons (so I can finish with the pros):
-I've read a bunch of the other reviews here, and I have to agree with a few points they make. The player base seems to be split into 3 groups.
-Skilled players. They're generally pretty good sports, but they're good; they will rek you, but they won't (for the most part) tell you how much you suck, or call you a noob. I want to belong to this group; I think I'm generally not a jerk, but I'm probably not that skilled (yet, heh).
-Poor-sport spammers. They're kind of the opposite of the above; they're NOT good sports, but if they manage to beat you by spamming the same heavy charge-up attacks (over, and over, and OVER again), they will be jerks about it afterward in the chat.
-And the noobs. Brawlhalla has a rapidly growing player base, so this is to be expected; I probably am still somewhat of a noob myself, to be honest. But I don't have a problem with noobs, really; sure, they don't really know much about the game, but they're learning! Treat them with some patience and respect, and soon (hopefully; after all, some never learn) they'll become suitable opponents.
-Something I hinted at above, spamming. It's quite an epidemic, particularly among less experienced players, but that's to be expected. It's when it's more experienced players who are doing it that it bugs me. However, it can be countered; dodging through a spammer's attacks and then quickly attacking them from the other side or throwing your weapon at them can often break a spamming streak.
-Lag. From what I have read, there are not that many servers, and so that contributes to the lag, since there are players all over the world. But, for me at least, it's not that bad; it's just frustrating to think you've hit an opponent and then have them shoot you off the map because you thought you were clear of them. Oh well; with time, this will hopefully improve.
-The "thrown into the deep end" nature of the game when you first start. It would be nice if there were a little tutorial that showed you the game mechanics and all the moves of one of the characters, maybe Bodvar for instance, since he's the flagship Legend. But if you've played fighting games before, you'll probably catch onto it fairly quickly, even just practicing in the single-player version, against bots.
Now, the pros:
-Creative ideas. I LOVE the design of the Legends; I love that they're different from the typical characters in fighting games. I mean, sure, Bodvar and Teros (aka the brave half-bear viking king, and the minotaur) are kind of cliches, but Asuri, Orion, Ada, Gnash, even Ember, they're all very creative. I like what the devs have done there. And they're not all stereotypical either! I mean, sure, Teros is strong, but one of the strongest characters is Scarlet, a female steampunk inventor, who uses a hammer and a rocket lance! Also, the rocket lance is a neat idea; I've never seen anything like that in any other game.
-The Lore. I really like how each character has a neat background, and while I get that the devs are busy making new characters and balancing the game and all that good stuff, but I would REALLY like to see more stuff with the lore! I want to know more about the characters! DEVS, PLEASE, MORE LORE! Thank you.
-An expanding cast of dynamic characters. I know I kind of said it before, but... I love the character list! They're all unusual and neat; there's no bland character, even among the more stereotypical ones.
-A (mostly) friendly community. In the most recent update, they added a thing that allows you to say "gg" just by pressing X, but even before that, most people would say "gg" at the end of a round, and if someone fought well, they generally will say as much. Or at least, I do, and many of the people I've played with do.
-It's simple, but that doesn't mean it's boring. You have 2 weapons, which means that you can really vary your fighting style. And that's another thing: I love the weapon dynamic. I have never seen it in another fighting game: each character has 2 (for the most part, depending on how you play) EQUAL weapons (not a main and a sidearm). Each weapon has standard moves that are mostly the same no matter which character you're using (you'll usually have at least 1 weapon in common with at least one person in any 1v1v1v1 match, such as a spear, sword, axe, guns, etc.), but then they also have moves unique to each character, which gives the characters more uniqueness from each other, besides just stats and looks.
In conclusion, it's just a good game, and you should get it, since it's FREE! What are you doing still reading? Download the game and play it already!

I am personally in love with the RWBY Series. Hench the reason I enthusiastically bought Grimm Ecplise. And boy, was I in for a heavy disappointment.
RWBY the series is al about friendship, teamwork and all that mushy stuff covered in a thick layer of humor and over the top insane battles. Now the game however is a repetition of a repetition.
- walking to Area A
- fight a few waves of the same enemies
- move to Area B
- fight a few waves of the same enemies
- move to Area C
- fight a few waves of the same enemies
- And finally defend a objective for 4 waves or the fourth wave is some sort of boss.
The battle system is the most boring I have ever seen. You basicly repeat light attack light attack heavy attack troughout the whole game. Sometimes hitting your ultimate attack once it is charged. There is an counter attack, but most of the time your locked in your combo. There are team attacks, which is initialized by chance from another player (mostly due heavy attacks or special attacks), but the enemies mostly die before you can execute them.
If I think of RWBY battles I think of running on walls, destroying buildings, switching my weapons from ranged to melee on the fly, using my ranged shot to empower my melee attacks or even using some french bread and water melons as weapons. Not walking to an area and using the same combo repeat. When I play as Ruby I want to be able to go into sniper mode, change ammo. Or when I am weiss I want to use as many types dust as possible.
Besides gameplay, I also find the graphics lacking the RWBY feel. Where the environment of the series is mostly steriel, minimalistic and lack of any detail. With hard contrasting colors and lightning as if the animators forgot to texture and light the scene at all. The music, while of great quality, is the same song repeating throughout the level. Every character has one or two lines which they sometimes yell out when doing a final hit on a wave or execute a team attack.
So verdict: If you love RWBY, it is the game you should love so you play it while you know it is rubbish. If you never heard of RWBY, go watch the series and leave this game alone.

time for my review
after spending several hundrets of hours with this game, i've got mixed feelings about it.
so hopefully this review comes usefull to the user and the devellopers
but before i start with my pros and contras i want to say that this is a great piece of work just out of balance.
the first class i choosed to play was the tanker and its still my favorite. but nonetheless one of the hardest to play theese days.
especially as the tank-class i spent much time analysing the battlefield.
so here are my impressions.
pro:
-free to play (build up a class of your choice for free, you need that expierience.... really. you can buy much with money, but if you dont know how to use it, you pay to die. however if you come to the point where you decide that you like the game and want to go on with it, you should probably do your part to keep this game running.)
-great potential for tactical teamplay (combine tanks, infantry, planes, recons and paratrooper depending on the situation)
-each class is specialized in their vehicles (except paratrooper for obvios reasons. 4 tank classes for tanker and 3 vehicle classes for infantry and 2 for recon, each with multiple options to choose from. + actually 3 planes, each has its own class)
-beautiful huge maps (as you need it if you want to fly or use tanks.)
-cool concept of combining a shooter/simulator with a strategic game (build up your own resources and send them to the battle of your choice and join it)
-many weapons available (earn your weapon of choice due combat expierience and customize it with mods and skins.)
contra ( i have to say that most of theese points are not generally bad, but sometimes a game requires rebalancing, if the players behaviors disturbe it.)
-every class can equip anti tank weapons, they are just way to expensive (making tanks almost useless in many situations. and definetly useless if the player doesn't know what to do, to avoid getting blown up. on the other side anti tank weapons are extremly expensive. but obviously this doesn't prevent some players to overuse them sitting at spawnpoints.)
-expensive prices effectively block some content ( the high ingame prices for mines and grenades makes it impossible to lay a minefield for example. furthermore this directly leads to the tactics where mines are placed near or on top of a tanks to be blown up by shooting them. what shouldn't harm a tank in most cases. plus these prices look for many people like p2w.)
-the effect range and angle of most explosives leads to an unbalanced use (it is easier and faster to destroy a tank without a tank, making tanks often a disadvantage)
-the ingame payment and expierience system (mixing the general ingame currency with the currency used for your resources or assault teams, leads to another unfortunate effect. having players farming money on matches that are build up with other poeples resources, not caring about winning, loosing or being carefully with the resources. what sometimes even leads to conflicts and therefore the most importand contra.)
conclusions
-Heroes & Generals is despite many problems a great game and if you like the genre or/and are wwII interested this is worth more than just one try.
-try every faction before you start to buy everything (usually worst teamplay: germans, usually best teamplay: ussr)
-think about joining a clan or play with friends
-tanker should be the last class to build up, because its generally the hardest to play (on the other side, it was my first and i'm still playing. it's tactical interesting and you CAN have a huge impact on a match)
-start hoping for a good rebalancing, because this is the only thing that makes this game for many people unplayable
personally i felt in love with this game and will go on with it and rebalance it with my personal skills. but for a good patch i would even invest something to reward it. as modder i know how much work goes into something like this.
i hope the developers don't get frustrated by all this negativity, coming from players that use their work for free. so that they can focus on making the game good again.
and having a look on some other reviews, i would recommend keeping in mind that the H&G team is constantly working on the game. maybe it would be more useful to try to help instead of loosing good manners
p.s.
i have to confess that this review started in anger caused by the matches fought before.
but having a last look on my crappy english gave me a slim hope i've done something constructive out of it.

The very basic quick/strong/throw/dodge controls have a nice bonus with the legend (character) dependent weapons and a counter with cooldown. -All items generally take more "farming" of coin in matches than other games with same unlock system (why you should buy the legends if possible with game)
-Not a game to play in real bulk chunks (4+ hours)

A peculiar cycle of games, the Call of Juarez series was one of the more thoughtful FPS shooters to be produced in many years.   The first game was a prequal to the second, using  a very post modernist way to tell its backstory. Well designed, Call of Juarez has an intuitive game system and graphics engine, no doubt. Despite the valleylike walls of the settings, which make the levels feel like open mazes, the environments are  pleasing tothe eye. The shooting dynamics are well implemented. Billy's whip and Ray's excellent handling of guns are interesting new features. However, the stealth chapters of the story tend deprive players of having more of a chance to have firefights, which is remedied later on in the game, but only in the final chapter. Also, interactions with NPC's of the chapters is reduced to a minimum, leading to the impression that there isn't much human involvement beyond the strictly necessary.
Call of Juarez is a useful case study and a compelling adventure, though it was a new breed of animal in its infancy. The game has to be appreciated for all that it's got, not the elements that sometimes don't feel satisfying or complete enough.

When I first bought Deathwatch I didn't know what I was in for. I mean, I like strategy games, I like Warhammer 40k a lot and I like what I know from the Deathwatch Chapter of Space Marines. But I didn't know what to expect of the game, for until now I didn't play a lot of that kind of turn-based tactical game.

I enjoy that bit of luck, that you don't fully no what kind of units or equipment you'll be getting next, and that's what makes it so loveable for me. Something totally different:
"There was a Japan AI,
which circuits were made not to fry.
It got caught in a loop.
It got caught in a loop.
It got caught in a loop."
While I had encountered a little bug concerning the enemy AI in a mission, I scanned through the reviews and was rathere surprised by the deep red of the first page of them. But finally I understood that this system with the packages was about the iOS version where you could spend real money to take away the coincidence and stuff.
Some reviews were rather contradictional, both had played the 'original', but the one said "it's too easy on PC" and the other "it's too grindy without the shop". Well, I can only assume that it felt easy when you restart the game, because if I'd play the first mission again now I'd be bored too.
And some mentioned that there were other games of the kind, most of all Xcom. And lucky I was that day, it's been on sale! :D :D :D So I bought it too, looking forward for it was said that it was more challanging.
I am not going to review Xcom now but let's say this: There's a whole browser-game of extra stuff about it, but the actual tactical fighting ain't that much different. And though some things are a little different, it is not that much more difficult. I'll admit it has a few more components to the fighting, but not too many and they don't play too great a relevance in most missions. So I frown a little at those reviews which compare these games with one another.
And on of the most important points that speak for Deathwatch is that it is a far more charming atmosphere if you love the apocalyptic univers of 40k. And the Marines actually get to know each other in a hidden mechanic! And they have so many hidden jokes and in-lore references, it's awesome! <3
And last, the price. You see, let's be a bit generally fair, all games got a bit more expansive than they deserve, and at the same time there are those game designers and programmers that need money to pay their rent. And what fun would summer / winter sale be without big numbers getting maximally minimized? :D I mean, when I feel the urge to buy something NOW than those 20 bugs might slip my pocket, but usually I've got enough other games to wait for the sales. With that little bit in mind, the price is not really a concern of any game. Just a lame excuse to buff up the red review - just my opinion, no offence.
And I see that those who bought the original already, bought all the in-app items and than- wow, wait, WHAT?!
You've already got the game, you've already paid tons of money for things you couldn't wait for within the game, and THEN you couldn't wait to buy the (pretty much) same game AGAIN and THEN got the nerve to complain about the price?

There's even a 12 minute Summary Video for Human Revolution in case you never played the first one or if you want to see what was made 'canon', though it leaves out all the misc. decisions like choosing whether to replace the bio chip or not.
Mid way the story does lose some steam whereas in Human Revolution it just made you question more and more and wanting to see just how far down the rabbit hole goes with the various twists that happen in the story. The ending is something for you to figure out.
The level design is much more complex than Human Revolution, I've no idea how many different ways you can get into the next area. I found quite a few on my first playthrough when I was trying to find a way into some areas of Golem City, second playthrough I found several more ways to get further into Golem City. There's just so many more ways to tackle each level and room since the added experimental augs further enhances how you want your playstyle to be.
The decisions this time around actually have alittle more weight than in Human Revolution, I'll leave it up to you on the rest of that, there was one decision I had to make that was very difficult mid way through the game.
I got used to the new VO for Sarif, fits him well, probably more than the original VO for Sarif in Human Revolution. But like all the characters including Jensen, they're all very well voiced and each character is interesting and all have some sort of backstory, it's just up to you if you want to ask each character on what their personal stories are.
Music is ok, but not as great and memoriable as Human Revolutions was.
The game is worth every penny it's asking for, whether you wait for a sale or not is up to you, you're not going to waste your money either way. But you really should play Human Revolution, more specially the Directors Cut which includes The Missing Link DLC that directly ties into Mankind Divided. You'll even find some things hidden in the the world of Mankind Divided that only players who played The Missing Link DLC will understand. Without Human Revolution, you really will be kinda lost on certain characters including Adam Jensen himself.

This game is fantastic, its like ecstasy of video gaming, Dynasty/Samurai Warriors in particular.
I've spent game after game, and I beat it around 90-100 times by now, and I never get sick of it.
This is a Battle Arena Hack&Slash / Mild Strategy type game, there is no fancy attack auto-lock here, there is skill & equipment to be combined and used, and particularly will need your effort to move, especially harder difficulties. Enemies will act fastest on Chaos with a motherlode of damage that WILL get you down after two-three hits, so are their soldiers, but also lower the Allies AI's ability to fight, I'm afraid. Its weird. But getting a Player Two might fix that little issue...
Dont judge it being easy, it's due to you playing lower difficulty or using higher class weapons or using bonuses in harder difficulties. I know that I dont get to tell you how to play, but your attack pace will get faster the higher class you use, which you'll need as to leech health, gain rage/musou faster, and etc. You have to upgrade to survive. Do yourself a favor and dont play on Begginer, but rather on Normal. NPCs and Player is just about the same playing field in terms of stats.
Easier difficulties makes AI easier to be taken down, give them less re-action time or more time between their heavier attacks, while Harder difficulties makes them more damage-sponge, act faster and deliver hits effective enough to take out a quarter of your health. You'll have to choose a playing field depending on what you feel, having extra points for goodies at the start of a game isnt a bad idea, but it might make the game rather less challenging but that's entirely up to you.
Along with Fast Pace, we got music.  Music will pump the hell out of you with Ear Worming about (If  you're a Payday 2 player, you know how that feels like). It's also one major thing that makes this game truly fun. Repetitive? Yeah. It will get repetitive. Hell I dont even know why I've spent so much time game after game and I'm still enjoying it, sure beats our fancy free-to-play MoBA's or 'Ability + Gear Measuring Contest' Games of ours (Kindna sucks everything isnt won by a chance or a dice game, huh?)
You can play as a Dynasty Warriors Character from the games, or you can make up your own characters, Units which are made up by your characters acting like one kingdom/vagabond, Horses, Soldiers, Flags. Though, there isnt much to customize with, I'd be lying, its just that there isnt much face accessories rather than clothing. You can choose your characters favored weapon sets, Special Attack, Rage attacks, you name it. I prefer Sword & Staff / Sword-Shield & Staff because one is more Area-attack while other is focused with attacking to an officer while keeping a defensive momentum at anytime.
Also, if 'Button mashing' Hack and Slash isnt your type, which requires some effin' effort, then you better stick to your fancy RPGs, cause in here, its the soul of the game. The game wont tell if you're succeeding the battle if you dont ♥♥♥♥ing participate. There is no Ability Mashing, but Combos. Combos are varied between weapons you use or pre-set favorite, and you'll want to make them work together if you wish to make through in one piece. No locking-on either, cause combos will ussually put you on the way where the enemy is, but you'll have to make effort to guide through. But if you find the right combination, then you'll enjoy the show. If you dont.. Well, better scoot over before you might get hit.
Though you might want to wait until it's in discount, I dont exactly see the reason to get DLCS but  they're expensive and bunch of skins and voices, pretty much. Dedicated people might get it though.
Controller Setup might be an issue though. Try refering to the Guide section, especially mapping them properly.
Also where in the name of hell is a Multiplayer Co-operative function? Samurai Warriors 4-II has it, why doesnt this game get one? With a discount and that option, this game can get ton of players if you ask me.
A Great pro-tip,
Try Switching your weapons if you noticed an enemy slowing down before a heavy attack, or middle of an attack, you'll stagger or counter them, giving you a chance to attack, use this to keep your momentum in battle. Blocking is an option too, but that'll push you back and might get you cornered when there are a group of officers attacking you and will eventually break your guard!

Firstly, I'd like to say that this is one of the most visually jaw-dropping games I've played for a while.
Now that that's out of the way, what's the /gameplay/ like?
Trine is a side-scrolling, co-op platformer/fighter. You control a wizard, thief or fighter as you and two friends team up to destroy everything in your path.
Or murder each other hilariously using the game's fantastic physics engine, that's another thing you could do.
While friendly fire doesn't exist, so you won't be getting in each others' way in combat, if you want to mess with your so-called-'friends' this is a hilarious game to play. Puzzle areas give you the opportunity to flambe your friends, shoot platforms out from under them, drop enemies on them, and generally have everyone give each other a hard time. Fortunately, Trine is  very forgiving, so as soon as the fun of killing each other is over you can easily drop by the closest respawn point and get on with the plot.
That's not to say that you won't die. If you play on hard, you can expect to die more often than not; but even if your whole party is wiped out, you can always respawn back at the last checkpoint, which are conveniently close together. It makes for an entertaining and challenging game without being punishing, and the cooperative puzzles are a blast. Playing Trine with my friends has prompted me to want to pull out Portal 2's co-op mode, that's how great the puzzles were. Everyone will be needed for the moments when you need to cooperate- and if you don't feel like cooperating at the moment, you can definitely go ahead by yourself and fight things on your own. It'll be more challenging, but you can do it. Few things are more awesome than being the sole survivor of the group, destroying the enemies that killed your friends as they watch, and going on to make it to the next checkpoint.
That said: Half the fun of this game is in messing around with your friends. You will NEED everyone to have a mic to play this well, and you really should play it with a full group of three. I haven't tried the solo gcampaign, but I doubt it'd be anywhere near as entertaining.
Overall, Trine is a great game, and you should pull together a group to play it pretty much as soon as possible.

There is a lot to say about this game, both good and bad. This game has a lot of design elements that aren't seen any more in other shooter franchises, for better or for worse. Seeing this game's multiplayer years ago during the early days of Counter Strike, I was enthralled by its advanced destruction physics and somewhat detailed gibs. Playing through the single player again recently, I nociced how fresh and different the weapon behaviours were.
The gameplay is fast and brutal, the enemies don't have a lot of health, and they have weapons that can rip you apart in an instant, encouraging players to play either carefully, or agressively. The weapons sound very meaty and are very satisfying to fire. There are also the inclusion of NPCs that react to your actions, either firing at them, pulling your weapon out, or approaching certain NPCs with an injury. In a way, there is a lot to be compared to Half-Life 1 with the fast, brutal encounters, the linearity with some tribute paid to exploration, the interactive NPCs, and the general Sci-Fi theme. What sets it apart though, are the advanced destruction physics which allows you to blow open walls and structures, sometimes revealing secret passages or shortcuts, giving players a feeling of agency.
However, there are plenty of issues that hold this game back, the most noteable of which is the pathfinding AI, which frequently gets enemy NPCs stuck on geometry or simply shut-down, turning them into still statues until you start shooting at them. The stealth sections felt crowbared in as a very flimsy excuse to reset the player inventory for each act, and they are not very compelling or properly implemented as the enemy AI creates scenarios where stealthing through each section are nigh impossible. It is often better to just run through the enemies, as they're too inaccurate to land enough hits on you to kill you, or blow through them, as they provide more than enough supplies when they die. Not only that, the stealth sections are programmed so that you can never fall below 1 health. Another thing is that the weapons that the enemies use during the third act of the game pretty much makes it so that the best way to get through a section would be to save-scum after every encounter, since the snipers can shoot at you through walls with their Rail-Drivers and it's extremely random whether they would hit or not. There's also the weak major boss battles where the only weapon capable of defeating them is the flamethrower, and the ending which throws an arrow guessing game at you at random instead of an epic battle.  One more final thing that holds this game back is that, unlike Half Life 1, the graphics and model quality simply didn't age well.
Despite its flaws though, there is a very good game underneath and I feel that had Volition had more time to polish and do QA testing, this game would be able to stand abreast of Half Life 1 as a landmark piece of gaming curios. Do I recommend this game? Definitely! There is a lot to like about this game, and for just $9.99 you can definitely do a worse than play this game. If you decide to pick this game up though, it is imperative that you download and install the Pure Faction 3.0 patch and the Pure Faction 3.0c beta update, as it adds a ton of fixes that improves the experience immensely, like widescreen resolution support and mouse raw input.

I got some of that satifaction via hearing the voice lines (what little there are) and getting to see the characters and world of Remnant. Now while the concept of fighting grimm itself sounds like great fun, it feels very tedious and spammy. Having played all eight characters, I believe I can safely say that, when it comes to Team RWBY, the different characters feel practically the same; AOE ult, two long ranged shots followed by a more powerful shot, mash mash mash with the only slight exeption to this being Yang, who's first two ranged shots only seem to hit a very short range in front of her. I can say that when it comes to Team JNPR, each of the characters feel different, at least moreso than Team RWBY. As Jaune has no form of long ranged attack in the series, he can charge at enemies, and instead of an AOE ult, it seems he buffs his allies. Pyrrha, meanwhile, has updgradable combos, and instead of two weak shots and one strong shot, she just has individual shots, which, while seeming somewhat underwhelming, actually comes as a nice change of pace. Nora and Ren seem to function a lot more like the members of team RWBY, but there are some differences due to their weapons.
I have only had the opportunity to play single player for the moment, but I can safely say that this game cries for a soulmate to play with. In single player, the environments, while they do look nice and give you the feeling you are in the world of Remnant, feel empty and predictable, spawning grim in wide open areas akin to arenas, while the only character on the field is yourself. I wonder why they couldn't allow for some AI characters for as a fan, I wanted to see more of character interactions, but if there is some amount of interaction between characters, you cant see it in single player. To wrap all the repatative gameply up is a formulaic structure of the levels: grim fight, walk, grim fight, walk, fight waves while waiting for an event, walk, grim fight, walk, defend a stucture while fighting waves. Granted I have only played through area three, but i have heard it doesn't really change. And finally, if you are thinking about buying for the story, as of where I am, the story is threadbear at best, and nonexistant at worst. While I will still try and slog through it and wish it weren't so, I can't in good faith reccomend RWBY: Grimm Eclipse from a single player experience. I pray that the game thrives in it's multiplayer.
Now while I can't really reccomend the game, if you want to play the game, I would suggest purchasing team JNPR. Their slightly more diverse kits feel a bit more entertaining to play, at least after playing as members of team RWBY.

To recommend or not to recommend, an impossible question without knowing who is asking and who much they're thinking of spending. The last six and a half years have be relatively kind to Call of Juarez but it is definitely one for the genre or series fans rather than everyone and the current Steam price of £14 that I'm seeing is definitely too much and I'm glad I didn't pay that much.
Mechanicially the game is quite interesting. The plot and the mechanics revolve arround two seperate characters, the young agile sneaky Billy and old psychopathic Reverend Ray. Billy's levels revolve arround stealth and movement, Ray's arround shooting everything that moves before it can shoot you. Neither is perfect, Billy's stealth ability to hide in bushes for instance is particularly dependant on the level designers whim rather than any sense of logic and the Reverend's bullettime ability with pistols is obscenely overpowered, makes no sense at all and breaks up the shooting almost as much as Fallout 3's V.A.T.S. system. So yeah, the run and gun character plays like something out of an RPG... Honestly, it isn't as bad as that sounds though and I had fun playing his levels, and Billy's for that matter, throughout the game. The fact that the mechanics are a bit different from the norm and have their own particular feel is really what has kept this game feeling fresh.
It also doesn't outstay its welcome, which admittedly is a flattering way of saying it is short but short and good is a heck of a lot better than long and boring any day. Particularly if you're not paying the sort of money that would demand a game that is both long and good.
Plot wise, well it is a western and as such it probably can't be expected to deliver too much and it doesn't really. Two fairly interesting main characters, Ray in particular wouldn't be that interesting just as a background character but as a viewpoint character he is a minor stroke of genus. Sadly the supporting cast are wooden cutouts at best. The female characters are particular badly done by. There are four in total that I noticed: there is Suzy, who works as a prosititute and who basically only exists to have her gun stolen by Billy while she is trying to "welcome you home" behind her pimp's back. Then there is Billy's mother who is brutally murdered before she even has a chance to appear in the game and exists pretty much only as an example of the woman in the fridge trope. Then there is the sheriff's wife who is a damsel that must be rescued from some random dudes for reasons. Then there is Molly, the love interest and main female character who is pretty much the most generic boring useless damsel in distress you could hope to meet. If any of these characters had anything approaching an actual character then I must have missed it. As a side note the game should probably come with a trigger warning for sexual violence since it can't seem to shut up about it. I guess they were trying to make it sound gritty but it is completely overdone.
Would I recommend it? Well for all my gripes I did have fun and for the couple of quid I paid for it I easily got value for money out of it. I didn't pay £14 for it though and I wouldn't recommend that you do either but as a game that is still fun and interesting, so yeah, I'll recommend it.

This game is truly awesome.
You start as a peasant (though having a male character with noble blood makes progression a bit easier) and work your way up to being king of your own faction, and eventually emperor of the whole land.
The thing I really like about this game is the flexibility of what role you want to play. Once you get a feel for the different kings and factions, it's usually pertinent to select a king for whom you will be a vassal. Want to help a faction become strong, building relationships with the troops, and help them crush a different faction or two, only to start siphoning off those troops for your own faction and rebel? Would you prefer taking the banner of a claimant to one of the factions and putting them on the throne of said faction? Perhaps you'd like to just be a successful mercenary until the political intrigue develops further? Much of the game's progression is a bit cerebral and imagined, so to speak (like a tabletop game). I don't think that is necessarily a bad thing.
The combat is interesting and quite fun to master. Protip: try to stay on your horse and kite them.
The different factions bring different troop trees to the table, each specialising in different things (archery, crossbows, large-shielded infantry, horse archery, heavily armored horses with polearms, etc) and you can build your army with combinations of these, and tell them what to do on the battlefield. For example, archers hold here on this hilltop, infantry charge.
The game is showing its age a bit, however that doesn't mean you should not play it.
My biggest criticism is it's grindy, but this can be mitigated by using mods, such as Diplovexed, which is my favorite vanilla mod (which gives you the added depth of the Diplomacy mod and Vexed's reduced grinding).
I -highly- recommend trying the Prophecy of Pendor mod, which is content-rich and still being updated (this is probably the best mod). If it had the diplomacy mod too it would truly be perfect, but I digress.
Also check out the battle size mod, letting you adjust how many units can be in the battle at once (units beyond that number come in reinforcement waves). I usually use about 1000 troops at once.
If you're not sure about this game but are somewhat interested I say definitely pick it up on a sale. It usually goes for something like six dollars. That's totally worth it.

As most other people have said, this is a game that everyone should play at least once. The story is touching, the atmosphere is incredible, and the scenery is varied and breathtaking. Despite being short (you can 100% the game in about two hours), it's a really special experience.
That being said...
* The younger brother is a little jackass. I had no sympathy for his plight, and went out of my way to let him die during a few puzzles, in the hopes that it might stick. Almost everything he interacts with ends up with him being a total assclown. I despite children like him in real life, and controlling one made me grit my teeth.
* The game is about 200% easier with a controller. I spent over half of it getting by with the keyboard controls. Which aren't BAD, really, and you can rebind them if needed, but for someone with hand/wrist issues, it was really painful. If you have a controller, use it. Just keep in mind that you can't rebind your buttons (which would have been massively helpful for my aforementioned physical problems).
* The enviornments are wide and varied; from a small village in the mountains to underground caverns, a snowy town to an enchanted forest, even the open sea. Every one of those place is beautiful and well-rendered (and screenshot-worthy, by looking at my uploads). But it IS all squeezed into about two hours, and the change of scenery can be almost jarring. Just when you've gotten used to one place, you're tossed into another.
* Make sure you grab the game while it's on sale. It's an incredible game, but the playtime (and lack of replay value) doesn't really warrant the full price.
Obviously, none of these things are game-breaking problems. Most of them are just annoyances. But all I otherwise have to say is the glowing praise everyone else has said. Go get it, Play it. Enjoy it. And hopefully I've mentioned some things that will make your playthrough a little smoother.

Play a sequence of turn based tactical missions with a squad of 5 Space Marines in a quest for better gear, stronger Marines, and get them more experienced along the way.
First of all, let's get the negatives out of the way :
The game is a bit sluggish in the beginning, with move animations taking way longer than needed, and it starts too easy. The loot drops are usually disappointing too. The UI should have been remade for PC too. It gets the job done, but doesn't use the RMB much, and requires too many clicks for some operations.
But the game starts coming together if you give it a bit more time, and around act 5 (so after 5h in), starts requiring you to find a good way to use the tools you got (marines and gear are randomly awarded when you complete a mission AND when you give not-money to the not-shopkeeper).
The game becomes much more satisfying after you finish it and unlock Veteran difficulty, and even more after you unlock heroic. And because you need to be more careful, and spend more time shooting and less time running, walk animation speed is not as bad as it used to in lower levels.
Higher difficulties reward  you with better gear and more requisition, and force you to play carefully during the missions your squad is not good at (some mission favor mobilities, other close quarter fighting, other long range devastation...).
In the end, it plays like some kind of Incubation 40K with a diablo-like loot system tackled on (the loot is not randomly generated, as the available pieces of equipment are fixed, but it has the same structure where you replay the campaign for better loot, and has very random loot distribution too).
So you probably won't be able to field your dream squad, but making do with what you have is also part of the experience (I planned to go heavy devastators, but had to change to a mostly melee Space Wolf squad with a touch of ranged support because I got better Space Wolf marines and gear).
And if you are not happy with the loot drop rate, you can always use cheat engine anyway.
- Let my Blood Angel sternguard go berserk. Ooops, he shot the bomb too. KBOOM. squad wipe.
- Brother Erik sharpfang, get there and cleave this hive tyrant to death.... I said the hive tyrant, not your Ultramarine brother!
- Let's engage this Carnifex in melee! Ooops, 3 Marines down. Let's play hide and seek with the remaining tactical and devastator marine. It looks like Tyranids were better at seeking than us at hiding. squad wipe.
- We need to get across this bridge, but we are overwhelmed. The 2 assault marine and the devastator will sacrifice themselves to tie as many tyranids as possible while Road Runner the tactical Marine and Flash the medic use stimpacks to dash to the endzone.
You should definitely get it if you can put up with its initial issues (UI, animation speed, and slow loot drop rate in the beginning), and don't mind a cousin of Incubation with a diablo loot feedback loop. I would say it is the best recent (=post THQ) 40K PC (or iOS too for that matter) game.
