A majestic platform puzzle game with a dash of action.
Rating 6/10
It’s similar in many ways to the classic Shadow of the Beast series and The Lost Vikings. You take control of one of three heroes, a wizard, thief and knight, whilst being able to character swap at any time even mid jump.  It's this fluid change from styles in the middle of battle or solving a puzzle that adds another dimension to what could turn into fairly simplistic gameplay. There are times when it doesn't work such as having your thief or knight die and only being left with a wizard who is rather useless in a fight. However there are enough character reviving checkpoints that it doesn't become too much of an annoying handicap.
Despite being a fairly traditional side scrolling platform game it's a truly beautifully made game, in artistic terms it's near perfect. It's this beauty coupled with the fun physics puzzles and quick action that keeps you playing as the plot is non-existent and the voice acting is weak.
The DLC adds a few new environments such as dusty desert and the inside of a giant worm and whilst every bit as stunning as the main game by this stage Trine 2 has overstayed it's welcome and it's a fairly boring slog through the last seven extra levels. The DLC doesn't add any real new mechanics or gameplay, it’s just more of the same.
So whilst trine 2 doesn't offer much in the way of innovative gameplay or a great story it's beauty has to be seen.

After over 1300 hours invested in the game in both single and mostly multiplayer, it pains me to give a negative review to this game. Let me preface that this has been my favorite game of all time until this point. The mistakes made herein by R* are so damaging that the community cannot even function in remotely the same fashion as it has been for the last four years.
Starting with MP, the gameplay decisions made by R* regarding online in the last year have been greedy at
. The latest multiplayer update introduces so many balance-breaking features it's nearly impossible to play in any manner that isn't DayZ-like self defense. The latest update has enabled modders to break the game even further for defenseless players by incorporating blantantly overpowered vehicles and weaponry while increasing the cost of such items immensely. It has encouraged the purchase of SharkCards like no other update prior. Because without cash, you're as good as ashes with this update. Everything is so unforgivingly expensive that if you aren't modding, aren't buying SharkCards, or aren't already sitting on a wad of cash, you have one hell of a fight just to get your car across Los Santos.
And of course, let's not forget the elephant in the room. The cease and desist of OpenIV. It was the saving grace of GTA. It gave GTA V longevity that its developers couldn't replicate. Thousands upon thousands of modding videos on YouTube garnering
of combined views are now useless. One of the biggest gaming communities on the earth with thousands of contributors, millions of users and players are now at a loss without modding. Modding videos, funny moments videos (most of which have mods), and other mod-inspired GTA videos such as role-play, cinematics, etc are now a relic of a bygone era. R*'s easiest and largest source of free advertisement is now utterly useless. The income of several YouTubers has also been damaged due to the sudden, unprovoked, and unprecedented actions by R* and its publisher Take2. The amazing GTA V Redux mod and others like it are now trash. The hundreds and thousands of hours and passion developers have poured into mods for the game are now for nothing.
I have single-handedly convinced dozens of people to buy GTA. I have bought GTA V for several more. After this, I regret ever making that mistake. After everything the fans have done for R* to put GTA V where it's at now just feels like a stab in the back. I can only presume that RD2 will fall to the same fate... Perhaps R* will learn in time for then. Until now, any future release just reeks of distrust and greed.

I am writing this review shortly after finshing the game, hence my apologies for any possible confused thought and opinion. I feel the urge of writing a couple of lines in appreciation of such a masterpiece.
There are titles where words are unnecessary, where a single utterance can easily ruin the idilliac atmosphere surrounding a simple, innocent yet mesmerizing narration.
Brothers - A tale of Two Sons easily embodies this description. It finds its strength in its simplicity which makes it innovative.
The decision of adopting a fictional language without subtitles immediately puts the players inside a real fantasy world, with no connection to reality. It feels like being dragged into that perfect place you'd love to live, perhaps the kind of place you can see in your dreams.
The visuals, the entities, the landscape and the invisible forces moving the fate of the two brothers, they all have dream-like features.
I honestly loved the fact that the player can find a bench every now and then, to simply admire the surrounding, or perform some "side quests" to simply help the others, without the need of a reward.
Morals and ethics are important subjects that are being strongly highlighted in this game, which seems to possess all the features that characterized the typical Bildungsroman.
The ability of using two characters at one, with their own independent control scheme is just splendid. Personally, this is the first time I am facing such a unique task (on a sidenote, even though the notice says that the game requires a controller, I must disagree with that: I played it with the keyboard and it works simply great) and it's extremely rewarding, besides being a necessary mean to develop with the story.
The difficulty of the game isn't particularly hard: there are tons of checkpoints and rarely you will be facing a potentially deadly situation, but I believe that is not a negative aspect, as it would lose its aura otherwise.
So what is Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons?
Is it a puzzle? A platform? A narrative game?
Is it even a game or perhaps a piece of virtual literature?
Perhaps it would require a genre of its own.
I don't know. I only know that this is a truly magnificent experience, and I am glad I had been a part of it.
Go hit "Add to cart" now, you'll thank me later.

I previously purchased this game for an Android tablet, and enjoyed it enough to purchase it here on Steam so I can play it on my desktop computer.  (I find the mouse interface superior, especially for the combat, because you can choose to cast lower level spells to conserve spell points).
Honestly, it's interesting to see the subtle (and not so subtle) differences that occur depending on some of your choices.  In fact, from what I can tell after multiple play-throughs, the frequency with which you have chosen each of the three dialogue options (joking, friendly, forceful) changes other dialogue during the game not directly tied to those decisions.  It's little touches like this, combined with the strong writing generally, that have made it a pleasure to replay the game.
Adding to the replayability are the skill trees and the number of party members.  It's possible to complete the game using almost exclusively the same 6 characters, or you can switch it up.  On later playthroughs, I have experimented with party set-ups, skill combos, and other combat options.  And, of course, there is the wide range of romantic options.
The difficulty descriptions are fairly apt, and the options are nice to have:
In easy, the combat, even against bosses, is almost laughably simple, but it allows you to focus more on the story.
Normal is a nice mix.  Combat takes some thought but is not too difficult.  There is no real need to grind and level up.
Hard is, well, hard.  Save often, because if you go into combat with the wrong set of characters or a lack of items and you're pretty well hosed.  I personally find it makes for a nice additional challenge on later playthroughs, but wouldn't recommend it on a first go-round.
The artwork is top notch, the characters are well-developed, and the storyline, while somewhat generic (unite the armies, kill the demons) is well-told.  I would definitely recommend purchasing the Castle of N'Mar expansion if you're going to get the game.  It adds a lot to the third chapter, including numerous sidequests and some romance options.  I liked it enough to buy it twice, so I'm going to go ahead and recommend purchasing it at least once ^_-

32 hours in, and I am loving this game. It's big, it's got more than enough content to satisfy any Deus Ex fan, and the hub world is full of all kinds of fun to explore.
Gameplay itself is a lot more viable, sneaking is good and all, but with the updated mechanics you can roll *aggressive* non-lethal, and still make it through the game.
The graphics? Ehhh, it's not the pretiest, but the amount of detail put into things more than makes up for it, from the scrollwork on the building to grease splotches on clothing - it's pretty clear the devs mde the best of what they had.
The controls (Well, the use button) are a big "meh", though. It's pretty clear this was made to conform to a console control scheme, so your use button...is also bound to "Check updated objective" or "Open new pocket secretary". More than once I've tried dragging a body off to some get-along-corner only to open my aug menu because look, you got a praxis point! And unfortunately, you can't rebind that to anything.
As for the store? Sure, it's a bad bit, but holy smokes, did the community *flip out* way too hard. Six hours into my playthrough, I had my build (Sneaky-hack-y, with batteries to spare) maxed out - There's not a single instance in the game where the devs pulled a bit where you *needed* to buy the store items (Praxis kits and credits, no game breaking weapons or buy-to-win items there). With ample forethought (Yes, frag grenades on a minetemplate will bust open a wall, if only a little louder) and sneaking, the entire game is open to you.
I just wish the main story had a little more...oomph to it. I was more invested in the various side quests than that, and the sidequests managed to run for hours at a time.
In short, if you're a Deus Ex fan, buy it or wait for sale. Don't let the negative reviews get you down.
EDIT: After clearing the game, the main story ends on a MASSIVE cliff hanger, it  honestly felt a little disappointing and a deliberate sequel hook...but the actual meat of the game (Side quest, exploration, freedom of choice) was very worthwhile.
Also, Breach mode is godawful. White contours on white contours make for some confusing level design - and it's the one mode where p2w is in full effect. Avoid that at all costs.

I'm relatively new to the Dynasty Warriors series. I originally started playing these games with Dynasty Warriors 5: Empires. I stuck with the Empires games over the normal series because I liked the open-ended game play and the ability to choose-your-own adventure. Plus, creating your own officers and building your own empire in ancient China was extremely fun! DW8E's port to PC (along with its DW8 counterpart) has been less than satisfying. I've played very little of DW8E and I can already tell that it's difficult to play. Here are the reasons why:
This game has NO optimization for controllers... at all. First off, what game that allows you to use controllers doesn't put camera control on the right thumbstick? This one apparently. I use an Xbox 360 controller and the camera rotation controls are put on the LT and RT buttons, which is insanely difficult to control in the heat of battle. Also if you want to customize your keys to fix the LT/RT camera rotation problem, all of the buttons are labeled as JB1 or Z-Axis - (which, if you're not completely comfortable as to which button is which on the Xbox Controller, just confuses you) and any keys displayed on the UI are all keyboard keys. There is also no mapped key on the controller that matches what the Space Bar does. So any time you need to press the Space Bar to do anything in the game, you have to press it on the keyboard. Seriously Koei, you made this game for the Xbox and the PS3, can you not just port over the control schemes for each and put them in the settings? This is just getting downright lazy.
The game forces you to use the Japanese voice-overs. There isn't even an option to pick the English voice-overs either. There's not even DLC to give you the English voice-overs (although if you had to pay for that, I'm sure fans would be incredibly upset). I don't know why when Koei/Temco have released console versions of DW and DWE with English dubs only, why they would suddenly change course and give you the Japanese voice-overs without any option to use it or not. Even in the Naruto games they give you the option of using the Japanese or English voices since it's all about which version of the show you watch. I love the English voice acting in the games and I've gotten used to it. Now I have to hear the Japanese voices and that means reading subtitles during crucial points in the game. Sure, the dialogue was mostly repetitive and once you've heard it a few dozen times, you don't even need to bother reading the text any more, but when it's all new, you find yourself distracted since you can't understand the Japanese language (that is, if you're like me and can't understand Japanese). The English voices should be patched in, free-DLC'd in, or something. It should not just be a Japanese-only game.
DW has been notorious for giving you extras in the form of DLC. There's lots of customization items from outfits, weapons, and scenarios that are locked away in neat, little DLC packages. Each one of these runs you anywhere from $5 to $13. When the main game went on sale during the Steam summer sale, all of the DLC's pricing was left untouched. This goes to show you that the devs obviously want you to pay money for the DLC over the actual game. Hoping that when you buy the game, you'll buy all of the DLC at once with it (and it costs well over $125 at full price). I know, I honestly thought about buying it when I bought the game too. But I hesitated and I'm glad I did. The content packages are pretty light and are mostly cosmetic, not really adding anything useful to the game. There's one scenario content DLC there but it seems like the devs just took the original Japanese description, ran it through Google Translate, copy/pasted it into the English version, and it's really hard to know what you're actually getting when you buy it. I understand in this DLC-happy gaming world we're in, companies are going to do the hard-sell on DLC over the original game, but when $125-worth of DLC doesn't go on sale with the main game, it says something to me... the original product is not that great while the devs hope to get your money with the DLC instead.
Controller issues aside, the gameplay is still the same DW fun. Part of the charm of the repetitive gameplay is being able to just be a super badass on the battlefield curb-stomping your way to 1000+ KOs. The new interface, although clunky, is interesting and gives you tons of options to play with as a Free Officer or as your own ruler. The graphics are pretty good, although one time I was looking at my character with some really shiny elbow guards that probably shouldn't have been so shiny... The game also lets you customize your own army, using all of the details right down to what your banner looks like, what your soldiers look like, what your horse looks like, and who your officers are (I think they can only be created officers). These get implemented into the game as well and can add some new flavor to the game. There's TONS of room for customization, so you can spend a lot of time just creating things on your own. If you know how to use the Scenario Creator, you can end up making replayability almost endless. It's just a shame that TONS of the content that can be used for created characters is locked away in DLC...
All in all, this is a bad port. I don't think Koei/Temco are even going to try to fix it, unfortunately. I think it's part of the fact that PC gaming is still 2nd fiddle to console gaming in Japan. Japanese devs don't respect PC gamers since they don't make them as much money as the console gamers do. So they churn out a lazy port to the PC and know that fans of the console games, like myself, will buy it without really understanding that their ports will be garbage. I've certainly learned my lesson on this and I'm not going to be buying any more DW ports to the PC, at least not until I can get some reliable information that they've fixed some of the major issues with their DW8 and DW8E ports.

CONS:

First Impression Gameplay:
Side-scrolling shoot-em up genres aren't typically my forte, but I have been thoroughly enjoying this game. The cut scenes and 3d movement through stages is seriously awesome and have kept me engaged.
From what I can tell, adventure mode covers an arcing story over a few different characters (who all have their own ships and special ability).  Time is a recurring theme, as when you get hit by an enemy you lose time to finish the stage, gain time when killing an enemy, have the ability to slow time, and the story overlaps through different characters viewpoints over the same time periods.
Various upgrades drop throughout play which can give you ammo for your special weapon, upgrade your main gun, give you more slow-down ability, etc.  Stages appear to have multiple boss fights which are both beautiful to look at, and fun to fight.  There is a Co-op mode, but I have not had someone to play it with as of yet.
As far as bug and glitches, I have not experienced any as of yet.  At first I thought I was hearing an audio glitch with characters repeating the same lines until I realized I was replaying the same moment in time through a different character.  A pretty cool concept to introduce into a game like this, where typically its all about the bullet-hell aspect.
All in all, this is a beautiful game with amazing graphics, great audio, good voice acting, and fun/engaging game play.  A solid recommendation.

takes place on one Halloween night. You play as Axel, an average 17 year-old, who heads into a nearby forest with his two friends to investigate a legend. According to local folklore, Halloween is associated with strange disappearances of people in the forest. Axel and his buddies try to find out if there is any truth to that but Axel soon finds out he may get more than he bargained for.
This game is a visual novel, a type of video game entirely story based. Most of what you do in this game is reading, though there are a couple of decision points along the way that affect the course of the story. This game has a total of eight different endings.
Overall, my impression of this game is that it is mediocre at best. To start off with, I am assuming that this game was not originally written in English because it felt like every third line in this game had a typo, grammatical error, or just really awkward prose. This really could have used a proofreader before being published. It is not impossible to understand, but it should have been better.
The artwork itself is fine, but nothing really special.
Like with most visual novels, the main thing is the story and writing. In this game, it really fell flat. First of all, the main premise of the game feels terribly unoriginal and the concept of witches hiding out in a forest and strange disappearances feels ripped straight from something like
. There is very little characterization in the game. The main character really had no traits at all, other than getting flustered when encountering cute girls. The two girls encountered in the story, Ashley and Lilian, also feel terribly underdeveloped. Too much of the story just felt like stuff happening without a plot and it really became boring. Even though I did unlock all of the endings, there was not much in this game that felt memorable.
Overall, I generally found this game to be boring. If you are a visual novel fanatic and have a couple of hours to kill, you might get some enjoyment out of it. Others can probably pass on it.

I am writing this review shortly after finshing the game, hence my apologies for any possible confused thought and opinion. I feel the urge of writing a couple of lines in appreciation of such a masterpiece.
There are titles where words are unnecessary, where a single utterance can easily ruin the idilliac atmosphere surrounding a simple, innocent yet mesmerizing narration.
Brothers - A tale of Two Sons easily embodies this description. It finds its strength in its simplicity which makes it innovative.
The decision of adopting a fictional language without subtitles immediately puts the players inside a real fantasy world, with no connection to reality. It feels like being dragged into that perfect place you'd love to live, perhaps the kind of place you can see in your dreams.
The visuals, the entities, the landscape and the invisible forces moving the fate of the two brothers, they all have dream-like features.
I honestly loved the fact that the player can find a bench every now and then, to simply admire the surrounding, or perform some "side quests" to simply help the others, without the need of a reward.
Morals and ethics are important subjects that are being strongly highlighted in this game, which seems to possess all the features that characterized the typical Bildungsroman.
The ability of using two characters at one, with their own independent control scheme is just splendid. Personally, this is the first time I am facing such a unique task (on a sidenote, even though the notice says that the game requires a controller, I must disagree with that: I played it with the keyboard and it works simply great) and it's extremely rewarding, besides being a necessary mean to develop with the story.
The difficulty of the game isn't particularly hard: there are tons of checkpoints and rarely you will be facing a potentially deadly situation, but I believe that is not a negative aspect, as it would lose its aura otherwise.
So what is Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons?
Is it a puzzle? A platform? A narrative game?
Is it even a game or perhaps a piece of virtual literature?
Perhaps it would require a genre of its own.
I don't know. I only know that this is a truly magnificent experience, and I am glad I had been a part of it.
Go hit "Add to cart" now, you'll thank me later.
They knew what they were doing. They know how to make a game.

This is not just a game, it's something that we as a person can go back and take a look at ourselves and see how things come into perspective.
Brothers-A Tale of Two Sons is a inmersive puzzle solving adventure game, with a beautiful art style and music fitting for each chapter and section of the game. It allows for a full-scale exploration, but certain features are still limited to only going along with the story.
You really connect with the two characters, and as you play you see how they grow and develop as a character. It feels weird, when one is missing and the game will always remind you of that, considering they can't move or go on without each other. We don't understand the language they speak, but we can still see it through their actions and expressions. You don't see much games in the market now, that is simple and have a plot that you can follow. The plot is rather simple, with the two brothers searching for a "magical" tree to save their father, but it gets more in-depth as you go along and see their past. You don't see much other characters, due to the fact the game is mainly centered around the other two, and the amount of people are also limited to a small selection.
Overall, it is one of the best games I play and I would recommend you to buy it, during a sale or for regular price.

Game is very fun, well presented and easily one of my favorites right now. It follows in the footsteps of 2d party fighter Smash Bros, but does not function like it. Differences end at presentation, because the attacks and characters are different and unique without feeling forced.
I would love to see more in terms of unlocks, and more to do with coins in the store because purchasing Legends will get old quickly. I'd love to see aesthetic accessories for characters. Maybe allowing a trade up for earned coins -> mammoth coins would be balanced as well, since keeping items behind a strict paywall while still calling the game "free to play" is a bit devious and unfair to users. A coin trade up would double the userbase for this game over night, as many players will not wish to pay for certain items with real money.
PROS:
- Great movement, everything is tuned and nothing feels "floaty". Your key presses matter!
- Combat is swift and learning is very easy. Second or third match and it's like you've been playing for years.
- Great presentation. Nothing glitching, no JPEG artifacts, no strange visual mishaps.
CONS:
- No in-match chat window. I'd love to quickly type messages as I'm respawning.
- More audio/visual/gameplay options in the options menu are needed.
- Unbalanced in-game store is very underwhelming when the rest of the package flows so well.
- "Free to Play" may be true but $115 of DLC says your experience is what you choose to pay for. Take that as you will.
Dispite my problems with paying for certain parts of the game as opposed to allowing a single purchase of a game and streamlining the whole process and experience, the game is fun and satisfies a real gaming itch! I really still highly recommend playing this game! (and I hope devs figure out a better Store/Loot system too.)

Full Review Below!
This game surprised me but in the best ways possible. I'm very glad I played this game. I was expecting a very short game with an intersting twist on gameplay, and I was surpriesed with a wondeful story. I feel bad because in my actual game play, I kept forgetting the names of everyone and pronounced the main brother's name wrong all the time. Luckly, I went back and go their names for the review below. I reccomend this game.
*****SPOILERS******
What is the actual story? (Spoilers)
Naiee, the younger brother, is paying respects to his fallen mother who had drowned at sea when his brother, Naia, calls him over because their father has gotten sick. Together, they take him to the town/ village doctor who examines the father. The only chance for them to save their father is to find water made by the Tree of Life. Throughout the journey, you will control both Naiee and Naia together in order to overcome challenges because there are some that Naiee cannot do on his own due to his height and strength where as Naia cannot do certain things because he is to big compared to his brother. The long journey takes them through the village, dungeons, the skies, a battlefield, a blood sacrificial ceremony, icy waters, spider’s web where Naia, unfortunately, takes a blow to the stomach, and ultimately ending up at the Tree of Life. Naia tells his brother to go on, and after a time, Naiee comes back to find his brother dead. Naiee buries Naia and flies back home to his village in order to save his father. The last shot of the game is where the father falls to his knees in sorrow for the loss of both his son and his wife while Naiee stands proud and strong, having mourned over his mother and brother already.
Now… on to the review!
Game-play?
This game is not multiplayer, rather, it is dual wielding: you control the older brother with W, A, S, D,  and Space while you control the younger brother with Up, Down, Left, Right and Right Control in order to solve these puzzles. The game-play for this game is interesting and unique in my opinion. The idea of controlling two characters at once in order to result in a singular outcome is a tough idea at first, but once you actually start to control them, it becomes a fun puzzle. For example, there are some times when Naia (older brother) cannot get into certain areas because he is to big to fit through the bars of gates, where as Naiee (younger brother) is smaller and easily able to fit in and out. The combination of sizes and different talents makes the double control of the two characters really fun. For a simple game with a powerful story, I say the game-play is very well done.
Graphics?
If you are looking for a game with graphics of realism, then this is not for you. The art style of this game is simple, but very good. It has an artistic element to it which changes it completely from a cartoon-like style, while still managing to make things real looking. This game does not weigh heavily on the graphics, but it doesn’t need too.
Vocals / Dialog
The game is not spoken in English… nor any other actual language in the game. The characters speak in a kind of made up language of sounds: for example, instead of answering, ‘yes’ or ‘yeah’ in response to a question, Naiee and Naia will answer with, ‘Dah’ or ‘Da’ depending. The only time you hear what sounds like English is when they call each others names. However, even though they have a more ‘sound’ based language, it is still every easy to understand what they are talking about just by watching and listening to the tone of their voices. I found it completely easy to understand, even though I didn’t understand the words, the actions spoke volumes, clearly narrating what was happening.
Characters?
There are a handful of main characters in this game:
Naiee – Younger Brother. Naieve, emotional, impulsive, but easily likable.
Naia – Older Brother. Strong willed. Cares about Naiee. Brave.
Father – Sick, but shows worry and care for his family.
Mother – Ghost seen very few times, acts as a helpful spirit seen by Naiee.
Doctor – Determined to help the boy’s father until the brothers get back.
There are other characters that appear, but those are the main focus.
How did I find this game?
Surprising. At first, I thought it would be a short, cute, beautiful adventure game with an interesting control twist. As I played, and as I found the challenges harder to overcome, I realized there is a darkness about this game that catches you off guard. One minute I’m running through beautiful fields, mountains, and flying a glider over rivers and sea only to end up in a bloody battlefield of dead giant solders all laying dead while the two brothers have to move their arms around just to get past the area. If that wasn’t dark enough, the game included a blood-alter sacrifical ceremony which threw me for a loop. Basically, when you thought this was all a happy-go-lucky game, it hits with you with a darkness and that carries you to the very sad ending. The ending, even though I should have expected it, caught me off guard. After all this time, you finally get to the ending and Naia dies right there at the Tree of Life and Naiee cannot save him, so he buries his brother instead and hitches a ride back to the village to save his father. I cried, I admit I did, because it was emotional and took me off guard. Games that make me elicit an emotional response are usually very good in my opinion.
Would you play this game again?
I would play it once or twice more, but no more after that. As far as replay value, I don’t think it’s too high. Definitely worth a try once.

Loren is an entertaining little game.
Compared to most RPGs, it plays quickly, which is to its advantage since the combat is bland. On the positive side, however, there are very few pointless fights with underlings. You usually can face the boss in 1-2 battles, moving on to the next part of the story.
The tale is written well enough, with a high level of replayablity. The player character will have different reactions based on being male and human or female and elf, obviously, but will also face difference based both on past occupation (there are 4 depending on the combo of class and workplace), and favored verbal approach (there are 3: Joking, Friendly, and Forceful). There's also a choice early on to work with either humans or elves, and that changes the first chapter of the story significantly, though it still dumps you back on the same main plotline.
The best part of this game is the characters. They have entertaining personalities as you get to know them better. And if you choose to romance them you'll get a good number of cut scenes that fill out their personalities. The best is probably our heroine, Loren, and the Amazon culture you're both a part of. Whether or not you romance her, she's the most rounded character in the game.
The game has between 3 and 5 different endings (depending on if you have the DLC), and lots of  minor variations based on the choices you make related to the group.
I'll also praise the incidental music for this story. It's appropriate and enjoyable. I can listen to it for hours.

Kingdoms of Amalur was one of those games that sat in my Steam library for a long time.  I’d often considered playing it, but… never did.  When I finally set myself to play it I really wasn’t expecting anything spectacular.  World of Warcraft style graphics covering an action RPG.  I kind of figured it would be little more than a linear hack and slash, with a couple of RPG-style tropes or choices as I fight my way to the boss … and then be done.
The world is quite large -- with multiple continents and biomes, and progression through each area feels linear, to be sure, but also natural.  While there are countless quests and an amazing amount of lore and stories to uncover, the two main story hooks for your character are:
Heh… Gadflow.
There are an incredible amount of NPCs with whom you can interact, and they are all voice acted.
Information, whether anecdotal snips or meaningful story content was provided in short, yet effective context.  I didn’t have to listen to excessive diatribes or minutes of meaningless exhibition for me to understand the character and for the NPC to get his or her point across.  Personally, I found the amount of information passed, while still feeling natural to the world, quite impressive in such short bursts.
Kingdoms of Amalur is an action RPG which uses a very simple timing mechanic to attack, block, dodge, or use an ability.  During combat, if your Fate meter is full, you can enter Reckoning Mode.  In reckoning mode time slows and even the hardest creature becomes your play thing.  Once the creature is defeated, and if you mash the appropriate button quickly enough, you can perform a pretty spectacular finishing move.
As the world is rather large, there is instant travel in the game to various cities, camps and points of interest.  There is also a rudimentary crafting and socketing system to create and upgrade weapons, armor, and potions.  You will also find housing in the game -- I owned a house, a mine, and a full fort (or keep) with inhabitants and quest giving NPCs, before all was said and done.
While KoA:R isn’t the deepest RPG ever made -- with every choice I make deciding the fate of the world -- it was an exceptionally full story experience.
Pros:
Cons:
A well done story-oriented game -- even as I review this at the end of 2017 -- hampered only by small UI issues, a never-before-used-in-the-game mechanic for the end boss fight, and the desire for a more meaningful use of the crating system.  I never felt the need or desire to craft more than a couple of potions or gems, and I kind of feel like that was a potentially large part of the game experience.

I would recommend this game.  I bought this game because I heard that a lot of people liked it better then Diablo 3.  While I still like Diablo 3 better this is a great game.  It is just complex enough to keep you looking for the next piece of loot, but it's also simple enough for a beginner to have a lot of fun even with no experience in RPGs.
The games story leaves a lot to be desired, but it makes up for it with the action.  The graphics look like they are from a pixar movie.  Just the way the characters are shaped makes it look like the Incredibles to me.  I love how gory the game is for how cartoon like the characters are.  It's definitely a pretty game.  That being said, the game will work on most modern computers with no problem.  Even with a lot of enemies on screen I never had any real problem with low framerates or slowdown or anything.
The fighting is like Diablo or Fate, which means it is really fun.  You find new weapons all the time and are always looking for new loot.  You can buy weapons or gems from traders in town.  Even with the socketable gems this game never gets as customizable or complicated as Diablo or PoE though.  Throughout my playthroughs I used weapons I found from chests or killing enemies and didn't really worry about socketing gems or anything like that.  Since there was so much variety in weapons dropped this was ok though.
The game is very easy on easy and normal modes.  If you have any experience with RPGs like this I would recommend starting on a harder difficulty because it will be too easy otherwise.  When you get to harder difficulties this game is really fun and even challenging at times.
Steam workshop is now available with mod support for this game.  There are a ton of mods, and I suggest to mod the game after you play through it the first time.  There are many classes, pets, dungeons, and other things on the steam workshop.  I ended up with Claptrap (from Borderlands) as my pet, and it was very fun.  There are mod packs out there that are designed so all the mods work together so I would look for one of those if you aren't that into modding.
The multplayer is over LAN or online.  You have to sign up for an account and remember a password to play online.  I wish it could automatically sign you in with your Steam information, but this is a small complaint.  Playing this game with 4 people is crazy and fun.  I'd recommend you play with some friends because randoms aren't that fun.  The community doesn't seem to be too helpful for new players.  But if you have 4 friends who want to play, I'd recommend getting a four pack and playing together.  I did run into a couple problems where I couldn't see that my friends were online when they were because of some server error.  I would often have to sign in and out 4 or 5 times just to connect to my friends.  This was annoying, but it always worked after I logged in and out a few times.
Overall, I would say this game is a must buy.  Great graphics, fun combat, and very fun co op, there isn't much reason not to pick up this game.  It comes on sale all the time, so keep your eyes open for a good deal.

Mod: Transmissions: Element 120
For the game: Half-Life 2
Developer and publisher: Shokunin Studios
Released: 16 June, 2016
Genre: First-Person Shooter with Horror
Canon status: Non-canon
Setting: 202X, an unnamed city, East Europe, Earth
Spoiler-free plot summary: After the events of Episode 2, you, Gordon Freeman, awaken to find yourself in a Combine-occupied city, and try to escape.
Full review: Transmissions: Element 120 is an hour-long mod for Half-Life 2. It isn't particularly difficult, or, despite being a horror mod, particularly scary.
Another Half-Life 2 mod, more typical Half-Life 2 gameplay of running-and-gunning and solving a few puzzles. The only new game mechanic introduced in Element 120 is a new Gravity Gun which, instead of pulling objects to you and pushing objects away from you, shoots out an overpowered Combine Energy Pellet which runs on the HEV suit's auxiliary power. This can pretty much be used as the only weapon in the game, but just in case you're trigger happy and run out of auxiliary power, you're provided with a crowbar, pistol, and other Half-Life 2 weapons.
A short, simple review for a short, simple mod. Do I recommend Element 120? Yes; it's higher in quality compared to other Half-Life mods, and it can entertain you for an hour. If Half-Life 2 is a meal and its episodes are dessert, then this mod is a breath mint; small and sweet.

This is by far the best Half-Life 2 mod I've ever played. The game features new areas and music that compliment the easter eggs within the game perfectly. However, the game lacks an in-depth story, leading the player to lose a motive to continue playing at some points. The game is brief (I 100%'d it in about an hour) and seems not meant to be replayed for a while after the first completion. Additionally, the game is puzzling at some point (not a bad thing) and requires the player to have some knowledge of mechanics from other Half-Life games as there is no introduction. In addition to previously known mechanics, the addition of the "Gravity Gun" gives the player unique opportunities such as gravity jumping. The game is well polished, but still has some areas that need some patchwork (there are some areas you can go into and remain stuck). Overall, a combination of polished gameplay, a to-the-point storyline, great new music, and a zero dollar price tag make the game a must-have for any Half-Life fans.

Amazing story driven FPS that in my opinion nearly equals Half Life 1 in terms of sheer amazing. You follow the role of Parker, a miner working at the Ultor facility on Mars. Ultor is a bunch of♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥and treats everyone like crap. Eventually, the miners revolt. Your job is to aid the revolution as best as you can, and call in the Earth Defense Force to free the miners permanently from their slavery. The journey takes you all over the surface (and under it) of Mars. From old dilapidated mines to secret plague generating labs, to a space station in orbit around Mars, you will have a blast with this game. For $2.50 there's no reason to not buy this.

The story is pretty thin, and the voice acting is somewhat horrendous, but decent overall. Very similar to the original Half Life, except with less puzzles and more shooting.
And I will admit, killing multiple enemies through walls with the Rail Driver is endlessly satisfying.

Back in 2001 when the game was first released, it was considered groundbreaking due to Voltion's GeoMod engine which allowed players to create paths around locked doors as well as blow out bridges when either a group of Ultor security guards walk over them or if its an APC.
And you also can pilot mining vehicles, submarines and other various vehicles in the game as well.
I highly recommend this game if you loved the later Red Faction games like Red Faction Guerrilla.

Trine 2 CS is an enchanting 2D side scroller game that steps into the realm of realism and jaw dropping graphics. Trine 2 bestow us with spectacular scenarios with ever changing level dynamics that shifts its paradigm with every level, the level of detail immerse you and binds you deeply into the game.
Trine 2 offers gameplay that is far more challenging and enticing than the previous version - Trine2 is a far cry from its predecessor in all the department and completely sets the benchmarks when it comes to 2D side scroller games. The lush , vibrant and detailed environment grasp you and moves you towards it. The Goblin Menace DLC deserves a special mention since it takes the game to a whole new level both in term of variety and features - loaded with new abilities and off the charts looks this is perhaps the best DLC ever created for any game.
Topped with brilliant music that soothes you and gels well with the game dynamics - the highs and low provide a perfect blend with the ever changing moments in the game. The really intriguing aspect of the game is the gameplay - a whopping 20+ hours of normal gameplay is not expected specially from an indie developer which obviously came as a surprise. You can stretch anywhere between 40-50 hours if you gunning for 100% achievements.
Aside from few lackluster boss level (which is good but not groundbreaking ) and some minor glitches here and there - Trine 2 is a gamer delight - oozing with beautiful graphics, bright colour, great gameplay with ever changing dynamics and tactics makes the game a must have item in your game library. Here's hoping that the next installment will be even more challenging and gorgeous than ever.

The Sims 3 is game that needs a bit of tweaking here and there to really get it going.
First up its pretty expensive so waiting for a sale is a given. I've spent a total of £37 on the game with both Seasons and Supernatural expansions. considering the vanilla game was £25 I'd say I got a great deal.
So! Pros and Cons!
Cons:
- The price, wait for the sale usually every summer/Christmas (or Halloween for supernatural!)
- The loading times can be really long, and they happen twice before you can play. (the more expansions, the longer loading)
- Limited or just plain ugly hair styles, especially for guys.
- Glitches (though I managed to fix a few) and sometimes the game crashed without warning. (gets worse per expansion)
- Few old features removed such as nanny and gardener. (I get they removed Gardner so you do it yourself but its dumb that you can't have one)
Pros:
- Create-a-style. The main reason the sims3 will always beat sims4. Almost everything is customisable. its incredible. Want a room with Victorian styled furniture but all with checked designs? pft. easy. done. you can even import your own designs into the game! this little feature truly makes it the best game ever.
- Mods are your best friend. I personally only get hairstyles/clothes type of mods and boy do they make a difference! and they are free! the modding community has some amazing stuff that can really add to the game. (just watch out for bad modders, can cause annoying glitches)
- Skills are better than before and have a nice synergy together, cooking goes well with gardening which goes well with fishing and so on.
- Aspiration points are a great, rewarding way to improve sims, without feeling like your cheating.
Overall, yes its expensive and yeah there are problems, but If you work you way around it you'll find yourself playing an awesome game!

TL:DR - It's a somewhat fun, free2play/pay2progress WW2 shooter that looks nothing like the screenshots and has a pretty toxic player base.
I want to like this game. I really do. But the more I play it, the less enthused I am about it. It feels quite like Battlefield 1942/3. However, it also looks like those games too. Oh yes, don't be fooled by the Steam bullshots. In-game graphics are nowhere near as good, even with the new render engine and everything maxed out. Graphics aren't everything in a game but it can be very hard to spot enemies at times because of the muddy, fuzzy quality of objects at range. Some maps are very brown, everything brown kind of blurs into each other, making it especially hard to spot Soviet players.
When you get a good game, it's a fantastic experience with moments like hiding in bushes as 3 Panzer tanks roll past just feet away from you. For the most part though, you'll just be getting steamrolled by veteran players. The new player experience really isn't very forgiving because matchmaking seems outright broken. Your first few games will see you on equal footing against other new players in a map with a single objective. As you level up, you will begin to notice other players killing you with things you don't have - grenades, a handgun, a scope, a melee weapon, a tank. This game doesn't start you off with anything besides a rifle. No pistol (have to unlock it then buy it). No grenades (unlock then buy them, then restock them after every game using in-game currecny). The odds are massively stacked against you as a new and free player and this 'skill' gap becomes more apparent the longer you play and the bigger the divide between your arsenal and your premium/veteran enemy's.
Standard weapons need modding in order to kill anyone in a timely manner (head shots aren't a OHK because people cried about it in the past) and these mods are quite a big cash sink for new players. As expected from a F2P game, everything is a drain on the currency you do earn to try and encourage you to spend real money. Weapons, for the most part, are 'balanced' between factions, but they have tiers you unlock with the higher tier generally being better. The stock T1 Greasgun for example is trash and is outclassed by a T2 Thompson or DE/USSR equivalent. But in order to unlock the T2 weapons, you have to persevere with the crappy T1 version. You'll likely have to spend money on mod to be competitive, or grind through with an inadequate weapon you hate until you finally unlock the T2  variant. Or of course, you can just get out your wallet and speed things up a bit.
Pushing into an objective is hard without the right weapons and with an M1 taking 2/3 hits to down an enemy at 100% health, you're gonna die fast facing an enemy who has an LMG or AR. Levelling is pathetically slow too. There's 0 reason to be at an objective unless you're capping it or the enemy is trying to take it. The gameplay is all about assaulting and capturing bases. Unless someone's coming for it, you're better off leaving because you'll get 0 XP sat there defending it. Heroes & Generals parades itself as a team game, yet there's absolutely nothing in-game aside from team/squad text chat for quickly communicating with your team. No voice chat. No quick message system. Squad leaders can tell their squad to attack or defend a point, but that's really it. Truck full of enemies rocking up to a point? Better stop what you're doing and type out a message like you're playing CS 1.6 (which actually had inbuilt VOIP!).
I can't speak for all factions, but USA has some pretty toxic, salty kids playing. This is to be expected in any FPS sadly, but the truth is new players get thrown into unbalanced matchmaking and often are just a liability because they have no idea what they're supposed to be doing and lack the firepower and tools necessary to help. And I honestly have no idea how matchmaking even works. You'll often find yourself in 20 vs 12 matches, or on a recon-heavy team whilst the enemy has infantry, paratroopers and tanks. Or you'll spawn into a game where one side has vehicles but the other only has default civilian transport (bicycles and a slow♥♥♥♥♥truck). Matches like this end in about 2 minutes because one side is able to quickly get to, capture and reinforce the middle point and force the other back to their spawn.
If you can tolerate it, you'll probably have fun once in a while but there are much better WW2 shooters out there. If you're gonna play it, probably best to play it with friends.

This is a curious game before it is a fun game.  At it's heart, it's a "follow the path" 3D platformer game, but not a difficult one.  You control both brothers at once, using a game console controller is a requirement... but the controls are really quite simple.  Jumping is automatic, and the few chances of dying actually reset quite forgivingly.
Turn down the music volume a bit (65 works), compared to the effects.  There isn't a subtitle option because the language is meant to be gibberish.
The first level is quite child-like dumbed down.
Then it's Prince of Persia parkour.
Mix in a little Zelda bosses (no real weapons in this game, trick your bosses).
Then it suddenly gets quite dark, quite morbid on an adult level.
Then it gets weird and spiritual.
Then it's banjo kazooie.
...and so forth.  Each chapter is very unique and forgiving only once you figure out the control bit.  As a result, replability is low, enjoy the original art the whole way through.  Story isn't really there.  You may or may not feel for the characters.  But it's a very beautiful world and a entertaining for the two gaming sessions it lasts (including going back for all achievements).  I'd say it's worth $5.

That being said. If I had to buy this game at full price, would I buy it? I wouldn't because you can finish the story quickly and easily. But at the discount price I got it at? Hell yes.

It's not often I see a good ol' fashioned text based RPG/Visual Novel like this, which also includes Drawn Illutstrations. I was actually moved by the nostalgia of the whole thing and I think I actually bought this game off-sale for that very reason... - That being said, I didn't really regret it - not very much, anyway...
The story is stereotypical, but I expected nothing less. And it's actually fairly well written, all things considered. Sure the art could be "shinier" and more detailed Sure the writing could be better, rosier or even more Novel-like. Sure the combat system could be more elaborate or in-depth and strategic. But- The question is, to all of the above, what the f for? Why put more spice on a cooked, seasoned meal?
I played through it a few times, experimenting with the difficulty, (and no, I didn't do all the endings yet, I'm saving it for a cold winter's day or something...) and, while a little long-winded and verbose, the story just plain works. It takes a good long while to build up, and it's a little challenging to wrap your head around how or why our "Heroes" get to have any part in saving the world, as anything other than a sidequest, but who cares... - You just roll with it, and have fun with it.
The story is interesting. It'll probably be even more interesting if you have or take the time to read it all.
The Graphics are good enough. The art is actually pretty good. It could have been better, we know, but it could've been OH so much worse...
The controls are... - well, if you're patient enough to learn how to use a turn based fighting system, it's difficult to mess up. It just takes time. It's not the most sophisticated system, but it doesn't have to be. It works.
The Funfactor is very, very, very, theme, concept and VN-based. The game is more RPG than VN, though you won't confuse it for any other RPG or JRPG.
Replayabillity: Given the simple fact that you can play again, with or without extra content, progressing in different ways, with different origins and even a different character (of a different sex,) there's obviously a good platform for replayabillity. - And if the Devs are of a mind, they might even add more on top of that...
As an RPG, LTAP is less than Average, but also more because of The Visual Novel element, which adds loads of ambience, locations, characters, plotlines, fights and outcomes than you'd care to do the probabillity math on.
It's not a game for everyone, but I urge those who like a good read, or a good bout of relaxed RPG, or perhaps even those who like both. (I happen to be one of those, so I have to assume others exist.)
This game takes time, (unless you just click away, in which case I can't fathom why you've bothered buying a VN tagged game in the first place,) so if you're going to get into it, make the time for it. - I'm not saying it'll be worth it, that's up to the individual, but if you rush, you won't have the chance to find out.

This review was initially postive but after rereading my review and thinking about what I've said and asking myself, "Do I really recommend this game?". The answer was no. After everything I typed, I thought "yeah, I had fun so I recommend it." but that was because I was fine with it. After reading what I put down, there was a lot of negatives so I thought about the people I would give it to, they wouldn't enjoy themselves. So after thinking about it, this review is negative.
I can't say anything about the graphics since I play everything except for the Texture Quality on low so everything but the officers look like♥♥♥♥♥♥because I have a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ computer. The gameplay itself is pretty much what you expect, you grab a weapon and pretty much kill everything in sight. The dlc weapons have come in without having to buy it which is quite nice like the bench, boots and the flame sword. So if you're expecting anything from the gameplay, you're pretty dumb to expect that. An issue that is known is that
will usually crash the game depending what menu your at. So be sure to save often since there's no autosave whatsoever or you'll have to restart.
The strategy in the game using strategems is actually quite nice. Some are more useful than others so you'll eventually have the 6 strategems you'll forever use. Large scale ones are quite good. They can either make or break a battle and it snowballs fast which I do enjoy and makes me feel like I deserve it especially when I'm losing. HOWEVER, ♥♥♥♥ any officer that has
(most notably Guan Yu) If I am disadvantageous in a battle and order everyone to defend. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ officer with that strategem will constantly use it and teleport in an enemy base inside enemy lines and proceed to say he's in trouble. Specific strategems for offense and defense like Fire Attack for advancing or Unity for defense should be used when the order is given, otherwise they just kill themselves.  The turn-based part of the Empire Mode is alright. I wish you could make alliances without it being a objective or that I could threaten another province without a specific officer having the ability to. As an officer, it feels like you're the only one doing anything like raiding and inviting officers which other officers do only if you're a ruler. They should've made it where like when you're a ruler, the ruler AI would make policies instead of invading every war council because being an officer is just a chore. You literally do all the work from invading because they can't take over a region without you, you do all the defending because they won't even try and they won't even try to increase your resources other than the guy that recruits troops randomly and he isn't even an officer. The shop, academy and blacksmith is kinda useless unless the prefect or strategist builds stuff for it which they won't and It involves having multiple ones. It honestly feels useless because gameplay is  easy already because the AI themselves aren't too great. They don't attack when you have an opening and are only a problem during 3 or more officers. After playing a couple more hours, I've noticed people take note of you if you're decimating them. What Koei should have done to make it rather interesting is that if someone notices how well you're doing they need to buff that officer and make him target you. When I say buff, I'm saying like double to attack, defense and speed and even super armor. (the super armor might be a bit much) And If they do beat you, there should be penalties like morale down. It would've made you feel like you were too good and you were enemy number 1. Instead they just say "Holy crap, that guy is really good!" and just keep doing what they were doing. They need to make it seem like we are really good and needed to be taken down. They also need to make enemies more aggressive and not scared to start swinging at you. I honestly felt there wasn't enough interactions between officers on and off the field. Like I would've liked my wife Wang Yi to at least not just give me a gift but also heal me by spending time together randomly like Dynasty Warriors 6 Empires. It felt like she could see I was working real hard and needed a break. Also being, there is dialogue for someone finding you suspicous however, I never could find where it would've been said. Even when I make my own ruler exile like 15 officers and make most of the regions unhappy. None of them say anything about it or even try to make them happy. No one really notices your actions and if they do, it's just the enemy and ask you to join them. Like no one has ever requested reinforcements, requested a joint attack, and no one has appeared as a guard.
Alright, now for the character customization. It's fairly good with many choices. You can make a variety of outfits, have many different looks and use all movesets, EX attacks and musou from both Dynasty Warriors 7 and 8 including the 2nd EX attacks from Dynasty Warriors 8 Extreme Legends. What I feel is like a miss was that you couldn't change what weapon type the weapon had like the Spear had whirlwind or that the Dragon Spear had dive. It would've been nice to switch some of these weapon types to make it feel more personalized. I personally love the moveset of the Double Voulge but I hate whirlwind. The customization for horses, banners and soldier are quite bland, nothing really special. I do like downloading other peoples custom characters they upload. A lot of them are pretty cool. You can see a lot of funny ones like I downloaded a custom group that were all Dwarves. The only complaints I have with the customization might just be personal reasons but I found the voices kinda unexpected. As in, I wish there was a gallery alongside the other Musou characters where it displayed their lines like the line they say when a battle starts. Also, there should've been at least 2 voices of an evil type. I wanted to make an evil character and the voice I thought sounded the most evil ended up saying "I'll be the light" or something like that so it was really disappointing.
Overall, the game needs lots of work. It decided to do something different and overall, didn't do every well. It lacks things present in the other Empire titles. If you're a big fan like I am, you'll probably buy it but you'll know what you're stepping into. If you're not a fan then just steer clear of this one. If you're still curious about Dynasty Warriors, I'd say buy Dynasty Warriors 8 Extreme Legends since it has way more to offer and gives a good introduction to the Three Kingdoms.

Trine 2 wasn't really on my radar, but I found myself the owner of the game after it was lumped into one of those bundled sales.  Having never played Trine 1, I was able to jump into Trine 2 feeling as if I hadn't missed anything important.  Immediately you notice how gorgeous the fairy tale graphics are, and I have to admit I am a sucker for this style of art work.  At times I find myself stopping play just to admire the stunning art work.
Trine 2  is a puzzle platform game where you can constantly switch among three characters each with unique skills that complement each other -- and that's what sets this apart from other platform puzzle games.  In many cases there are more than one way to solve the puzzle so you can often stick with the character that matches your style.  In addition to puzzles there are semi-hidden chests and orbs that grant you points to upgrade your abilities.  I think finding the hidden stuff was one of the top high lights of the game.
The game also mixes in fight and boss sequences giving a nice balance between puzzle solving and action.  Thus I found the game more enjoyable than say a pure puzzle platform game like Limbo.  The game includes several achievements as well as a multiplayer mode giving you many hours of enjoyment.  Highly recommended.

As a longtime fan of Deus Ex, going back to the original in 2000, I may be a little biased, but overall DE: Mankind Divided is a good game. Not great, but good and I'll tell you why.  As soon as I started playing, I could not put it down.  I clocked in at 40 something hours for the main story, doing all the sidequests and reading every E-book I can.  The game has amazing atmosphere and draws you in.  It encourages you to develop your cool new augmentations and use them to hack stuff, turn invisible, jump to places you could not previously get to.  Prague, the main hub, has a ton to do with many sidequests.  Main missions and side missions feel alive and you feel like you actually make an impact once you complete them especially if you "do it right", using the CASIE mod to convince some character the folly of their ways.
The main negative is that the game is simply too damn short.  Go back to the original Deus Ex and see how long it takes to complete, while doing side quests and reading every book. I definitely think it would take longer that 30-40 hours.  The ending feels cut off...ok so you got the main bad guy, but wait I thought there were all these illuminati and billionaires pulling strings in the shadows? You never get a chance to go after them, even though the game introduces them.  Namely Bob Page, Lucius DeBeers and Manderley.  Seems like we got some big dumb tank out of the picture, but the real culprits got away. Um maybe another title 3 years from now and another $60 is what we will have to spend to get the REAL ending?

I wouldn't describe Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons as a video game. It's a movie like experience which requires a controller in your
hands.
While the store page mentions that a controller is required, the game works fine with just a keyboard. In fact, I had trouble getting the game to work with a controller in the first place. But I'd say that a controller is absolutely necessary.
During the game you control two brothers simultaneously, a big and a young one. Each half of the controller is dedicated to one of the brothers. After a few minutes the controls feel natural and I didn't encounter too many problems except when a device needs both brothers to control it. I often ended up with one brother on the "wrong" side, which the game did not allow.
During your journey you encounter many puzzles which are centered around the "Singleplayer co-op" premise. It uses the different characteristics of the brothers. The big brother is strong but bigger, so he's the one that pulls the levers. The small brother has a smaller posture, so he's able to fit in small/tight places. These puzzles don´t take long to figure out and I don´t think the average gamer will be challenged by this game. Only one puzzle really stuck with me, and there's a big chance you´ve already seen most puzzles in other games before. They focus more on the "Oh, that's cool!" factor.
Combat, except for two "boss fights", is non-existent. Because of this there is also pretty much no replay value, unless you want to experience the story again. I did went back to collect the achievements I missed but these didn't add a lot to the game.
The slow nature of the game doesn't make the game for everyone though. It's comparable to games like Limbo, Journey and Gone Home.
These gameplay elements, while fun to watch, aren't what makes the game great though.
The story is pretty bare-bones: the brothers lost their mother and now their father is sick. The only thing that can heal him is juice from a big "godlike" tree on the other side of the world. And thus the brothers go on a slow paced, but epic, journey. Besides a dream sequence, there's not much here to make you think twice.
It all builds up to the climax, which is pretty predictable. But the way they deal with this is brilliant and what makes this game so memorable. It really uses what you've learned and how you used the controller, which is why this story can only be told via a video game.
I implore you to not watch any videos of this game and experience it all first hand.
Where the game really shines is the world. During the 3 hours duration of the game you explore a collection of beautiful and varied landscapes. This goes from your standard forest and snowy areas, to a battlefield still brimmed with corpses, all designed very well with tons of colours. I won't spoil too much, because they're really fun to discover yourself.
You encounter a small cast of interesting characters, varying from humans to animals to trolls.
The brothers each have a distinct personality and this is seen when each brother interacts with the world and it's characters. The big brother is more serious, while the small brother is very playful and light hearted.
This game is very pretty to look at. The character models aren't particulary high quality, but you won't see them up close too often. The lightning and art direction are beautiful, though. During a particular sequence a large foorprint could be seen in the snow, and the way the lightning interacts with it made me stop and admire it.
The world is littered with benches, even on places where it doesn't make sense. So there are always moments to sit back and enjoy the scene it's looking over.
The music in this game fits the atmosphere and the world very well. There weren't any songs that really stuck with me, but there weren't any boring or annoying songs in the game either.
Treat it like a movie: dedicate an evening to this game, sit back on your couch and play it in one sitting. It's a game everyone should at least try out. And for €1.49, can you really go wrong?

Have you experienced your body tremble, not because of the cold winter breath brushing your naked skin. But because your body is ridden with sorrow and sadness?

Your nails will break. Your fingers, cracked. And your hands, bleeding.
You won't even feel any physical pain.  If.  That was your concerns.
Nay, you wouldn't even feel the frostbites.

Is one thing.
..

Someone once said that "To Save a man means to Risk your own"

you lose
of your Control.

Having played most of the games by Winter Wolves, I would say that, without a doubt, Loren: The Amazon Princess is the best game that has come out. After I finished Plant Stronghold by the same developer, I liked that game a lot and so was looking forward to Loren and sure enough, it didn't disappoint me. Out of all the games in my Steam library, this one has been played the most. For those wondering why I put in so many hours, I wanted to play all the romance paths without taking any shortcuts. Otherwise, my play time would have been much shorter. Also, I wanted to get as much of the experience trying out the different fighter classes, customizing characters, etc.
Upon first glance, this game sort of made me think of the Lord of the Rings series because it is classified as an epic fantasy and I tend to think of LoTR as the same. However, there are noteable differences and additions in Loren that make it nothing like LoTR.
I like how you can start customizing your playable character, choosing to play as either a male or female and determining the fighter classes and stats. As you progress in the game, you can recruit up to 11 characters to join you on your journey. (This is assuming that you purchase the DLC in addition to the base game. I would recommend buying the DLC, btw, as it gives an additional side story and thus allows for longer gameplay.) The quests you complete will give you experience points (standard for any RPG) which allows you to level up your characters accordingly. You can either go through one playthrough using the same characters or switch them up. I found that I used basically the same characters for most of the quests although for certain ones, I had no choice but to switch them up.
Since other reviews have summarized what Loren is about, I won't repeat that. Instead, I'd like to say how much I enjoyed this game. However, it did have some weaknesses. At times, I noticed that there were typos and repetition of words which should have been corrected by a proofreader. Although there weren't a lot, there were some and it would be beneficial to the developer if they were corrected in a future update to make reading the story easier.
Also, I have to admit that there were times I thought the character development could have been improved. For instance, at the beginning of the game, Loren comes off as stubborn and seemingly all knowing (even though she clearly is not). I had hoped that Loren would have become less stubborn as the game progressed and although there were times that she did, there were instances late in the game where she would suddenly become stubborn again and that annoyed me. Of course, this could be more of a preference on my part. I prefer characters that grow for the better rather than continue to have a static personality. There were other characters who had the problem of having a static personality as well but as Loren is one of the main characters, I had hoped that she would have developed and matured more as a person. Although the game says that she does, I couldn't see it so well for myself (or there weren't enough instances to show me otherwise). Having heard that there is going to be a sequel for this game, I hope we'll get to see a more mature, wiser Loren.
Finally, again, this is more of a personal preference than anything but I wish the art style had been somewhat different in regards to the characters. I wasn't a fan of how the majority of the women were portrayed since I would have liked to have seen different body styles to show more realistic versions of women.
Despite my criticisms, though, I did enjoy Loren very much and had lots of fun with the battles as well as interacting with most of the characters. I can tell that a lot of time and effort went into this game and it paid off. I would highly recommend this game to anyone who likes RPGs and also likes visual novels, as there are some of those aspects here as well, such as romancing certain characters. (Of course, it's not necessary to pursue a romance at all but it makes the game all the more enjoyable if you do so.)

In short: get it on a high-discount sale if you're a big VN fan and like solid characters and can forgive a weak plot and grinding combat.
The characters are the strongest point of the game, maybe the ONLY strong point. The story itself is weak and jumps from point to point without any real sense of justification or getting you emotionally involved. When characters speak, they're believable and consistent, and I swear I laugh out loud every time Draco talks (he's definitely my favorite). But the bits of narrative that move the story along have no sense of creative description, relying on "telling" you the story rather than "showing" it. Plot points are revealed in advance by the narrator, rather than organically exposed by playing the game.
The combat is awful. I tried both modes available but eventually just slapped the game down on "easy" so I could click through them as quickly as possible. The sound effects are repetitive and any "strategy" is a joke. I don't even think the RNG works. There's repeatable in-town battles you can do for money and XP, and as I grinded the same battle about a dozen times, I noticed that despite a given range of possible damage whenever I mouseovered an attack (a range of about 80 or so), the damage ended up being rolled the same number EVERY SINGLE TIME.
I do like seeing how scenes change according to my character's personality, mostly in the sense of their interaction with the other characters, but the story they're all set in is just bland as can be.

Yes, the story is cliche, and yeah the turn-based combat was shallow, but I truly enjoyed my time with Loren the Amazon Princess. The story, artwork, and music are all simple, but done well. This game is the definition of a simple but very solid RPG/Visual novel. I would reccomend this vehemently, but especially to people like me, who have limited experience with Visual Novels.

This game is great!  I haven't played many visual novels, but after the strong recommendation of a friend I gave Loren a try.   It's been more fun than I expected, I've gifted it to a couple friends hoping they enjoy it, too.
The blending of RPG and visual novel is really well done, and the pacing is such that you can decide how much you want to do and when.  In fact, this is one of the things I like about it the most--once you get rolling, you can take it in bite-sized pieces, or sit down for a marathon, it's up to you.  The ability to save anywhere, plus lots of places to explore, shop, or grind means you have plenty to enjoy (and stop and start up again instantly).
The characters are interesting and varied, and there are enough fights that you can try all sorts of combos and give everyone a chance to be used.  I would have liked a way to reset skill points after I figured out what works and what doesn't work nearly as well, but that's what additional playthroughs are for, I guess (and if I missed a way to reset them, let me know).
The writing is strong, the story interesting enough to keep you going, and the romances fun to pursue while everything else is going on.  You can also unlock an uncensored version painlessly (see the forums for more) if you prefer a little hot sauce (and I do mean a little, imo it's just for fun and not so over-the-top that it's distracting).   And about the romances, I liked all the ones I pursued.  While you can't do every combination, there are enough choices for all tastes to keep it interesting.
What else can I say?  Well, I'll repeat that the combat is surprisingly enjoyable.  It's a simple system, but it's a rewarding one, and if you put in enough time you can become so strong you don't even have to know what you're doing (heheh).   Gearing up, powering up, and trying out all sorts of party members was a joy.  Finally, the ending was superb.  I really felt it was worth all my investment into the game and it was both satisfying and moving.
Good job, Winter Wolves!  Looking forward to Loren 2.  :)

For me the deverloper WInter Wolves is mostly known for it's Heileen series that were okayish VN games but nothing special to really remember in the longer run. 10/10 game that now sets the bar for other VN games that try to flesh out by adding RPG elements. This is the way it should be done!
