RWBY is a game I wish was fun, but it's not.

The combat is about as boring and shallow as God of War. Attacks were designed in a similar fashion as a Dynasty Warriors game, you have a light attack button that throws out a combo and a heavy attack button that does a chargeable attack and various attacks based on how far into the light attack combo you are. There's no way to string attacks together and no incentive (like a style score or being useful for different scenarios) to vary up your attacks, so there's no reason not to just whatever combo does the most damage or has the best crowd control.
You also have a dodge that doubles as a sprint button when held, a ranged attack that's not worth using unless you just don't want to deal with something, and a garbage parry mechanic. The dodge works fine, it has iframes like a dodge should but there's not much to say about it. The ranged attacks can stun depending on your character, but if you can use melee attacks then you may as well just smack 'em around. The parry lets you block certain attacks to stun enemies. I say that because other action games like Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, or Metal Gear Rising rewards you for waiting until the very last second - no, frame - to defend yourself. Playing like that here will get you killed as the window to parry ends
the attack comes out. A better way to handle the controls would be something like what the aforementioned games where almost all attacks have their own input method that allows you to chain attacks together and make your own combos.
The health system is bad. It rechargeable like in most FPS games. This means that you're incentivized to run away like a coward when low on health and you don't have much health to begin with. I understand that it seems to be like this for lore reasons, but I still think the health should have worked differently. I would go with something that requires items or health drops to recover while having a bigger health bar. Maybe only having health recovery when a fight ends.

First and foremost, enemies can and (especially on higher difficulties) will attack you from off screen. This is highlighted best by the three-legged enemies that can burrow underground and attack out of nowhere with little to no warning. There's an audio cue, but that's only for parryable attacks. An easy fix without changing the game itself would be to just zoom out the camera to make it easier to see around you, but ideally enemies just shouldn't attack while off screen.
As the game goes on, it introduces enemies that explode when killed, and parrying their attacks is a sure fire way to make sure they explode in your face since parrying teleports you towards the enemies. These enemies shouldn't have parryable attacks of any kind.
There's also enemies that have a lot of unparryable attacks and very short windows to even identify attacks let alone deal with them. I haven't tested it (so don't take my word for it, please) but it seems like some of their attacks are even too fast to react to. You are given less a fraction of a second to identify whether the attack can be parried and act accordingly. The fact that the the parry window ends before the attack comes out means you have even less time to react, then you also have to consider input lag taking up a few frames and you're left with attacks that are more difficult to react to than they should be. If the parry didn't depend on a QTE to work and rewarded well timed parries, this may have seemed more fair. Enemies having attacks that need to be dodged in different ways would also allow for more time to react while still being challenging, maybe even have some projectiles that can be deflected.
Then there's the higher difficulties where the devs seem to carelessly throw hordes of enemies at you. All attacking at the same time and from off screen. It's absolutely frustrating to deal with as one hit can get you stuck in hitstun as enemies chew through your health. There are several different things that could have been done to fix this. Having greater areas of affect for attacks would have made it easier to manage the crowds. When you're attacked, either you should be knocked away, be able to break out of a combo, or just have a chance to defend yourself in some way.

The game is short, super short. It should take you a few hours to complete. There's almost nothing outside of the game's combat. You can go off the beaten path for s little extra xp, but that's it. It's just going to the next fight. If the combat were any good then I would count this as a good thing. There's a story, too. But it's sort of just, well, there.

Okay, there actually are some tricks I found while playing. Since holding dodge makes you walk faster, I got into the habit of holding the button at all times, releasing it only to press it again when I need to dodge. Dodges in the air cover more distance than on the ground. Stunned enemies take additional damage on the next attack, so you have to charge a heave attack to take advantage of it. There's probably more that I can't think of. Finding then incorporating these into my gameplay was fun and satisfying. If there's ever a sequel, adding some depth like this would make the game more enjoyable.

NOTE: Skip the first paragraph if you know what the game is about. It is a simple basic summary to describe the game for the unknowing minds. The actual review begins in the second paragraph.
RWBY: Grimm Eclipse is a 4 player beat-em-up game based on the Rooster Teeth show "RWBY". In the current version of the game (the date of this review is October 8th 2016), there are four playable characters; Ruby Rose, Weiss Schnee, Blake Belladonna, and Yang Xiao Long, all apart of a team in the show known as team RWBY. There are two modes that both follow the same campaign, being Singleplayer and Multiplayer (up to 4 players can join). There are no AI teammates if one or more are lacking. The game features a level-up system that maxes out at 10 and a skill system where you gain skillpoints per level and unlock skills through an amount of points or by completing an achievement AND using points. There's also a ranking system, however I do not know much about it. That's a basic summary, onto the actual review part.
As a newer RWBY fan, I was really excited to play this so I picked it up last night and began playing. Note that I only played as Ruby throughout my playthrough. There are 10 levels where you kill monsters (known as Grimm) for experience and complete objectives such as defending a control point for a few "waves" of Grimm. By completing these, you progress in the level. There are bosses/minibosses in the levels that appear in the waves. The game is a beat-em-up and that's what you do: beat monsters up, level up, and complete the level. Pretty normal. Here are some pros and cons of the game.
Pros:
-Four playable characters (team RWBY). Soon to be 8 playable characters as team JNPR DLC is added along with Horde mode.
-Fun beat-em-up you can play with a few friends or by yourself.
-Great voice acting.
-Really nice graphics.
-Great devs that are responding to the community and listening to their opinions.
Cons
-Story is meh. Not terrible but it isn't in-depth.
-No unlockable/purchasable costumes for characters.
-Not a ton of skills.
-Gameplay can be quite repetitive.
-High price tag.
-The final boss is horribly designed and should be rebalanced or reworked. Can be very difficult for Singleplayer players.
-Gameplay can be a kitefest.
As it stands right now, RWBY: Grimm Eclipse is likely not worth the $28.00 CAD price tag. It definitely is fun, however it took me approximately 4-5 hours to complete in Singleplayer mode playing as Ruby. There is a lot of kiting of enemies in this game, just a heads up. As for other things to do, there isn't much. Fortunately, they are adding new content, being new characters and a new mode (see Pros list). The new mode will be in a free update and it is rumored that the character DLC will be $4.99 (USD?) for the new team. Besides that, the game lacks content. No costumes, no new skills for the already small skill trees, and lack of modes.
I personally enjoyed the game up into the final boss fight. This final boss had me tearing my hair out. I'm not going to spoil what it is, but you can search it up if you'd like. I spent loads of time kiting it in the later stages of the fight and I lost multiple times due to the fact that an enemy that is spawned alongside the boss is actually way harder to deal with than the boss itself (the enemy is red, not going to spoil it exactly). I eventually beat it and huzzah, the game was over.
If you're a big RWBY fan and want to kick Grimm♥♥♥♥♥ buy the game. If you aren't, or if you just dislike that $28.00 CAD price tag, wait for it to lower/go on sale or for them to add more content to the game (I will likely update the review with the new update). I'd personally recommend the game, but it certainly has issues you should be wary of.
My rating: 7/10

My thoughts in 50 words or fewer:
What drew me to Loren the Amazon Princess was that I wasn't the main character, that my job was to make sure everyone else stayed alive. Though the combat was nice, it wasn't anything special. It was the story and character development that really sucked me into it.

(To those of you worried about my play time, I play most of my games in offline mode)
(For people who want to know how to get the uncensored version [you know who you are],
)
This game is an interesting one.  The story is lots of fun and the branching endings give it a surprising ammount of replayability, ut what really keeps me coming back is the combat.  It's turn-based and entirely minimalistic, but oh man, it's a very fun system.  I've gone through two run-throughs of this game and I've realized that that was part of the reason that I loved this so much.  It's amazingly done, especially considering the game was built in Ren'Py.
While I wouldn't recommend this game to everyone, pick it up if you want a solid game that has plenty of hidden content that will keep you coming back for more every time you find out something new.

In Short: if you enjoy fantasy RPGs, Dungeons and Dragons, party member interactions, and/or romance subplots then you will likely enjoy Loren the Amazon Princess.
The Pros
There is a long list of party members to choose from to customize your combat style.
There are a variety of locations and enemy types to keep the game from stagnating.
You may choose between three conversation responses to give your character a bit of color.
There are multiple romance options to choose from and each feel well fleshed out.
There are points where your choices feel like they have weight on the plot and characters.
The Cons
The game's art style leans a little too heavily on burly men and busty women, both in revealing, ineffectual armor. Not that I entirely disapprove, but it's a little too overt.
Replaying immediately after beating the game is a bit tedious, at least at the beginning. I'm skipping a lot of dialogue so I can get back into the heart of the story.
I would have liked to see more variety for the protagonist's class, and build options.
It has several cringe-worthy 'romance' moments - the kind where you hope no one is reading over your shoulder.

When evaluating the game, it is necessary to make a distinction between the game itself and the fluff that surrounds it.
Is the DLC/Preoder fluff situation abhorent? Almost definitely. Single-use boosts should have no place in a single player game. Is the in-game shop bad? Yeah, but it is completely ignorable.
Now, the game itself is brilliant. Not Witcher 3-level brilliant and definitely lacks polish, but brilliant nonethless. The level design is superb, the side missions are engaging and the gameplay is stellar.
The narrative of the game does feel unfinished/rushed, but still tells a cohesive story-arc. With some extra exploration done, the world truly comes to live—it is very well-built.
If you are looking for well-spent 25 or so hours, the game is worth it. Though I would definitely recommend getting it on sale—$60 is too much for it.

Well, where should I start? I have to admit, that this game is well-made. Of course, it has some problems on the launch like FPS drops and minor glitches, but, actually, it is completely playable.
So, frankly, I anticipated this game very much and expected it to be longer, than it turned out to be. (I do really hope that DLCs will expand main story) Also, I thought this game was going to be a link between Human Revolution and original Deus Ex, but it seems, that a lot of stuff remains untold... yet.
Pros:
*Memorable and interesting quests (Cult of Personality, for example)
*Highly detailed locations such as Golem City, Prague and beautiful
character models
*More cinematic approach in storytelling
*
*Improved gameplay (guns now shoot much better, but I still prefer Non-Lethal Ghost approach)
*
*Astonishing soundtrack
*Russian mobsters (AT LONG LAST!) voiced by russian voice actors (I've clearly heard Peter Ivashchenko)
*Vast variety of ways to complete a mission (you can go guns blazing or sneak-'n-hack). Level design is amazing
Cons:
*Adam's stories (a directory, which gives you access to DLC missions) are not integrated into the game, what ruins the flow of story
*Cliffhanger - game ends at the moment, when things become quite intriguing
*Only one boss in main story (Second boss might be encountered in the side-mission)
*Less global story as it mainly concerns Czech Republic
*Some locations aside from city hub are poorly-made (GARM Factory and London)
*Main story is quite short, but thanks to Side-missions the game has a lot to offer
So, in the conclusion, I'd like to say that I really enjoyed that game and I can't wait to see a continuation to the story.

1. Plenty of free DLC content, with replayability, fun toys and a few nice quality of life improvements. Except all of it is multiplayer only.
2. Players in multiplayer are actively incentivized to prevent other players from making money.
3. There are tons of hackers in every other multiplayer lobby, often making it unplayable (and potentially exposing other players to the very strict ban policy).
4. You know how FTP games are generally a lot more expensive than normal games? Yeah, prime example. The most recent upgrade, Gunrunning, would cost you around 400$ or 320 hours of making in-game money (or around 200 hours of pure no-fun farming). That's avoiding #2 and #3 above and assuming you ain't big on cosmetic upgrades. Oh, and if all you want is just one fancy toy from the update, you can't buy it on its own: its useless without a certain (costly) upgrade, which is unlocked through random (costly) research, and then you need a bunker (costly) to do research, and then you need a special new workshop (costly) to install the said upgrade, and then this workshop can only be deployed inside a new truck (costly)... You see where I'm going by now.
5. How do the new updates to the game greet you? Right, with a black loading screen with a huge notice about what they'll do to you if you try to cheat. Yep, gaming mood going, going, gone...
6. Take Two and Rockstar pretty much spit into the customers faces by issuing a cease and desist vs Open IV - modding tool that allowed the community to at least try to address #1 above; they essentially banned modding for single-player.
All things considered, here's hoping to The Elder Scrolls: Vice City.

There are UPS and DOWNS:
DOWNS (FIRST):
1) The graphics for this game is quite inappropriate for PC and I mean this because the graphics for XL PC Version and Empires look quite different (XL looks much cleaner).
2) It MAY become a bit repetitive. Which may get a bit boring...
3) There is no given STORY. Beware! This game makes YOU start a story and make YOU finish it (So nothing historical)

2) The Event battles have upgraded to top-notch excitement from its previous boring ones. This actually excites me when playing these battles.
3) Nice improvement in PERSONAL relationships. I mean this as Character-to-Character system. This includes, Sworn-Siblings, Spouses and Children in the game. It brings out a great perspective of how to be a leader as well as being a good PERSON.
OVERALL, the game is good. I give it 8/10. Just the graphics and the story being a bit short just bugs me. However, It is their FIRST Updated Empires game of the series for PC since DW4E and they WILL (I hope) improve in the future. Just give them a chance and as for YOU, I recommend this game, TRY IT!

This is the sloppiest game I've ever seen Koei's name on. I'm talking 70% budget cut sloppy. But I've still enjoyed it.
~Pros~
-Improved character creator
-The whole in-battle strategems system works smoothly in this edition
-Downloading and sharing created characters online is a cool new feature
-The characters and all weapons play nicely, with fun combo and special attacks
-The framerate is quite good, considering how laggy older entries could get
~Cons~
-If you so much as minimize this edition of the game in menus, the whole thing crashes
-Character lines have been reduced tenfold
-There's a whole 5 historical scenarios when you buy the game
-There aren't actually any proper videos I've encountered yet (not referring the cheap sub in various officer clips either where the troops raise their spears), not even for major historical battles, when there have been up to 20-ish in other Empires games
-The game contains Japanese voice acting only, the English dubs were a nice option in older entries
-You pay over 50 bucks for the game, without any form of online play which you would get on the XBox version
-The PC optimization of this game is a mess
Koei needs to look back to the days of SW2E, or DW5E to see how an empires game should really be done, this game overall is a pretty large step back from how good empires games used to be, and I believe still can be. I'm still enjoying the game far more than I should be, despite the several incredibly disappointing aspects. If you're a sucker for warriors games like I am you should still find plenty of enjoyment in this installment, but only get it when it's on sale of course as this is closer to a $25 game at most, not a whopping $55 one.

It's a  a fun and simple platform brawler. However it may not appeal to all, especially those wanting more of a deep and complex fighting game experience. Smash bros is already a casual fighting game, Brawlhalla is even more simpler than that.  But if you never tried anything like smash bros, this might appeal to you. For now they seem to stick to their ad: No Pay to Win. No Pay to Play. No hidden fees. No monthly costs. No pay walls. No  gimmicks. If you ever feel cheated when grand chase and elsword was advertised as a BALANCED free to play fighting game(which is terribly unbalanced salt generating p2win game), or certain mobas just unecessary nerfing/buffing certain characters just to make the game feel different. Brawlhalla will wash away(hopefully) the bitterness gained from those games. The characters are balanced, there aren't any "cheap" characters so far. It's not an action rpg like elsword/grandchase so there's no gear disparity in game.
Pros
-Free to play (characters are unlocked via in game currency or cash from store, free rotational characters per week) no game breaking items in cash shop
-Simple and solid balanced fighting game, all the characters have equal winning chances against each other
- Great cartoon visuals
- good music
- chat disabled during fights (less salt generated from salty players)
- multiple ways to play: offline, free for all, 1v1,2v2
- easy to learn
- compatible with gamepads

Cons
-It's a casual game. The game might not appeal to players who are looking for a deep fighting experience. Even smash bro, a casual game offers a deep combat compared to Brawlhalla's
- The characters  feel a bit  copy pasted. there's not much mastery needed to play every character effectively. It feels as if there's no  real "playstyle" to mess around with the characters.  Example, Link plays differently from Marth although they both use swords, Ken and Ryu both uses hadouken but they have different playstyles. Traditional fighting game characters have their own unique supers, there's none of that here. If this would be a moba it feels like it would be a moba  where heroes don't have ults and only basic skills to use.
Suggestions:
The game mechanics are fine, it is a casual game after all, but the characters really need something. maybe a unique move for each character? Unique visuals,passive stats and weapons are not enough. We need something more exciting for each characters. Like having that feeling when facing a certain character, and you have to be wary of what his/her shenanigans are. Give characters their turn-the-tides moves, like a proper counter attack move, a teleport,something truly their own and not a  just sparkly attack. each character does have these, but I feel like it's a little lacking,even something like a fatality move would help the characters be recognized. some Voiceovers would be nice addition too.
on free for all, I believe we need more crazy here like how crazy smash bro is, Crazy changing stages, random stuff going on, explosions, random items and possibly a smash ball.
this is just a minor one, But I would like an option to put the life bar on the lower left, instead of the upper right corner.
If possible make it percentage too, honestly I don't  notice when will me or my opponents  will be killed by a final blow. the life bar icon's a bit small for me, and I honestly prefer it be percentage in big text instead.
Overall as a casual game it is good, so I would still recommend it, however for those looking for the usual complexities of fighting games, it's best to find it elsewhere. Despite being simple if you're in for  casual fun, Brawlhalla still delivers.

A Rose in the Twilight is a puzzle-platformer, where you solve puzzles by switching between two playable characters. Each character has their own traits and abilities.
The game is set in a cursed world, where everything has lost its color and consequently, is frozen in time. Only by returning something its color you can make it move again.
The main playable character is Rose. One day, she wakes up among the ruins of some old castle and starts to wander around. At first it's not clear why everything's like this, but gradually the story will unfold, revealing the accident which made the place the way you see it now — colorless and still.
The lack of color is caused by the thorns, parasitic flowers which overgrown the castle. These thorns drain color from everything they attach theselves to. They've attached to Rose, too. One of the thorned flowers grows on her own body, like a stigma.
But this flower doesn't only live off Roses color, it also provides her with some of its own abilities. Thanks to that, Rose can also drain color from objects, freezing them, and imbue it back to make them move again. Working with color and time is one of the game's core puzzle mechanics. Another ability Rose gained from that flower is that she can now interact with some of the other flowers. For example, a crystal "checkpoint" flower will bring her back to life whenever she dies.
The other playable character is the giant. Rose finds it drained of color, somewhere among the ruins. She then gifts it some color and giant comes alive. The giant perceives as it's duty to follow and protect Rose — and from now on you can switch controls to it. Unlike fragile Rose, giant is invincible to
all of game hazards. It's also a poweful creature, so it can lift, move and throw different object and items, including Rose herself.
As you may've sensed already, the tone and the story of this game is somewhat dark.
Everything around is dead, still and bleak. The red color which you control is also not a random choice — blood plays a significant part in this game, and there are situations where Rose needs to draw her own blood by killing herself
. Another use of blood in this game is for memories. During exploration you'll encounter bodies of the fallen, and Rose will be able to read their memories by taking in their blood. These memories are presented as short cutscenes, arranged as a cutout theatre. Its purpose is to give you more insight into what happened. Another way to get information is via various notes found here and there. You can watch collected memories and read notes at any time from game menu.
The game has a flower-like map structure. You have a central room — a hub, from which you can travel to various and unlock other locations, with several linear levels each. There is also fast travel. You can teleport to any visited room through the map screen.
The puzzles in Rose in the Twilight have a very decent variety, and are not boring. The difficulty of the puzzles is ok — not too hard and not too easy. Each location introduces several fresh puzzle mechanics, so you'll definetly be entertained. Developers have really put their minds into this aspect, each introduced mechanic is based on it's own principle. I  should probably note that a couple of end-game puzzles took me about an hour to solve,  but it was still a pleasant experience — when you get the solution, you realize how simple it is, and after you already know it, it takes only minutes to solve.
As many puzzle games these days, Rose in the Twilight incorporates some puzzles based on physics. Usually, you have to move something, or place something, or create a platform
, etc. What's worth mentioning, is that unlike many other games, where half-аssed physics engine only makes a hassle, it's done pretty well in Rose. Interactions are intuitive most of the time and don't require an absolute precision.
Besides regular puzzles, the game also has a couple of bossfights. As Rose is a puzzle-platformer, you'll have to find a special way to beat each of the bosses. Beating the boss often includes a lot of specific actions performed with a decent speed. So it may take you a lot of tries before you realize exactly what to do. Still, you'll like the bosses of Rose in the Twilight.
The game has three endings. You unlock them sequentially — after you get one of the endings, it unlocks the next one, along with some new locations and more difficult puzzles, to make it  more interesting to clear. Beating the game also unlocks time attack mode, which can be very entertaining, when you already know all the puzzles and can concentrate on speed. The  game shows you results for each room, so you always know where you should improve your times.
It's hard to review Rose in the Twilight without looking back at its predecessor - htoL#NiQ: The Firefly Diary. TL;DR: if you liked The Firefly Diary, you'll definetly like Rose in the Twilight. With their new game, developers took into account all previous experience, made a lot of improvements and streamlining. For example, game story is now presented in a less obscure way, and supported by in-game text notes, to make it easier for the player to interpret and understand what's going on. Compared to The Firefly Diary, puzzles in Rose have more variety, they're easier to understand, and the difficulty curve rises more gradually than it did before. Here Rose won't encounter the same problems, as Mion had with the fourth boss in The Firefly Diary
Some changes may still be questionable, though. For example the pallete of sepia and reds here may be not everyone's cup of tea, and some may even see it as bland. Still, it's an imporant element of artistic presentation, but it affects your perception of locations. In the previous game locations had vivid visuals and looked more distinct thanks to different colors. Rose in the Twilight also has distinct locations, but mainly thanks to set pieces, like a garden full of flowers, library full of bookshelves, etc. But in some other locations everything just blends together and becomes hard to tell apart. Nevertheless, a storybook-like artstyle of Rose in the Twilight is great and is a good match for games story-telling.
The music in Rose is nice and soothing, I even have some tracks in my favorites playlist
, but melodies on first few levels sound too similar, at least for my taste. This wasn't the case with the previous game, as each location had a very distinct melody. Still music matches the gameplay perfectly, be it slow-paced puzzle-solving or a slightly faster-paced bossfight.
Overall, Rose in the Twilight is a really good game, and a true spriritual successor to htoL#NiQ, with a distinct visual style, soothing soundtrack, good story and many great puzzles. At the time of this review, SteamSpy estimates its sales as around 3k, which is really a shame. This game definetly deserves more attention, at least from the puzzle-lovers.

curator.

The worst game I've ever played, and I do not say that lightly. As a game developer myself the poor design choices and number of bugs are shocking.
===========================
ENTERING THE GAME
Plenty of spelling errors - even in the main menu. I knew there was trouble when the first thing you see when you load the game is a message telling the player to post any bugs or complaints in a forum - ie 'stop bugging us to fix things, we don't want to hear it'.
The game has a tutorial option from the main menu, and even though I already had some misgivings with the whole bug reporting and spelling errors on the front screen I was cautiously optimistic. Unfortunately it would be too much to hope for a full tutorial game mode for new players such as myself - instead there were walls of text explaining some game elements.
I left that for the time being and began my save file, after navigating the poor user interface of the main menu - seriously, the 'back' button is a cross next to the menu title? Why not a button that says 'close', or moving the placement of the cross to somewhere more intuitive? Poor UI design.
===========================
STARTING THE GAME
You load up in presumably what is your house. There are tooltips onscreen, but its execution is poor. Some tooltips flash for a second. Some functionality is disabled unless you follow the tooltips - but you aren't told this. Tooltips don't stay on screen as 'objectives' and thus are assumed to be optional....... until you accidentally fulfill one and something that wasn't working before suddenly works.
For example, the first one says 'Press F to travel from your house to the store backroom'. I press F and nothing happens, so I instead decide to go for a wander through town and find my shop myself. No stress, I get that done, the shop is opposite my house - except I can't open the chests in the backroom to retrieve my ordered items once I'm done ordering my first batch of inventory. Turns out the tooltips are railroaded in the worst way - hindering what I was able to do without informing me of this, but also with no way to review them or find out what triggered them to show so I was able to be reminded how to follow them.
By accident I decided to go back to the house, apparently had to stand in proximity with a trapdoor on the floor before pressing F, then I was taken back to the backroom and ONLY THEN I was able to interact with the chests and retrieve the items I had already gone ahead and ordered.
Why not a simple objective system? Or why not let players fumble through the game, as already you have to do, but don't disable core functionality? Like, even an additional tooltip saying "You cannot do this until you have completed X" would help.
Tooltips also did not have a consistent format - some are white in color and show up as an overlay on the UI, another couple were yellow and hovering in the environment.
===========================
GAMEPLAY
I started off my business by selling small potions and some runes I found in the trash on smaller pedestal display stands. Every single time I left the shop and returned, they'd have fallen off the pedestals - without fail. It was funny the first 4 or 5 times, but was pretty annoying after that. As the game is unclear with how the sale system worked, I was unsure if AI customers would be able to buy stock if it was on the floor, so I'd have to keep taking them off display and putting them back on the pedestals again.
More spelling errors.
There are several different overlay interfaces in the game - one for ordering stock, one for interacting with villagers etc - they all needed different keys to be pressed to exit them (why not a universal exit button??). Though in saying this, thankfully ESC seemed to always work when I fell back on it.
Again, there seems to be a sequence to the tooltips but again, functionality seems to be disabled until you've fulfilled the last one - which you might have missed as it blinked on screen.
Had to rebind my keys in the Options menu in order to increase profit margin of my items - game would not pick up on me pressing my + button.
Every time you try to jump with spacebar, you get snarky responses from the developers, lovingly voice acted. Might have been a bit funny if this was a good game, but just really grated on my already stretched patience.
===========================
CONCLUSION
I tried to give this game a fair go, was even excited when I picked it up at my local EBgames but goodness what a disappointment. I understand if this was a fluke that took off, what with 100,000+ downloads (most of which I assumed were paid for) but there seems to have been no proper overhaul or QA testing from alpha build to its present state.  Fair enough if this was a three man project that accidentally took off - but if you can't design, hire someone who can and if you are charging money for it then you have no excuse not to release a finished, polished product. This game should either be free-to-play, with all bugs and poor design intact, or it should be overhauled and only then charged money for.
If I were the developer, I would personally would be ashamed to exploit this game for money. I probably wouldn't even want people playing it for free without some serious changes being made to it. I hope I can get a refund through Steam, and support a game with the proper care and attention to detail put into it.

Let's start with Mount & Blade: Warband's very interesting take on singleplayer where you hire troops, complete missions, fight, trade, conquer and strive to rule the kingdom that I really enjoy. I've never really seen it done like this before, it's really a cross between an RPG and strategy game kind of meshed into one. I think there's plenty to do and ways to play in the singleplayer but if you do start to get bored, there's a million massive overhaul mods which add almost everything you could ever ask for.
Now to what I like most about the game, the multiplayer. This game has the best multiplayer competitive gameplay experience ever. Period. Well, I guess that's just my opinion, but I love this game. There's been other games after this like War of the Roses, Chivalry Online and Life is Feudal, just to name a few and in my opinion, they don't even come close to the perfection of combat that this game is. The combat basics are very simple, and anyone can fight using a shield (to varying degrees, obviously), but when you have to fight with blocking, it becomes a whole 'nother game. The combat is smooth, responsive, impactfut, strategic and intense. I know that's a lot of words, but really, the combat is a masterpiece. I have never seen it done better. Now, what makes the multiplayer even better than just the superb combat system is the class architype system. Yes, it's been used in many other games but honestly, they feel completely different and have their own high skill ceiling to master. The classes, Infantry, Cavalry and Archer/Crossbow all are extremely enjoyable to play and can have a huge impact on the game. The gamemodes are typical of any other game, sieges, one-life round based money system where you just kill your enemies, deathmatch etc. The money system is really awesome the way that the better you play, the more income you earn which lets you buy better weapons and armour. "But doesn't that mean one person could get gear up then wreck everyone?" you might say! But what makes it EVEN BETTER is that fact that since this is a 100% skill based game, a naked person with a club who is the better player can beat a fully armoured knight with a great sword. Anyway, where this multiplayer system REALLY shines is when you have clan wars. Having a group of players assigned to different roles and fighting in medieval combat against other clans with an insane amount of skill involved where one good player could literally defeat 10 people on his own, is immensly enjoyable and satisfying. That being said, it can also be extremely frustrating if you make a mistake, die early, or get focused. The skill ceiling in this game is one of the highest I have ever seen, in any game, ever. One good player can make the biggest difference in a match, and a fight between two good players is a sight to behold, let alone two clans full of amazing players fighting it off - there's nothing more intense.
Now to the negatives I can think of. The graphics are quite dated now even though it's a decent looking game. The factions are quite imbalanced which sucks. The community, atleast in Australia, is tiny now and the competitive scene is long gone. It's basically just a group of trolls who play now which is no fun.

Game Name: Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons
Original Release: 2013
Personal Rating: A
Estimated Playtime: 3 hours
Multiplayer/Coop?: None
Played on: Steam Controller
Brothers- A Tale of Two Sons is a great game. I received my Steam Controller a while ago and decided that I needed to get into the groove of using a controller. I've always used a keyboard and mouse combo, and this seemed like a great game to use the controller with, and I couldn't cheat and use KB/M since it is controller only.
Controls:  The controls are very simple to use. A joystick to move and the trigger allow the brother to use their special move. The twist? You have to control both brothers at the same time. On the steam controller this meant using the joystick and the right touchpad. Was it useable? Definitely. Not to mention that it was easy enough for a controller noob like me to get used to.
Graphics: The graphics are very indie-ish. This isn't a demanding game at all, but what makes it special is how the graphics interact with the artwork and the background to create the story. The creators place benches around the game and through the brother's special moves, you are able to sit down and observe the scenery.
Music: The music fits the mood perfectly. From the funny and entertaining interactions that the brothers have with the other characters, to the scary and odd moments that leave you satisfied with the way that the scenes end.
Overall: Highly recommended. It is basically an interactive movie. The cut scenes meld together with storyline, audio, art and graphics that allow you to forget that you are playing a game. You will love entering the world of brothers trying to save their single father, all the while speaking an unknown language, and will have you crying by the end.

First ever public review: I am compelled to not recommend this and I hate that I have to. Minor Spoilers within.  TL;DR wait until it goes on sale and the only thing you are buying is content.
The Good:  Gunplay and "route choices" are excellent, better than HR in terms of ways you can go about actually playing the game.  The balance is a bit too extreme in some cases however, it does trivialize a great deal of it's content because of the sheer power the improved cover and stealth system offers.  Distractions you can create to isolate enemies add another layer of creative gameplay and on the whole this is very well done if not a tad bit overpowered.
The general atmosphere of the game and it promoting exploration is excellent.  I do wish you could use the info you gathered in a meaningful way somehow, *spoiler* for instance getting into a certain apartment in golem basically tells you who the bomber was and you can infer who the big baddie is... you cannot act on that info in any way.
There are a few sidequests that are exceptionally well done.
When the graphics aren't in slowdown mode the game looks and plays amazing.
Overall, the actual game itself is very well done and you can get a solid 40+ hours in the first playthrough if you take your time.  Voice actors and animations in general are top notch, a few of the maps are extremely well done and thought out, especially the bank map.  The developers just nailed it from a gameplay standpoint.  I do wish however there were more breach opportunities in the main game.
The Bad:
The port to PC is a joke.  Either they don't care about PC gamers or they are just haphazard in their testing.  There are spots in the game that are very poorly optimized and was forced to drop the quality.  I can tolerate the showstopping bugs I encountered, one they already fixed.  A game this complex needs some leeway for bugs imo, and to be honest they weren't that bad.
The "spacebar" from quicksave in cover will get you fkin destroyed in the wrong spot.  Also, it is very annoying to drag people away out of sight lines and constantly bring up some objective menu or pocket secretary or the crafting, it's really obnoxious on the guard mission toward the end. "Drag" needs to be remaped to takedown.
Speaking of keyboard mapping, I was very disappointed I was unable to bind a key with an ALT modifier.
The story does taper off quite badly toward the end and feels a bit rushed compared to the fleshed out feeling of the first half of the game.
The Ugly: Why this is getting a negative review from me is quite simple and has been repeated numerous times.  The blatant disregard for the customer in terms of these microtransactions in a singleplayer RPG and one time use DLC items was a *very poor* choice on someone's part.  I paid 90 bucks for a game that insults people for more money.  I did this on the good faith of the previous game which while this is a worthy sequel in many ways, it also feels like half a game in many ways... and the nickel and diming doesn't help.
I find it ironic that a game franchise whose general theme is "don't trust tech companies" is essentially giving us a reason to not trust a tech company.  This is EA think and I am very saddened to see it come to this.  This isn't quite on the level of One Man's Lie, but it feels like a similar betrayal.  SQenix has just dropped a few pegs in my mind over this one.
This crap needs to come to an end, and the only way it does is to lambast your game needlessly.  If it wasn't for this issue I would say it's well worth the 90 bucks for the future content.  Goodwill in this business goes a long way and while you may have snowed us this time, it came at the cost of cutting your own throat.

"Do you recommend this game?" That's an interesting question, Steam. Disclaimer: Huge RWBY fanboy here. Been there, done that, bought the t-shirt. (Literally. Wearing it right now.)
TL;DR: Painfully average third person action game that I want to recommend to everyone, but too tough a sell in its current state at $25. Boring as f*ck solo on lower difficulties, but lots of fun can be had with a good team, and Eclipse mode presents a nice challenge if nobody else is playing. New game mode (horde) coming soon™, will update review then.
I'll say this: I enjoy this game. I bought it within hours of it going up on Early Access, and about 90 hours of my playtime was pre-"release." I've had fun, I've met some cool people, and I've enjoyed my two-ish-hour spans of pummeling waves of Grimm. Unfortunately, that's about all the game has to offer right now, and it was only ten bucks back then. I'll update this review when I've gotten some time in the always "coming soon™" Horde mode that is miraculously releasing some time in the next week or so, but as of right this moment? There is simply not enough content here to justify a $25(USD) price tag.
And that's about it. For about two and a half hours a run, for as many runs as it takes for you to get bored. You unlock upgrades for your skills by killing stuff, and you complete challenges (i.e. grind a lot) to "rank up." This resets all of the skills you've unlocked, resets your characters' levels, and gives you a shiny badge next to your name and a fresh set of challenges. Once you reach rank ten, you unlock... an achievement. Woo f*ckin' hoo.
On the technical side, the game runs pretty well. Even has a "Potato" graphics preset for those of you who didn't spend four figures on your rig. Runs decent on medium on my fairly old laptop, and stays at 60 admirably on Ultra on my 970. Actual graphics options are almost nonexistent outside of the presets (TotalBiscuit would be very disappointed). Full controller support, but no rebinding for KBM or controller. Not even presets.
As I said at the top, I like the game. If you are a huge RWBY fan like me, you might like it, too. The question is whether you'll like it enough to get your money's worth with what's been presented as the official release version. When it goes back on sale, $10-$15, maybe. Probably. Enough to get an acceptable percentage of the achievements. At $25, it becomes a much tougher sell. Again, update coming when horde drops, soon™, and it might be awesome. But for now, I cannot say that the average third-person action fan browsing the store should buy this in its current state at the current price. I really want to, because there is a lot of potential here, but this still feels too much like an early access game to be 25 bucks. Sorry, RTGames. It's a decent effort from a tiny team, but you really should've considered RTX '17 as your release window. I think this is a safe generalization to make: we RWBY fans prefer perfection to a quick turnaround.
PS. First review! Hopefully the formatting isn't borked, so I don't have to go back and fix it. If you do buy the game, or own it already and stopped by to read the reviews, feel free to add me and we can play, grind, or just have as much fun as the game allows. I've managed nearly 200 hours of it thus far, and still find myself wanting to play. Probably blinded by RWBY Vol. 4 hype, but that's why I put in the disclaimer at the top.

RWBY grim eclipse Review.
Intro. RWBY grim eclipse is the first video game based off of the youtube animation series RWBY up to its 3rd season as of time of writing. The fourth season of the show is coming out this month.the game is running in the unity engine and was originally a fan made game by Jordan Scott.
Pros
1  The game is high quality and was officially endorsed by rooster teeth, so the game not only has the official voice actors from the show, but it also has the same music that has sold very well I would personally recommend that you buy the RWBY soundtrack as the music from the show is excellent and that shows itself in the game.
2  The game has 10 fairly long levels, and that is plenty for the price with 4 characters it should have lots of replay value, the game has great 3rd person hack and slash brawler style gameplay with a level up system like a moba game, I have never played a game like that before so it might be a first, the gameplay has a satisfying difficulty.
3 The game used to have poor performance while it was in early access but now it runs flawlessly on ultra for me even when playing online. The game is very stable now and can run on lower specs, the game has wonderful controller support, it plays well on mouse and keyboard and even when there are many enemies on screen the game still runs fine.
Cons
1 There is no local multiplayer, that is a huge downside as this game is very fun to play in multiplayer. If the game had  at least 2 player split screen, or better yet 4 player, then it would have been a much better game. It has a nice online multiplayer system, but I found myself wanting to play with others much more than I wanted to play alone as it seems the game was made that way.
2  The game feels very linear, it has few no extra modes, puzzles or mini games to other than the hack and slash combat. The game feels much shorter than it really is because of this and after beating the game a few times once you start to get sick of the combat there isn't much else to do, the game does take quite a while to beat and it does have multiplayer but it could have used another game mode, a mini game or puzzles.
3 The game has a nice story and setting for its short length, I found the game added a little to the RWBY story and I found the plot quite interesting although it was not too much to take in, but if you want story I would recommend watching the show for that as the game has a short story, however I did enjoy all the characters however many from the full cast of RWBY were missing.
To Conclude RWBY grim eclipse   is not very much content for its price. I bought the game for 16.99$ and yes for that price I recommend the game, I very much enjoyed it but I seem to have bought the game when it was cheaper on sale or in early access because now it is 27.99$ and for that price I can not recommend the game to you unless you are a massive fan of the RWBY series. You can go watch it for free on youtube's rooster teeth channel or the RWBY website, you could also buy the show on steam or DVD if you want.
Do I recommend you buy this game? To put it bluntly, yes and no. For 27.99 $ dollars or around that price, no I don't. I would recommend you buy it for 19.99$ to 15.99$ dollars or so. The game is wonder full and I absolutely don't hate the game or the series its just that its too much for me to recommend you buying it at that price. If the game got more content added to it, then it would be worth the price but sadly there is not enough in the game to pay 27.99$ dollars for. (note: this is Canadian prices if it cheaper in your region then it might be more or less worth it.)

Loren is a fantasy visual novel with lite turn-based RPG minigames.  The writing reads distinctly shoujo doujinshi derivative, more suited to a breathless girls romance novel than more typically masculine fantasy writing, but never-the-less it has its charms.  The plot was interesting enough to keep my attention, and exploring the various character's motivations and backstories were rewarding enough.   Overall my experience with the game had a distinct "guilty pleasure" feel about it.  It's honestly not that great a game, even by the very low standards of visual novel style games, but I had fun regardless from beginning to end.  Given that, I can't help but give it a positive review.  Sometimes you can't help but fall in love with misfit toys.

The feel of the game: Despite attacks seeming flashy and "cool", I'm not a fan of the pacing, no movement options, floaty/unrespinsive /slippery controls, no fast fall, no attack options, these things are easily felt within playing the game for the first 2 minutes, the game restricts out of the box combos and DI seems to almost be none existant, all these makes the game feel slow and lacks any sorts of skill ceiling, sure it could be a "fun" party game if you don't have SSB as an option, but thats about it.
Each characters feel like "clone" as they all share the same normals, weapons and animations, the only way to diffrentiate between the characters is their skin specials they obtain with weapons. Weapons is another problem with the design of the game, each character relies heavily on the randomly spawned weapons which makes the game unbalanced and ruins the pacing and a huge fundamental flaw with the design of the game, it doesn't make the game more fun, it does not add to the experience, and I can't seem to understand the reasoning behind it being developed in such manner.
I'd easily prefer to a selection of a limited well thought of characters, each with their own unique single weapon that they use at all times with more options and tighter controls.
The aesthetics of the game: Every character uses the same ugly flash like animations that have a cheap feel to them, the same idle animations, the same attack animations, the same movement animations. It doesn't help that the levels look like they were made by a random generator like the mario maker level in SSB4 with just different still images as back grounds, to make things worse, it uses unmemorable generic music that adds to the game lifelessness.
No offense intended, overall, I want to say Brawlhalla is style over substance, but it even lacks in style. I cannot get over this statement "Quick attacks are based on the weapon instead of the character as a deliberate choice to make it easier to move from one character to another.", it feels more like an excuse put less effort into characters and rush them out more than anything. I've played casual platforming fighters like DoN and Digimon Rumble Arena 2, nothing spectacular but each had its own unique merits that made them stand out and be fun for a while, Brawhalla doesn't offer more of the same, its less of the worst.
Check out Rivals of Aether, a game that is actually comparable to SSB.
tl;dr
-Not satisfying or competitive to play, very slow and floaty.
-Characters are literally clones: sharing both the dull move sets and the poor animations. Not even clones have so much in common.
-Generic unmemorable soundtrack.
-Uninspired level design.

Brawlhalla? this has become more of my life than it is just a game. I can't compliment the good aspects of this ENOUGH.

Brawlhalla is a fighting arena, where players can have fun playing the fame, or take it to a more technical, competitive edge. Don't downgrade this game just because it's light and bouncy, and not overly technical like Smash. That's unfair to rank these two games under the same umbrella. I came from Melee background, and I find this JUST as enjoyable as I would any other game in any other format.
REVIEW UPDATE:
There are still always ongoing changes and improvements to this game. A recent update proves that BMG openly listens to the community and takes the suggestions sent to them.
A lot of people coming from the smash community were upset that there was no fast fall mechanic. That was recently changed to accomodate the faster paced players. This doesn't not have a large impact on the game, but atleast enough to provide more creative variables. No you can't just speed hop all over the place, but you wont run into issues with players always being able to read you.

The only downsides would be its easier difficulty (and as far as I'm aware you can't change it) and its length (took me about an hour to play through), but hey, it's free!

I like Brawlhalla, its really nice to see a game try to bring "smash" style fighting to a larger PC audience. While the game does have multiple similar mechanics to the Smash Bros. games, there are a good deal of differences. Brawlhalla is 2D, it has a much smaller character roster, who's character are unlockable and rotation. There are a variety of modes including local game modes and ranked game modes! Good news if you are already excited to play. The game itself is going to be free to play when it releases and is going into open beta soon!
Brawlhalla has a few things I dont like about it as well, im not just here to talk up the game I want to tell you about some of the cons the I have found in the game. At this moment the fighters dont feel very unique, they all have a similar profile and with the exception of a small handful of fighters the majority feel very similar. There also is not a very large selection of items at the moment, two types of explosives and a few weapons from what I have seen (the weapon pickup is determined by what character you use, different characters get different weapons from the pickup), side note there is also a spike ball that can be thrown.   Content wise I feel like Brawlhalla does not have much yet.
The game has a few more noticeable cons for me, I feel like the servers are not stable enough yet for competitive play, ill often see people complain of lag after fights, or even see people lag out of the map and suicide! Even with all these early game shenanigans I still see the potential in Brawlhalla, and I definitely recommend it to smash fans or anyone looking to try it out. There might not be enough content in the game for you yet, so you can get bored pretty fast, but im interested in seeing where this game goes!

An interesting but horribly executed game.
The unique appearance and art of the game is its main selling point. The environmental art itself really doesn't look remotely as detailed or interesting as it is on the characters. The environment might as well be a blur, since that's what it feels like. The environmental design as a whole feels very unimmersive and just awkward. It doesn't feel at any point like the character is in a world or even a building, they're just running around on assets suspended infront of a very distant and vague background texture.
The gameplay starts off really great, the mechanics are interesting and the puzzles require enough thought that it is satisfying but not enough that it becomes frustrating or boring. This lasts for two biomes before the game decides to stop being fun and start being challenging, at which point many of the puzzles become very frustrating. Biome three and much of biome four are just obnoxious and over complicated, and honestly it's better to just look up a guide then to bash your skull against the puzzle when you get stuck. It's not worth the frustration at all. Furthermore, a couple of the puzzles in those two biomes are very point and click or horror game esque in that the solution is absurdly unintuitive and just shows how little the developers are able to distance themselves from the fact that they know everything about the game and the player does not. Even worse, if and when you find the solution sometimes it still doesn't work. Because either the puzzle is so ridiculous that getting the solution to work actually requires effort, or, the solution isn't actually the solution. The solution requires additional steps to be taken to make it be the solution, so sometimes when you figure out the answer it's not actually the stupid answer.
The lore is a relatively classic style in line with many animated films and such. And while the lore is told, it's very terribly played out. Players essentially find lore cutscenes as collectables, and that's it. That's the only plot in the game. The entire game is just puzzle, after puzzle, after puzzle; there's almost no plot or cutscenes or anything other then just puzzles over and over. The only reprieve is the collectable cutscenes and extremely uncommon live cutscene. It does not feel at all like there is a plot or story to the world, because there technically isn't one. Adding in collectable cutscenes to a game and having almost nothing else that contributes to the plot or lore, is not a story. And it feels nothing like one.
The developers obsession with making the cute little girl protagonist sacrifice themselves to death machines in order to open each new area is also, questionable. Because this to serves no purpose at all to anything in the game, other then to be torture pornography.
The fact the game has a final boss is nice, the fact the final boss is the low point of the main game is not. The final boss attacks in the same pattern every time, and can only be harmed by manipulating specific attacks of theirs into a weapon against themself. If you get hit once, the whole fight resets. So while you are trying to figure out the awkward way you have to contort their own attacks against them, some of which will kill you until you learn how, everytime you get hit once you die and the whole thing resets. It was boring, and infuriating, and was basically just trial and error. Having to repeat sequences you already know how to beat until you reach the one you actually are trying to learn how to beat because each time you fail at that one it hard resets you; is horrible.
The game also has general design oversights, which can lead to certain areas becoming unplayable and players just have to reset the map and try again. Other oversights can force players to repeat entire rooms or spend near double digit minutes walking around because of said oversight. So, if you get a quest item in room one, need to take it to room five and die in room four; you respawn in room four and the quest item respawns in room one. So you have to return to room one, redo the room, get the item, then do it all again.
It's also nice that the game has a post story, it's not nice that the post story map is literally just assets from all the previous maps mashed together. Literally, it's just assets from every previous map used all at once. And the post story puzzles are literally try die repeat, there's very little thought anymore it's mostly just doing what the puzzle wants you to, and hoping it works. Retrying if it doesn't. It feels completely like a chore, and I literally stopped halfway through and just decided to not play anymore. It wasn't fun or interesting and seeing the end of the miniscule plot was not worth how bad it felt to just grind and toil over a thing that's supposed to be fun.
But the game does have one of the cutest moments of all time so there's that, and only that.
Isn't worth the price at all, it has an okay length but most of that is just work as opposed to fun. There's no real production or design value to the game. For half the price it could be recommended to players who exclusively adore puzzles but that's all the game has is sometimes nice, sometimes unfair, sometimes boring puzzles and one really nice moment.

: Nippon Ichi Software, Inc
: NIS America, Inc.
==========
I initially passed over A Rose In The Twilight when I first saw it, but I’m glad I’ve finally given it a chance and got the opportunity to play it. It’s an intriguing puzzle platformer with a dark yet touching story that most players are sure to enjoy. With a decent price point, it’s a great way to spend an evening or two while enjoying an interesting story.
==========
You begin the game as a small girl named Rose. Our small hero is the bearer of a nasty curse which physically manifests on her back as a bleak, grey rose. This flower allows her to absorb blood from the environment and pass it into certain objects to manipulate them in some ways. Most of the story is told through small flashback scenes that show her gruesome and tragic past. These are shown by absorbing special pools of blood that are cleverly hidden in some areas. These pools of blood and memories are a soft requirement for progressing to some areas and must be found.
The entirety of the story is told with no words. It’s up to the player to interpret what they see, however some of it is rather straightforward. As cute as Rose can be, the overall theme of the game is very dark. There are times when Rose knows that she has to die in order to progress, and even knowing she will be brought back to life by her curse, it’s still very hard to watch these scenes.  Regardless, Rose must work together with the Giant to make their way through the castle, collecting her memories, and try to find a way out.
When objects in the environment are colorless, they are frozen in time. However, when Rose passes blood to them, they come to life and are able to be interacted with more. Rose’s curse is also a blessing. It allows her to come back to life at special flower buds should she fall to the castle’s many traps and threats. There are even areas that can only be opened by offering some of her own blood. These “execution rooms” are pretty dark and graphic, so a fair warning for small children who might be playing. Even though the animation is fairly minimal, you can still make out that Rose sees that there is no other choice but to offer up her own blood in these rooms.
Each area is fairly small, with hazards scattered throughout. These hazards become increasingly numerous as you progress. Manipulating blood between objects allows you to create paths through each of these areas and to avoid the traps you encounter. A nice feature you can find in your pause menu is a small map with which you can use to move freely between areas, should you miss a blood spatter for a story cutscene.
Along the way, Rose meets a hulking Giant. This Giant can use his considerable strength to carry Rose around to avoid hazards and even interact with things that Rose cannot. It can also throw Rose to otherwise inaccessible areas. Together, they compliment each other well and work upon each other’s strengths. You will find that the Giant is an indispensable ally in Rose’s quest. Their interactions with each other are quite cute and sometimes endearing, such as when he puts himself in harms way to save Rose from falling rubble or some other hazard.
==========
Artistically, this game is pretty stunning. It has almost a hand-painted kind of feel, and it’s amazing. Everything has a vintage sort of washed out aesthetic which works very well for the theme of the game. Lots of grey and red offers some much needed contrast to set objects apart from the environment. Each section of the castle is unique, with pieces scattered throughout that distinguish the area from others.
==========
Most of the game’s sound design comes from the atmospheric noises and tracks that play throughout the castle. They really set the mood and tone of each area, as they should. The audio for a game is one of my favorite aspects of video games for this reason, and I am a big fan of games that use the audio perfectly. Other things might seem a bit minimalistic, but they really perform well.
==========
Ran great. I experienced no issues. Controller is fully supported, although I had a tad of difficulty figuring out some of the controls and changing them. Ran at a great framerate (60 FPS in most cases), and I had no random crashes or anything of that nature.
==========
A Rose in the Twilight is one of those games that needs to be experienced for one’s self. It is not the same watching someone play it or reading about it. Simply explaining it to someone else will never do it justice. You have to play it yourself to feel the full impact. While it can be a bit slow paced, and by the time it starts to get really good it’s all but over (I finished it in just a couple of hours), it’s still more than worth giving a try for the unique art style and touching story.

Very good little gem of a game. Both a plateformer and a puzzle game, the game has you control Rose and the giant alternatively to progress through levels and collect blood to unlock both memories and progression.
The game's difficulty is a bit all over the place thanks to occasional difficulty spikes, but for the most part easy enough that you won't get stuck often. That said, the game's physics are a bit of a wild card, which will make the game both easier (by allowing you to do things clearly not originally intended) and harder than intended on occasions. Overall, though, the gameplay is enjoyable, and the game always renews itself, and thus is never boring.
While there is barely any dialog, the game does a good job of telling its story through notes, memories, and environmental storytelling, and it's a charming story.
As for length, the game is roughly 10-15 hours long if you don't do the time attack challenges but collect everything. That was just right for me, but might feel short for some.
Most people should have a great time playing this game, even without any particular skill in plateformers or puzzle games.

Even though there is no voice acting, the character interactions and memory events are capable of telling you a story. Gameplay-wise, very simple and easy to control. Solving each room puzzle is fun and feels great when you beat them. At the time of this review, I am currently working on Time Attack and finding the locations of two elusive achievements. I recommend this game if your looking for a decent puzzle challenge, relatively short game, or just a nice story.

Great game, easy to learn and play. When you start out, it takes a little time to get into it, you'll probably die a couple times before you get the hang of it, thus losing to stronger players all the time.
The only bad thing about the game now, which has nothing to do with the game, is there's not a lot of other players playing now. So, a lot of the people left playing it are higher levels. So, the function that controls associating people with people more close to their level, thus making it easier to fight each other, is disabled, practically. I've been on there recently, and there's usually around a 100 people, globally on, when I'm on. This is the only problem I usually find, as it affects gameplay. Without enough people, each multiplayer game has a hard time surviving.
Now, if you want my honest opinion of the game, it's great, awesome even.
I usually delve into campaign when I don't have anyone to play with. However, even in campaign I get the opportunity to shoot up a lot of cpu's so it's great.
The key is learning how to learn to use each weapon as quick and efficiently as possible and learn how to use your character as best you can. Ex. wall running and moving while shooting is key. The moment you stop running, especially in multiplayer deathmatches, you're dead. All it takes is a guy to come up behind you, or snipe you from afar, and bang, you're gone.
The loss of a bunch of people makes this game harder, as you have to face down really tough opponents at times, and there's a lot less people to have fun with. You aren't able to get through the campaign as easy, due to this, also.
My advice to others is, if you have steam friends, have them come along with you, at least when you start out. This will allow you to further both of your profile characters and gain a lot in the process.
Also, don't forget to log in everyday as you get daily rewards, as well as rewards for winning a specific amount of normal matches, usually 2 or 3. Use gold to unlock characters and weapons, mainly, although, if you don't really care what to use gold on, they have much much more to save up for.
You can spend money on this game, but you really don't have to. I haven't seen a need.
I should address, before closing, that when you start, if you're going to pick a character that'll last in a fight, and gain you gold more quickly, I'd pick either Elena or Max. If you don't care gender wise, Elena or Max is perfect. Elena's got the best for far away battles, which is a lot of times better. Max is good on offense and defense, with a massive shield built for ultimate defense and ultimate pummeling of opponents. These two are quite honestly, the best characters in my opinion, and will take you far quicker.
Ivan is often a common choice, although, he is likely to die quicker, as he acts mainly as a melee fighter. If you're going to use him, I recommend being familiar with his third weapon, a sniper rifle. To activate the scope, right click when using and you'll be able to see cross-hairs and a lot close up. On a fun note, the sniper can actually hit more than one target if the targets are really close to where you fired. However, the cross-hairs must be directly on a target, not an inch off, in order to hit.
Lastly, this is important for any new players, or anyone who is playing who doesn't know this. On a laptop, especially the newer ones, like I have a Toshiba laptop, you have the special keys which control volume and so much more. Now, when playing campaign, you have things called revival coins. It'll ask when you die to press F5, or F6. However, when you press the key on a laptop, it doesn't work, and you usually have no idea why. I only figured it out recently, that you have to press the key on your laptop named "FN." It's a little blue key on my computer on the left side in between my "windows" key and my "CTRL" key. It's on the bottom. You'll have to press the "FN" key plus F5, or F6, as asked by the computer, in order to revive.
So, to repeat, "FN" + F5 (or F6) = revive coin use
Now, just to warn you, you'll respawn in different places in the room. It'll usually be in some beginning part of the room you're in, not in the very beginning of the campaign, so don't worry about that. However, where you respawn isn't always where you want to. So be careful when respawning sometimes, as you sometimes wind up in the wrong spot and die quickly.
Alright, I think this'll do it for now. Hope this helps, and hope you all enjoy.
