First off, what is Our Nation's Miner? What it's supposed to be is a space game where you pilot a ship, gather resources, craft, and better your ship. So far so good. In reality,  Our Nation's Miner a good attempt at a good idea, but it falls short.
If you are about to add Our Nation's Miner to your cart, here's what you're getting yourself into:
.Story/Premise.
There's not much of one. Basically shoot stuff to make stuff so that you get the clearance to shoot more stuff and make more stuff.
.Controls.
Sloppy and slippery. In some situations, this can be a good thing (heh)... Just not when you're trying to pilot your super cool space ship all over an admittedly beautiful universe in order to shoot at asteroids or sell materials. They feel entirely unresponsive and, even if you aren't moving your ship using the wasd keys (you use the mouse to aim your lazers), it tends to drift all on its own until it hits something and is forced to stop. It's unnecessarily difficult to manuever into the ports that
The firing is also unsatisfactory. It sounds nothing like a lazer and the feedback when blasting an asteroid to smithereens is lacking.
.Loading screens.
Personally, an automatic red flag. There's one of these babies (not too long, but still) every time you move between areas.
.Soundtrack.
The best part of the game. It's chill and pleasant.
.Graphics.
The space theme is well done with metal structures and glowing bits. It's pretty, but I prefer funtional any day.
.Bottom line.
I can't with a good conscience recommend this game--and especially not for 15.99. It feels more like an alpha than the finished product.

My playthrough was on the normal difficulty level.
I played this game through with an excitement that I haven't felt for many games in recent memory.  If you check my steam profile you'll notice that I have played Human Revolution for about ~90 hours at the time of writing this.   This review will be comparing to DE:HR more thank Mankind Divided as a standalone product.  If this is your first outing with the series, I would give this game about an 8/10, where the 2 points lost are for mechanics, bugs, and a few immersion breaking moments / annoying dialog pieces.
For those who have played the series, here's what you'll dislike about this game:
-The active cover system is just plain horrid.   It's clunky, at times it's weird, and sometimes if you're loading from a save and you're in cover (why wouldn't you be?) hitting spacebar to load your game will make you run out into the open.... this is a pretty glaring flaw.
-Certain weapons can't decide if they want to be silent or not.   During my playthrough I should have gotten the Foxiest of the Hounds achievement but didn't because of a bug involving the stun gun alerting enemies and the TESLA alerting enemies that are already unconscious.  It's fine, I'll just do another playthrough at some point, but it is annoying.
-The story of the game itself was a bit weaker than DE:HR.   Without giving away much of the plot -- The Illuminati gets called out by name a lot, there's a general air of there being a conspiracy, and there's an overall sense that the characters know that there's an underlying conspiracy, where in DE:HR there was more of a sense that things were more about how the player percieved them.   During multiple points in the story I found it hard to relate to characters that I was working with (Chicane wasn't easily liked, nobody in the juggernaut collective was really wonderful, and there was a couple of people at Interpol that were...decent.)
(MINOR SPOILER ALERT:  TALKING ABOUT ENDING BELOW)
-The ending itself was pretty "meh" and to my understanding I got the best one (I saved both sets of people), and was basically a "To Be Continued" of sorts.
So at long last, pros and cons:
Pros:
-Augments / abilities were pretty familiar to those of us that played DE:HR
-New Augments / Abilities didn't make a huge impact on gameplay and weren't required to complete areas
-Graphics are beautiful as long as you're not super-close to anything
-Gunplay is better than DE:HR overall
Cons:
-Story / Ending were weaker than DE:HR
-Game feels like it's a very minor part of a larger story
-Despite many branches in the story, the ending seems like few choices truly "mattered"
-Ending might actually make some people "mad"
-Despite having 44.6 hours played, the game is only about 12-15 hours long with MOST of the subquests getting completed, full stealth / ghost / pacifist  I think I had 1-2 detections all game.
-You can get detected by some bugs with the Stun Gun / TESLA.
Overall if you are a fan of the series I'd give this game a 8.5/10
If this will be your first installment -- Buy Deus Ex: Human Revolution first, then play this... if not you'll say 7.25 - 7.5

Let's talk about a developers need to be ready for a game at launch.
Fans wait. For what feels like forever, and is really only 4-6 years before some titles launch sequels. We hash out the older games, even when we are bored with them. Searching for something new to do on a game that hasn't been updated for years. Because we love the classics.
I waited a day before buying this one. I had to have it, too much nostalgia.
Played it for practically 3 days straight, story brings you in just like the original. Tons of politics. Lots of different possibilities.
But then, as you approach the final portions of the game, you get crashes. Hard crashes. More specifically, on the subway walking scene after you do the harvester mission. To the point where you simply cannot progress in the game. There's nothing to do but to wait on these people to fix the game you've been waiting on.
The game they took this long to develop, to work out kinks. The game that's still not free roam, restricted on what and when you can explore, and is mostly linear: They can't even make work correctly through one playthrough.
I'm so disappointed. Frustrated.
I will come back, and play it again.  Mainly because they can tell an extremely good story despite having a main character who is always a monotone♥♥♥♥♥♥ and that there is enough to do. But paying 60$ for a title that you expect will deliver, just for it to fall short of expectations really blows.

Second, there are some frustrating glitches that detract from the experience. Granted, it's been less than a week since release, and some of these have already been patched. Hopefully there are more patches coming. Third, a lot of the spoken dialogue is poorly written/edited and just comes off as being really odd. Lastly, lip sync and character animations aren't the greatest, but this is something I've come to expect after the last Deus Ex game.  All of that being said, I still thouroughly enjoyed playing Mankind Divided. It's gorgeous, the level design is incredible, and most importantly it's a lot of fun to play.

From what I've played so far, 'Our Nation's Miner' seems to be a modern take on the classic 'Asteroids' experience with a bright, colourful design and a decent upgrade system. Essentially, it's a mix of the old and the new. Flying around the hub areas can be surprisingly serene, with impressive background aesthetics and a soothing sci-fi soundtrack. When it comes to blasting asteroids, playing around with the various weapons as you unlock them can be a satisfying experience, and the visual effects combine with the audio to create an oddly calming atmosphere. It's like comfort food.
The only cons I can think of right now are that the interior spaces are quite small, the lore, while intriguing, is not fully explored, and there could be more to spend well-earned cash on. All of which would be great to see expanded upon in a future update. Apart from that, the game is fun! If you're looking for an arcade-style space shooter, I say give it a try.

It's my first review and the thing is I really love this game but I can't bring myself to recommend this to anyone
So here's the problem (MY opinion)
First off, It's not Gunz 1, if you are expecting tough skill and grind to win (minus using UC and Rebinders and stuff) this is not the game, it's still however fast paced, exciting as hell and good fun if you aren't serious.
1. It's straight out P2W, the game itself can be supplemented with good skill but really at the end of the day, you're going to have problems once the skilled players have the cash to buy the weapons imbued with lightning, fire extra dmg etc. Yeah sure, you can wait and play and win to collect crystals to buy that stuff, but still P2W players are gonna get it first. It's a gamble if you wish to obtain the weapon you want and if you're not paying, you're going to take MUCH longer.
2. The characters are severey imbalanced, of course as a player you must identify what you want and purchase the right items and etcetera to balance the playing field, some characters are just going to be better than others in certian situations
-For Example, Max is OP BIG time but clunky as hell.
-Rena is fun as hell and great 1 v 1 but in range and hp she's so bad you'd die before fully enjoying her and that's the problem, the game strangles whatever fun you have if you are new to the game especially if you are playing characters that require the dexterity to deal with enemies.
-You have Wayne he's hard to use but great if know how especially in gladiator (purely swords)
-There's the rocketeer she's hard as hell to use again, great if you know how
-You have Elena who's pretty all rounded and for some reason at campaign fantastic
-And finally Ivan, now if you are new, I'd recommend this guy, purely because he's rather blanced unless you are certain no amount of sniping is good for you.
Now as you can see, it actually takes -----loads of skill to adapt to new characters if you really want to play right. It doesn't require the effort and dexterity as Gunz 1 but you know what, it's not supposed to, some elements of K-style remain but not enough to qualify it as a K-style based game. It's really easy to run up walls, manuver and for a third person fast paced MOBA kind of shooter this actually has a great setup which is really entertaining (AT TIMES)
3. The game lacks content event the cash shop, in terms of looks there is hardly anything to differentiate the characters from one another there is so little in terms of aestatics asides from the stuff you buy from 2.99 USD to add to your character like sunglasses or a hat. there's nothing to do in terms of looks or the sex of characters (hairstyles color of hair etc) , this should have been improved from the first game. I understand the typical Korean 3rd person MOBAs doesn't allow that but it's time we allowed this honestly, in Gunz 1 only by playing as a female character did you have an advantage in performing the K-style move butterfly and this made late game in the higher levels populated with 'female' characters there were so few 'guys' it was laughable. I don't know about you but as a player I want my character to be personification of me, my avatar, my extention in game, to be restricted of choice was just strange to me.
4. Host system hoooooo, this is a doosie, it's..... how do I put this.... ____ING HORRIBLE, there is no excuse or a better word for this, on lowly populated servers you can be paired with people wayyyyy more powerful than you if you just started, you QUEUE, I repeat queue to enter games.
I don't know what made MAIET decide this was right instead of having the old Gunz 1 system of hosting a game but there's no level difference unlike the first one, the wait times in lowly populated servers are ____ing ridiculous and inaccurate and to top it all off, the host has this unfair advantage of being less lag free in this P2P based game while the rest of the players even with 20 ping sometimes have to struggle to fight the lag, you'd think alright 'I've dodged the bullets' and BAM! every bullet lands on you. Or sometimes the match would start and you'd just be helplessly flailing around with your sword while others are shooting at you since you can't see ---- happening! Now this is unacceptable for a game, it saps the fun of playing a game and you never know who the hell you are gonna be paired up with after a game, you can however join your friends in the queue BUT only if it works which by the way half the time doesn't cause of bugs.
5. The campaign? What's the campaign, it's a joke that's what it is, it's fun but there's no variation to it, move here kill these guys, move here kill these guys there are less types of baddies out there than I can count with my fingers. After your third play you'll get so bored you'd die just because. There are practically no rewards to playing this over versus, it just doesn't matter unless you have  a burning itch to fight a tonne of the same enemies over and over again. The final boss is hilarious once you get the hang of it , you can practically solo it. Certain missions do sometimes require teamwork but that is no excuse for the lack of content given to it, the game as of now seems like it's still in Early Access here. Stuff like this isn't updated at all.
The one thing they finally nailed is a more proper ban on hacks, with Gunz 1 people were floating into walls breaking the crap out of the game, injecting .dlls, good to see this has finally been rectified.
Even so, it is just not enough to make you say, yeah I love this game, everyone should play it, there's just no real sense of direction to the game at you'd question yourself as to why you're playing, like great I finaly got his rare item, that's it? No more items? Oh great, I look like every other idiot that has bothered to waste time/effort/money to get here. No real uniqueness the items where your weapon looks just like the other guy's I do however enjoy that certian weapons are interchangeble between characters though. But it's just so boring, the thrill of killing in the past was so you could level up your stuff make it cool get better weapons, there's just so few things to pick from in this that you forget why you wanted these things in the first place.

That being said, after hearing all this, if you still want to play this game, go ahead, it greaat fun if you just don't give a crap about winning and just want a fast paced game that will challenge you.

Pros:
-Good story, pretty well written for what it's worth
-different romance paths that cater to males and females
-characters are interesting
Cons:
-the default ending(s) is rather a huge downer unless you have the DLC
-DLC has the better ending
-only way to skip battles is to beat the game once, which after they unlock cheats for you. one being able to skip battles entirely.
worth the money: eh, it depends if you're willing to pay for the DLC too
overview:
the visual novel is has a very solid story, good enough to keep you going at least. your companions aren't on the same level as the Mass Effect series, but they're still interesting enough to learn more about, and most of them are able to be romanced.
The battle system isn't anything special, and for me, is one of the weaker points in the game in regards that you have to do battles, otherwise you can't continue the story at certain points. only way to bypass battles entirely, as I said earlier, is to beat the game and unlock cheats mode.
in regards to the ending, once again comparing it a bit to the Mass Effect series, it's not as bad, far from it, but it almost doesn't matter what choice you make in the end. early on they'll tell you what is going to happen, and the only thing you can do is simply choose who at the end dies.
the DLC is a mix opinion for me. I felt as though the price was a bit much for what it had, though it also helped make a few things better, story wise. if you plan on playing, you'll probably be somewhat upset at the ending unless you have the DLC, at which then it gives the golden ending.
Overall, it's a good visual novel, great for people starting out in the genre. the battle system is somewhat uneccesary for those interested in the story alone, and the DLC is somewhat neccesary if you want a happy ending.
You are on an adventure, and it's amazing and great and there's lesbian boobs and here's a branching path you can't do without the DLC.

Loren the amazon princess is a visual novel with fighting elements where you pick a gender and set forth to help the kingdom of the amazon by finding the queen who went missing.
First of all the game is censored in the steam version, basically♥♥♥♥♥♥artwork and so on is gone. There is a workaround from the dev for this for anyone who wants to enjoy the  (great) original artwork.
The artwork of the visual novel is nice, some pictures are rather mediocre, others are really well made. No masterpieces by all means, but some were really good looking.
The story is rather mediocre. Go on , find karen the queen while discovering a bigger plot with some big evil overlord at the end of the game to kill. Only real twist was the ending and some of the characters story were atleast interestening, but mostly stereotypes. I liked the setting with the amazons that you are a loyal slave of the princess and people from the kingdom of man really disliked that amazons had slaves.
Choices often matter, game is pretty immersive in that regard, you can even kill mayor plot characters sometimes. I only disliked the talking system because it was basically only to in three ways: make a joke answer, be angry, or just a friendly answer. Meh. Also constantly making joke answers to the princess doesnt really make her be mad at you pretty much despite threatening you. Well a few moments later you can choose just the answer market with a heart to collect 5 hearts and when you got 5 you can have sex with her. This is basically how every romance works. Really sucked. Also everyone can be gay or hetero what is kinda strange, makes the people dont have any personality if everything works in my opinion.
Fighting system is broken. Basically the first fights can only be tough at bosses because they have so much life. But halfway trough the game my party became a killing machine and i had so many potions left because my characters used the most op abillity and setup i made. I played on hard by the way and it was so easy.
The writing is mediocre, while i liked some of the dialogue especially when you are meeting people you can recruit or when you first arrive in the imperium of the man who hate slavery and are democratic(kind of), i disliked many of the boring filler speeches with people around you. Most of the plot and characters were stereotypical.
The soundtrack is pretty good in my opinion escpecially the battle music. But the sound effect are ranging from bad to mediocre.
4.5/10 Game is slightly below average, only because the games art was fun to look at, choices you could make really immersed you into the game and the soundtrack helped with that very well. I found myself bored sometimes and wanted to finally have a fun conversation again or a choice i could make. Only recommenable to people who are new into visual novels and want to try out this genre but dont want to pay a full priced visual novel.

A few things before I start. I did enjoy this game. I have a few critical things to say about it but over all I had a good time, I enjoyed the story. The characters, the scenery, the world history all interesting and fascinating. I have a good time uncovering the lore, meeting the new characters, uncovering the new towns and looking over the lovely weapon designs.
Over all I give it a 7/10 for its creativity and interesting story
SPOILERS AHEAD
Now to the critique;
The story was a bit rushed. You met the characters rather easily and the only lengthening or extension of plot was in combat. Not a bad thing to be sure, a lot of titles do it but there was little to no interparty conflict or even just a consistent note of conviction with each character.
Even when pressed or given something that was supposed to contend with their morals or nature they seemed to acquess quite easily. Even those party members whom were at odds with eachother. Such as Rei and Mesphit, who ever volatile with eachother they still seem to immediatly listen to the people around them making their arguements seem rather stale.
Myrth, when in battle and in conversation with other characters expresses a dislike and abhorrence to violence yet when presented with someone she was at odds with and whated something from, Mesphit or the human wizard (I know his name it is simply rather long and I dont really want to type it), she relents and even agrees to kill, without arguement.
A lot of the characters seem to lack conviction. Not all of them mind but those that do are considered stubborn or evil in their intent. It bothered me a bit the rate at which you could acquire them if your views differed so heavily to the point of open hostility. It stuck with me through the game but since not every character showed quite a lack of will it was fine for the most part.
There are a few other gramatical problems and simple fixes but like I stated earlier not a bad game. I know its a few years out now so I reserve judgement on that front since there have been other games.
All in all however, would play again and I can not wait to see what the more recent games that have some out have in store.

Holdfast: Nations at War is an amazing game, despite its silly sounding name. I am just tired of having to say the made up word "Holdfast" out loud whenever I'm trying to describe this game to somebody in real life. If you have ever played Mount and Blade: Napoleonic Wars, you will have a good idea of what this game is all about. If you haven't, here's a description below.
Holdfast: Nations at War is a multiplayer first or third person action game that attempts to replicate Napoleonic Era gunpowder line battle combat. Imagine Empire: Total War's unique line battle mechanics, but from the perspective of "boots on the ground".  This era of warfare is characterized by bright, colorful, and beautifully emblazoned uniforms that never once considered the value of camouflage, fearless captains standing impetuously in the face of death, drummers and fifers playing inspiring music for the troops, and orderly, timed firing of inaccurate muskets in volleys of neat, orderly lines. There is something undeniably romantic about this era of warfare. The world had never seen anything like this form of combat, and will never see anything like it again. The sheer will, training, and grit of these real life men is something seems almost mythic in nature. If I saw a line of sharply dressed infantry aiming their muskets at me, loaded and presented, ready to fire, I would throw myself down and hug the earth hoping the imminent storm of steel would pass overhead, but in real life, soldiers of the era stood in the face of fire again, and again, reloading and moving in good order even as their comrades were cut down around them by artillery and musket fire. Sure there were panicked retreats and disorderly conduct when the♥♥♥♥♥♥the fan, but the very fact that they managed to actually fight effectively in such a matter is something I can hardly imagine, or even comprehend.
Muskets take 7 seconds to reload in game, which is far from realistic(in real life, under perfect conditions, a well trained line infantry soldier could reload in 20 seconds), but trust me when I say those 7 seconds are an eternity as you frantically pump away with your ramrod as a line of the King's guard charges you with bayonets. Weapons are also incredibly inaccurate, so expect to hit 1/10, or maybe even 1/20 of your shots. If you're hoping to 360 no scope an enemy from more than 50 meters away, this game isn't for you. However the RNG aspect of the smooth bore muskets is accurate to the time period they were used. Rifling technology had been around for centuries, but unfortunately cost prohibitive due to difficulty of mass manufacturing such precision tools. Napoleon, one of the most brilliant military tacticians of all of human history, famously didn't incorporate rifles in any significant numbers into his infantry, due to this drawback. In Holdfast, there is a limited rifleman class in the game which is highly coveted, since the difference in accuracy is palpable, but since there is a cap on this class, the majority of gameplay will be using inaccurate smoothbore muskets.
In addition to these line battles, there are artillery mechanics, which is only effective when you have a spotter peeping through a monocular, helping you spot targets and adjust aim. The cannon loading and firing mechanics translate over into the naval gameplay, which legitimately might even be as fun as Blackwake, a game that's 100% dedicated to Age of Sail combat alone. Crew a variety of ships ranging from one cannon gunboats to gigantic galleons, taking on roles as sailors, marines, and captains. Frantically lug chain shot to reload the cannons in bombastic, naval cannon battles, leap from ship to ship to stab the enemy captain in the face with a long pike, and play a sad, slow violin ditty as your ship takes on water and slowly sinks below the waves. Even when this game devolves into a cluster ♥♥♥♥, it is still a bundle of fun.
Teamwork is absolutely critical, so pay attention to the officers and obey their instructions in the game. You will usually see them wearing a peculiar looking hat, and holding a saber above their heads to get a line formed. You're not a special forces badass, you're just one man with a primitive firearm that can barely hit the side of the barn. Instead of being an individual during combat, you are more like a cog in a machine, just a portion of a greater, more effective whole. The more you play Holdfast, the more you begin to understand why line battles played out the way that they did in real life. Having good order, synchronized reload and firing lines, all coordinated by musical instruments are an important part of the the strategy of an effective fighting force. Being part of an organized group, not only are you hidden in the greater mass of meat shields, but firing in time and with the guidance of a skilled officer means your shots can cut down larger groups of men together, causing confusion and disarray in the ranks, versus an individual who would be lucky to kill even a single enemy before being shot himself. The coordinated volley also creates large clouds of gunpowder smoke to obscure you and your fellow troops, like a passive, unintended smoke screen whose benefits are not to be underestimated. Not to mention, during bayonet rushes, charging as a group means that even though you may die, and your friend to your left may die, the friend to your right will manage to get through to plant his bayonet in the heart of the enemy soldier. The voice chat in the game works well (despite some music spammers), but you could always hear the voice chat of the opposite team. It's a wonderful experience to bayonet charge a firing line, hearing the enemy commander's voice panic, "HOLD STEADY MEN.... FIRE! RELOAD!♥♥♥♥♥♥FIRE AT WILL! ah crap, well....GOOD LUCK MEN, IT'S BEEN AN HONOR" as you charge into the ranks. The Fifer, Drummer, and Flag bearer classes all provide passive bonuses, as well as add some excellent, catchy music to the slaughter. Definitely the most intense and violent musical based game I've ever played. I honestly think I've had the most fun playing as the Fifer, bravely marching into battle, idly piping away at my litttle flute. It's a ridiculous, surreal experience to hear the whimsical melodies of a flute in the midst of all this carnage and death, but it's all part of the game's charm. This game is just SO damn good that even playing one of the more passive classes yields so much enjoyment for me. Not to mention nice touches like how the time of day and weather changes dynamically during a match, which can lead to gorgeous sunsets, or rain soaked towns, or other effects that can alter the gameplay of the limited maps.
This game isn't finished, hence the early access tag. The carpenter has nothing to do, since there are no fortification or base building mechanics implemented yet. The melee combat is.... janky, and not nearly as polished as it SHOULD be. The game HAS the Mount and Blade style four direction blocking system, but it simply just does not work yet. In addition to this, there is no limbering/ unlimbering of artillery pieces using horses yet, or any calvary at all, so there still aren't any epic calvary charges. The naval combat also definitely still needs work, no grappling hooks or boarding mechanics other than leaping at another boat and hoping to avoid plunging into the surf.
Despite all of these issues that need to be addressed, I still whole heartedly recommend this game. The basics of shooting, reloading, and organized line battling are all rock solid, and the performance is decent, despite some laggy servers. If you have any interest at all in what the Age of Gunpowder or Age of Sail would've looked and felt like to a grunt on the ground, you HAVE to check ou this game. The addition of mechanics and Prussian forces are soon to arrive on the future, and I have nothing but the highest confidence that Holdfast: Nations At War will become an Early Access success.

A great excuse to jump into the mysterious world of Half Life 2 again. The pacing is well done, the atmosphere is tense and creepy, with at least two genuinely scary moments even if you've grown desensitized to this universe's zombies, and the little music the game uses is well utilized, especially in the action packed finale, which rivals some set pieces from the main game and its expansions. The fact that it's free excuses its brevity, and hopefully more great free content like this makes its way to the Steam store more frequently, because this is easily better than a lot of the excuses for first person games that you usually see around, especially in the horror category. No cheap and mind numbing jump scares here, just quality gameplay that reminds you why you fell in love with Half Life in the first place.

This game is simply spectacular. From the art style to the gameplay, everything just feels...perfect. Lots of people call this "Smash Bros. for the PC", but it's really not that similar. Each character has two weapons, which some other characters have access to as well. Each weapon has a set of light attacks, which is the same for any character who has the weapon. The "signature" moves for each weapon, however, are unique to that character. With the weapon mechanic, one character has three different movesets they could be using at any given time (weapon 1, weapon 2, and unarmed). The community is pretty amazing; the only time you find any toxic players are the lower ranks of Ranked 1v1. Everywhere else (i.e. higher ranks and Reddit), the people are simply amazing. The dev team constantly listens to the community and quickly responds to and acts on ideas the community have put forth. Overall, this game is 10/10.
TL;DR: This isn't a Smash Bros clone, the devs and players are amazing, and I got beat up by a Pink Bull with 3D glasses and loved it. 10/10

This may come off as just a simple puzzle game. Well that’s it isn’t it? All it is a puzzle game, pure and simple and I really do enjoy the formula of Picross and this not only scratches that itch with its basic modes of easy, medium and hard, but Picross Touch also includes a crap-ton of other player-created puzzles for me to work through. If it’s one thing you’d want in a puzzle game you’re enjoying, it’s for it not to end. Picross Touch does that in spades. If you are a fan of puzzle games and Picross Touch sounds interesting, you really have nothing to lose since it’s free and doesn’t try to milk any money out of you. If you’ve not heard of Picross before, but hate Sudoku, you may want to try out the easy and medium puzzles, but I may say hold off on the larger ones until you grasp the basics because it will probably make you want to punch a kitten and that’s just mean. There are some good brain sit-ups to be had here.
Full Review:
I’ve enjoyed many a different Picross games in the past. I’ve even got a few versions on my 3DS currently. It can be rather frustrating at times when you mess up and my Co-Op partner mentioned not appreciating it as he watched me play. He also said he may download it just to try and beat my times. Does the Steam version continue to be as worthy of my time or is it a simple free to play game that tries to pull you in only to squeeze some money out of you? Let me break it down for you.
First up, I guess there may be some of you that have not played a Picross game before so I’ll briefly try to explain it. You’re given a 5×5 up to a 25×25 sized grid and there are numbers all along two  edges of the board. Those number indicate what amount of squares should be filled in, in any given row, but it don’t tell you which ones. If there is a “5” on a 5×5 grid, you would fill that whole row or column in. If there is a “4” on the same grid, you know that 4/5 of those are filled in, but you can’t know from just that information where it starts or ends. You can infer that the middle three are filled in because while you can’t tell where it starts and ends, the line of four has to cross all three middle spaces no matter where you place it. You’ll be using this and other techniques to fill out the rest of the board.
It obviously gets harder when you add more squares to the mix. A 25×25 board will give you a lot more trouble than a 10×10 depending on the picture they are painting. You’ll be drawing Creeper faces and Mario’s head and I’ve even completed one puzzle that made a skeleton. (You can expect a lot of generic 1-9’s on the 5×5’s player-made puzzles from all of the people just making one for the achievements.) The neat part is that even when you finish all 366 of the games given puzzles, there is the Workshop option as well where you can make your own Picross puzzles. Other players have submitted thousands of 5×5 to 25×25 puzzles to keep you going if you just can’t stop. I’m not sure I’ll be sticking around to finish all 5800+ puzzles, but I’ll stick it out to complete about 2000… because achievements. It’s not something that needs to be done, but it’s something I can just keep coming back to. I’m not going to grind it out in a day or so, but it’s something I will complete.

So just for the workshop alone, this is a must for Picross/Hanjie/Nonogram fans!

As disappointing as it's promising, Kingdom Of Amalur: Reckoning has good combat and character progression systems, which unfortunately cannot compensate for its flurry of bad technical/design decisions. A great concept, with a bland execution.
Several other reviews mention the general boredom emanating from the game. After reading, I wondered "How bad can that be?"
Not recommended.
+ Depending on the player's taste, the art style is a hit or miss but still got old very gracefully
+ The combat system is great
+ The levelling system is interesting
+ Lots of content
± OST is uneven, sometimes great, sometimes forgettable
± Fights could leverage the combat system way better
± Character design is generally unoriginal
- Generic story
- Bland, mute, expresionless main character
- Generic level/world design
- Drop system is antiquated (if enemies visibly drop weapons, LET ME PICK THEM UP!)
- A giant heap of bad game design that constantly break both immersion and motivation
- Not challenging enough to justify its length, not innovative enough to justify the lack of challenge.
Kingdom Of Amalur: Reckoning is a wRPG which has everything needed to become a force to be reckoned with: you're spawned, resurrected into a vast world divided by an ancient war between Fae people and Humans, and it is up to you to learn more about your own destiny through a huge amount of quests and lore.
Clever skill tree and destiny system support a great combat gameplay. Combat is a cornerstone of this game, and doesn't feel like it has aged even if the game was released in 2012. The art style, if not too out of the ordinary, has also aged very gracefully.
Unfortunately, though, one can only flee the curse of aging for so long until it catches up. KoA:R skin might still be silky smooth, but its values are from another time.
In 2017, after the advent of Skyrim, Dragon Dogma, The Witcher 3 and Zelda: Breath of the Wild as new standard setters, the game feels like it's been collecting all the typical RPG design mistakes to combine them into one stack of fun-killing can't-have-good-thingness.
Where we could have had a truly open world experience, testing our mettle in beautifully choreographed combats and transporting us into an epic, emotion laden story, we get RNG in all the wrong places (wolves dropping iron swords and theft spotted in empty rooms), a mute hero meddling with underwhelming characters (yes, we get it, you were a drunk, could you please stop mentioning it until your next Fateweaver Anonymous meeting?), useless dialog choices (the obvious answer VS the blurt on crack cocaine), and a level design so dull the whole game couldn't be less linear if it were a never ending corridor.
This, probably comes from a design perspective where players have to go through the game 'as intended by the developers', instead of delivering a universe to explore on their own, along with the mechanics to do so in a creative and enjoyable way. Maybe it still worked in 2012?
On the top of these already immersion-breaking problems, come several technical issues, and man how do they pile up. The camera seems to never quite catch the right angle, the HUD is humongous (about 20% of the screen space) and can't be customised, the main character pulls equipment out of nowhere (I know, I know, but really, every time a non-magical shield seems to unfold from the palm of its user out of the somehow dimension, a baby dragon dies), loading a save from an empty dungeon spawns enemies at you as soon as the game is loaded... and there's more, but I think you get the gist by now.
The cherry on the sugar free, carb free, gluten free cake: in normal difficulty, fights can be summed up by spamming a couple of technique again and again, without any real strategy (disclaimer: I'm not even a fan of hard games), so much that even the city guards aren't much of a challenge. The lack of a tactical dimension defeats the whole purpose of the combat system, and adds some boredom to the mix.
Some titles do have their flaws, I am thinking of Sleeping Dogs, another 'Good concept but wew is this thing finished?' kind of game, which is full of good ideas but whose design flaws make it permanently walk the line between enjoyable and mediocre. Sleeping Dogs, though, tries. There is a story, there is some sparkle to the work, some vibrance here and there that helps players stick with the story and make the whole work worth more than the sum of its parts.
KoA:R though, is the opposite, and lets the sum of its parts overpower its general concept, leaving the player languishing for a potential that never really manifests... kind of the feeling you would get if you were expecting to drink Sprite and ended up gulping down soda water (no offence meant, soda water).
In conclusion, I can't recommend this game, even at a discount price, except if you're using it to study bad design decisions (then it's a huge bang for your bucks).

Please note the following:
1. The product that Eidos Montreal created here is absolutely great.
2. The product that Square Enix shipped - now that's garbage.
Do I like the game? Yes, I love it, I think it's great, and better than Deus Ex: HR in many ways. The visuals are great. The environments are rich and detailed. The sidequests are interesting. The wolrd feels belieavable, the augments are fund to play with, the voice acting is ok, the sounds design is pretty good. There we have it. A great game.
So, you would ask, why the negative review, if the game is good? Well, the game is good, but the product that Square Enix shipped is not. Microtransactions in a single-player game? One-time-use-only DLCs and pre-order bonuses? They have tried pulling off "augment your pre-order" stunt on us - it backfired, and now cash-shop in a single-player game. Microtransactions are a caner in any full-price AAA game, and this is a dangerous precedent - to see the said microtransactions creeping about in a single-player experience. If we, as a consumer base, don't actively fight against it, and push back, then reality is, more and more games will be flooded and made with cash-shops and microtransactions in mind, it has already happened in multiplayer, and giving a foothold in single-player story-driven games is not something I can stand for.
Should you buy the game? No, at this stage don't. Wait untill it's discounted, hit SE where it hurts - the revenue. I for one will not be buying any SE games anytime soon just for that reason. I was not aware that Mankind Divided will have microtransactions when I've purchased the title, and I was not aware that it will have single-use pre-order consumables, would I be aware of it - I'd reconsider my purchase until the product is heavily discounted.
Is the game good? Yes, it's a great experience, and probably one of the better games that came out this year. It has it's flaws (optimisation, stiff animations. minor bugs with side-quests markers), but it's a great game. I praise the people that created the game, and take my hat off in recognition of  Eidos Montreal's immensive work and manhours spend on creating a good addition to the series.
It has the variety of gameplay, that has been a trademark of Deus Ex for years -
You want stealth? You got stealth.
You want shooting and action? Here you go.
You want a mix of both? Enjoy your gameplay.
Multilayerd levels with places to explore, computers to hack and various routs to take? It's all here. Distopian future where corporations rule the world? The game offers it to you with ease.
Illuminati and consipary theories? Why where you go sir, enjoy (ok, this one is a bit lacking)
Crips textures and detialed environments, with atmposphere on par with Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light? Yup, there are scenes that will easily rival the scenes from Metro, giving an instant and clear picture of how the augs live in gethos, trying to survive when the whole world is turned against them.
Sure, there are negative aspects to the game - some might see the plot lacking, some might say that the NPC's are a tad dumb, some might not like the "stick it to the walls" traversal mechanic (it sucks, at least that was my experience with "press F to stick to the wall and "SPACE" to move to designation location - I can never get Jensen to move in a manner that I expect him to move, and so I've played without using this gameplay element).  It's not a perfect game, but it's likely to be the best action-adventure game with RPG and Stealth elements (or a stealth game with action elements?) this year, at least until Dishonored 2 comes in knocking on the door; and certainly the best AAA "cyberpunk" game of this year.

This will be both a critique and a review.
A surprisingly fun RPG from 2012. This one I ignored for far too long as it sat in my backlog. Let's start everything at 10 points and see what remains.
Visuals: starting at +10
================
An extremely well polished game with plenty of detail in just about each and every area. The graphics, while old, still look fantastic, and will probably age indefinitely due to how clean they are. They are very World of Warcraft-ish, which works great for this kind of game seeing as it's a fairly open worlded. Well done to the developers.
- Textures are a bit flat however and could have used a little bit of bump mapping or reflective lighting (depending on the texture of course). -1
Final Score: 9/10
Sound/Music: +10
=============
Music appears to be orchestra. It sounds great when it plays. Sound effects are crisp and match what they're attached to. Sounds have weight behind them. The standard criteria for sound/music holds up pretty well.
- Some areas have great music, while others are lacking in music entirely. Feels inconsistent. -1
- Sound mix between pre-rendered cutscenes and real-time rendering world cuts off between transitions. It sounds very bad when this happens, and it appears to happen with each and every cutscene past a certain point in the game. -1
- Jump scares. I'm not even joking. The sound design has jumpscares both in certain cutscenes and around the world map with various enemy encounters. Bad. -1
+ Voice acting is SUPERB. +1
Final score: 8/10
Performance: +10
=============
+ Never crashed once
+ Solid 60FPS always
+ Alt tabs well
+ Mouse locks to whichever screen the game is being played on (it's surprising how much of an issue this is on some games).
Final score: 10/10
Story: +10
========
You were dead and now you're alive. Let's go find out why!
- Overall story isn't bad. Major characters are cool and the great voice work really brings them to life. However, it doesn't really make you think... at all. Very cliche on the whole and there's no real plot points that will make you want to keep playing the game. I kept playing it like a robot, going from one point to the next waiting for something big to happen. It only happened right at the very end. Too generic unfortunately. -2
+ Still a better story than FF15.
Final score: 8/10
Gameplay: +10
===========
Alright...time to get the pitchforks. Gameplay hinges upon some hack n slash for all 3 major classes, along with spells/abilities for each of those classes. Mages will have magic, warriors will have some physical abilities and tankiness, rogues will have stealth and surprise attacks. There is also a bow for ranged combat. Wizards won't need a bow for obvious reasons.
+ No matter which class you end up specializing in (or multiclassing), you will feel like a badass. All classes are balanced in that none of them have any real hindrances to them requiring you to play a certain way (like a mage needing mana because it doesn't restore slowly overtime). A warrior can cast magic, a mage can fight head on. They all have their pros and cons though, but it's more like strengths and weaknesses, with nothing overbearing. Great job. +2
+ The slow down time insta kill attack is pretty darn cool. Every class gets it. +1
+/- Putting the Run button and Interact button on the same key/controller input is annoying as hell. You'll just be running along and you'll randomly talk to someone on the way when you're just trying to get full sprint to whatever your next chosen objective is. -0 however, as it's mostly just me griping about a minor issue.
- Whenever you die on a higher difficulty, the game will want to remind you every few deaths or so, that you should probably switch to a lower difficulty. Don't do this, ever. -1
- Some enemies will have seemless and perfect attacks between each other while attacking your character, who gets knocked back on attacks, and you'll just slowly die without being able to dodge away or attack back. It doesn't happen often, but when it does, it's extremely annoying. -1
- On the whole, the game is FAR too easy. I played on Hard mode, and only really died during cheesefest moments like the one in the point above. -1
- The ability tree takes far too long between abilities to start getting new abilities. You'll be using 1 ability for the first third of the game. Then you'll get a new ability for the second third of the game, etc. Made the gameplay very repetitious. -1
- Weapon durability. Why is this ever added in a game? Not only that, but good weapons have FAR too outrageous money requirements to get them repaired, all while repair kits are cheap as hell and you can do it yourself. Inconsistent balancing on money. Yes, I'm actually grading the economy of this game. -1
- The game screams "let me jump" but there is no jump button. You are almost entirely stuck on rails throughout each and every path. -1
- Boring and monotonous side questing. -1
10 + (-7) + 3 = 6
Final score: 6/10

lets turn our attention to the elephant in the room - micro-transactions - yes, this subject has made many understandably sore, but frankly, i had not known about them until half way through the game. lets be honest, they can be completely ignored and contribute essentially nothing - the game progresses just fine without them.
despite some low FPS issues, which i have since resolved after some tinkering with my settings, the game looks and feels amazing. even on the lowest settings, you'll marvel at the attention to detail they've obviously slaved away at in this game. from intricate designs to some rather impressive... clutter, you'll want to explore every square inch of this game just to see what it has to offer.
The gameplay itself nearly mimics Human Revolution, which is a good thing in my opinion, allowing you to pick up this game without feeling like you have to completely relearn any controls. they've also added extra features and abilities which only enhance the whole experience; have also improved pre-existing functions.
The story itself is not really worth writing home about, and the ending of the game is lack-luster, but everything in between (gameplay, side missions, exploration, +more) kept me playing this title. if you want to set the difficulty to the easiest purely for story, id recommend you'd wait until it goes on sale. but if that is not your focus, buy it now.
either way, this game is a must buy

Alright, first game reveiw ever.
Grimm Eclipse, for what I paid for it, is a fantastic game. It is a simple game featuring some of my favorite characters from any show.
so far, with the new combat system (which you must opt-in for) has improved the game immesly in my opinion. the camera is excellent with an XBOX gamepad, the combat is simple but fun to try and mix up different combos for certain enemies. I have only played Ruby and Yang so far, with Yang being the only one I've played the new update with and have been impressed. My only fault with Yang is that her ranged attack is kinda 'meh'. More to be added later. I would recommend this to basically anyone looking for some RWBY goodness.
EDIT as of Sept 17th 2016
I fel I must preface with that I love, fanatically so, the RWBY series. I really, REALLY, wanted to love this game and what it was... and what it could've been. I'm going to hold out hope that Horde Mode will breathe some more life into the game but, I honestly doubt it at this point.
at this point in time after following this game basically since it's inception, I have to not reccomend this game to new players who didn't jump on early and get it cheap. The game is almost embarrassingly short. As well as the mechanics for the game are still reletivly clunky.
If you read my previous statements I feel I need to revise my opinion on some of them. I will admit, all the characters play differently. It isn't much but it is something... Until you realize what particular combo to spam for said character. After a couple of playthroughs the system has become repetitive and boring to slog through.
Game still plays well enough with a Gamepad so there's that.
The story itself was quite bland, especially with the content that was written and presented in Volume Three of RWBY.
As I'm writing this, I'm finding less and less reasons to fight for this game. And I really wanted to fight for it. But what they presented and called a 'finished product' just did not live up to what I was expecting. And no, I was not expecting some groundbreaking acheivement that would rival a AAA title like say, Witcher 3 as an example. What I expected was to play a game that felt like it had more than the bare minimum put into it.
I think one of the final nails in the coffin would be when I found out that the soon to be released Team JNPR will be a PAID DLC. As I said beofre, I feel that the product thta is available can't be considered 'finished'. So unless there will be some sort of deal in the future where it's on sale I will not be buying it. Doubly so if you arepaying just to throw JNPR in RWBY's shoes and play the same campaign again. It just wouldn't be worth it in my eyes.
In closing (for now), this game has devolved into nothing more than a money grab. Something that could've had so much life was wrung dry in an attempt to make a meager profit. I think it's intial success can only be attributed to the success of the series it is based on because honsetly, that's the reason I purchased the game. I wanted to support a series that unfortunately, couldn't deliver in the gaming department. At least, in my eyes.

Although relatively short, Transmissions - Element 120 - offers a great addition to the Half-Life universe. The eerie atmosphere and small, detailed camera effects are immersive, but also give off a completely different vibe from that of the original games. Transmissions has unique features such as decoding and a modified gravity gun, but doesn't truly use all of it's potential. Decoding is only used once or twice and has no real purpose or importance towards the end. The modified gravity gun is one of the main tools used to solve puzzles, yet is devolved into a simple traveling device at the last fight, whereas Valve games usually force you to use the strategies you've been shown to help you beat the last level.
The story is very ambiguous. Not much information is given about the location of the game or even who the main protagonist is, though it is implied in the end that it is Gordan Freeman, according to the G-Man.
I particularly liked the level design. A big open town with destructible buildings and striders chasing and attacking you? A small room with a pit full of zombies and a switch to open the next door right in the center of them? That's what I call a thrill ride!
I know this review is too long for such a short game, but I think this game should be played by all Half-Life fans. This game is like an homage to the Half-Life games and it shows that people still care about it's continuation. Despite me enjoying it, I can't recommend this to anyone who is not familiar with the franchise because of it's ambiguity I stated above. For all the rest, try it; it's free you know.

I'm not usually into visual novel type games, this one caught my attention for the interactive RPG elements spread through out. Rather than passively just watch a story, you do level up, equip your characters, and can make choices that somewhat steer how things go. In truth, it's a game with a lot of character and personality with the unusual design of playing a character largely subordinate to another who occupies a primary hero role. That said, you are not left in the dust and what interactions you chose to have with fellow party members feels reasonably meaningful.
Graphically the game is pleasant although much imagery is reused, with characters only appearing different by facial expressions in dialogue. In combat, everything is largely static headshots so I speak only of the story elements (of which there is a lot). Speaking of the combat, it basically consists of simple actions versus enemy actions- you succeed by exploiting their weaknesses and managing your team's welfare. It's fairly standard and generally not too hard, although if you have a less than suitably team array, some battles will drag on and on (particularly with healer enemies).
The music is fair, I don't have much criticism to speak of, although it comes and goes abruptly on scene transitions. The spoken dialogue in combat is... not so good. A lot of it is generic or doesn't fit the situation. Hearing one of your party mage's utter "Filthy creature!" or casually talk about getting something to eat after beating on a former/confused ally is off putting.
I think the story was pretty solid. It's largely about racism and overcoming negative perceptions of others to become stronger as a whole. It's a somewhat standard story, but well told. NPCs and the main cast have a lot of personality. You may even choose to engage in romance with some of your party members, but the option comes up when it doesn't make much sense in dialogue- you either follow it when you get the chance, or potentially lose out in the long run.
One problem I have actually pertains to the choice in the dialogue system. You get the options of 'Joking', 'Friendly' or 'Forceful', but you're given no real idea what your character will actually say in that situation. It's just sort of a guess as to what comes out. I found if I didn't choose Friendly most of the time, the responses of others were usually on the pissy side.
Lastly, I have mixed feelings about the ending. In a way, it's a good ending, but depending on what happens, it is also extremely bittersweet and depressing. I don't want to spoil the how's and why's, but let's say I wasn't a fan of the highly vague 'pass or fail' options of the final scenario- characters may or may not be acting out of turn and the choices you're given sometimes don't make sense with the characterizations you knew them to have at the core. It was a very long and frankly emotionally frustrating sequence that made me wish it wasn't there to begin with. To potentially lose characters permanently that I've soaked hours into with very little fanfare was very depressing and unsatisfying. But at least to the game's credit, it made me care outside of game mechanics, to not to want them to die so there is that.
Despite my displeasure with the last sequence, I wouldn't be against playing more Loren (sequel please?) and I intend to go through it again playing the other starting choice. It's a pretty good socially themed fantasy story with a solid build up all throughout.
(About the DLC: Honestly? I didn't feel it added much. The Castle of N'Mar is a very short and limited area which does change how things turn out with the core story, but I didn't feel any of it was too involving or deep. You do get the potential to have a nifty monster companion join the team, although he doesn't contribute to the story in any capacity and is barely acknowledged by the characters. There's also a certain interaction between the major NPCs that should have been addressed, but you get no option to do so- you merely choose who you will kill and that's about it.)

Ok, among this review bombing by angry players, I'm going to try to spread some truth here. This was the developers' first game. Coming from a game developer, it is nearly impossible to maintain your first game. The code is horrible, nothing is optimized, and nothing was written with the intent of expanding. It's not feasible to continue working on your first game past a certain amount of time. At some point, you need to rewrite the entire code behind the game, at which point, you need the funding to do it. It's an inescapable fact of game development. They've given 8 major content updates in this game for free, and they're running out of money. They can't maintain this for free, and very likely can't release DLC because the game was probably not designed to handle DLC.
To the fans, you guys need to chill out. No one can put months of effort in without pay. The devs are trying their best to create a game that both gets them the money they need to keep a roof over their head and makes the players happy. Those two things are a direct correlation.
To the devs, you should have kept Shoppe Keep 2 under the radar for a while and tried to tie in the loose ends of this game before announcing it. It was probably getting nearly impossible to do anything, but you needed to at least have it semi-finished before announcing a new game.

Trine 2 is one of my favorite games to come out in years. It builds on the great gameplay brought in the first game by bringing in more exciting abilities, even better graphics, and a much more immersive story. The music is fantastic, the puzzles are exciting and fresh, and the mechanics of working together as a team are excellent. A special mention should be made to the incredible visuals in this game. It is by far the most colorful and beautifully stunning game to come out on PC in years. Whether you are trecking through a desert, a jungle castle, or the beaches of a beautiful sea, this game never misses a chance to wow you with its visuals. It is also a fantastic game to play with your spouse, or a couple of your close friends. Simple to pick up, you get to work together as a team, and it makes each puzzle more fun and intriguing. I would recommend this game to anyone who plays games, bar none.

Dynasty Warriors 8: Empires is fun. It provides the amazing Musou gameplay and the small, but fun tactical level of Empires. Managing your actions over the year, befriending generals, conquerin, raiding, building to finally unite China. What bothers me though is the fact that we - once again - only got a messy PS3 port. The graphics look plain bad, soldiers pop in and out at random, 360 pad configuration is a mess, a few important screen resolutions are missing and I heard of a handful bugs.
It's fun and has enough contents for hundreds of hours of gameplay, thanks to the edit mode, but you should think twice about what you're supporting with buying this game.

Does it have rough patches? Yes.
Does it need to have better control integration? Yes.
Could the graphics be better? Atleast more akin to the console version? Yes.
All those things can deter you, but for me it comes down to being glad to have this game and games like it on steam... and most importantly...
Is it fun? Yes.

In short, Mankind Divided lives up to Deus Ex name, maintaining if not improving upon the positive aspects of Human Revolution, whilst toning down the negative, even though Mankind Divided is in fact afflicted with some hiccups and insatisfactory loose ends.
The Good:
+++ Very deep story with many themes and intricacies that will require multiple play through to fully grasp.
++ Asthetically, the game shines. It's graphics (particularly the textures) and soundtrack more than live up to the expectations of modern AAA games.
+++ Gameplay allows for a variety of different styles and approaches to nearly every situation. The combat has been improved upon from Human Revolution, as has the AI and many other things.
++ High replay value
+ Unlike Human Revolution, your choices will carry over to the sequel.
The Bad:
-- Bugs. A problem with mouse acceleration, a few unexpected crashes, and worst of all, a repeating crash that almost prevented me from finishing the game. I had to load a previous save a ways back. The good news is that the developers have said they should soon have a fix for all of these issues.
-- DLC holes. Even though you'll get quite a few hours on even the first playthrough, the game's completeness is somewhat bare bones; it finishes the sequence it was intended to tell, but I get the feeling that there is going to be a lot of DLC that should have been part of the game in the first place. There's nothing wrong with DLC. It doesn't even need to be free, the problem lies when a lack of it harms the original game.
The Ugly:
> The game prides itself on allowing diversity of play style, though non-lethal play throughs aren't terribly viable unless you go the stealthy route.
> The UI can be a bit flashy for my taste, especially in the hacking portion.
> The ending doesn't feel conclusive. If you're expecting the game to end with a bang, or hate anticipatory endings, then you will be disappointed. I have mixed feelings on this given that its clear this is the case because there will be a closely-tied sequel.
All-in-all, despite the aforementioned shortcomings, I still recommend this game on the grounds that the issues will resolve themselves, especially if you're willing to get the season pass. Even if not, I'd still say the vanilla game is worth it.

First off, I played GunZ: The Duel International when it came out.  I was sad the moment ijji(or whatever that company name, which also sold it to aeria after) took the game.  That said, I was ecstatic when I heard about GunZ 2, and how Guntrix is back( he was also very active in the first GunZ).
Alright, time for the review.  I see that there are tons of bad reviews which are taking themselves too seriously, and some of those are really unfair.  I'll try to give this review a fair point of view, and compare it to GunZ, which in my opinion was an awesome game until hackers slowly destroyed it.
PROS OF GUNZ 2
1.  A bit more newbie friendly:  GunZ 1 is not really newbie friendly.  If a new player entered and played the game, and see tons of k-stylers just flying around and ripping people up, it would turn them off.  The removal of such glitch abuse from GunZ 1 can only benefit the new players coming in GunZ 2.  While some of us will indeed miss it, I would rather have the new system of GunZ 2 as it would not take you that long to start playing well if you were decent at FPS games before.  While k-style indeed made GunZ what it is(for the most part), it did push off new guys away from the game.
2.  Classes:  Gunz 1 didn't have this so everyone is basically running around with the same set of weapons at one point(everyone had a shotgun or dual revs).  Having classes encourage team play rather than one guy going rambo on the other team.  GunZ 2 is still new, I believe the matchmaking system and game modes will be improved in due time, which seems to be the issue on why other classes seem OP.
3.  Special moves:  Some will say this is a con, but I don't think so.  While it becomes annoying to die to one hit from a special move, there are tons of ways to avoid them(as almost all of them are in melee to short-medium range).  Special moves also ensures that new players coming in on this game can at least net a kill in the first pvp game they join.
4.  Campaign mode:  GunZ 1 had the "Quest" thingy that no one ever bothered with unless they were super bored.  I like how they try to put story mode in.  My only issue is the time limit as new guys will have a hard time with time pressure(if they try to solo the campaign mode).   Rewards should be better though.
5.  Gameplay: I like how they still try to make it unique even though they removed tons of stuff from gunz 1.  Wall running and stuff are still there and gives some kind of matrix feel when doing it while shooting people.  I can never get past that idea.  That sort of stuff(and katanas on a game) really got me hooked on GunZ 1 so it was nice to see them in GunZ 2.
of course there are CONS in every new game:
1.  The host p2p system just do not work on an International online game.  I know they are testing dedicated servers, and I think that is what the game would need to fix latency issues.  I had around 100-200 ping on GunZ 1 due to my poor connection then, but it is still playable and you only need to lead your shots a bit.  having several people with fluctuating pings is harder to manage.  The p2p system also fixes us to only play with players on the same country.  That just do not sound really good for an international game.
2.  The Tesla shop could need some improvement.  having random items with random time limits can be annoying to new players.
3.  Resources needed for Tesla shop should not be in the cash shop.  While the tesla items provide only a bit of increase in stats of the weapons, it could still call for the unfair "pay2win" comments just because of it.
4.  Way fewer gamemodes than GunZ 1.  I know everything is still in the early stage, but hopefully they at least give the old players the Deathmatch game mode.
All in all, I find GunZ 2 decent even though it has flaws.  Still early so a lot can change.  Having servers for each region should be their very first step though.
BOOBIES

I'm afraid I cannot recommend this game. I tried, I played it for a while and I might continue to play it (in a more limited way), but honestly I think I'm done.
There are a few technical problems with the game:
Performance of the game varies highly between updates. I got anything from sustained 60 fps (with vsync on) at high quality setting to 20-25 on the lowest quality.
Weird lag issues. Game freezes momentarily on certain occasions, sometimes at crucial events, eg. just before being killed. This is not related to CPU or memory nor GFX card. I doubt it's network related. If it is, it's server side.
The game also feels a bit unbalanced. If enemy has air superiority, you're doomed. As ground unit there's not a lot you can do. This brings me to the next frustrating fact: you have several characters each has several weapons. You cannot swap
weapons during a match. You have to leave the match, leave the squad and then you can swap weapons.
There's a lot of griding as many have said. Personally I don't mind griding per se. What  I do mind is having to play for extended amount of time at a severe disadvantage. So either you pay money to upgrade fast or you are basically working for Reto as unpaid cannon fodder for their paying customers. In some games if you're good you may get a fighting chance. But not here. As infantry - yes. As tank crewman, not really. You will be put against superior tanks that you cannot harm with your puny cannon. And when you die you'll have to wait before spawning again and then walk or drive for a while to get to the action. There's a lot of waiting and walking in this game. I guess that makes it a more realistic military simulation. ;)
The grind is the price of a free game you say. Fair enough. However this game also suffers from the same problems as any other FPS, free or not. The lack of teamplay. When I first started playing H&G I saw how team actions (capturing) actually gives you significantly more score points compared to just killing an enemy. I said "wonderful, they found a way to make people actually do objectives". Sadly I was mistaken. Points schmoints. There are still very few people who will actively engage in coordinated cooperative gameplay. You'll get a circle of campers just outside capture zone. People will use resources without considering they're limited and waste them. Tank drivers will not rotate tanks so that support gunners may engage targets. Vehicles with MGs are never parked with their guns facing enemy positions. A fair amount will not follow common sense regarding objective selection and some will even roam aimlessly around the map.
I'd gladly pay money for a game with a nice teamplay-oriented community but this one isn't it.
So, should you play this free game? After all I said I might continue. If you do, stick to infantry, most vestatile, easiest to survive. Get a car or a motorbike to get from spawn area to the action. If you go for any other class, expect a lot more grinding and consider that your leveling strategy and point investment may be subverted by game designers at any point.
